contents.heading: streaming
contents.content: The reasoning parameter works the same way with streamText:

contents.heading: precedence-rules
contents.content: Provider-specific settings take precedence over the corresponding fields derived from reasoning. Partial configurations may still use portable reasoning to fill missing fields; summary and display settings can be used alongside it.

contents.heading: precedence-rules
contents.content: This design lets you use the portable reasoning parameter by default and fall back to providerOptions only when you need provider-specific features like exact token budgets.

contents.heading: provider-support
contents.content: The reasoning parameter is supported by providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Groq, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Fireworks, Amazon Bedrock, Mistral, Cohere, Alibaba, Open Responses, OpenAI Compatible, and Perplexity. Each provider translates the value to its native reasoning API.

contents.heading: provider-support
contents.content: Providers with a distinct native maximum tier, such as supported OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, and Moonshot AI models, receive 'max' directly. Amazon Bedrock preserves 'max' for its Anthropic and OpenAI effort mappings, while Amazon Nova 2 maps 'xhigh' and 'max' to 'high' with a compatibility warning. Providers whose highest native tier is lower coerce 'max' to their closest supported tier and emit a compatibility warning when their adapter supports warning propagation. OpenAI-compatible and Open Responses endpoints receive 'max' directly so compatible servers can interpret it.

contents.heading: provider-support
contents.content: Some providers use a numeric token budget instead of an enum for reasoning control. In those cases, 'max' maps to 95% of the model's maximum output tokens by default, subject to the provider's minimum and maximum reasoning budget limits.

contents.heading: provider-support
contents.content: Maximum reasoning can substantially increase token usage, latency, cost, and the chance of reaching request or output limits. Use it when the model's additional reasoning depth is worth those tradeoffs.

contents.heading: provider-support
contents.content: Providers and models that do not support reasoning configuration emit an unsupported warning and ignore the parameter.

contents.heading: migrating-from-provideroptions
contents.content: If you currently control reasoning via providerOptions, you can migrate to the top-level reasoning parameter for portability across providers.

contents.heading: after-anthropic-with-older-model
contents.content: If you need to enforce an exact token budget (e.g. exactly 12000 tokens), keep using providerOptions instead of the top-level reasoning parameter.

contents.heading: after-openai-with-reasoningsummary
contents.content: You can combine providerOptions with reasoning for provider-specific features such as reasoning summaries or display settings. Explicit effort or budget values override the corresponding mapped fields; partial configurations may still use portable reasoning to fill missing fields. See Precedence Rules for details.

metadata.title: Reranking
metadata.description: Learn how to rerank documents with the AI SDK.

contents.content:
Reranking is a technique used to improve search relevance by reordering a set of documents based on their relevance to a query.
Unlike embedding-based similarity search, reranking models are specifically trained to understand the relationship between queries and documents,
often producing more accurate relevance scores.

contents.heading: reranking-documents
contents.content:
The AI SDK provides the rerank function to rerank documents based on their relevance to a query.
You can use it with reranking models, e.g. cohere.reranking('rerank-v4.0-pro') or bedrock.reranking('cohere.rerank-v3-5:0').

contents.heading: working-with-object-documents
contents.content: Reranking also supports structured documents (JSON objects), making it ideal for searching through databases, emails, or other structured content:

contents.heading: understanding-the-results
contents.content: The rerank function returns a comprehensive result object:

contents.heading: understanding-the-results
contents.content: Each item in the ranking array contains:

contents.heading: understanding-the-results
contents.content: originalIndex: Position in the original documents array

contents.heading: understanding-the-results
contents.content: score: Relevance score (typically 0-1, where higher is more relevant)

contents.heading: understanding-the-results
contents.content: document: The original document

contents.heading: top-n-results
contents.content: Use topN to limit the number of results returned. This is useful for retrieving only the most relevant documents:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Reranking model settings can be configured using providerOptions for provider-specific parameters:

contents.heading: retries
contents.content:
The rerank function accepts an optional maxRetries parameter of type number
that you can use to set the maximum number of retries for the reranking process.
It defaults to 2 retries (3 attempts in total). You can set it to 0 to disable retries.

contents.heading: abort-signals-and-timeouts
contents.content:
The rerank function accepts an optional abortSignal parameter of
type AbortSignal
that you can use to abort the reranking process or set a timeout.

contents.heading: custom-headers
contents.content:
The rerank function accepts an optional headers parameter of type Record<string, string>
that you can use to add custom headers to the reranking request.

metadata.title: Runtime and Tool Context
metadata.description: Learn how runtime context, tool context, and telemetry context filtering work together.

contents.content:
Context lets you pass server-side state through a generation or agent loop
without putting that state into the prompt. The AI SDK separates shared runtime
state from per-tool execution state so agents can keep track of their work while
tools only receive the values they need.

Use context for values such as tenant information, feature flags, session data,
request IDs, API credentials, access tokens, or other application state that
should affect execution.

contents.heading: context-types
contents.content: Concept

contents.heading: context-types
contents.content: Where you define it

contents.heading: context-types

contents.heading: context-types
contents.content:
In agents, runtimeContext is the agent's shared runtime state. It flows
through the loop and can be read or updated in prepareStep between model
calls. Tool-specific data stays in toolsContext, where each tool receives only
its own validated context.

contents.heading: runtime-context
contents.content:
Pass runtimeContext when you need shared state for the whole generation or
agent loop. It is not added to the model prompt automatically. Use it to
configure step preparation, track server-side state, or correlate lifecycle
events.

contents.heading: runtime-context
contents.content:
prepareStep can return a new runtimeContext. The new value affects the
current step and all subsequent steps, which makes it the right place to update
agent state between turns of the loop.

contents.heading: tool-context
contents.content:
Use toolsContext for values that belong to a specific tool. Each tool declares
the context it expects with contextSchema; the matching toolsContext entry is
validated and passed to the tool as context.

contents.heading: tool-context
contents.content:
When at least one tool declares contextSchema, toolsContext is required for
the tools that need context. A tool receives only its own context, not the full
toolsContext map. Tool description functions receive the same typed context
before each model call, so descriptions can change with the current tool
context.

contents.heading: tool-context
contents.content:
Treat tool context as immutable inside tools. If you need to change tool context
between steps, inspect the previous step in prepareStep and return an updated
toolsContext.

contents.heading: tool-context
contents.content:
For ToolLoopAgent, set context in the constructor. For context that changes
with each invocation, use callOptionsSchema and prepareCall. See
Configuring Call Options.

contents.heading: telemetry-context-filtering
contents.content:
Context often contains values that are useful inside your application but should
not be sent to telemetry providers. Use telemetry.includeRuntimeContext to
include selected top-level runtime context properties in telemetry, and
telemetry.includeToolsContext to include selected top-level tool context
properties per tool.

contents.heading: telemetry-context-filtering
contents.content:
In this example, telemetry receives runtimeContext with only requestId and the
customerLookup context with only region.

contents.heading: telemetry-context-filtering
contents.content:
Context filters only affect telemetry integrations, including OpenTelemetry
integrations. Tool execution, lifecycle callbacks, and returned results still
receive the full context values.

contents.heading: telemetry-context-filtering
contents.content:
Context telemetry filtering is shallow. For telemetry.includeRuntimeContext, only
top-level properties marked as true are sent when it is configured; if it is
omitted, no runtime context properties are sent. For
telemetry.includeToolsContext, only top-level tool context properties marked as
true are sent when it is configured; if it is omitted, no tool context
properties are sent.

contents.heading: choosing-the-right-context
contents.content:
Use runtimeContext for state shared by the whole generation or agent loop,
such as request metadata, tenant settings, feature flags, or agent progress.

contents.heading: choosing-the-right-context
contents.content:
Use toolsContext and contextSchema for values needed by a specific tool,
such as API keys, scoped clients, user permissions, or default tool settings.

contents.heading: choosing-the-right-context
contents.content:
Use prompt messages for information the model should reason about or mention
in its answer.

contents.heading: choosing-the-right-context
contents.content:
Use telemetry.includeRuntimeContext and telemetry.includeToolsContext to
reduce telemetry exposure, not as a general security boundary.

metadata.description: Learn how to configure the AI SDK.

Example: Per-chunk timeout for streaming (streamText only)
Example: First-content timeout for streaming (streamText only)

contents.content: Large language models (LLMs) typically provide settings to augment their output.
All AI SDK functions support the following common settings in addition to the model, the prompt, and additional provider-specific settings:

Some providers do not support all common settings. If you use a setting with a
provider that does not support it, a warning will be generated. You can check
the warnings property in the result object to see if any warnings were
generated.

contents.heading: language-model-call-options
contents.content: Language model call options (LanguageModelCallOptions) are settings that influence how the language model generates its response — token limits, sampling behavior, penalties, stop sequences, seed, and reasoning. They are forwarded to the underlying model.

contents.heading: maxoutputtokens
contents.content: Maximum number of tokens to generate.

contents.heading: temperature
contents.content: Temperature setting.

contents.heading: temperature
contents.content:
The value is passed through to the provider. The range depends on the provider and model.
For most providers, 0 means almost deterministic results, and higher values mean more randomness.

contents.heading: temperature
contents.content: It is recommended to set either temperature or topP, but not both.

contents.heading: topp
contents.content: Nucleus sampling.

contents.heading: topp
contents.content:
The value is passed through to the provider. The range depends on the provider and model.
For most providers, nucleus sampling is a number between 0 and 1.
E.g. 0.1 would mean that only tokens with the top 10% probability mass are considered.

contents.heading: topp
contents.content: It is recommended to set either temperature or topP, but not both.

contents.heading: topk
contents.content: Only sample from the top K options for each subsequent token.

contents.heading: topk
contents.content:
Used to remove "long tail" low probability responses.
Recommended for advanced use cases only. You usually only need to use temperature.

contents.heading: presencepenalty
contents.content: The presence penalty affects the likelihood of the model to repeat information that is already in the prompt.

contents.heading: presencepenalty
contents.content:
The value is passed through to the provider. The range depends on the provider and model.
For most providers, 0 means no penalty.

contents.heading: frequencypenalty
contents.content: The frequency penalty affects the likelihood of the model to repeatedly use the same words or phrases.

contents.heading: frequencypenalty
contents.content:
The value is passed through to the provider. The range depends on the provider and model.
For most providers, 0 means no penalty.

contents.heading: stopsequences
contents.content: The stop sequences to use for stopping the text generation.

contents.heading: stopsequences
contents.content:
If set, the model will stop generating text when one of the stop sequences is generated.
Providers may have limits on the number of stop sequences.

contents.heading: seed
contents.content:
It is the seed (integer) to use for random sampling.
If set and supported by the model, calls will generate deterministic results.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Controls how much reasoning the model performs before generating a response.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Value

contents.heading: reasoning

contents.heading: reasoning

contents.heading: reasoning

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Provider-specific settings take precedence over the corresponding fields derived from reasoning. Partial configurations can still use portable reasoning to fill missing fields; summary and display options can be used alongside it. For example, Bedrock preserves an explicit thinking budget while deriving a missing enabled type from portable reasoning.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: See the reasoning guide for details on per-provider mapping and migration from providerOptions.

contents.heading: request-options
contents.content: Request options (RequestOptions) are settings that affect transport, retries, cancellation, and timeouts — not model generation behavior. They control how the SDK communicates with the provider's API.

contents.heading: maxretries
contents.content: Maximum number of retries. Set to 0 to disable retries. Default: 2.

contents.heading: abortsignal
contents.content: An optional abort signal that can be used to cancel the call.

contents.heading: abortsignal
contents.content:
The abort signal can e.g. be forwarded from a user interface to cancel the call,
or to define a timeout using AbortSignal.timeout.

contents.heading: timeout
contents.content: An optional timeout in milliseconds. The call will be aborted if it takes longer than the specified duration.

contents.heading: timeout
contents.content: This is a convenience parameter that creates an abort signal internally. It can be used alongside abortSignal - if both are provided, the call will abort when either condition is met.

contents.heading: timeout
contents.content: You can specify the timeout either as a number (milliseconds) or as an object with the following properties:

contents.heading: timeout
contents.content: totalMs: The total timeout for the entire call including all steps.

contents.heading: timeout
contents.content: stepMs: The timeout for each individual step (LLM call). This is useful for multi-step generations where you want to limit the time spent on each step independently.

contents.heading: timeout
contents.content: firstChunkMs: The timeout until the first content-bearing output of each step (streaming only). Text deltas, reasoning deltas, tool-input deltas, generated files, and tool calls satisfy the timeout. Response metadata, stream starts, empty deltas, raw chunks, and transport activity do not satisfy or reset it.

contents.heading: timeout
contents.content: chunkMs: The timeout between content-bearing output chunks after output has started (streaming only). Non-content chunks do not reset it. This is useful for detecting streams that stall after generation begins.

contents.heading: timeout
contents.content: toolMs: The default timeout for all tool executions. If a tool takes longer, it aborts and returns a tool-error so the model can respond or retry.

contents.heading: timeout
contents.content: tools: Per-tool timeout overrides using {toolName}Ms keys (e.g. weatherMs, slowApiMs). Takes precedence over toolMs. Tool names are type-checked for autocomplete.

contents.heading: headers
contents.content: Additional HTTP headers to be sent with the request. Only applicable for HTTP-based providers.

contents.heading: headers
contents.content:
You can use the request headers to provide additional information to the provider,
depending on what the provider supports. For example, some observability providers support
headers such as Prompt-Id.

contents.heading: headers
contents.content:
The headers setting is for request-specific headers. You can also set
headers in the provider configuration. These headers will be sent with every
request made by the provider.

metadata.title: Skill Uploads
metadata.description: Learn how to upload skills and use provider references with the AI SDK.

contents.content:
The AI SDK provides the uploadSkill
function to upload custom skills to a provider and get back a ProviderReference that
can be passed to subsequent inference calls.

A skill is a bundle of files (e.g. a SKILL.md describing the skill's behavior)
that providers can load, e.g. in sandboxed container environments.

In the AI SDK, the uploaded skill is identified by a ProviderReference — a
Record<string, string> mapping provider names to provider-specific identifiers.
This concept is used for other provider specific asset references too, such as
uploaded media files.
As a shorthand, you can pass a provider instance directly to api instead of calling .skills() explicitly — the SDK will call .skills() for you:

contents.heading: skill-files
contents.content:
A skill is composed of one or more files, each with a relative path and content.

metadata.title: Speech
metadata.description: Learn how to generate speech from text with the AI SDK.

contents.content:
The AI SDK provides the generateSpeech
function to generate speech from text using a speech model.

contents.heading: telemetry
contents.content:
generateSpeech accepts the standard telemetry option. Registered
integrations receive start, end, and error events with the provider and model,
source text, generated audio byte length, media type and format, warnings,
response metadata, provider metadata, and usage when the provider reports it.
Raw generated audio is not included in telemetry events.

contents.heading: telemetry

Use recordInputs: false or recordOutputs: false when the text or output
metadata should not be recorded by telemetry integrations.

contents.heading: telemetry

contents.heading: provider-specific-settings

contents.heading: abort-signals-and-timeouts
contents.content:
generateSpeech accepts an optional abortSignal parameter of
type AbortSignal
that you can use to abort the speech generation process or set a timeout.

contents.heading: custom-headers
contents.content:
generateSpeech accepts an optional headers parameter of type Record<string, string>
that you can use to add custom headers to the speech generation request.

contents.heading: warnings

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: When generateSpeech cannot generate a valid audio, it throws a AI_NoSpeechGeneratedError.

metadata.title: Telemetry
metadata.description: Using OpenTelemetry with AI SDK Core

title.children: Supplemental AI SDK attributes on OpenTelemetry spans

contents.content:
The AI SDK uses OpenTelemetry to collect telemetry data.
OpenTelemetry is an open-source observability framework designed to provide
standardized instrumentation for collecting telemetry data.

Check out the AI SDK Observability Integrations
to see providers that offer monitoring and tracing for AI SDK applications.

contents.heading: step-1-register-the-opentelemetry-integration
contents.content: OpenTelemetry span collection requires the @ai-sdk/otel package. Install it and register the integration once at application startup:

contents.heading: nextjs
contents.content: For Next.js applications, create an instrumentation.ts file in your project root and register the AI SDK telemetry integration alongside your OpenTelemetry provider setup:

contents.heading: nextjs
contents.content: See the Next.js OpenTelemetry guide for more details on setting up OpenTelemetry in Next.js.

contents.heading: nextjs
contents.content: For Node.js applications (without Next.js), register the integration at the top level of your entry file.

contents.heading: step-2-enabling-telemetry
contents.content:
Once a telemetry integration is registered, supported AI SDK calls emit
telemetry events by default. This includes text and object generation,
embeddings, reranking, speech generation, and both non-streaming and streaming
transcription.
You can still pass telemetry to attach metadata (like functionId) or to opt out of a specific call:

contents.heading: step-2-enabling-telemetry
contents.content: By default, both inputs and outputs are recorded. You can disable them by setting the recordInputs and recordOutputs options to false.

contents.heading: step-2-enabling-telemetry
contents.content:
Disabling the recording of inputs and outputs can be useful for privacy, data transfer, and performance reasons.
You might for example want to disable recording inputs if they contain sensitive information.

contents.heading: step-2-enabling-telemetry
contents.content:
For generateSpeech, input telemetry contains the source text and output
telemetry contains the generated audio byte length, media type, and format.
For transcribe and experimental_streamTranscribe, telemetry contains the
input audio byte length and media type plus the output transcript. Raw audio is
never included in telemetry events. Streaming transcription reports its final
byte length when the audio stream has been consumed and the transcription
finishes.

contents.heading: step-2-enabling-telemetry
contents.content:
Custom integrations receive stable generateSpeech and transcribe
operations through onStart and onEnd. To keep the experimental API isolated,
experimental_streamTranscribe uses
experimental_onStreamTranscriptionStart and
experimental_onStreamTranscriptionEnd; all three operations report failures
through onError.

contents.heading: step-2-enabling-telemetry
contents.content:
An integration that wraps or delegates to another integration must explicitly
forward the experimental streaming transcription callbacks. Forwarding only
the stable onStart and onEnd callbacks does not observe
experimental_streamTranscribe.

contents.heading: step-2-enabling-telemetry
contents.content:
The built-in OpenTelemetry integrations record numeric provider usage by
default, preserving each reported unit. The modern integration uses attributes
such as gen_ai.usage.characters, gen_ai.usage.seconds, and
gen_ai.usage.input_tokens; LegacyOpenTelemetry uses the corresponding
ai.usage.* attributes. The provider-native usage object remains available to
callbacks, and can also be included as the supplemental ai.response.usage
attribute by enabling usage: true.

contents.heading: opting-out
contents.content: Telemetry is opt-out. To disable telemetry for a specific call, set isEnabled: false:

contents.heading: opting-out
contents.content: Not registering integrations with registerTelemetry() prevents delivery to globally registered integrations, but does not disable per-call integrations or Node.js tracing-channel subscribers. To disable telemetry events for a call, including tracing-channel events, pass telemetry: { isEnabled: false }. Apply this setting to every call if you want to opt out throughout your application.

contents.heading: telemetry-metadata
contents.content:
You can provide a functionId to identify the function that the telemetry data is for,
and runtimeContext to include additional information in the telemetry data.
For the broader context model, see
Runtime and Tool Context.

contents.heading: runtime-context-telemetry-inclusion
contents.content: runtimeContext can contain values that are useful inside your application but should not be sent to telemetry providers, such as user identifiers, tenant IDs, or credentials. Use telemetry.includeRuntimeContext to mark the top-level runtimeContext properties that should be included in telemetry:

contents.heading: runtime-context-telemetry-inclusion
contents.content: In this example, telemetry integrations receive runtimeContext as { requestId: 'req_abc' }. Properties set to false or omitted are excluded. If telemetry.includeRuntimeContext is omitted, no runtime context properties are included. telemetry.includeRuntimeContext is supported by generateText, streamText, ToolLoopAgent, embed, embedMany, rerank, and experimental_decide.

contents.heading: runtime-context-telemetry-inclusion
contents.content:
telemetry.includeRuntimeContext only filters telemetry integrations,
including OpenTelemetry integrations. Lifecycle callbacks and returned results
still receive the full runtimeContext.

contents.heading: tool-context
contents.content:
Tool-specific context can also contain values that are useful during execution but should not be sent to telemetry providers, such as API keys or access tokens.
Use telemetry.includeToolsContext to include selected top-level properties from a tool's context in telemetry:

contents.heading: tool-context
contents.content:
In this example, telemetry integrations receive toolsContext.weather and tool execution telemetry event toolContext as { defaultUnit: 'fahrenheit' }.
Properties set to false or omitted are excluded. If telemetry.includeToolsContext is omitted, no tool context properties are included. telemetry.includeToolsContext is supported by generateText, streamText, and ToolLoopAgent.

contents.heading: tool-context
contents.content:
telemetry.includeToolsContext only filters telemetry integrations, including
OpenTelemetry integrations. Tool execution, lifecycle callbacks, and returned
results still receive the full tool context. See Runtime and Tool
Context for the difference
between tool execution context and telemetry event context.

contents.heading: custom-tracer
contents.content: If you want your traces to use a TracerProvider other than the one provided by the @opentelemetry/api singleton, pass a custom Tracer to the OpenTelemetry constructor:

contents.heading: telemetry-integrations
contents.content: Telemetry integrations let you hook into the generation lifecycle to build custom observability — logging, analytics, DevTools, or any other monitoring system. Instead of wiring up individual callbacks on every call, you implement a Telemetry once and register it globally or pass it via telemetry.integrations.

contents.heading: telemetry-integrations
contents.content: The OpenTelemetry and LegacyOpenTelemetry from @ai-sdk/otel are the built-in integrations for collecting OpenTelemetry spans (see Enabling telemetry above).

contents.heading: registering-integrations-globally
contents.content: Use registerTelemetry to register an integration once for all AI SDK calls:

contents.heading: registering-integrations-globally
contents.content: You can also register multiple integrations in a single call by passing them as additional arguments. They all receive the same lifecycle events:

contents.heading: per-call-integrations
contents.content: You can also pass one or more integrations to individual generateText or streamText calls. When per-call integrations are provided, they replace the globally registered integrations for that call:

contents.heading: per-call-integrations
contents.content: You can combine multiple integrations — they all receive the same lifecycle events:

contents.heading: per-call-integrations
contents.content: Errors inside integrations are caught and do not break the generation flow.

contents.heading: tracing-channel
contents.content:
In Node.js, AI SDK telemetry lifecycle and execution events are also traced on
the ai:telemetry tracing channel.
This lets observability providers subscribe to AI SDK telemetry events without
requiring users to register a separate telemetry integration, and bind async
context across provider calls and tool executions.

contents.heading: tracing-channel
contents.content:
Tracing-channel events follow the same per-call telemetry settings as other
telemetry integrations. Setting telemetry: { isEnabled: false } disables both
registered integrations and tracing-channel events for that call.

contents.heading: building-a-custom-integration
contents.content: Implement the Telemetry interface from the ai package. All methods are optional — implement only the lifecycle events you care about:

contents.heading: available-lifecycle-methods
contents.content:
Experimental decision events use the four experimental_* callbacks above.
They are not included in the stable onStart and onEnd event unions.

contents.heading: available-lifecycle-methods
contents.content: The event types for each method are the same as the corresponding lifecycle callbacks. See the lifecycle callbacks documentation for the full property reference of each event.

contents.heading: collected-data
contents.content:
The @ai-sdk/otel package provides two integrations that emit different span formats.
The OpenTelemetry follows the OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions and is the recommended integration.
The LegacyOpenTelemetry integration emits legacy AI SDK-specific spans.

contents.heading: genai-semantic-conventions
contents.content:
The OpenTelemetry emits spans that follow the OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions for GenAI.
By default, attributes use the gen_ai.* prefix. Provider names are mapped to well-known values (e.g. openai, anthropic, gcp.vertex_ai).

contents.heading: generatespeech--transcribe--experimental_streamtranscribe
contents.content: gen_ai.request.stream: true for streaming transcription and false otherwise.

contents.heading: generatespeech--transcribe--experimental_streamtranscribe
contents.content: gen_ai.input.messages: speech generation input text as a user message with a text part, when recordInputs is enabled.

contents.heading: generatespeech--transcribe--experimental_streamtranscribe
contents.content: gen_ai.output.messages: the completed transcript as an assistant message with a text part, when recordOutputs is enabled. Streaming transcription records this once on completion.

contents.heading: generatespeech--transcribe--experimental_streamtranscribe
contents.content:
The existing ai.request.text and ai.response.text attributes are also retained.
Audio byte length, media type, and output format remain in the
ai.request.audio.* and ai.response.audio.* attributes, subject to the
corresponding input/output recording controls. Raw audio is not captured, so
transcription input and speech output do not populate message attributes with
audio content or placeholder audio parts.

contents.heading: experimental_decide
contents.content:
For experimental_decide, the integration records two spans with CLIENT
kind: a decide {modelId} root span for the whole operation and one
decide {modelId} child span for decision model work, including
retries. Both include the provider and requested model with
gen_ai.operation.name: "decide". Token
usage is recorded on the child span. When decision attributes are enabled,
answers are recorded on both spans so the operation span contains its output.

contents.heading: experimental_decide
contents.content:
decide is an AI SDK-defined custom operation name, not a well-known
OpenTelemetry GenAI operation. OpenTelemetry permits custom operation names
when no well-known value describes the operation.

contents.heading: experimental_decide
contents.content:
OpenTelemetry's gen_ai.evaluation.result event describes the result of
evaluating a GenAI output for quality or other characteristics. In contrast,
experimental_decide can use arbitrary JSON state for classification,
routing, scoring, and similar tasks. The integration therefore does not emit a
gen_ai.evaluation.result event.

contents.heading: experimental_decide
contents.content:
Decision state, questions, and answers also do not have applicable GenAI
semantic-convention attributes. Enable the experimental_decision
supplemental option to record them under AI SDK-specific
ai.decision.* attributes.

contents.heading: genai-message-format
contents.content:
The gen_ai.input.messages and gen_ai.output.messages attributes follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions message format.
Messages are JSON arrays of objects with a role and a parts array. Each part has a type and type-specific fields:

contents.heading: genai-message-format
contents.content: text: { type: "text", content: "..." }

contents.heading: genai-message-format
contents.content: reasoning: { type: "reasoning", content: "..." }

contents.heading: genai-message-format
contents.content: tool_call: { type: "tool_call", id: "...", name: "...", arguments: ... }

contents.heading: genai-message-format
contents.content: tool_call_response: { type: "tool_call_response", id: "...", response: ... }

contents.heading: genai-message-format
contents.content: blob: { type: "blob", modality: "image"|"video"|"audio", mime_type: "...", content: "..." } (base64-encoded)

contents.heading: genai-message-format
contents.content: uri: { type: "uri", modality: "image"|"video"|"audio", mime_type: "...", uri: "..." } (for URL-based files)

contents.heading: genai-message-format
contents.content: Output messages also include a finish_reason field (e.g. "stop", "tool_call", "length", "content_filter").

contents.heading: genai-message-format
contents.content: Instructions supplied through instructions (or the deprecated system option) are recorded separately in gen_ai.system_instructions as a JSON array of { type: "text", content: "..." } parts. System messages supplied as chat history with allowSystemInMessages remain in gen_ai.input.messages in their original positions.

contents.heading: genai-tool-call-spans
contents.content: Tool call spans (execute_tool {toolName}) are nested under the step span and contain:

contents.heading: genai-tool-call-spans
contents.content: gen_ai.operation.name: "execute_tool"

contents.heading: genai-tool-call-spans
contents.content: gen_ai.tool.name: the name of the tool

contents.heading: genai-tool-call-spans
contents.content: gen_ai.tool.call.id: the tool call ID

contents.heading: genai-tool-call-spans
contents.content: gen_ai.tool.type: "function"

contents.heading: genai-tool-call-spans
contents.content: gen_ai.tool.call.arguments: the input arguments (stringified JSON, when recordInputs is enabled)

contents.heading: genai-tool-call-spans
contents.content: gen_ai.execute_tool.duration: the tool execution duration, in seconds

contents.heading: genai-tool-call-spans
contents.content: gen_ai.tool.call.result: the output result (stringified JSON, when recordOutputs is enabled). Only set when the tool call succeeds.

contents.heading: custom-opentelemetry-span-attributes
contents.content:
Use enrichSpan to add custom attributes to spans created by the
OpenTelemetry integration. This is useful when an observability backend needs
vendor-specific attributes that are not AI SDK-owned semantics.

contents.heading: custom-opentelemetry-span-attributes
contents.content: The callback runs when each span is created and receives:

contents.heading: custom-opentelemetry-span-attributes
contents.content: spanType: the type of span being created (operation, step, languageModel, tool, embedding, reranking, or experimental_decision).

contents.heading: custom-opentelemetry-span-attributes
contents.content: operationId: the AI SDK operation ID for the current call, such as ai.generateText or ai.streamText.

contents.heading: custom-opentelemetry-span-attributes
contents.content: callId: the unique ID for the current AI SDK call.

contents.heading: custom-opentelemetry-span-attributes
contents.content: runtimeContext: the telemetry-filtered runtime context for text generation, embedding, reranking, and decision spans. Text generation spans also reflect updates from prepareStep.

contents.heading: custom-opentelemetry-span-attributes
contents.content:
Custom attributes are merged with AI SDK attributes on the span. AI SDK-owned
attributes take precedence when a custom attribute uses the same key.

contents.heading: custom-opentelemetry-span-attributes
contents.content:
telemetry.includeRuntimeContext is applied before telemetry integrations receive
runtimeContext, so custom span enrichment only receives top-level runtime context
properties explicitly set to true. If the option is omitted, no runtime context
properties are included.

contents.heading: custom-opentelemetry-span-attributes
contents.content:
Embedding and reranking operations can share the same runtime context with text
generation to attribute their spans to the same application request:

contents.heading: custom-opentelemetry-span-attributes
contents.content:
A globally registered OpenTelemetry({ enrichSpan }) integration receives
{ requestId: 'req_abc' } for the operation span and its embedding model span.
The same applies to every chunk in embedMany and to the operation and model
spans in rerank. The onStart and onEnd callbacks receive the full context.

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: The GenAI semantic conventions cover the core model, prompt, response, tool call, and usage data. You can opt into additional AI SDK-specific attributes for data that is not represented by GenAI semantics:

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: This does not create additional AI SDK-specific spans such as ai.generateText, ai.generateText.doGenerate, or ai.toolCall. Instead, it adds only the selected supplemental attributes to the spans emitted by OpenTelemetry, such as invoke_agent {modelId}, step {n}, chat {modelId}, and execute_tool {toolName}.

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: All supplemental attributes are disabled by default. Enable only the data you want to collect:

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: The available options are:

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: usage: detailed usage attributes that are not covered by GenAI usage attributes, such as uncached input tokens and output text/reasoning token details.

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: providerMetadata: ai.response.providerMetadata on operation, step, and model-call spans.

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: embedding: embedding inputs and outputs.

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: reranking: rerank input documents and ranking output.

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: experimental_decision: experimental decision state, questions, and answers.

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: runtimeContext: ai.settings.context.*.

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: headers: ai.request.headers.*.

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: toolChoice: ai.prompt.toolChoice.

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: schema: object generation schema and output mode attributes.

contents.heading: supplemental-ai-sdk-attributes-on-opentelemetry-spans
contents.content: The recordInputs and recordOutputs telemetry options are still respected for supplemental input and output attributes.

contents.heading: legacy-ai-sdk-spans-legacyopentelemetry
contents.content:
The LegacyOpenTelemetry integration emits spans using AI SDK-specific ai.* prefixed attributes.
This is the legacy format. Consider migrating to the OpenTelemetry for better compatibility with observability platforms.

metadata.title: Testing
metadata.description: Learn how to use AI SDK Core mock providers for testing.

contents.content:
Testing language models can be challenging, because they are non-deterministic
and calling them is slow and expensive.

To enable you to unit test your code that uses the AI SDK, the AI SDK Core
includes mock providers and test helpers. You can import the following helpers from ai/test:
MockEmbeddingModelV4: A mock embedding model using the embedding model v4 specification.
MockLanguageModelV4: A mock language model using the language model v4 specification.
mockId: Provides an incrementing integer ID.
mockValues: Iterates over an array of values with each call. Returns the last value when the array is exhausted.
You can also import simulateReadableStream from ai to simulate a readable stream with delays.

With mock providers and test helpers, you can control the output of the AI SDK
and test your code in a repeatable and deterministic way without actually calling
a language model provider.

contents.heading: examples
contents.content: You can use the test helpers with the AI Core functions in your unit tests:

contents.heading: toolloopagent
contents.content:
You can provide a sequence of mock responses to test an agent that calls a tool
and continues to a final response:

contents.heading: simulate-ui-message-stream-responses
contents.content:
You can also simulate UI Message Stream responses for testing,
debugging, or demonstration purposes.

contents.heading: simulate-ui-message-stream-responses
contents.content: Here is a Next example:

metadata.title: Tool Search
metadata.description: Let models discover tools on demand, with direct calling or cache-preserving code mode.

contents.content:
toolSearch() lets a model find the tools it needs without loading every tool's
definition into its initial context. Register tools with deferLoading: true;
search matches their names and descriptions and makes them available on the
next model step.

Use it with generateText, streamText, ToolLoopAgent, or WorkflowAgent from
@ai-sdk/workflow. The model supplies a search query; the factory optionally
accepts an application-defined search callback and a maxResults limit.
WorkflowAgent supports direct tool calling; the other APIs also support
cache-preserving code mode.

contents.heading: direct-tool-calling
contents.content:
The model initially sees only search. After searching, matching definitions are
added to the provider's tool list and the model calls those tools directly. This
changes the tool definitions and can invalidate the cached prompt prefix.

contents.heading: code-mode
contents.content:
With code mode, the model searches and calls tools
through generated code. Set toolDiscovery: 'conversation' to announce discovered
definitions in user messages while keeping the provider-visible code tool
unchanged. This preserves the tool-definition cache as tools are discovered.
Actual prompt-cache reuse depends on the provider.

contents.heading: code-mode
contents.content: Using the weather tool defined above:

contents.heading: code-mode
contents.content:
The model first runs tools.search({ query: 'weather forecast' }). On the next
step, it receives the updated capability catalog and can call
tools.weather({ city: 'Bangalore' }).

contents.heading: code-mode
contents.content:
In both modes, search loads up to five matches by default, respects activeTools
and caller routing, and keeps discovered tools available for the rest of the
generation.
MCP client tools work too: add deferLoading: true to the tools returned by
client.tools().

contents.heading: code-mode
contents.content: Set maxResults to change the number of matching tools loaded per search:

contents.heading: code-mode
contents.content:
maxResults must be a positive safe integer. A larger limit can load related
tools in one search, but also adds more tool definitions to the model context.
It does not change keyword matching or ranking.

contents.heading: custom-search
contents.content:
Provide a search callback when your application needs different matching or
ranking. It receives the query and all eligible deferred tool names and resolved
descriptions, and returns ranked names. It can be synchronous or asynchronous.

contents.heading: custom-search
contents.content:
The SDK filters unknown names and duplicates before keeping the first maxResults
valid results (five by default). Tools excluded by activeTools or caller routing
remain unavailable.
Discovery still takes effect on the next model step. Without a callback, search
keeps its default keyword matching and ranking.

contents.heading: custom-search
contents.content:
See the toolSearch() reference for
input, output, and matching details.

metadata.title: Tool Calling
metadata.description: Learn about tool calling and multi-step calls (using stopWhen) with AI SDK Core.
