contents.heading: maximum-output-tokens
contents.content: The maxTokens parameter has been renamed to maxOutputTokens for clarity.

contents.heading: converttocoremessages--converttomodelmessages
contents.content:
For more information about model messages, see the Model Message
reference.

contents.heading: content--parts-array
contents.content: For UIMessages (previously called Message), the .content property has been replaced with a parts array structure.

contents.heading: data-role-removed
contents.content: The data role has been removed from UI messages.

contents.heading: uimessage-reasoning-structure
contents.content: The reasoning property on UI messages has been moved to parts.

contents.heading: reasoning-part-property-rename
contents.content: The reasoning property on reasoning UI parts has been renamed to text.

contents.heading: file-part-changes
contents.content: File parts now use .url instead of .data and .mimeType.

contents.heading: stream-data-removal
contents.content: The StreamData class has been completely removed and replaced with UI message streams for custom data.

contents.heading: custom-data-streaming-writemessageannotationwritedata-removed
contents.content: The writeMessageAnnotation and writeData methods from DataStreamWriter have been removed. Instead, use custom data parts with the new UIMessage stream architecture.

contents.heading: custom-data-streaming-writemessageannotationwritedata-removed
contents.content:
For more detailed information about streaming custom data in v5, see the
Streaming Data guide.

contents.heading: provider-metadata--provider-options
contents.content: The providerMetadata input parameter has been renamed to providerOptions. Note that the returned metadata in results is still called providerMetadata.

contents.heading: tool-definition-changes-parameters--inputschema
contents.content: Tool definitions have been updated to use inputSchema instead of parameters and error classes have been renamed.

contents.heading: tool-result-content-experimental_totoolresultcontent--tomodeloutput
contents.content: The experimental_toToolResultContent option has been renamed to toModelOutput and is no longer experimental.

contents.heading: tool-property-changes-argsresult--inputoutput
contents.content: Tool call and result properties have been renamed for better consistency with schemas.

contents.heading: tool-execution-error-handling
contents.content: The ToolExecutionError class has been removed. Tool execution errors now appear as tool-error content parts in the result steps, enabling automated LLM roundtrips in multi-step scenarios.

contents.heading: tool-execution-error-handling
contents.content: For streaming scenarios, tool execution errors appear as tool-error parts in the stream, while other errors appear as error parts.

contents.heading: tool-call-streaming-now-default-toolcallstreaming-removed
contents.content: The toolCallStreaming option has been removed in AI SDK 5.0. Tool call streaming is now always enabled by default.

contents.heading: tool-part-type-changes-uimessage
contents.content: In v5, UI tool parts use typed naming: tool-${toolName} instead of generic types.

contents.heading: dynamic-tools-support
contents.content: AI SDK 5.0 introduces dynamic tools for handling tools with unknown types at development time, such as MCP tools without schemas or user-defined functions at runtime.

contents.heading: new-dynamictool-helper
contents.content: The new dynamicTool helper function allows you to define tools where the input and output types are not known at compile time.

contents.heading: mcp-tools-without-schemas
contents.content: MCP tools that don't provide schemas are now automatically treated as dynamic tools:

contents.heading: type-safe-handling-with-mixed-tools
contents.content: When using both static and dynamic tools together, use the dynamic flag for type narrowing:

contents.heading: new-dynamic-tool-ui-part
contents.content: UI messages now include a dynamic-tool part type for rendering dynamic tool invocations:

contents.heading: breaking-change-type-narrowing-required-for-tool-calls-and-results
contents.content: When iterating over toolCalls and toolResults, you now need to check the dynamic flag first for proper type narrowing:

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: Tool UI parts now use more granular states that better represent the streaming lifecycle and error handling.

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: State Changes:

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: partial-call → input-streaming (tool input being streamed)

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: call → input-available (tool input complete, ready to execute)

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: result → output-available (tool execution successful)

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: New: output-error (tool execution failed)

contents.heading: rendering-tool-invocations-catch-all-pattern
contents.content: In v4, you typically rendered tool invocations using a catch-all tool-invocation type. In v5, the recommended approach is to handle each tool specifically using its typed part name (e.g., tool-getWeather). However, if you need a catch-all pattern for rendering all tool invocations the same way, you can use the isToolUIPart and getToolName helper functions as a fallback.

contents.heading: media-type-standardization
contents.content: mimeType has been renamed to mediaType for consistency. Both image and file types are supported in model messages.

contents.heading: reasoning-text-property-rename
contents.content: The .reasoning property has been renamed to .reasoningText for multi-step generations.

contents.heading: generate-text-reasoning-property-changes
contents.content: In generateText() and streamText() results, reasoning properties have been renamed.

contents.heading: continuation-steps-removal
contents.content: The experimental_continueSteps option has been removed from generateText().

contents.heading: image-generation-changes
contents.content: Image model settings have been moved to providerOptions.

contents.heading: step-type-removal
contents.content: The stepType property has been removed from step results.

contents.heading: step-control-maxsteps--stopwhen
contents.content: For core functions like generateText and streamText, the maxSteps parameter has been replaced with stopWhen, which provides more flexible control over multi-step execution. The stopWhen parameter defines conditions for stopping the generation when the last step contains tool results. When multiple conditions are provided as an array, the generation stops if any condition is met.

contents.heading: step-control-maxsteps--stopwhen
contents.content: Common stopping patterns:

contents.heading: step-control-maxsteps--stopwhen
contents.content: Important: The stopWhen conditions are only evaluated when the last step contains tool results.

contents.heading: usage-vs-total-usage
contents.content: Usage properties now distinguish between single step and total usage.

contents.heading: ai-sdkrsc-package-extraction
contents.content: The ai/rsc export has been extracted to a separate package @ai-sdk/rsc.

contents.heading: react-ui-hooks-moved-to-ai-sdkreact
contents.content: The deprecated ai/react export has been removed in favor of @ai-sdk/react.

contents.heading: react-ui-hooks-moved-to-ai-sdkreact
contents.content: Don't forget to install the new package: npm install @ai-sdk/react

contents.heading: usechat-changes
contents.content: The useChat hook has undergone significant changes in v5, with new transport architecture, removal of managed input state, and more.

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content: The maxSteps parameter has been removed from useChat. You should now use server-side stopWhen conditions for multi-step tool execution control, and manually submit tool results and trigger new messages for client-side tool calls.

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content:
Important: When using sendAutomaticallyWhen, don't use await with
addToolOutput inside onToolCall as it can cause deadlocks. The await is
useful when you're not using automatic submission and need to ensure the
messages are updated before manually calling sendMessage().

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content: This change provides more flexibility for handling tool calls and aligns client behavior with server-side multi-step execution patterns.

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content: For more details on the new tool submission approach, see the Tool Result Submission Changes section below.

contents.heading: initial-messages-renamed
contents.content: The initialMessages option has been renamed to messages.

contents.heading: sharing-chat-instances
contents.content: In v4, you could share chat state between components by using the same id parameter in multiple useChat hooks.

contents.heading: sharing-chat-instances
contents.content: In v5, you need to explicitly share chat instances by passing a shared Chat instance.

contents.heading: sharing-chat-instances
contents.content: For a complete example of sharing chat state across components, see the Share Chat State Across Components recipe.

contents.heading: chat-transport-architecture
contents.content: Configuration is now handled through transport objects instead of direct API options.

contents.heading: removed-managed-input-state
contents.content: The useChat hook no longer manages input state internally. You must now manage input state manually.

contents.heading: message-sending-append--sendmessage
contents.content: The append function has been replaced with sendMessage and requires structured message format.

contents.heading: message-regeneration-reload--regenerate
contents.content: The reload function has been renamed to regenerate with enhanced functionality.

contents.heading: onresponse-removal
contents.content: The onResponse callback has been removed from useChat and useCompletion.

contents.heading: send-extra-message-fields-default
contents.content: The sendExtraMessageFields option has been removed and is now the default behavior.

contents.heading: keep-last-message-on-error-removal
contents.content: The keepLastMessageOnError option has been removed as it's no longer needed.

contents.heading: chat-request-options-changes
contents.content: The data and allowEmptySubmit options have been removed from ChatRequestOptions.

contents.heading: request-options-type-rename
contents.content: RequestOptions has been renamed to CompletionRequestOptions.

contents.heading: addtoolresult-renamed-to-addtooloutput
contents.content: The addToolResult method has been renamed to addToolOutput. Additionally, the result parameter has been renamed to output for consistency with other tool-related APIs.

contents.heading: addtoolresult-renamed-to-addtooloutput
contents.content:
addToolResult is still available but deprecated. It will be removed in
version 6.

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: The automatic tool result submission behavior has been updated in useChat and the Chat component. You now have more control and flexibility over when tool results are submitted.

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: onToolCall no longer supports returning values to automatically submit tool results

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: You must explicitly call addToolOutput to provide tool results

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: Use sendAutomaticallyWhen with lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls helper for automatic submission

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: Important: Don't use await with addToolOutput inside onToolCall to avoid deadlocks

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: The maxSteps parameter has been removed from the Chat component and useChat hook

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: For multi-step tool execution, use server-side stopWhen conditions instead (see maxSteps Removal)

contents.heading: loading-state-changes
contents.content: The deprecated isLoading helper has been removed in favor of status.

contents.heading: resume-stream-support
contents.content: The resume functionality has been moved from experimental_resume to resumeStream.

contents.heading: dynamic-body-values
contents.content: In v4, the body option in useChat configuration would dynamically update with component state changes. In v5, the body value is only captured at the first render and remains static throughout the component lifecycle.

contents.heading: dynamic-body-values
contents.content: For more details on request configuration, see the Chatbot guide.

contents.heading: usage-information
contents.content: In v4, usage information was directly accessible through the onFinish callback's options parameter. In v5, usage data is attached as metadata to individual messages using the messageMetadata function in toUIMessageStreamResponse.

contents.heading: usage-information
contents.content: Then, on the client, you can access the message-level metadata.

contents.heading: usage-information
contents.content: You can also access your metadata from the onFinish callback of useChat:

contents.heading: request-body-preparation-experimental_preparerequestbody--preparesendmessagesrequest
contents.content: The experimental_prepareRequestBody option has been replaced with prepareSendMessagesRequest in the transport configuration.

contents.heading: ai-sdkvue-changes
contents.content: The Vue.js integration has been completely restructured, replacing the useChat composable with a Chat class.

contents.heading: message-structure-changes
contents.content: Messages now use a parts array instead of a content string.

contents.heading: ai-sdksvelte-changes
contents.content: The Svelte integration has also been updated with new constructor patterns and readonly properties.

contents.heading: properties-made-readonly
contents.content: Properties are now readonly and must be updated using setter methods.

contents.heading: removed-managed-input
contents.content: Like React and Vue, input management has been removed from the Svelte integration.

contents.heading: ai-sdkui-utils-package-removal
contents.content: The @ai-sdk/ui-utils package has been removed and its exports moved to the main ai package.

contents.heading: ai-sdkui-utils-package-removal
contents.content: Note: processDataStream was removed entirely in v5.0. Use readUIMessageStream instead for processing UI message streams, or use the more configurable Chat/useChat APIs for most use cases.

contents.heading: usecompletion-changes
contents.content: The data property has been removed from the useCompletion hook.

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content: The useAssistant hook has been removed.

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content:
The useAssistant hook was specific to the OpenAI Assistants API. OpenAI has
deprecated that API in favor of the Responses API. Configure useChat for your
route as shown above, then return a UI message stream from the route:

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content:
For persistent conversation state and built-in tools, see the
OpenAI Responses API guide.

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content:
If you need to connect useChat to another backend, see the
transport documentation and
stream protocol. For migrating existing
OpenAI Assistants data and API calls, see OpenAI's
Assistants migration guide.

contents.heading: attachments--file-parts
contents.content: The experimental_attachments property has been replaced with the parts array.

contents.heading: attachments--file-parts
contents.content:
Some models do not support text files (text/plain, text/markdown, text/csv,
etc.) as file parts. For text files, you can read and send the context as a text part
instead:

contents.heading: provider-options-for-embeddings
contents.content: Embedding model settings now use provider options instead of model parameters.

contents.heading: raw-response--response
contents.content: The rawResponse property has been renamed to response.

contents.heading: parallel-requests-in-embedmany
contents.content: embedMany now makes parallel requests with a configurable maxParallelCalls option.

contents.heading: langchain-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdklangchain
contents.content: The LangChainAdapter has been moved to @ai-sdk/langchain and the API has been updated to use UI message streams.

contents.heading: langchain-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdklangchain
contents.content: Don't forget to install the new package: npm install @ai-sdk/langchain

contents.heading: llamaindex-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdkllamaindex
contents.content: The LlamaIndexAdapter has been extracted to a separate package @ai-sdk/llamaindex and follows the same UI message stream pattern.

contents.heading: llamaindex-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdkllamaindex
contents.content: Don't forget to install the new package: npm install @ai-sdk/llamaindex

contents.heading: streaming-architecture
contents.content: The streaming architecture has been completely redesigned in v5 to support better content differentiation, concurrent streaming of multiple parts, and improved real-time UX.

contents.heading: stream-protocol-single-chunks--startdeltaend-pattern
contents.content: The fundamental streaming pattern has changed from single chunks to a three-phase pattern with unique IDs for each content block.

contents.heading: reasoning-streaming-pattern
contents.content: Reasoning content now follows the same start/delta/end pattern:

contents.heading: tool-input-streaming
contents.content: Tool inputs can now be streamed as they're being generated:

contents.heading: onchunk-callback-changes
contents.content: The onChunk callback now receives the new streaming chunk types with IDs and the start/delta/end pattern.

contents.heading: file-stream-parts-restructure
contents.content: File parts in streams have been flattened.

contents.heading: source-stream-parts-restructure
contents.content: Source stream parts have been flattened.

contents.heading: finish-event-changes
contents.content: Stream finish events have been renamed for consistency.

contents.heading: proprietary-protocol---server-sent-events
contents.content: The data stream protocol has been updated to use Server-Sent Events.

contents.heading: data-stream-response-helper-functions-renamed
contents.content: The streaming API has been completely restructured from data streams to UI message streams.

contents.heading: stream-transform-function-renaming
contents.content: Various stream-related functions have been renamed for consistency.

contents.heading: error-handling-geterrormessage--onerror
contents.content: The getErrorMessage option in toDataStreamResponse has been replaced with onError in toUIMessageStreamResponse, providing more control over error forwarding to the client.

contents.heading: error-handling-geterrormessage--onerror
contents.content: By default, error messages are NOT sent to the client to prevent leaking sensitive information. The onError callback allows you to explicitly control what error information is forwarded to the client.

contents.heading: id-generation-changes
contents.content: The createIdGenerator() function now requires a size argument.

contents.heading: idgenerator--idgenerator
contents.content: The type name has been updated.

contents.heading: language-model-v2-import
contents.content: LanguageModelV3 must now be imported from @ai-sdk/provider.

contents.heading: middleware-rename
contents.content: LanguageModelV1Middleware has been renamed and moved.

contents.heading: usage-token-properties
contents.content: Token usage properties have been renamed for consistency.

contents.heading: stream-part-type-changes
contents.content: The LanguageModelV3StreamPart type has been expanded to support the new streaming architecture with start/delta/end patterns and IDs.

contents.heading: raw-response--response-1
contents.content: Provider response objects have been updated.

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: The experimental_prepareStep option has been promoted and no longer requires the experimental prefix.

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: The prepareStep function receives { steps, stepNumber, model } and can return:

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: model: Different model for this step

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: activeTools: Which tools to make available

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: toolChoice: Tool selection strategy

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: system: System message for this step

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: undefined: Use default settings

contents.heading: temperature-default-removal
contents.content: Temperature is no longer set to 0 by default.

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content:
If you have persisted messages in a database, see the Data Migration
Guide for comprehensive
guidance on migrating your stored message data to the v5 format.

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content: In v4, you would typically use helper functions like appendResponseMessages or appendClientMessage to format messages in the onFinish callback of streamText:

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content: In v5, message persistence is now handled through the toUIMessageStreamResponse method, which automatically formats response messages in the UIMessage format:

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content:
Important: When using toUIMessageStreamResponse, you should always
provide both originalMessages and generateMessageId parameters. Without
these, you may experience duplicate or repeated assistant messages in your UI.
For more details, see Troubleshooting: Repeated Assistant
Messages.

contents.heading: message-id-generation
contents.content: The experimental_generateMessageId option has been moved from streamText configuration to toUIMessageStreamResponse, as it's designed for use with UIMessages rather than ModelMessages.

contents.heading: message-id-generation
contents.content: For more details on message IDs and persistence, see the Chatbot Message Persistence guide.

contents.heading: using-createuimessagestream
contents.content: For more complex scenarios, especially when working with data parts, you can use createUIMessageStream:

contents.heading: default-provider-instance-uses-responses-api
contents.content: In AI SDK 5, the default OpenAI provider instance uses the Responses API, while AI SDK 4 used the Chat Completions API. The Chat Completions API remains fully supported and you can use it with openai.chat(...).

contents.heading: default-provider-instance-uses-responses-api
contents.content:
The Responses and Chat Completions APIs have different behavior and defaults.
If you depend on the Chat Completions API, switch your model instance to
openai.chat(...) and audit your configuration.

contents.heading: strict-schemas-strictschemas-with-responses-api
contents.content: In AI SDK 4.0, you could set the strictSchemas option on Responses models (which defaulted to true). This option has been renamed to strictJsonSchema in AI SDK 5.0 and now defaults to false.

contents.heading: strict-schemas-strictschemas-with-responses-api
contents.content: If you call openai.chat(...) to use the Chat Completions API directly, you can type it with OpenAIChatLanguageModelOptions. AI SDK 5 adds the same strictJsonSchema option there as well.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: The structuredOutputs option is now configured using provider options rather than as a setting on the model instance.

contents.heading: compatibility-option-removal
contents.content: The compatibility option has been removed; strict compatibility mode is now the default.

contents.heading: legacy-function-calls-removal
contents.content: The useLegacyFunctionCalls option has been removed.

contents.heading: simulate-streaming
contents.content: The simulateStreaming model option has been replaced with middleware.

contents.heading: search-grounding-is-now-a-provider-defined-tool
contents.content: Search Grounding is now called "Google Search" and is now a provider defined tool.

contents.heading: snake-case--camel-case
contents.content: Provider options have been updated to use camelCase.

contents.heading: provider-utils-changes
contents.content: Deprecated CoreTool* types have been removed.

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: If you experience TypeScript server crashes, slow type checking, or errors like "Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite" when using Zod with AI SDK 5.0:

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: First, ensure you're using Zod 4.1.8 or later - this version includes a fix for module resolution issues that cause TypeScript performance problems.

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: If the issue persists, update your tsconfig.json to use moduleResolution: "nodenext":

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: This resolves the TypeScript performance issues while allowing you to continue using the standard Zod import. If this doesn't resolve the issue, you can try using a version-specific import path as an alternative solution. For detailed troubleshooting steps, see TypeScript performance issues with Zod.

contents.heading: async-converttomodelmessages
contents.content:
Use the add-await-converttomodelmessages codemod to automatically update
your codebase.

contents.heading: tooltomodeloutput-changes
contents.content: toModelOutput() receives a parameter object with an output property in AI SDK 6.

contents.heading: tooltomodeloutput-changes
contents.content: In AI SDK 5, the output was the arguments.

contents.heading: tooltomodeloutput-changes
contents.content:
Use the wrap-tomodeloutput-parameter codemod to automatically update your
codebase.

contents.heading: remove-name-from-function-tool-definitions
contents.content:
Function tool names come from their keys in the tools object. In AI SDK 5, a
name property could pass type checking because it was part of the
provider-defined member of the Tool type, but it did not set the name of a
function tool. The AI SDK 6 types no longer accept the property in a function
tool definition.

contents.heading: remove-name-from-function-tool-definitions
contents.content:
Remove name from tool() and use the intended name as the key in the tools
object:

contents.heading: cachedinputtokens-and-reasoningtokens-in-languagemodelusage-deprecation
contents.content: cachedInputTokens and reasoningTokens in LanguageModelUsage have been deprecated.

contents.heading: cachedinputtokens-and-reasoningtokens-in-languagemodelusage-deprecation
contents.content:
You can replace cachedInputTokens with inputTokenDetails.cacheReadTokens
and reasoningTokens with outputTokenDetails.reasoningTokens.

contents.heading: toolcalloptions-to-toolexecutionoptions-rename
contents.content:
The ToolCallOptions type has been renamed to ToolExecutionOptions
and is now deprecated.

contents.heading: toolcalloptions-to-toolexecutionoptions-rename
contents.content:
Use the rename-tool-call-options-to-tool-execution-options codemod to
automatically update your codebase.

contents.heading: per-tool-strict-mode
contents.content: Strict mode for tools is now controlled by setting strict on each tool (PR #10817). This enables fine-grained control over strict tool calls, which is important since strict mode depends on the specific tool input schema.

contents.heading: flexible-tool-content
contents.content: AI SDK 6 introduces more flexible tool output and result content support (PR #9605), enabling richer tool interactions and better support for complex tool execution patterns.

contents.heading: toolcallrepairfunction-signature
contents.content: The system parameter in the ToolCallRepairFunction type now accepts SystemModelMessage in addition to string (PR #10635). This allows for more flexible system message configuration, including provider-specific options like caching.

contents.heading: embedding-model-method-rename
contents.content: The textEmbeddingModel and textEmbedding methods on providers have been renamed to embeddingModel and embedding respectively. Additionally, generics have been removed from EmbeddingModel, embed, and embedMany (PR #10592).

contents.heading: embedding-model-method-rename
contents.content:
Use the rename-text-embedding-to-embedding codemod to automatically update
your codebase.

contents.heading: warning-logger
contents.content: AI SDK 6 introduces a warning logger that outputs deprecation warnings and best practice recommendations (PR #8343).

contents.heading: warning-logger
contents.content: To disable warning logging, set the AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS environment variable to false:

contents.heading: warning-type-unification
contents.content: Separate warning types for each generation function have been consolidated into a single Warning type exported from the ai package (PR #10631).

contents.heading: finish-reason-unknown-merged-into-other
contents.content: The unknown finish reason has been removed. It is now returned as other.

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-approval-states
contents.content:
AI SDK 6 adds approval-requested, approval-responded, and output-denied
to the tool UI part state union. Update exhaustive switch statements and
other state handling to cover the three approval states.

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-approval-states
contents.content:
See Tool execution approval
for handling approval requests and responses in a chat UI.

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-helper-functions-rename
contents.content: The tool UI part helper functions have been renamed to better reflect their purpose and to accommodate both static and dynamic tool parts (PR #XXXX).

contents.heading: istooluipart--isstatictooluipart
contents.content: The isToolUIPart function has been renamed to isStaticToolUIPart to clarify that it checks for static tool parts only.

contents.heading: istoolordynamictooluipart--istooluipart
contents.content: The isToolOrDynamicToolUIPart function has been renamed to isToolUIPart. The old name is deprecated but still available.

contents.heading: gettoolname--getstatictoolname
contents.content: The getToolName function has been renamed to getStaticToolName to clarify that it returns the tool name from static tool parts only.

contents.heading: gettoolordynamictoolname--gettoolname
contents.content: The getToolOrDynamicToolName function has been renamed to getToolName. The old name is deprecated but still available.

contents.heading: strictjsonschema-defaults-to-true
contents.content: The strictJsonSchema setting for JSON outputs and tool calls is enabled by default (PR #10752). This improves stability and ensures valid JSON output that matches your schema.

contents.heading: strictjsonschema-defaults-to-true
contents.content: However, strict mode is stricter about schema requirements. If you receive schema rejection errors, adjust your schema (for example, use null instead of undefined) or disable strict mode.

contents.heading: structuredoutputs-option-removed-from-chat-model
contents.content: The structuredOutputs provider option has been removed from chat models (PR #10752). Use strictJsonSchema instead.

contents.heading: default-provider-uses-responses-api
contents.content: The @ai-sdk/azure provider now uses the Responses API by default when calling azure() (PR #9868). To use the previous Chat Completions API behavior, use azure.chat() instead.

contents.heading: default-provider-uses-responses-api
contents.content:
The Responses and Chat Completions APIs have different behavior and defaults.
If you depend on the Chat Completions API, switch your model instance to
azure.chat() and audit your configuration.

contents.heading: responses-api-providermetadata-and-provideroptions-key
contents.content: For the Responses API, the @ai-sdk/azure provider now uses azure as the key for providerMetadata and providerOptions instead of openai. The openai key is still supported for providerOptions input, but resulting providerMetadata output now uses azure.

contents.heading: structured-outputs-mode
contents.content: Anthropic has  introduced native structured outputs for Claude Sonnet 4.5 and later models . The @ai-sdk/anthropic provider now includes a structuredOutputMode option to control how structured outputs are generated (PR #10502).

contents.heading: structured-outputs-mode
contents.content: The available modes are:

contents.heading: structured-outputs-mode
contents.content: 'outputFormat': Use Anthropic's native output_format parameter

contents.heading: structured-outputs-mode
contents.content: 'jsonTool': Use a special JSON tool to specify the structured output format

contents.heading: structured-outputs-mode
contents.content: 'auto' (default): Use 'outputFormat' when supported by the model, otherwise fall back to 'jsonTool'

contents.heading: providermetadata-and-provideroptions-key
contents.content: The @ai-sdk/google-vertex provider now uses vertex as the key for providerMetadata and providerOptions instead of google. The google key is still supported for providerOptions input, but resulting providerMetadata output now uses vertex.

contents.heading: providermetadata-and-provideroptions-key
contents.content:
Use the rename-vertex-provider-metadata-key codemod to automatically update
your codebase.

contents.heading: mock-classes
contents.content: V2 mock classes have been removed from the ai/test module. Use the new V3 mock classes instead for testing.

contents.heading: mock-classes
contents.content: Use the rename-mock-v2-to-v3 codemod to automatically update your codebase.

Tool UI Part Helper Functions Rename
structuredOutputs Option Removed from Chat Model
Responses API providerMetadata and providerOptions Key

contents.heading: minimum-nodejs-version
contents.content: AI SDK 7.0 requires Node.js 22 or later. The SDK is tested on Node.js 22, 24, and 26.

contents.heading: minimum-nodejs-version
contents.content: Node.js 18 and 20 are no longer supported. Node.js 22 reached end-of-maintenance on April 30, 2026; for production workloads, prefer Node.js 24 (LTS) or Node.js 26. See the Node.js release schedule for current status and support timelines.

contents.heading: minimum-nodejs-version
contents.content: Update the engines field in your package.json if you enforce a minimum Node.js version:

contents.heading: esm-only--commonjs-support-removed
contents.content: All AI SDK packages are now ESM-only. The require() function is no longer supported.

contents.heading: esm-only--commonjs-support-removed
contents.content: If your project uses CommonJS (require()), switch to ESM import syntax:

contents.heading: esm-only--commonjs-support-removed
contents.content: If your package.json does not already include "type": "module", add it or rename your files to use the .mjs extension.

contents.heading: provider-management-remove-deprecated-experimental_customprovider
contents.content: The deprecated experimental_customProvider export has been removed in AI SDK 7. Replace it with customProvider.

contents.heading: provider-management-remove-deprecated-experimental_customprovider
contents.content:
This is only an import and symbol rename. The customProvider options and
behavior are unchanged.

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-experimental_generateimage-export
contents.content: The deprecated experimental_generateImage export has been removed in AI SDK 7. Replace it with generateImage.

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-experimental_generateimage-export
contents.content: The deprecated Experimental_GenerateImageResult type export has also been removed. Replace it with GenerateImageResult.

contents.heading: experimental_transcribe-renamed-to-transcribe
contents.content:
The transcription API has graduated out of experimental status and has been
renamed to transcribe. The Experimental_TranscriptionResult type has also
been renamed to TranscriptionResult.

contents.heading: experimental_transcribe-renamed-to-transcribe
contents.content:
The old names continue to work as deprecated aliases in AI SDK 7 and will be
removed in a future major release.

contents.heading: experimental_generatespeech-renamed-to-generatespeech
contents.content:
The speech generation function has graduated out of experimental status and has
been renamed to generateSpeech. The Experimental_SpeechResult type has also
been renamed to SpeechResult.

contents.heading: experimental_generatespeech-renamed-to-generatespeech
contents.content:
The old experimental_generateSpeech and Experimental_SpeechResult exports
continue to work as deprecated aliases in AI SDK 7 and will be removed in a
future major release.

contents.heading: structured-outputs-remove-deprecated-experimental_output-option-and-result
contents.content: The deprecated experimental_output option has been removed in AI SDK 7. Replace all remaining usages with output.

contents.heading: structured-outputs-remove-deprecated-experimental_output-option-and-result
contents.content: The deprecated generateText() result property experimental_output has also been removed. Read result.output instead.

contents.heading: structured-outputs-remove-deprecated-experimental_output-option-and-result
contents.content: This name was deprecated in AI SDK 6, so if you already migrated to output, no changes are needed. Otherwise, update both the call options and any result access:

contents.heading: callsettings-renamed-to-languagemodelcalloptions-and-requestoptions
contents.content: CallSettings has been split into LanguageModelCallOptions (model-facing options) and RequestOptions (transport options). Replace usages in custom wrappers or helpers:

contents.heading: callsettings-renamed-to-languagemodelcalloptions-and-requestoptions
contents.content: CallSettings → LanguageModelCallOptions & Omit<RequestOptions, 'timeout'> (note: CallSettings never included timeout)

contents.heading: callsettings-renamed-to-languagemodelcalloptions-and-requestoptions
contents.content: The deprecated CallSettings type remains available in AI SDK 7.

contents.heading: stop-condition-helper-rename-stepcountis---isstepcount
contents.content: Rename imports and usage in tool-loop stop conditions:

contents.heading: system-renamed-to-instructions
contents.content:
The top-level prompt option for system instructions has been renamed from
system to instructions.

contents.heading: system-renamed-to-instructions
contents.content:
This applies to AI SDK functions that accept prompt or messages, including
generateText, streamText, generateObject, streamObject, and streamUI.

contents.heading: system-renamed-to-instructions
contents.content:
The same rename applies to prepareStep results for generateText and
streamText, and to the options passed into experimental_repairToolCall:

contents.heading: system-renamed-to-instructions
contents.content:
The system option is still accepted as a deprecated fallback. When both
instructions and system are provided, instructions takes precedence.

contents.heading: preparestep-instructions-carry-forward
contents.content:
In AI SDK 7, instructions returned from prepareStep are used in future steps
until prepareStep returns another instructions or system override. This
matches how messages returned from prepareStep carry forward.

contents.heading: preparestep-instructions-carry-forward
contents.content:
In AI SDK 6, prepareStep instruction overrides only applied to the current
step. Later steps fell back to the top-level system instructions unless they
returned their own override.

contents.heading: preparestep-instructions-carry-forward
contents.content:
If your prepareStep logic depends on one-step-only instruction overrides,
return the desired instructions for each step explicitly:

contents.heading: preparestep-instructions-carry-forward
contents.content:
The prepareStep callback receives both instructions, which is the current
instruction state for the step, and initialInstructions, which is the
top-level instruction value from the original call.

contents.heading: preparestep-instructions-carry-forward
contents.content:
If your tool call repair function forwards the current system instructions to
another model call, read and pass instructions instead of system:

contents.heading: preparestep-instructions-carry-forward
contents.content:
Lifecycle callback events for generateText, streamText, and agents also use
instructions instead of system:

contents.heading: prompt-messages-system-messages-in-prompt-or-messages-are-rejected-by-default
contents.content: AI SDK 7 rejects system messages in the prompt or messages fields by default. System instructions should usually be passed with the top-level instructions option.

contents.heading: prompt-messages-system-messages-in-prompt-or-messages-are-rejected-by-default
contents.content: This can break older persisted chats or custom prompt arrays that include { role: 'system' } messages:

contents.heading: prompt-messages-system-messages-in-prompt-or-messages-are-rejected-by-default
contents.content: Move system instructions to the instructions option when possible:

contents.heading: prompt-messages-system-messages-in-prompt-or-messages-are-rejected-by-default
contents.content: If you need to keep existing chat histories that already contain system messages, opt in to the previous behavior with allowSystemInMessages: true:

contents.heading: prompt-messages-system-messages-in-prompt-or-messages-are-rejected-by-default
contents.content:
Only use allowSystemInMessages for trusted messages. If users can submit or
edit these messages, they could inject a system message that overrides or sets
the system prompt. In most cases, system instructions should only be set by
trusted server-side code through the instructions property.

contents.heading: prompt-messages-system-messages-in-prompt-or-messages-are-rejected-by-default
contents.content: This applies to AI SDK functions that accept prompt or messages, including generateText, streamText, generateObject, streamObject, and streamUI.

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-experimental_preparestep-option
contents.content: The deprecated experimental_prepareStep option has been removed in AI SDK 7. Replace all remaining usages with prepareStep.

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-experimental_preparestep-option
contents.content: This option was deprecated in AI SDK 5, so if you already migrated to prepareStep, no changes are needed. Otherwise, update generateText calls:

contents.heading: preparestep-message-overrides-carry-forward
contents.content: When prepareStep returns messages, those messages are now used as the base for subsequent steps. The next step receives those messages plus the response messages from the previous step.

contents.heading: preparestep-message-overrides-carry-forward
contents.content: In AI SDK 6, a messages override only applied to the current step. To keep that behavior, rebuild the current step's messages from initialMessages and responseMessages inside prepareStep:

contents.heading: experimental_onstart-renamed-to-onstart
contents.content:
The generation start callback for generateText, streamText, and agents has
been renamed from experimental_onStart to onStart.

contents.heading: experimental_onstepstart-renamed-to-onstepstart
contents.content:
The per-step start callback for generateText, streamText, and agents has
been renamed from experimental_onStepStart to onStepStart.

contents.heading: onfinish-renamed-to-onend
contents.content:
The final lifecycle callback for generateText, streamText, and agents has
been renamed from onFinish to onEnd.

contents.heading: onfinish-renamed-to-onend
contents.content:
The same rename applies to streamText, Agent.generate(),
Agent.stream(), and ToolLoopAgent settings. The onFinish option is still
accepted as a deprecated alias. When both onEnd and onFinish are provided,
onEnd takes precedence.

contents.heading: onstepfinish-renamed-to-onstepend
contents.content:
The per-step lifecycle callback has been renamed from onStepFinish to
onStepEnd.

contents.heading: onstepfinish-renamed-to-onstepend
contents.content:
This applies to generateText, streamText, generateObject,
streamObject, agents, workflow agents, and UI message stream helpers.
Telemetry integrations should implement onStepEnd.

contents.heading: onstepfinish-renamed-to-onstepend
contents.content:
The onStepFinish option is still accepted as a deprecated alias for
user-facing callbacks. When both onStepEnd and onStepFinish are provided,
onStepEnd takes precedence.

contents.heading: embed-callbacks
contents.content: The per-call callback option for completed embed and embedMany operations has been renamed from experimental_onFinish to onEnd.

contents.heading: rerank-callback
contents.content: The per-call callback option for completed rerank operations has been renamed from experimental_onFinish to onEnd.

contents.heading: cachedinputtokens-and-reasoningtokens-removed-from-languagemodelusage
contents.content: The deprecated top-level cachedInputTokens and reasoningTokens fields have been removed from LanguageModelUsage.

contents.heading: cachedinputtokens-and-reasoningtokens-removed-from-languagemodelusage
contents.content: Use inputTokenDetails.cacheReadTokens and outputTokenDetails.reasoningTokens instead:

contents.heading: opentelemetry-moved-to-ai-sdkotel
contents.content: OpenTelemetry span collection is no longer built into the ai package. To continue receiving OpenTelemetry traces, you must install the new @ai-sdk/otel package and register the OpenTelemetry instance globally.

contents.heading: opentelemetry-moved-to-ai-sdkotel
contents.content: Previously, OpenTelemetry spans were emitted automatically when experimental_telemetry was enabled:

contents.heading: opentelemetry-moved-to-ai-sdkotel
contents.content: Now, you must install @ai-sdk/otel and register the OpenTelemetry instance once at application startup. For Next.js, place this in your instrumentation.ts file alongside your OpenTelemetry provider setup:

contents.heading: opentelemetry-moved-to-ai-sdkotel
contents.content: For Node.js applications (without Next.js), register the integration at the top level of your entry file.

contents.heading: opentelemetry-moved-to-ai-sdkotel
contents.content: This applies to all AI SDK functions that accept experimental_telemetry, including generateText, streamText, ToolLoopAgent, embed, embedMany, and rerank.

contents.heading: enabled-by-default-when-an-integration-is-registered
contents.content: In AI SDK 6, telemetry was opt-in — you had to set experimental_telemetry: { isEnabled: true } on every call to emit events. In AI SDK 7, telemetry is opt-out: once you register a telemetry integration (for example OpenTelemetry or DevToolsTelemetry), all AI SDK calls emit telemetry events by default.

contents.heading: enabled-by-default-when-an-integration-is-registered
contents.content: You can safely remove experimental_telemetry: { isEnabled: true } from all of your calls. If you are already passing other fields like functionId or integrations, keep them — only isEnabled: true is redundant:

contents.heading: enabled-by-default-when-an-integration-is-registered
contents.content: To opt out of telemetry for a specific call, set isEnabled: false:

contents.heading: enabled-by-default-when-an-integration-is-registered
contents.content: To disable telemetry globally, do not register any telemetry integrations.

contents.heading: enabled-by-default-when-an-integration-is-registered
contents.content: This applies to all AI SDK functions that accept experimental_telemetry, including generateText, streamText, ToolLoopAgent, embed, embedMany, and rerank.

contents.heading: tracer-property-removed-from-experimental_telemetry
contents.content: The tracer property on experimental_telemetry has been removed. If you were passing a custom OpenTelemetry Tracer, pass it to the OpenTelemetry constructor instead:

contents.heading: tracer-property-removed-from-experimental_telemetry
contents.content: This applies to all AI SDK functions that accept experimental_telemetry, including streamText, generateObject, streamObject, embed, and embedMany.

contents.heading: tracer-property-removed-from-experimental_telemetry
contents.content: If you were not passing a custom tracer (relying on the default global tracer), no changes are needed — the OpenTelemetry is registered globally by default and uses trace.getTracer('ai') when no custom tracer is provided.

contents.heading: experimental_telemetry-renamed-to-telemetry
contents.content: The telemetry option has graduated out of experimental status and has been renamed to telemetry. The old name experimental_telemetry continues to work as a deprecated alias in AI SDK 7 and will be removed in a future major release.

contents.heading: experimental_telemetry-renamed-to-telemetry
contents.content: This applies to all AI SDK functions and agents that accept telemetry configuration, including generateText, streamText, generateObject, streamObject, embed, embedMany, rerank, ToolLoopAgent, and WorkflowAgent.

contents.heading: experimental_telemetry-renamed-to-telemetry
contents.content: No behavior changes beyond the rename. You can migrate incrementally — mixed usage of telemetry and experimental_telemetry in the same codebase is supported during the deprecation window.

contents.heading: onrerankfinish-renamed-to-onrerankend
contents.content: The telemetry integration callback for individual reranking model calls has been renamed from onRerankFinish to onRerankEnd.

contents.heading: onrerankfinish-renamed-to-onrerankend
contents.content: This also applies to the type field emitted on AI_SDK_TELEMETRY_TRACING_CHANNEL: tracing-channel subscribers now receive onRerankEnd instead of onRerankFinish.

contents.heading: onrerankfinish-renamed-to-onrerankend
contents.content: Update telemetry integrations and tracing-channel subscribers to use onRerankEnd.

contents.heading: onembedfinish-renamed-to-onembedend
contents.content: The telemetry integration callback for individual embedding model calls has been renamed from onEmbedFinish to onEmbedEnd.

contents.heading: onembedfinish-renamed-to-onembedend
contents.content: This also applies to the type field emitted on AI_SDK_TELEMETRY_TRACING_CHANNEL: tracing-channel subscribers now receive onEmbedEnd instead of onEmbedFinish.

contents.heading: onembedfinish-renamed-to-onembedend
contents.content: Update telemetry integrations and tracing-channel subscribers to use onEmbedEnd.

contents.heading: streamtextresultfullstream-renamed-to-stream
contents.content:
The full event stream returned by streamText has been renamed from
fullStream to stream.

contents.heading: streamtextresultfullstream-renamed-to-stream
contents.content:
The fullStream property is still available as a deprecated alias for
stream.

contents.heading: streamtext-onchunk-receives-all-stream-parts
contents.content:
In AI SDK 7, streamText calls onChunk for every TextStreamPart emitted by
the stream. In AI SDK 6, onChunk only received a subset of stream parts such as
text deltas, reasoning deltas, sources, tool calls, tool input deltas, tool
results, custom parts, and raw chunks.

contents.heading: streamtext-onchunk-receives-all-stream-parts
contents.content: Update handlers that assume the old subset to guard the chunk types they process:

contents.heading: streamtext-onchunk-receives-all-stream-parts
contents.content:
onChunk can now also receive lifecycle, boundary, and terminal parts such as
start, start-step, text-start, text-end, reasoning-start,
reasoning-end, tool-input-end, finish-step, finish, abort, and
error.

contents.heading: move-includerawchunks-to-includerawchunks
contents.content: The top-level includeRawChunks option on streamText is deprecated in AI SDK 7. Move it into the include options object as rawChunks.

contents.heading: move-includerawchunks-to-includerawchunks
contents.content: The deprecated top-level option continues to work in AI SDK 7, so you can migrate incrementally.

contents.heading: rename-experimental_include-to-include
contents.content:
The experimental_include option for generateText, streamText, and
ToolLoopAgent is now stable and has been renamed to include.

contents.heading: rename-experimental_include-to-include
contents.content:
The deprecated experimental_include name continues to work for backwards
compatibility. If both include and experimental_include are provided,
include takes precedence.

contents.heading: request-and-response-bodies-are-excluded-by-default
contents.content:
In AI SDK 7, generateText and streamText no longer include request bodies in
step results by default. generateText also no longer includes response bodies
by default. This reduces memory usage, especially when prompts or provider
responses contain large payloads such as images or files.

contents.heading: request-and-response-bodies-are-excluded-by-default
contents.content:
If your application reads result.request.body, step.request.body,
result.response.body, or step.response.body, opt in with include.

contents.heading: request-and-response-bodies-are-excluded-by-default
contents.content: For streamText, only requestBody is available:

contents.heading: step-response-messages-are-no-longer-accumulated
contents.content:
In AI SDK 7, step.response.messages on each StepResult only contains the
response messages produced by that particular step.

contents.heading: step-response-messages-are-no-longer-accumulated
contents.content:
In AI SDK 6, step.response.messages accumulated response messages from all
previous steps. If your application reads step.response.messages from an
intermediate or final step and expects the full assistant/tool message history,
use the top-level result.responseMessages instead.

contents.heading: step-response-messages-are-no-longer-accumulated
contents.content:
If you specifically need to reconstruct response messages from step results,
flatten the per-step messages:

contents.heading: step-response-messages-are-no-longer-accumulated
contents.content:
Prefer result.responseMessages when you want the full response message history.
It also includes response messages produced before the first model step, such as
tool results from approved tool calls in the input messages.

contents.heading: tool-execution-callbacks
contents.content: The tool execution callback options for generateText and streamText have been renamed:

contents.heading: tool-execution-callbacks
contents.content: experimental_onToolCallStart is now onToolExecutionStart

contents.heading: tool-execution-callbacks
contents.content: experimental_onToolCallFinish is now onToolExecutionEnd

contents.heading: tool-execution-callbacks
contents.content: The old names continue to work as deprecated aliases in AI SDK 7 and will be removed in a future major release. They are only used as fallbacks when the new callback names are not provided.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: In AI SDK 7, the tool callback option previously exposed as experimental_context has been renamed to context and is now stable.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: The bigger behavioral change is that AI SDK now separates:

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: tool-specific context, which is passed to tool callbacks from toolsContext

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: shared generation/agent runtime data, which flows through runtimeContext

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: In AI SDK 6, tools often read from one generic runtime context object. In AI SDK 7, each tool gets its own scoped context, and you provide those values through toolsContext, keyed by tool name.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: tool() infers the type of a tool's context from its contextSchema, so each tool only sees the fields declared for that specific tool.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: In AI SDK 6, tool code often accessed experimental_context and had to cast it manually:

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: In AI SDK 7, rename experimental_context to context, declare the tool-specific context with contextSchema, and pass the per-tool values through toolsContext. The execute callback, approval callback, and tool input lifecycle hooks then receive a typed context automatically:

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: Use runtimeContext for shared generation or agent state that should be visible in prepareStep, events, and step results. Tool callbacks no longer read from that shared object. A tool's context now comes from its own entry in toolsContext, so it is limited to the fields that tool declared in contextSchema.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: Potential breaking issues:

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: If you still destructure experimental_context in tool callbacks, rename it to context.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: If you were previously passing one shared runtime object for both orchestration and tools, split it into runtimeContext and toolsContext.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: Move tool-specific values into toolsContext under the matching tool name.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: Rename shared top-level context usage to runtimeContext in generateText, streamText, and ToolLoopAgent.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: Rename prepareStep usage from context to runtimeContext.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: If a tool callback accesses fields that are not declared in its contextSchema, TypeScript will now report errors. Add those fields to that tool's schema.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: If you have helper types or wrappers that assumed experimental_context or context was unknown, update them to accept a generic CONTEXT type.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: If at least one tool declares contextSchema, toolsContext becomes required and only includes the tools that actually declare contextual data.

contents.heading: context-experimental_context-became-tool-context-and-shared-runtime-data-moved-to-runtimecontext
contents.content: If you were relying on every tool callback seeing the same full runtime object, move shared step data to runtimeContext, or explicitly provide the needed per-tool data in each tool's toolsContext entry.

contents.heading: migrate-deprecated-needsapproval-to-toolapproval
contents.content:
The needsApproval property on tool() and dynamicTool() is deprecated in
AI SDK 7 for generateText, streamText, and ToolLoopAgent.

contents.heading: migrate-deprecated-needsapproval-to-toolapproval
contents.content:
Move approval logic to the toolApproval setting on the call or agent instead.
This keeps approval policy close to the generation or agent configuration and
lets you vary it by request.

contents.heading: migrate-deprecated-needsapproval-to-toolapproval
contents.content:
If you were using needsApproval: true, migrate it to
toolApproval: { myTool: 'user-approval' }. If you were using a
needsApproval function, move that logic into a per-tool
SingleToolApprovalFunction or a generic toolApproval callback. This
guidance applies to generateText, streamText, and ToolLoopAgent.

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-experimental_activetools-option
contents.content: The deprecated experimental_activeTools option has been removed in AI SDK 7. Replace all remaining usages with activeTools.

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-experimental_activetools-option
contents.content: This option was deprecated in AI SDK 5, so if you already migrated to activeTools, no changes are needed. Otherwise, update both generateText and streamText calls:

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-toolcalloptions-type
contents.content: The deprecated ToolCallOptions type has been removed in AI SDK 7. Replace all remaining usages with ToolExecutionOptions.

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-toolcalloptions-type
contents.content: If you already migrated away from the deprecated name in AI SDK 6, no changes are needed. Otherwise, update imports and type references:

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-istoolordynamictooluipart-function
contents.content: The deprecated isToolOrDynamicToolUIPart function has been removed in AI SDK 7. Replace all remaining usages with isToolUIPart.

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-istoolordynamictooluipart-function
contents.content: If you already migrated away from the deprecated name in AI SDK 6, no changes are needed. Otherwise, update imports and calls:

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-media-content-part-type
contents.content: The deprecated tool result content part of { type: 'media' } has been removed in AI SDK 7.

contents.heading: remove-deprecated-media-content-part-type
contents.content: Use { type: 'file', mediaType, data: { type: 'data', data } } for inline tool-result file content, including images, as described below. The legacy file-data variant still works through runtime auto-migration, but is deprecated.

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: All image-* and legacy file-* content part types for toModelOutput results are deprecated in AI SDK 7 in favor of a single canonical file variant that mirrors the top-level FilePart shape. Auto-migration is applied at runtime, so existing tool outputs continue to work without code changes. However, updating to the new shape is recommended.

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: The new shape carries a tagged data discriminated union, and it always has mediaType:

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: { type: 'file-data', data, mediaType, filename? } → { type: 'file', mediaType, filename, data: { type: 'data', data } }

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: { type: 'file-url', url, mediaType } → { type: 'file', mediaType, data: { type: 'url', url: new URL(url) } }

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: { type: 'file-reference', providerReference } → { type: 'file', mediaType, data: { type: 'reference', reference: providerReference } }

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: Images are just files with an image media type, so the image-* aliases collapse into the same shape — pass mediaType: 'image' (or a more specific image/* subtype) instead:

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: { type: 'image-data', data, mediaType } → { type: 'file', mediaType, data: { type: 'data', data } }

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: { type: 'image-url', url } → { type: 'file', mediaType: 'image', data: { type: 'url', url: new URL(url) } }

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: { type: 'image-file-reference', providerReference } → { type: 'file', mediaType: 'image', data: { type: 'reference', reference: providerReference } }

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: The -id content part types (file-id and image-file-id) are also generally deprecated in favor of the reference data shape, which carries a full ProviderReference (a provider-to-file-ID map like { openai: 'file_123', anthropic: 'file_abc' }) that lets the same logical file be reused across providers. The single-ID -id variants required the runtime to know which provider the ID belonged to; the explicit reference shape removes that ambiguity:

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: { type: 'file-id', fileId } → { type: 'file', mediaType, data: { type: 'reference', reference: { [provider]: fileId } } }

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: { type: 'image-file-id', fileId } → { type: 'file', mediaType: 'image', data: { type: 'reference', reference: { [provider]: fileId } } }

contents.heading: tool-result-content-migrate-away-from-image--and-file--variants-to-file
contents.content: mediaType on the new file variant accepts either a full IANA type (e.g. 'image/png') or just a top-level segment (e.g. 'image', 'audio', 'video', 'text'). When only a top-level segment is provided, the subtype is auto-detected from inline bytes where possible. Update parsing/validation and discriminated unions to handle the single canonical file variant.

contents.heading: message-parts-migrate-away-from-deprecated-image-part
contents.content: The { type: 'image', image, mediaType? } user-message content part is deprecated. Use { type: 'file', data, mediaType } with an image mediaType instead.

contents.heading: message-parts-migrate-away-from-deprecated-image-part
contents.content: mediaType on FilePart now accepts either a full IANA type (e.g. 'image/png') or just a top-level segment (e.g. 'image'). When only a top-level segment is provided, the subtype is auto-detected from inline bytes where possible.

contents.heading: message-parts-handle-new-reasoning-file-content-type
contents.content: Some models can now return files as part of their reasoning trace, separate from regular output files. These files, which would have previously were using the file type, are now in a distinct reasoning-file type.

contents.heading: message-parts-handle-new-reasoning-file-content-type
contents.content: Update all exhaustive part handling (TypeScript unions, switch statements, runtime validators, renderers, serializers) to support type: 'reasoning-file'.

contents.heading: message-parts-handle-new-reasoning-file-content-type
contents.content: Also audit any code that reads generated files from result.files or step.files: files referenced in reasoning are now represented as reasoning-file parts in content / reasoning. In practice, this should rarely require an update because models usually reference the same file in their reasoning that they later output as regular content. Prior to supporting reasoning-file as a distinct type, this would result in the same files appearing in result.files or step.files as a duplicate.

contents.heading: reasoning-configuration-remove-overlapping-settings
contents.content: The new top-level reasoning option is the provider-agnostic way to control reasoning effort.

contents.heading: reasoning-configuration-remove-overlapping-settings
contents.content: When migrating to the top-level reasoning option, remove overlapping reasoning settings from providerOptions.

contents.heading: reasoning-configuration-remove-overlapping-settings
contents.content: If both are present, provider-specific reasoning settings in providerOptions take precedence, which can silently bypass your new top-level reasoning configuration.

contents.heading: generatetext-and-streamtext-usage-now-includes-all-steps
contents.content: The usage property on generateText and streamText results now returns the total token usage across all steps. This matches what totalUsage previously represented.

contents.heading: generatetext-and-streamtext-usage-now-includes-all-steps
contents.content: Use finalStep.usage to read the previous usage behavior, which only returned token usage from the final step:

contents.heading: generatetext-and-streamtext-usage-now-includes-all-steps
contents.content: totalUsage is deprecated. Replace result.totalUsage with result.usage.

contents.heading: generatetext-and-streamtext-result-properties-now-include-all-steps
contents.content:
The top-level content, toolCalls, staticToolCalls, dynamicToolCalls,
toolResults, staticToolResults, dynamicToolResults, files, sources,
and warnings properties on generateText and streamText results now return
values accumulated across every step.

contents.heading: generatetext-and-streamtext-result-properties-now-include-all-steps
contents.content:
In AI SDK 6, these properties only returned values from the final step. Use
finalStep to read the previous behavior:

contents.heading: generatetext-and-streamtext-result-properties-now-include-all-steps
contents.content: For streamText, await finalStep first when you need final-step-only values:

contents.heading: final-step-result-properties-moved-to-finalstep
contents.content: The top-level reasoning, reasoningText, request, response, and providerMetadata result properties on generateText and streamText are deprecated in AI SDK 7.

contents.heading: final-step-result-properties-moved-to-finalstep
contents.content: Use result.finalStep when you need final-step reasoning or final-step metadata:

contents.heading: final-step-result-properties-moved-to-finalstep
contents.content: For streamText, await finalStep first:

contents.heading: final-step-result-properties-moved-to-finalstep
contents.content: The deprecated top-level aliases continue to work in AI SDK 7 so you can migrate incrementally.

contents.heading: generatetext-and-streamtext-onend-result-properties-changed
contents.content:
The onEnd callback for generateText, streamText, and agents follows
the same result property changes as generateText and streamText results:

contents.heading: generatetext-and-streamtext-onend-result-properties-changed
contents.content:
usage now contains usage across all steps. totalUsage is deprecated; use
usage instead.

contents.heading: generatetext-and-streamtext-onend-result-properties-changed
contents.content:
content, toolCalls, toolResults, files, sources, and warnings now
contain values from all steps.

contents.heading: generatetext-and-streamtext-onend-result-properties-changed
contents.content:
Final-step-only properties are available on finalStep. The top-level
reasoning, reasoningText, request, response, and providerMetadata
properties are deprecated.

contents.heading: generatetext-and-streamtext-onend-result-properties-changed
contents.content:
The deprecated top-level aliases on the onEnd event continue to work in AI
SDK 7 so you can migrate incrementally.

contents.heading: streamtext-response-helpers-deprecated--use-stateless-helpers
contents.content: The toUIMessageStream, toUIMessageStreamResponse, pipeUIMessageStreamToResponse, toTextStreamResponse, and pipeTextStreamToResponse methods on the streamText result are now deprecated. They still work in v7 (with deprecation warnings) and will be removed in the next major release.

contents.heading: streamtext-response-helpers-deprecated--use-stateless-helpers
contents.content: The equivalent stateless helpers live on the top-level 'ai' export. Use them directly so the same transformation can be composed over any stream / textStream — not just a streamText result.

contents.heading: streamtext-response-helpers-deprecated--use-stateless-helpers
contents.content: UI message stream

contents.heading: streamtext-response-helpers-deprecated--use-stateless-helpers
contents.content: UI message stream Response

contents.heading: streamtext-response-helpers-deprecated--use-stateless-helpers
contents.content: Pipe UI message stream to Node.js response

contents.heading: streamtext-response-helpers-deprecated--use-stateless-helpers
contents.content: Text stream Response

contents.heading: streamtext-response-helpers-deprecated--use-stateless-helpers
contents.content: Pipe text stream to Node.js response

contents.heading: mcp-transport-redirect-default-changed-from-follow-to-error
contents.content: The redirect option on MCPTransportConfig (used by both HTTP and SSE transports) now defaults to 'error' instead of 'follow'. This means HTTP redirects are rejected by default to prevent server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks where an MCP server could redirect requests to unintended hosts.

contents.heading: mcp-transport-redirect-default-changed-from-follow-to-error
contents.content: If your MCP server relies on HTTP redirects, explicitly set redirect: 'follow' in your transport configuration:

contents.heading: mcp-transport-redirect-default-changed-from-follow-to-error
contents.content: If the MCP server you use does not issue redirects, no changes are needed — the new default is more secure.

contents.heading: chat-class-deprecated-in-favor-of-usechat-composable
contents.content: The Chat class exported from @ai-sdk/vue is deprecated in AI SDK 7 in favor of the new useChat composable. useChat exposes reactive refs for messages, status, and error, and automatically recreates the underlying chat when its init object changes — so reactive inputs (a route param, a selected model, etc.) flow through without manual orchestration.

contents.heading: chat-class-deprecated-in-favor-of-usechat-composable
contents.content: To make the init reactive (recreate the chat when its inputs change), pass a getter or ref:

contents.heading: chat-class-deprecated-in-favor-of-usechat-composable
contents.content: The Chat class continues to work as a deprecated export, so you can migrate incrementally.

contents.heading: responses-reasoning-summary-defaults-to-detailed
contents.content: For the OpenAI Responses provider, setting reasoning or providerOptions.openai.reasoningEffort to a value other than 'none' now defaults providerOptions.openai.reasoningSummary to 'detailed'.

contents.heading: responses-reasoning-summary-defaults-to-detailed
contents.content: If you want to keep reasoning summaries disabled, set providerOptions.openai.reasoningSummary to null.

contents.heading: providermetadataanthropiccachecreationinputtokens-removed
contents.content: The Anthropic-specific cacheCreationInputTokens field on providerMetadata.anthropic has been removed from the responses of generateText and streamText (as well as the @ai-sdk/google-vertex/anthropic sub-provider). This duplicated information that is already available on the standard, provider-agnostic usage object.

contents.heading: providermetadataanthropiccachecreationinputtokens-removed
contents.content: Use result.usage.inputTokenDetails.cacheWriteTokens to read the number of tokens written to the cache, and result.usage.inputTokenDetails.cacheReadTokens to read the number of tokens served from the cache:

contents.heading: providermetadataanthropiccachecreationinputtokens-removed
contents.content: If you need the raw Anthropic-shaped usage payload (including cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation, service_tier, etc.), it is still available unchanged at result.finalStep.providerMetadata?.anthropic?.usage.

contents.heading: renamed-types-classes-and-functions-generativeai-affix-removed
contents.content: Every type, class, and function in @ai-sdk/google that contained GoogleGenerativeAI has been renamed to use simply Google — for example, createGoogleGenerativeAI → createGoogle and GoogleGenerativeAIProvider → GoogleProvider.

contents.heading: renamed-types-classes-and-functions-generativeai-affix-removed
contents.content: The old names still work as deprecated aliases, but you should migrate to the new names, if you currently reference them.

contents.heading: renamed-types-classes-and-functions-generativeai-affix-removed
contents.content: The main entry point the google constant, remains unchanged, so if that's all you use from the provider, no changes are required.

contents.heading: default-model-now-uses-the-responses-api
contents.content: In AI SDK 7, xai(modelId) (and xai.languageModel(modelId)) uses the xAI Responses API by default instead of the Chat Completions API. Both APIs were already available in AI SDK 6 via xai.chat(modelId) and xai.responses(modelId); AI SDK 7 only changes which one xai(modelId) uses by default. To keep using the Chat Completions API, use xai.chat(modelId).

metadata.title: Versioning
metadata.description: Understand how the AI SDK approaches versioning.

contents.content: Each version number follows the format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
Major: Breaking API updates that require code changes.
Minor: Blog post that aggregates new features and improvements into a public release that highlights benefits.
Patch: New features and bug fixes.

contents.heading: experimental-apis

changes.

metadata.title: Agent (Interface)
metadata.description: API Reference for the Agent interface.

contents.content: The Agent interface defines a contract for agents that can generate or stream AI-generated responses in response to prompts. Agents may encapsulate advanced logic such as tool usage, multi-step workflows, or prompt handling, enabling both simple and autonomous AI agents.

Implementations of the Agent interface—such as ToolLoopAgent—fulfill the same contract and integrate seamlessly with all SDK APIs and utilities that expect an agent. This design allows users to supply custom agent classes or wrappers for third-party chains, while maximizing compatibility with AI SDK features.

When you want to compare the similarity of embeddings, standard vector similarity metrics
