metadata.title: createAgentUIStreamResponse
metadata.description: API Reference for the createAgentUIStreamResponse utility.

contents.content: The createAgentUIStreamResponse function executes an Agent, runs its streaming output as a UI message stream, and returns an HTTP Response object whose body is the live, streaming UI message output. This is designed for API routes that deliver real-time agent results, such as chat endpoints or streaming tool-use operations.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: A Promise<Response> whose body is a streaming UI message output from the agent. Use this as the return value of API/server handlers in serverless, Next.js, Express, Hono, or edge runtime contexts.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: Use onUIMessageStepEnd to persist the accumulated UI response after every agent step. The callback is awaited before the corresponding finish-step chunk continues. Use idempotent writes and protect model output, reasoning, tool inputs, and tool outputs as sensitive conversation data. The existing onStepEnd callback remains the low-level generation callback for usage, finish reasons, and raw step details.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: UI Message Validation: Validates the incoming uiMessages array according to the agent's specified tools and requirements.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Model Message Conversion: Converts validated UI messages into the internal model message format for the agent.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Streaming Agent Output: Invokes the agent’s .stream({ prompt, ... }) to get a stream of chunks (steps/UI messages), passing through options such as experimental_sandbox.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: HTTP Response Creation: Wraps the output stream as a readable HTTP Response object that streams UI message chunks to the client.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Your agent must implement .stream({ prompt, ... }) and define a tools property (even if it's just {}) to work with this function.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Server Only: This API should only be called in backend/server-side contexts (API routes, edge/serverless/server route handlers, etc.). Not for browser use.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pass experimental_sandbox when your agent tools need an experimental sandbox environment during execution.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Additional options (headers, status, UI stream options, transforms, etc.) are available for advanced scenarios.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: This leverages ReadableStream so your platform/client must support HTTP streaming consumption.

metadata.title: createAgentUIStream
metadata.description: API Reference for the createAgentUIStream utility.

title.children: Persisting the UI Message After Each Step

contents.content: The createAgentUIStream function executes an Agent, consumes an array of UI messages, and streams the agent's output as UI message chunks via an async iterable. This enables real-time, incremental rendering of AI assistant output with full access to tool use, intermediate reasoning, and interactive UI features in your own runtime—perfect for building chat APIs, dashboards, or bots powered by agents.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: A Promise<AsyncIterableStream<UIMessageChunk>>, where each yielded chunk is a UI message output from the agent (see UIMessage). This can be consumed with any async iterator loop, or piped to a streaming HTTP response, socket, or any other sink.

contents.heading: persisting-the-ui-message-after-each-step
contents.content: Use onUIMessageStepEnd when you need the accumulated UIMessage after each agent step:

contents.heading: persisting-the-ui-message-after-each-step
contents.content: onStepEnd and onUIMessageStepEnd serve different layers. onStepEnd receives the low-level generation step result, including usage, finish reason, and tool call details. onUIMessageStepEnd runs after that step has been converted to UI message parts and receives the response message accumulated so far.

contents.heading: persisting-the-ui-message-after-each-step
contents.content: The callback runs as the UI stream is consumed and is awaited before the finish-step chunk continues through the stream. This delays UI stream delivery; it does not guarantee that the next model call has not started. If it throws, the error is passed to onError and streaming continues. Use idempotent writes because each callback contains a growing snapshot of the same response message. UI messages can contain model output, reasoning, tool inputs, and tool outputs, so apply the same access controls and sensitive-data handling that you use for final conversation persistence.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: UI Message Validation: The input uiMessages array is validated and normalized using the agent's tools definition. Any invalid messages cause an error.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Conversion to Model Messages: The validated UI messages are converted into model-specific message format, as required by the agent.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Agent Streaming: The agent's .stream({ prompt, ... }) method is invoked with the converted model messages, optional call options, abort signal, experimental_sandbox, and any experimental transforms.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: UI Message Stream Building: The result stream is converted and exposed as a streaming async iterable of UI message chunks for you to consume.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The agent must implement the .stream({ prompt, ... }) method and define its supported tools property.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: This utility returns an async iterable for maximal streaming flexibility. For HTTP responses, see createAgentUIStreamResponse (Web) or pipeAgentUIStreamToResponse (Node.js).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The uiMessages parameter is named uiMessages, not just messages.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: You can provide advanced options via UIMessageStreamOptions (for example, to include sources or message metadata).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Use onUIMessageStepEnd for per-step UI message persistence. Use onStepEnd for low-level generation telemetry and step details.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: To cancel the stream, pass an AbortSignal via the abortSignal parameter.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pass experimental_sandbox when your agent tools need an experimental sandbox environment during execution.

metadata.title: createMCPClient
metadata.description: Create a client for connecting to MCP servers

contents.content: Creates a lightweight Model Context Protocol (MCP) client that connects to an MCP server. The client provides:
Tools: Automatic conversion between MCP tools and AI SDK tools
Resources: Methods to list, read, and discover resource templates from MCP servers
Prompts: Methods to list available prompts and retrieve prompt messages
Completions: Methods to request autocompletion suggestions for prompt arguments and resource template variables
Elicitation: Support for handling server requests for additional input during tool execution
Experimental events: Discover events and manage webhook subscriptions with client.experimental_events

It currently does not support in-band notifications from an MCP server. For
experimental webhook delivery, see the MCP Events guide,
event methods reference, and
webhook handler reference.

Import MCPClientError from @ai-sdk/mcp and use its isInstance method to

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content:
The error exposes the optional code, statusCode, url, and responseBody
properties. code is the JSON-RPC application error code. statusCode, url,
and responseBody contain HTTP transport context when it is available. They
are undefined for failures without an HTTP response, such as network errors,
timeouts, aborted requests, and stdio transport failures.

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content:
MCPClientError also represents configuration and protocol errors, so its
type or a missing statusCode alone does not indicate a retryable failure.
OAuth failures can instead throw the separately exported UnauthorizedError
or MCPClientOAuthError.

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content:
Avoid logging url or responseBody without redacting sensitive endpoint,
query parameter, or server response data.

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: For tool execution, errors are propagated as CallToolError errors.

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: For unknown errors, the client exposes an onUncaughtError callback that can be used to manually log or handle errors that are not covered by known error types.

This allows you to set up custom model configurations, alias names, and more.
The custom provider also supports a fallback provider, which is useful for

aliases for decision model instances or string IDs. The returned provider adds
decisionModel(alias): Experimental_DecisionModelV4. String aliases resolve
through Gateway by default, or an explicitly configured default provider with

contents.content: extractReasoningMiddleware is a middleware function that extracts delimited reasoning sections from generated text and exposes them separately from the main text content. This is particularly useful when you want to separate an AI model's reasoning process from its final output.

For models that emit non-XML delimiters, pass literal opening and closing

opening delimiter:

metadata.title: MCP Events
metadata.description: Reference for experimental MCP event methods, the webhook handler, and subscription and storage types.

contents.content:
This page covers the experimental methods on client.experimental_events, the webhook
handler, and their public types. Create the client with
createMCPClient. See the
MCP Events guide for the application flow.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content:
experimental_events accepts Experimental_MCPEventsConfig.
In direct mode, the store is required for subscribe, refresh, and unsubscribe.
Alternatively, configure a managed adapter as described below. Discovery works
without configuring either mode. Mount the
webhook handler before subscribing.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The methods below belong to client.experimental_events; they are not standalone imports.

contents.heading: clientexperimental_eventslist
contents.content: Sends events/list and returns one catalog page.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: The optional argument has these properties:

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: Promise<Experimental_ListEventsResult>:

contents.heading: returns
contents.content:
See Experimental_MCPEventDefinition
for the definition fields. Pagination is explicit; this method does not fetch all pages.

contents.heading: managed-subscriptions
contents.content:
Configure experimental_events: { adapter } to delegate subscription lifecycle
operations to a backend. The adapter implements Experimental_MCPEventsAdapter
from @ai-sdk/mcp; it is bound to the authorized account and destination by your
application or integration package.

contents.heading: managed-subscriptions
contents.content:
authenticatedTransport and eventsAdapter are supplied by your application.
Use the same authorized account for discovery and subscription management.
Never derive account identity, destination or authorization from model arguments.

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content:
These types are exported as Experimental_ManagedSubscription and
Experimental_ManagedSubscribeInput. Supply exactly one monitoring lifetime:
a positive ttlMs, an ISO deadline in expiresAt, or expiresAt: null to
monitor until stopped. The backend validates these values and enforces its limits.

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: Experimental_MCPEventsAdapter has four operations:

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: Operation

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: Input

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: Result

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: subscribe

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: Experimental_ManagedSubscribeInput

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: Experimental_ManagedSubscription

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: getSubscription

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: { id, options? }

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: Experimental_ManagedSubscription

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: listSubscriptions

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: Optional { cursor?, limit?, status?, options? }

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: { subscriptions, nextCursor? }

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: unsubscribe

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: { id, options? }

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content: Experimental_ManagedSubscription

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content:
All operations return promises. The client passes inputs, cancellation/timeout
options, results and errors through without retries or remapping. The adapter
must implement request-option handling and retain actionable backend errors,
such as consent required, quota exceeded or temporary unavailability.

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content:
Managed IDs identify backend records. expiresAt is the application's monitoring
deadline, not the upstream MCP refreshBefore grant. A pending result means
durable acceptance by the backend; upstream setup may still be running.
Stopping can return cleanupStatus: 'pending' while remote cleanup continues.

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content:
The backend owns callback URLs, secrets, upstream subscription calls, verification,
renewal and cleanup. Managed subscribe does not implicitly discover the catalog,
generate a secret, write a local store or call upstream events/subscribe.
getSubscription and listSubscriptions are adapter methods, not MCP wire methods.
The managed facade has no refresh(); the backend renews finite upstream leases
even when the application watch has no deadline.

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content:
Persist an application intent and reuse its idempotency key after an uncertain
create result, within the backend's documented recovery window. A timeout or
aborted request does not prove that a remote subscription was cancelled.
Closing the MCP client does not unsubscribe managed watches.

contents.heading: adapter-contract
contents.content:
Managed delivery is separate from this client. Use the backend's delivery verifier
and receiver contract; experimental_createMCPEventWebhook serves direct MCP
webhooks. Applications still own authorized routing, durable receipt acceptance
and idempotent work dispatch. The adapter does not invoke event callbacks.

contents.heading: configuration-and-types
contents.content:
Choose either experimental_events: { adapter } or experimental_events: { store }.
Mixing them is rejected in TypeScript and at runtime. validateArguments is a
direct-mode option; managed validation belongs to the backend. The unreleased
events configuration spelling is replaced by experimental_events.

contents.heading: configuration-and-types
contents.content:
createMCPClient infers Experimental_ManagedMCPClient with
Experimental_ManagedMCPEvents when an adapter is configured. Both modes use
MCPClientConfig, whose experimental_events property accepts the
Experimental_MCPEventsConfig union. Direct clients keep MCPClient and
Experimental_MCPEvents. The input and result types of each mode remain distinct.

contents.heading: configuration-and-types
contents.content:
Use satisfies MCPClientConfig when saving a configuration to retain inference of
the selected mode. A configuration whose mode is only known at runtime returns a
union of the two client types; it does not promise direct-only methods such as
refresh(). Omit experimental_events entirely for catalog discovery without a
store or adapter.

contents.heading: configuration-and-types
contents.content: The remaining subscribe, refresh and unsubscribe sections describe direct mode.

contents.heading: clientexperimental_eventssubscribeoptions
contents.content:
Discovers the named event, checks webhook support, saves a pending subscription,
and sends events/subscribe.

contents.heading: parameters-1
contents.content: options has type Experimental_SubscribeEventOptions:

contents.heading: parameters-1
contents.content:
Pending records are retained when subscription creation fails, because a timed-out
request might have registered remotely. Obtain the pending record's key from
your application's store and recover with refresh({ key }), or
cancel with unsubscribe({ key }). Both reuse the saved callback
identity even when no server ID was saved. Calling subscribe again
creates a new callback identity.

contents.heading: returns-1
contents.content: Promise<Experimental_SubscribeEventResult>:

contents.heading: returns-1
contents.content:
The result excludes the signing secret. The store is updated with the server ID,
deadline, cursor, and active status before the method resolves.

contents.heading: clientexperimental_eventsrefreshoptions
contents.content:
Loads a saved subscription by ID or storage key and sends events/subscribe with
its original name, arguments, callback URL, secret, requested lifetime, and latest
saved cursor.

contents.heading: clientexperimental_eventsrefreshoptions
contents.content:
The subscription is marked pending before renewal. Event deliveries return 503
until the response saves the new expiration and restores active status. If renewal
fails, the record stays pending because the server may have renewed it already;
you can retry refresh or unsubscribe using the saved ID or key.

contents.heading: clientexperimental_eventsrefreshoptions
contents.content:
Verified termination messages for a subscription with a saved ID are handled even
while renewal is pending. For example, if access was revoked, onTerminated can
still run and the saved subscription is removed after successful handling.

contents.heading: parameters-2
contents.content: Provide exactly one of id or key.

contents.heading: returns-2
contents.content:
Promise<Experimental_SubscribeEventResult>, with the same fields as
subscribe. The new deadline and cursor are saved locally.

contents.heading: returns-2
contents.content:
Your application schedules renewal before refreshBefore. The SDK does not run
a background renewal timer. Refresh reuses the saved filters without calling
validateArguments again.

contents.heading: clientexperimental_eventsunsubscribeoptions
contents.content:
Resolves the ID or storage key to the saved name, arguments, and callback URL and
sends events/unsubscribe. It deletes the local record only after the server
succeeds.

contents.heading: parameters-3
contents.content: Provide exactly one of id or key.

contents.heading: returns-3
contents.content:
Promise<void>. If the server request fails, the local record is retained.
Calling client.close() only closes the MCP connection; it does not unsubscribe.

contents.heading: request-options
contents.content:
All four methods accept an options property with the following fields.
The listing method takes { params, options }; the other methods include
options alongside their own parameters.

contents.heading: errors
contents.content:
The client rejects requests to servers without the events capability.
Subscription lifecycle methods require experimental_events.store; refresh and unsubscribe
also require a known subscription ID or storage key. Subscribe rejects unknown
event names, unsupported delivery modes, invalid callback URLs, signing secrets,
or lifetime settings. These checks use MCPClientError, except URL parsing may
throw TypeError.

contents.heading: errors
contents.content:
MCP request errors, store failures, and application validation errors propagate
to the caller. Event requests are not retried by the client's tool-call retry
setting. See MCP client error handling.

contents.heading: experimental_createmcpeventwebhook
contents.content:
Creates a Web Request/Response handler for experimental MCP webhook events.
It verifies callback challenges and event signatures using subscriptions saved by
client.experimental_events.subscribe.

contents.heading: example
contents.content:
Mount this route before subscribing. The handler and subscribing client must
access the same private subscription store.

contents.heading: parameters-4
contents.content:
The argument has type
Experimental_MCPEventWebhookOptions.

contents.heading: callback-arguments
contents.content: onEvent receives:

contents.heading: callback-arguments
contents.content:
See subscription metadata
and event fields for their full types.

contents.heading: callback-arguments
contents.content:
onGap and onTerminated receive the same safe subscription metadata and a
messageId from the signed webhook-id header. Each callback receives only its
matching control payload, so no type check is needed. Deduplicate retries by
subscription ID and messageId.

contents.heading: callback-arguments
contents.content:
onGap receives gap: { type: 'gap', cursor, truncated: true }. It means some
events are no longer available for replay. Reconcile application state or
notify the agent. The helper adds truncated: true and saves it with the fresh
cursor after the callback resolves. The subscription remains active and event
delivery continues.

contents.heading: callback-arguments
contents.content:
onTerminated receives
termination: { type: 'terminated', error: { code, message, data? } }. It means
the server has ended the subscription. Inspect the error for the reason and
notify the agent. After the callback resolves, the helper deletes the saved
subscription record.

contents.heading: callback-arguments
contents.content:
Both return 204 after successful handling. State updates also occur when
the corresponding callback is omitted. Callback or storage failures return 503
for retry. Events and gaps return 503 until activation or renewal is persisted.
Termination is also accepted during pending renewal when the subscription ID is
already saved; subscriptions without a saved ID still return 503.
Controls are processed even if the saved expiration has passed. They are never
sent to onEvent or validatePayload. The helper does not run or notify an agent
automatically.

contents.heading: returns-4
contents.content:
The handler accepts POST requests with Content-Type: application/json.
Pass the original request body bytes and preserve the mcp_event_subscription
query parameter added by the subscribing client. Do not parse and reserialize
the body before passing it to this handler.

contents.heading: returns-4
contents.content:
The server must include webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature,
and X-MCP-Subscription-Id. The helper verifies Standard Webhooks v1 HMAC-SHA256
signatures and accepts signing timestamps within five minutes of the current time.
An event's eventId must match webhook-id, and its name must match the subscription.

contents.content: The following types are exported from @ai-sdk/mcp and are experimental.

contents.heading: event-types
contents.content:

is not exported from @ai-sdk/mcp.

contents.content:
Experimental_MCPEventControl is the union of the lifecycle payloads. onGap
receives its gap variant; onTerminated receives its terminated variant as
termination:

contents.heading: webhook-controls
contents.content:
Unknown extension fields are preserved. Verification challenges are echoed
automatically and do not invoke onEvent, onGap, or onTerminated.

metadata.title: Output
metadata.description: API Reference for Output.

contents.content: The Output object provides output specifications for structured data generation with generateText and streamText. It allows you to specify the expected shape of the generated data and handles validation automatically.

contents.heading: outputtext
contents.content: Output specification for plain text generation. This is the default behavior when no output is specified.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: No parameters required.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: An Output<string, string> specification that generates plain text without schema validation.

contents.heading: outputobject
contents.content: Output specification for typed object generation using schemas. The output is validated against the provided schema to ensure type safety.

contents.heading: returns-1
contents.content: An Output<OBJECT, DeepPartial<OBJECT>> specification where:

contents.heading: returns-1
contents.content: Complete output is fully validated against the schema

contents.heading: returns-1
contents.content: Partial output (during streaming) is a deep partial version of the schema type

contents.heading: returns-1
contents.content:
Partial outputs streamed via streamText cannot be validated against your
provided schema, as incomplete data may not yet conform to the expected
structure.

contents.heading: outputarray
contents.content: Output specification for generating arrays of typed elements. Each element is validated against the provided element schema.

contents.heading: returns-2
contents.content: An Output<Array<ELEMENT>, Array<ELEMENT>> specification where:

contents.heading: returns-2
contents.content: Complete output is an array with all elements validated

contents.heading: returns-2
contents.content: Complete output is validated against minItems and maxItems

contents.heading: returns-2
contents.content: Partial output contains only fully validated elements (incomplete elements are excluded)

contents.heading: returns-2
contents.content:
Set minItems and maxItems to the same value to require an exact number of
elements. The bounds are included in the provider-facing schema when the
provider supports them. The AI SDK also validates the completed output, so
providers that ignore these schema keywords cannot return an out-of-bounds
result.

contents.heading: streaming-with-elementstream
contents.content: When using streamText with Output.array(), you can iterate over elements as they are generated using elementStream:

contents.heading: streaming-with-elementstream
contents.content:
Each element emitted by elementStream is complete and validated against your
element schema, ensuring type safety for each item as it is generated. If the
model generates more than maxItems, elementStream errors before emitting
the first excess element. Provider generation is not aborted automatically,
and the final output promise also rejects.

contents.heading: outputchoice
contents.content: Output specification for selecting from a predefined set of string options. Useful for classification tasks or fixed-enum answers.

contents.heading: returns-3

contents.heading: returns-3

contents.heading: outputjson

metadata.title: pipeAgentUIStreamToResponse
metadata.description: API Reference for the pipeAgentUIStreamToResponse utility.

contents.content: The pipeAgentUIStreamToResponse function runs an Agent and streams the resulting UI message output directly to a Node.js ServerResponse object. This is ideal for building real-time streaming API endpoints (for chat, tool use, etc.) in Node.js-based frameworks like Express, Hono, or custom Node servers.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: A Promise<void>. The function completes when the UI message stream has been fully sent to the provided ServerResponse.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: Use onUIMessageStepEnd to persist the accumulated UI response after every agent step. It is awaited before the corresponding finish-step chunk is piped. Use idempotent writes and protect model output, reasoning, tool inputs, and tool outputs as sensitive conversation data. Use the existing onStepEnd callback when you need low-level generation usage, finish reasons, or raw step details instead.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Runs the Agent: Calls the agent’s .stream method with the provided UI messages and options, converting them into model messages as needed and passing through options such as experimental_sandbox.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Streams UI Message Output: Pipes the agent output as a UI message stream to the ServerResponse, sending data via streaming HTTP responses (including appropriate headers).

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Abort Signal Handling: If abortSignal is supplied, streaming is cancelled as soon as the signal is triggered (such as on client disconnect).

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: No Response Return: Unlike Edge/serverless APIs that return a Response, this function writes bytes directly to the ServerResponse and does not return a response object.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Abort Handling: For best robustness, use an AbortSignal (for example, wired to Express/Hono client disconnects) to ensure quick cancellation of agent computation and streaming.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Node.js Only: Only works with Node.js ServerResponse objects (e.g., in Express, Hono’s node adapter, etc.), not Edge/serverless/web Response APIs.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Streaming Support: Make sure your client (and any proxies) correctly support streaming HTTP responses for full effect.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Parameter Names: The property for input messages is uiMessages (not messages) for consistency with SDK agent utilities.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pass experimental_sandbox when your agent tools need an experimental sandbox environment during execution.

metadata.title: createProviderRegistry
metadata.description: Registry for managing multiple providers and models (API Reference)

contents.content:
When you work with multiple providers and models, it is often desirable to manage them
in a central place and access the models through simple string ids.

createProviderRegistry lets you create a registry with multiple providers that you
can access by their ids in the format providerId:modelId.

In TypeScript, registry model IDs are inferred from the registered provider IDs.
When a provider exposes literal model ID types, editors can suggest the combined
providerId:modelId values.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: You can create a registry with multiple providers and models using createProviderRegistry.

contents.heading: custom-separator
contents.content: By default, the registry uses : as the separator between provider and model IDs. You can customize this separator by passing a separator option:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can access language models by using the languageModel method on the registry.
The provider id will become the prefix of the model id: providerId:modelId.

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content:
You can access text embedding models by using the .embeddingModel method on the registry.
The provider id will become the prefix of the model id: providerId:modelId.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content:
You can access image models by using the imageModel method on the registry.
The provider id will become the prefix of the model id: providerId:modelId.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
You can access video models by using the videoModel method on the registry.
The provider id will become the prefix of the model id: providerId:modelId.

contents.heading: files-and-skills
contents.content:
You can access a provider's files and skills interfaces by calling
registry.files(providerId) and registry.skills(providerId).

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: The createProviderRegistry function returns a Provider instance. It has the following methods:

contents.heading: experimental-decision-models
contents.content:
The inferred return type also exposes decisionModel('providerId:modelId'),
returning Experimental_DecisionModelV4. The provider must expose an
decisionModel factory. Custom separators and model ID
inference work as they do for video models. Language and image middleware do not
wrap decision models. ProviderRegistryProvider remains a stable interface;
use the inferred return type or Experimental_DecisionProviderRegistry to
retain experimental decision access.

contents.heading: experimental-decision-models
contents.content:
Unavailable decision capabilities or models throw NoSuchModelError with
modelType: 'decisionModel'; unknown registry providers throw
NoSuchProviderError. These capabilities are structural extensions and are not
added to the stable ProviderV4 contract. Direct decision string IDs default
to Gateway when no default provider is configured.
See Decisions
for runnable usage patterns.

metadata.title: ToolLoopAgent
metadata.description: API Reference for the ToolLoopAgent class.

contents.content: Creates a reusable AI agent capable of generating text, streaming responses, and using tools over multiple steps (a reasoning-and-acting loop). ToolLoopAgent is ideal for building autonomous, multi-step agents that can take actions, call tools, and reason over the results until a stop condition is reached.
Unlike single-step calls like generateText(), an agent can iteratively invoke tools, collect tool results, and decide next actions until completion or user approval is required.

For agents, runtimeContext is the shared runtime state that flows through the
loop. For guidance on runtimeContext, toolsContext, tool context, and
sensitive context filtering, see Runtime and Tool
Context.
Pass experimental_sandbox to generate() or stream() when tools need access to a command
or code execution environment.
To see ToolLoopAgent in action, check out these examples.

contents.heading: generate
contents.content: Generates a response and triggers tool calls as needed, running the agent loop and returning the final result. Returns a promise resolving to a GenerateTextResult.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: The generate() method returns a GenerateTextResult object (see generateText for details).

contents.heading: stream
contents.content: Streams a response from the agent, including agent reasoning and tool calls, as they occur. Returns a StreamTextResult.

contents.heading: returns-1
contents.content: The stream() method returns a StreamTextResult object (see streamText for details).

contents.heading: activetools
contents.content: Limits an agent step to the listed tool names. undefined means no tool restriction is applied.

contents.heading: inferagentuimessage
contents.content: Infers the UI message type for the given agent instance. Useful for type-safe UI and message exchanges.

contents.heading: example-with-message-metadata
contents.content: You can provide a second type argument to customize the metadata for each message. This is useful for tracking rich metadata returned by the agent (such as createdAt, tokens, finish reason, etc.).

metadata.title: toolSearch
metadata.description: Search deferred tools and load their definitions on demand for direct calling or code mode.

contents.content:
Creates a tool that searches the surrounding generation's deferred tools, using
keyword matching by default or a custom search callback. Use it with generateText,
streamText, ToolLoopAgent, or WorkflowAgent from @ai-sdk/workflow.
WorkflowAgent supports direct tool calling. The other APIs also support code
mode configured with toolDiscovery: 'conversation'.

See the Tool Search guide for direct-calling and
code mode examples, including how code mode preserves the tool-definition cache.

contents.heading: options
contents.content: Pass an optional configuration object to control the result limit:

contents.heading: options
contents.content:
maxResults is the maximum number of matching tools returned and discovered per
search. It defaults to 5 and must be a positive safe integer. Invalid values
throw InvalidArgumentError when creating the search tool. The model-facing
description reflects the configured limit.

contents.heading: options
contents.content:
The limit applies to both default keyword search and custom search callbacks,
without changing their matching or ranking. Discovered tools accumulate across
searches, so this is not a limit on the total number of tools loaded during a
generation.

contents.heading: options
contents.content:
Pass a search callback to select and rank tools using your application's search
logic. The callback can return synchronously or asynchronously:

contents.heading: options
contents.content: The callback has this signature:

contents.heading: options
contents.content:
tools contains all eligible deferred tools, before keyword matching or ranking.
Eligibility respects activeTools and caller routing. Descriptions are resolved
using the current tool context and sandbox; schemas are not included.

contents.heading: options
contents.content:
Return tool names in ranked order. The SDK ignores unknown or ineligible names,
removes duplicates while preserving order, and keeps the first maxResults valid
names (five by default). Returned descriptions come from the SDK's candidate
catalog. An empty array
discovers no tools. Callback errors follow normal tool-execution error handling;
the SDK does not fall back to keyword search.

contents.heading: options
contents.content: Without a callback, toolSearch() uses the default keyword search described below.

contents.heading: model-input
contents.content: The model supplies the following input to the search tool:

contents.heading: model-input
contents.content:
query is a required, nonempty string. By default, search is local and
case-insensitive, matching words in tool names and descriptions. Camel-case names
are split into words. Name matches rank above description matches; equal scores
preserve registration order. Function descriptions are resolved with the current
tool context and sandbox. The default search uses no embedding service or
additional model call. A custom callback can use either.

contents.heading: output
contents.content:
Results contain at most maxResults matching tools (five by default), with their
names and optional descriptions. They do not include schemas. No matches returns
{ tools: [] }.
Every returned match is queued for discovery. Newly discovered tools can only be
called on the next model step, after their definitions have been provided. A
parallel call in the same response as the search cannot use a newly discovered
tool. For code mode, finish the current execution and wait for the capability
update.

contents.heading: discovery-lifecycle
contents.content:
Before the next model step, the SDK makes discovered tools available through
their configured callers:

contents.heading: discovery-lifecycle
contents.content: Direct calling: the provider receives the updated tool definitions.

contents.heading: discovery-lifecycle
contents.content:
Code mode: the SDK appends a user message containing the updated capability
catalog. The provider-visible code mode definition stays unchanged. Existing
catalogs remain in the conversation; the latest catalog describes the complete
currently available tool set.

contents.heading: discovery-lifecycle
contents.content:
Actual prompt-cache reuse depends on the provider. Code mode search still requires
toolDiscovery: 'conversation'; description discovery and provider callers are
not supported.

contents.heading: discovery-lifecycle
contents.content:
Discovered tools remain loaded for the rest of the generation, subject to
activeTools. Search cannot discover tools excluded by activeTools. Discovery
state is isolated between generation calls, including calls that reuse the same
agent or tool instances.

contents.heading: discovery-lifecycle
contents.content:
Set a multi-step stopWhen condition with generateText and streamText so the
model can search, use the discovered tools, and answer.

metadata.title: tool
metadata.description: Helper function for tool type inference

contents.content: Tool is a helper function that infers the tool input and context for its execute method and lifecycle callbacks.
It does not have any runtime behavior, but it helps TypeScript infer the types for the tool callbacks.

Without this helper function, TypeScript is unable to connect the inputSchema and contextSchema properties to the tool callbacks,
and the callback argument types cannot be inferred.

For the full model of runtimeContext, toolsContext, tool context, and
sensitive context filtering, see Runtime and Tool
Context.
The Tool type is a union of four tool kinds:
FunctionTool: a user-defined function-style tool with known input and output types.
DynamicTool: a function-style tool defined at runtime, with unknown input and output types.
ProviderDefinedTool: a provider-defined tool that your code executes.
ProviderExecutedTool: a provider-defined tool that the provider executes.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: The tool that was passed in.

metadata.title: UIMessage
metadata.description: API Reference for UIMessage

contents.content: UIMessage serves as the source of truth for your application's state, representing the complete message history including metadata, data parts, and all contextual information. In contrast to ModelMessage, which represents the state or context passed to the model, UIMessage contains the full application state needed for UI rendering and client-side functionality.

contents.heading: type-safety
contents.content: UIMessage is designed to be type-safe and accepts three generic parameters to ensure proper typing throughout your application:

contents.heading: type-safety
contents.content: METADATA - Custom metadata type for additional message information

contents.heading: type-safety
contents.content: DATA_PARTS - Custom data part types for structured data components

contents.heading: type-safety
contents.content: TOOLS - Tool definitions for type-safe tool interactions

contents.heading: creating-your-own-uimessage-type
contents.content: Here's an example of how to create a custom typed UIMessage for your application:

contents.heading: textuipart
contents.content: A text part of a message.

contents.heading: reasoninguipart
contents.content: A reasoning part of a message.

contents.heading: tooluipart
contents.content: A tool part of a message that represents tool invocations and their results.

contents.heading: tooluipart
contents.content:
The type is based on the name of the tool (e.g., tool-someTool for a tool
named someTool).

contents.content:
approval.descriptor contains optional opaque metadata supplied as
approvalDescriptor on the approval request stream chunk. It is preserved when
the tool part transitions from approval-requested to approval-responded and
in later approval-bearing output states.

contents.heading: tooloutputerroruipart

A static or dynamic tool part whose execution failed. Use the
isToolOutputErrorUIPart type guard when rendering messages so your code does
not need to check the tool state discriminator directly.

contents.heading: tooloutputerroruipart
contents.content:
The generic ToolOutputErrorUIPart<TOOLS> type preserves the input types of
static tools and also includes dynamic tool errors:

contents.heading: customcontentuipart
contents.content: A provider-specific custom content part of a message.

contents.heading: sourceurluipart
contents.content: A source URL part of a message.

contents.heading: sourcedocumentuipart
contents.content: A document source part of a message.

contents.heading: fileuipart
contents.content: A file part of a message.

contents.heading: datauipart
contents.content: A data part of a message for custom data types.

metadata.title: zodSchema
metadata.description: Helper function for creating Zod schemas

contents.content:
zodSchema is a helper function that converts a Zod schema into a JSON schema object that is compatible with the AI SDK.
It takes a Zod schema and optional configuration as inputs, and returns a typed schema.
You can use it to generate structured data and in tools.

You can also pass Zod objects directly to the AI SDK functions. Internally,
the AI SDK will convert the Zod schema to a JSON schema using zodSchema().
However, if you want to specify options such as useReferences, you can pass
the zodSchema() helper function instead.

When using .meta() or .describe() to add metadata to your Zod schemas,
make sure these methods are called at the end of the schema chain.

metadata is attached to a specific schema
instance, and most schema methods (.min(), .optional(), .extend(), etc.)
return a new schema instance that does not inherit metadata from the previous one.
Due to Zod's immutability, metadata is only included in the JSON schema output
if .meta() or .describe() is the last method in the chain.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: A Schema object that is compatible with the AI SDK, containing both the JSON schema representation and validation functionality.

preserved unchanged.

Receiving an error chunk in a completion data stream
Receiving a text-delta chunk without a preceding text-start chunk
Receiving a text-end chunk without a preceding text-start chunk
Receiving a reasoning-delta chunk without a preceding reasoning-start chunk
Receiving a reasoning-end chunk without a preceding reasoning-start chunk
Receiving a tool-input-delta chunk without a preceding tool-input-start chunk
Attempting to access a tool invocation that doesn't exist
This error often surfaces when an upstream request fails before any tokens are streamed and a custom transport tries to write an inline error message to the UI stream without the proper start chunk.

This is an empty string for chunks, such as completion error chunks, that do

The sandbox is forwarded to every agent.stream() call as

Use the agent option for agents that can run directly from free-form user

encounters a defined value.

contents.heading: deprecated-rawinput-field
contents.content:
When both fields are present, input takes precedence when it is non-nullish.
For backward compatibility, rawInput remains the fallback when input is
null or undefined. Migrate stored messages to input before the next major
version, when rawInput will be removed.

contents.heading: tool-approval-states
contents.content: convertToModelMessages preserves tool approval state from UI messages when converting them back into ModelMessages for a follow-up generateText or streamText call.

contents.heading: tool-approval-states
contents.content: Tool parts with approval metadata produce tool-approval-request content parts. approval.requestReason is forwarded as the request reason when present.

contents.heading: tool-approval-states
contents.content: Tool parts in approval-responded state also become tool-approval-response content parts. The separate response reason is forwarded when present.

contents.heading: tool-approval-states
contents.content: Automatic approval metadata is preserved by forwarding approval.isAutomatic to the tool-approval-request part.

contents.heading: tool-approval-states
contents.content: Denied tool approvals also produce a synthetic tool-result with output: { type: 'execution-denied', reason?: string }, so the model receives a complete tool lifecycle and can respond to the denial in the next step.

setOutcome records the composer's policy without writing a chunk or closing
the stream. The first outcome declared through setOutcome is retained, but a
fatal execution, merge, error-handling, or downstream processing failure makes

Single-process applications

metadata.title: pruneMessages
metadata.description: API Reference for pruneMessages.

contents.content: The pruneMessages function is used to prune or filter an array of ModelMessage objects. This is useful for reducing message context (to save tokens), removing intermediate reasoning, or trimming tool calls and empty messages before sending to an LLM.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: An array of ModelMessage objects, pruned according to the provided options.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: reasoning: Removes reasoning parts from assistant messages. Use 'all' to remove all, 'before-last-message' to keep reasoning in the last message, or 'none' to retain all reasoning.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: toolCalls: Prune tool-call, tool-result, and tool-approval chunks from assistant/tool messages. Default is an empty array (no pruning). Options include:

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: 'all': Prune all such content.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: 'before-last-message': Prune except in the last message.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: 'before-last-N-messages': Prune except in the last N messages.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: 'none': Do not prune.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: Or provide an array for per-tool fine control, e.g., [{ type: 'before-last-message', tools: ['search', 'calculator'] }] to prune only specific tools.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: emptyMessages: Set to 'remove' (default) to exclude messages that have no content after pruning.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: Tip: pruneMessages is typically used prior to sending a context window to an LLM to reduce message/token count, especially after a series of tool-calls and approvals.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: For advanced usage and the full list of possible message parts, see ModelMessage and pruneMessages implementation.

metadata.title: readUIMessageStream
metadata.description: API Reference for readUIMessageStream.

contents.content: Transforms a stream of UIMessageChunks into an AsyncIterableStream of UIMessages.
UI message streams are useful outside of Chat use cases, e.g. for terminal UIs, custom stream consumption on the client, or RSC (React Server Components).

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: An AsyncIterableStream of UIMessages. Each stream part represents a different state of the same message as it is being completed.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: For comprehensive examples and use cases, see Reading UI Message Streams.

metadata.title: useChat
metadata.description: API reference for the useChat hook.

title.children: React rendering and shared Chat instances

contents.content: Allows you to easily create a conversational user interface for your chatbot application. It enables the streaming of chat messages from your AI provider, manages the chat state, and updates the UI automatically as new messages are received.

The useChat API has been significantly updated in AI SDK 5.0. It now uses a
transport-based architecture and no longer manages input state internally. See
the migration
guide for
details.

contents.heading: react-rendering-and-shared-chat-instances
contents.content:
In React, messages, status, and error describe the snapshot for the current render.
The underlying Chat updates as stream chunks are processed. React may batch updates,
and throttle can delay message rendering without delaying stream processing or callbacks.
Status and error updates include the latest messages, so a completed or failed response
is rendered with its final message snapshot.

contents.heading: react-rendering-and-shared-chat-instances
contents.content:
Each useChat({ chat }) call subscribes independently. Consumers sharing a Chat
can display different message snapshots when they use different throttle intervals.
A functional setMessages updater receives the Chat's latest messages, which may be
newer than the messages in the current render.

contents.content: Chatbot

contents.heading: learn-more
contents.content: Chatbot with Tools
