metadata.title: Codex
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Codex harness adapter.

contents.content:
The Codex harness adapter connects HarnessAgent to the Codex app-server.
The adapter runs a bridge inside the sandbox and streams Codex thread events
back to the host over a sandbox-exposed WebSocket.

Harness packages are experimental. Expect breaking changes between
releases as this early API gets further refined.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content:
The adapter bootstraps the Codex bridge dependencies inside the sandbox when
the first session starts.

contents.heading: import
contents.content: codex is equivalent to createCodex() with its default configuration.

contents.heading: basic-usage
contents.content:
To use this agent, ensure environment variables include VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN for
Vercel Sandbox, and one of the variables listed under authentication
for Codex.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Use createCodex() to configure the runtime:

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Settings:

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
auth: authentication mode (auto, direct, or ai-gateway) or an
isolated authentication environment.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
credentialForwarding: optional synchronous or asynchronous callback that
customizes each credential immediately before the harness adapter forwards it
into a sandbox process. It receives the credential value that would otherwise
be forwarded (either the real credential or a masked value) and the
environment variable name used to expose it. This callback only controls the
value forwarded into the sandbox process. It does not restrict which
credentials the harness adapter can discover, read, or otherwise access in
the host process.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
codexConfig: additional native Codex configuration. Values pass through as
provided, so use the snake_case keys from Codex's config.toml reference.
The adapter's managed values take precedence over conflicting entries.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: mcpServers: MCP server definitions keyed by server name.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: reasoningEffort: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: webSearch: allow live web search.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: port: bridge port override.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: startupTimeoutMs: maximum time to wait for the bridge to start.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
reconnect: reconnect timing after an established bridge WebSocket
connection drops. maxElapsedMs controls the total retry window, including
connection establishment and backoff delays, and defaults to 30 seconds.
initialDelayMs defaults to 50 milliseconds, and maxDelayMs defaults to
2 seconds. These retries use exponential backoff and are separate from
startupTimeoutMs. They cannot recover when the sandbox, bridge process, or
bridge endpoint is permanently unavailable.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
mintBridgeToken: synchronous function that receives the sandbox id and
returns the bridge authentication token. By default, the adapter generates a
random 32-byte token. Custom implementations must return a suitably secret
token.

contents.heading: built-in-tool-filtering
contents.content:
Codex supports activeTools and inactiveTools for bash, webSearch,
apply_patch, and view_image. Host tools are filtered before they are sent
to Codex. Native Codex configuration disables bash, view_image, and
webSearch individually. When bash, apply_patch, and view_image are all
inactive, the adapter disables Codex environments and explicitly disables
bash and view_image. When apply_patch is inactive but bash or
view_image remains active, the adapter installs a Codex PreToolUse hook
that denies patch execution. Before starting each turn, the adapter checks
that Codex loaded and trusted the hook and fails the turn if it did not.
Including webSearch in activeTools does not enable it on its own; set
webSearch: true on createCodex() to allow live search.

contents.heading: structured-output
contents.content:
Codex supports schema-backed HarnessAgent structured output.
The adapter passes the JSON Schema through the Codex app-server's turn/start
outputSchema parameter.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
The auth setting selects how credentials are resolved from the host
environment:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
auto (default): use AI Gateway credentials when available, then fall back
to direct OpenAI credentials.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: direct: use OpenAI credentials.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: ai-gateway: use AI Gateway credentials.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
When the sandbox supports additive request transformations, the bridge receives
placeholders and the adapter injects credentials into matching outbound
requests. Sandboxes without that capability retain direct credential
forwarding.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: Supported environment variables:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: OPENAI_API_KEY

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: CODEX_API_KEY

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: OPENAI_BASE_URL

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: OPENAI_ORGANIZATION

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: OPENAI_PROJECT

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
If no applicable credential environment variable is set, the adapter attempts
to resolve a native subscription from the host system unless AI Gateway
authentication is selected.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: Select a specific authentication mode when you do not want automatic detection:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
Pass an authentication environment to use programmatically resolved
credentials without reading process.env:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
The supplied record replaces the host environment for authentication
discovery. Only recognized authentication variables are forwarded.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: For OpenAI-compatible endpoints, select direct and set OPENAI_BASE_URL.

contents.heading: sandbox
contents.content:
Codex requires a network sandbox with at least one exposed port,
e.g. @ai-sdk/sandbox-vercel:

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content: The adapter exposes these Codex built-ins through agent.tools:

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content: bash and webSearch use the common cross-harness tool names.

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content: apply_patch accepts Codex's freeform patch string.

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content:
view_image accepts a local image path, with optional detail and
environment_id fields.

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content:
Codex file changes may also appear as dynamic fileChange tool parts because
some Codex file mutations do not originate from a visible model-callable tool.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
Codex does not currently support built-in tool approval requests. Use
permissionMode: 'allow-all' with this adapter. Host-executed AI SDK tool
approvals still work.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
When the app-server must cold-resume a thread, Codex does not provide raw
events for apply_patch and view_image, so those tool calls and results
cannot be surfaced for that resumed thread.

metadata.title: Cursor
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Cursor harness adapter.

contents.content:
The Cursor harness adapter connects HarnessAgent to
Cursor CLI through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP).
The adapter delegates ACP sessions, streaming, tools, and lifecycle management
to @ai-sdk/harness-acp.

Harness packages are experimental. Expect breaking changes between
releases as this early API gets further refined.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content:
Create a Cursor user API key and set CURSOR_API_KEY. The key authenticates
Cursor CLI in the sandbox regardless of how Cursor authenticates to the model
provider.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content:
The adapter installs Cursor CLI inside the sandbox with the official Cursor
install command when the first session starts.

contents.heading: import
contents.content: cursor is equivalent to createCursor() with its default configuration.

contents.heading: basic-usage
contents.content:
To use this agent with Vercel Sandbox, provide VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN and
CURSOR_API_KEY in the host environment.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Use createCursor() to configure the runtime:

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Settings:

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
auth: accepts the shared ACP modes auto, direct, or ai-gateway, or an
isolated authentication environment for CURSOR_API_KEY. This cannot change
Cursor's provider authentication route. Explicit direct and ai-gateway
values emit a configuration reminder; auto does not because it does not
declare an expected route.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
credentialForwarding: optional synchronous or asynchronous callback that
customizes each credential immediately before the harness adapter forwards it
into a sandbox process. It receives the credential value that would otherwise
be forwarded (either the real credential or a masked value) and the
environment variable name used to expose it. This callback only controls the
value forwarded into the sandbox process. It does not restrict which
credentials the harness adapter can discover, read, or otherwise access in
the host process.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: mcpServers: MCP server definitions keyed by server name.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: port: ACP bridge port override.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: startupTimeoutMs: maximum time to wait for the ACP bridge to start.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
reconnect: reconnect timing after an established bridge WebSocket
connection drops. maxElapsedMs controls the total retry window, including
connection establishment and backoff delays, and defaults to 30 seconds.
initialDelayMs defaults to 50 milliseconds, and maxDelayMs defaults to
2 seconds. These retries use exponential backoff and are separate from
startupTimeoutMs. They cannot recover when the sandbox, bridge process, or
bridge endpoint is permanently unavailable.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
mintBridgeToken: synchronous function that receives the sandbox id and
returns the ACP bridge authentication token. By default, the adapter generates
a random 32-byte token. Custom implementations must return a suitably secret
token.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
The adapter fixes the install command and ACP launch command. These
implementation details cannot be overridden through createCursor().

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: Cursor has two independent authentication layers:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
CURSOR_API_KEY authenticates Cursor CLI to the Cursor account. The harness
requires this key for every auth mode.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
Cursor's account settings determine how Cursor authenticates to the model
provider. The harness cannot read or change this setting.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
If no applicable credential environment variable is set, the adapter attempts
to resolve a native subscription from the host system unless AI Gateway
authentication is selected.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
For direct routing, configure the model provider in Cursor. For AI Gateway,
configure Cursor's OpenAI API key with an AI Gateway API key and set
Override OpenAI Base URL to
https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/cursor/v1 in Cursor settings. Cursor resolves that
credential from its account configuration; the harness does not use
AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY or VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN for model-provider authentication.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
Explicit direct and ai-gateway values emit a warning that the selected route
must be configured in Cursor. auto is accepted without a warning:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
Supply a programmatically resolved Cursor account credential without mutating
or reading process.env:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
This record configures Cursor CLI authentication only. Cursor's account
settings still control model-provider routing.

contents.heading: sandbox
sandbox
contents.content: The first session requires network egress to run Cursor's official installer.

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content:
The adapter maps Cursor's terminal, glob, and grep tools to the common bash,
glob, and grep tools. It also exposes Cursor's remaining built-ins under
stable names, including read, edit, ls, semanticSearch, webSearch,
task, and the Cursor planning, MCP, browser, and environment tools.

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content:
Cursor host-tool calls use ACP MCP transport. The adapter recognizes Cursor's
MCP payload and correlates the call with the host-side tool execution.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
Cursor's model-provider authentication route must be configured in Cursor.
The auth adapter setting cannot switch it programmatically.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
ACP v1 does not expose model-step boundaries or per-step usage. The adapter
infers boundaries and reports unknown per-step usage when Cursor does not
provide totals.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content: ACP v1 has no portable manual compaction or mid-turn steering API.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
ACP v1 has no portable built-in tool filtering API. Filtering host tools is
supported, but filtering Cursor built-ins throws an unsupported-capability
error.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
Cursor does not currently support built-in tool approval requests. Use
permissionMode: 'allow-all' with this adapter. Host-executed AI SDK tool
approvals still work.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
Cursor ACP does not expose a structured-output metadata mapping, so schema-backed
structured output is unsupported.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
Custom headers are not natively supported and only applied via
sandbox-external request transformations. When a sandbox without that
capability is provided, custom headers therefore cannot be passed and are
ignored.

metadata.title: Deep Agents
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Deep Agents harness adapter.

contents.content:
The Deep Agents harness adapter connects HarnessAgent to
Deep Agents, a LangGraph-based agent
runtime. The adapter runs a Node bridge inside the sandbox that drives the
deepagents package and streams its streamEvents output back to the host over a
sandbox-exposed WebSocket.

Harness packages are experimental. Expect breaking changes between
releases as this early API gets further refined.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content:
The adapter bootstraps the bridge's Node dependencies (the deepagents package
and LangChain) inside the sandbox via pnpm when the first session starts.

contents.heading: import
contents.content:
deepAgents is equivalent to createDeepAgents() with its default
configuration.

contents.heading: basic-usage

Vercel Sandbox, and one of the variables listed under
authentication for the model provider.

into a sandbox process. It receives the credential value that would otherwise
be forwarded (either the real credential or a masked value) and the
environment variable name used to expose it. This callback only controls the
value forwarded into the sandbox process. It does not restrict which
credentials the harness adapter can discover, read, or otherwise access in
the host process.

contents.heading: adapter-settings

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: port: bridge port override.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
recursionLimit: maximum LangGraph super-steps per turn. When omitted, the

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: startupTimeoutMs: maximum time to wait for the bridge to start.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
reconnect: reconnect timing after an established bridge WebSocket

2 seconds. These retries use exponential backoff and are separate from

random 32-byte token. Custom implementations must return a suitably secret

contents.heading: structured-output
contents.content:
Deep Agents supports schema-backed HarnessAgent structured output.
The adapter applies a per-turn LangChain tool strategy and returns the graph's
validated structuredResponse as JSON text.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
Deep Agents always drives the Anthropic client. Non-Anthropic models reach it
through AI Gateway's Anthropic-compatible endpoint, which translates to any
model (Gemini, OpenAI, etc.), tool calls included.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
The auth setting selects how credentials are resolved from the host
environment:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
auto (default): use AI Gateway credentials when available, then fall back
to Anthropic credentials.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: anthropic: use Anthropic credentials.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: ai-gateway: use AI Gateway credentials.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
When the sandbox supports additive request transformations, the bridge receives
placeholders and the adapter injects credentials into matching outbound
requests. Sandboxes without that capability retain direct credential
forwarding.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: Supported environment variables:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN

contents.heading: authentication

The fx harness adapter connects HarnessAgent to fx through
the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). The adapter delegates installation, sessions,
streaming, tools, and lifecycle management to @ai-sdk/harness-acp.

Harness packages are experimental. Expect breaking changes between

contents.heading: setup
contents.content:
The ACP harness runs the canonical fx installer
inside the sandbox when the first session starts. The installer tracks the
latest fx release and installs the executable into the ACP implementation's
private home directory.

contents.heading: import
contents.content: fx is equivalent to createFx() with its default configuration.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Use createFx() to configure the runtime:

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Settings:

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
auth: selects auto, direct, or ai-gateway authentication, or accepts
an authentication environment for programmatically resolved credentials. fx
always sends model requests through Vercel AI Gateway, so
direct and ai-gateway differ only in how the harness passes the Gateway
credential into the sandbox.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
credentialForwarding: optional synchronous or asynchronous callback that
customizes each credential immediately before the harness adapter forwards it
into a sandbox process. It receives the credential value that would otherwise
be forwarded (either the real credential or a masked value) and the
environment variable name used to expose it. This callback only controls the
value forwarded into the sandbox process. It does not restrict which
credentials the harness adapter can discover, read, or otherwise access in
the host process.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
mcpServers: MCP server definitions keyed by server name. fx ACP sessions
use only the servers supplied by the ACP client.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: port: ACP bridge port override.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
portEndpoint: host endpoint for the ACP bridge when the sandbox session
cannot expose ports directly.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: startupTimeoutMs: maximum time to wait for the ACP bridge to start.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
reconnect: reconnect timing after an established bridge WebSocket
connection drops. maxElapsedMs controls the total retry window, including
connection establishment and backoff delays, and defaults to 30 seconds.
initialDelayMs defaults to 50 milliseconds, and maxDelayMs defaults to
2 seconds. These retries use exponential backoff and are separate from
startupTimeoutMs. They cannot recover when the sandbox, bridge process, or
bridge endpoint is permanently unavailable.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
mintBridgeToken: synchronous function that receives the sandbox id and
returns the ACP bridge authentication token. By default, the adapter generates
a random 32-byte token.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
The adapter fixes the installation source, executable, launch command, and ACP
version. These implementation details cannot be overridden through
createFx().

fx uses Vercel AI Gateway authentication.
Set one of these environment variables:

contents.heading: authentication

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
If no applicable credential environment variable is set, the adapter attempts
to resolve a native subscription from the host system unless AI Gateway
authentication is selected.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
fx prefers VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN when both are available. The adapter brokers the
selected credential only to the configured Gateway origin when the sandbox
supports request transformations. Other sandboxes retain direct credential
forwarding.

contents.content:
Pass an authentication environment when the host resolves credentials at
runtime instead of exposing them through process.env:

contents.content:
The supplied record replaces the host environment for authentication
discovery. The adapter does not add its credentials to process.env or include
their values in persisted ACP lifecycle identity.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: Both authentication configurations reach AI Gateway:

contents.heading: sandbox
contents.content:
fx runs inside the sandbox through @ai-sdk/harness-acp. It requires a network
sandbox with at least one exposed port:

contents.heading: sandbox
contents.content:
The first session requires network egress to download fx. Subsequent model and
web requests also require network access.

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content:
The adapter maps glob_files, grep_files, and web_search to the common
glob, grep, and webSearch harness tool names.

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content:
Other tools remain available under their native fx names, including
list_files, read_file, write_file, edit_file, file mutation and metadata
tools, terminal, semantic_search, web_fetch, skill tools, subagents, MCP
discovery tools, ask_user_question, vision, and read_tool_result.

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content:
The adapter maps allow-reads and allow-edits to fx's ask ACP mode.
allow-all maps to fx's code ACP mode. The allow-edits mapping is
conservative because fx does not provide a mode that allows file edits while
still requiring approval for terminal commands. fx may resolve safe operations
or apply its own permission policy without sending an ACP permission request.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
fx's ACP v1 tool updates omit the programmatic tool name and raw input except
when requesting permission. Native tools still execute, but ordinary native
tool events cannot always be associated with a typed built-in tool name.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
ACP v1 does not expose model-step boundaries or per-step usage. The adapter
infers boundaries and reports unknown per-step usage when fx does not provide
totals.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content: ACP v1 has no portable manual compaction or mid-turn steering API.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
ACP v1 has no portable built-in tool filtering API. Filtering host tools is
supported, but filtering fx built-ins throws an unsupported-capability error.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
fx ACP does not expose a structured-output metadata mapping, so schema-backed
structured output is unsupported.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
Custom headers are not natively supported and only applied via
sandbox-external request transformations. When a sandbox without that
capability is provided, custom headers therefore cannot be passed and are
ignored.

streaming, tools, approvals, and lifecycle management to
@ai-sdk/harness-acp.

Harness packages are experimental. Expect breaking changes between
releases as this early API gets further refined.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content:
The ACP harness installs the pinned GitHub Copilot CLI inside the sandbox when
the first session starts. It never uses a host or globally installed Copilot
CLI. The launch command disables GitHub Copilot's automatic updates so the
installed version remains fixed for that bootstrap.

contents.heading: import
contents.content:
githubCopilot is equivalent to createGitHubCopilot() with its default
configuration.

contents.heading: basic-usage
contents.content:
To use this agent with Vercel Sandbox, provide VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN and one of
the variables listed under authentication in the host
environment.

contents.heading: basic-usage
contents.content:
Sessions support multiple turns, attach and detach, cold stop and resume, turn
suspension and continuation, and stopWhen slicing through the shared ACP
bridge lifecycle.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Use createGitHubCopilot() to configure the runtime:

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Settings:

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:

an isolated authentication environment. The default is auto, which selects
AI Gateway when Gateway credentials are present and direct GitHub Copilot
authentication otherwise.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
credentialForwarding: optional synchronous or asynchronous callback that
customizes each credential immediately before the harness adapter forwards it
into a sandbox process. It receives the credential value that would otherwise
be forwarded (either the real credential or a masked value) and the
environment variable name used to expose it. This callback only controls the
value forwarded into the sandbox process. It does not restrict which
credentials the harness adapter can discover, read, or otherwise access in
the host process.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
reasoningEffort: reasoning effort for reasoning-capable models. Supported
values are none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, and max.
When omitted, GitHub Copilot uses its configured default.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
mcpServers: ACP-native stdio, HTTP, or SSE MCP server definitions keyed by
server name.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: port: ACP bridge port override.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
portEndpoint: host endpoint for the ACP bridge when the sandbox session
cannot expose ports directly.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: startupTimeoutMs: maximum time to wait for the ACP bridge to start.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
reconnect: reconnect timing after an established bridge WebSocket
connection drops. maxElapsedMs controls the total retry window, including
connection establishment and backoff delays, and defaults to 30 seconds.
initialDelayMs defaults to 50 milliseconds, and maxDelayMs defaults to
2 seconds. These retries use exponential backoff and are separate from
startupTimeoutMs. They cannot recover when the sandbox, bridge process, or
bridge endpoint is permanently unavailable.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
mintBridgeToken: synchronous function that receives the sandbox id and
returns the ACP bridge authentication token. By default, the adapter generates
a random 32-byte token. Custom implementations must return a suitably secret
token.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
reasoningEffort is fixed for the launched GitHub Copilot server and applies
to every session it creates.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
The adapter pins the GitHub Copilot CLI, executable, launch command, and ACP
version. These implementation details cannot be overridden through
createGitHubCopilot().

GitHub Copilot supports direct GitHub authentication and AI Gateway
authentication. Set one or more of these environment variables:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
If no applicable credential environment variable is set, the adapter attempts
to resolve a native subscription from the host system unless AI Gateway
authentication is selected.

contents.content:
For direct authentication, GitHub Copilot checks the three GitHub token
variables in the listed order. Fine-grained personal access tokens require the
Copilot Requests permission; classic personal access tokens are unsupported.
For AI Gateway, the adapter uses VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN or AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and
honors AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL.

contents.content:
When the sandbox supports request transformations, the adapter brokers each
credential only to matching outbound requests. Other sandboxes retain direct

contents.content:
Pass an authentication environment when the host resolves credentials at
runtime:

contents.heading: authentication

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
AI Gateway model requests do not require GitHub authentication, but built-in

contents.heading: sandbox
contents.content:
GitHub Copilot runs inside the sandbox through @ai-sdk/harness-acp. It
requires a network sandbox with at least one exposed port:

contents.heading: sandbox
contents.content:
The first session requires network egress to install GitHub Copilot CLI.
Subsequent model, GitHub, web, and MCP requests also require network access.

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content:
The adapter maps bash, grep, and glob to the corresponding common harness
tools.

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content:
Other tools remain available under their native GitHub Copilot names, including
read_bash, stop_bash, list_bash, view, create, edit, web_fetch,
skill, sql, agent tools, and task. GitHub and user-configured MCP tools
remain dynamic.

contents.heading: built-in-tools
contents.content:
The shared ACP harness applies the configured Harness permissionMode when
GitHub Copilot sends a permission request. allow-reads approves read
operations, allow-edits also approves file mutations, and allow-all approves
every request. Shell execution still requires approval under allow-edits.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
ACP v1 does not expose a stable programmatic name for every native tool event.
The adapter uses standard title, kind, and schema matching and leaves
unmatched tools dynamic.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
ACP v1 does not expose model-step boundaries or per-step usage. The adapter
infers boundaries and reports unknown per-step usage when GitHub Copilot does
not provide totals.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content: ACP v1 has no portable manual compaction or mid-turn steering API.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
ACP v1 has no portable built-in tool filtering API. Filtering host tools is
supported, but filtering GitHub Copilot built-ins throws an
unsupported-capability error.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
GitHub Copilot does not currently support built-in tool approval requests. Use
permissionMode: 'allow-all' with this adapter. Host-executed AI SDK tool
approvals still work.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
GitHub Copilot ACP does not expose a structured-output metadata mapping, so
schema-backed structured output is unsupported.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
GitHub Copilot ACP does not expose any question tool, so askUserQuestions
is unsupported.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
GitHub Copilot CLI does not surface reasoning content over ACP for any
model. reasoningEffort controls reasoning depth, not visibility: emitting
a reasoning summary requires a parameter that ACP's session/new and
session/set_config_option (limited to mode, model, reasoning_effort,
allow_all, and agent) never expose to a client. The only code path that
sets it lives in GitHub Copilot's interactive terminal UI, which does not
run in headless --acp --stdio mode.

contents.heading: known-limitations
contents.content:
Custom headers are not natively supported and only applied via
sandbox-external request transformations. When a sandbox without that
capability is provided, custom headers therefore cannot be passed and are
ignored.

@opencode-ai/sdk. The adapter runs a bridge inside the sandbox, starts an
OpenCode server in that sandbox, and streams OpenCode session events back to
the host over a sandbox-exposed WebSocket.

Harness packages are experimental. Expect breaking changes between
releases as this early API gets further refined.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content:
The adapter bootstraps the OpenCode bridge dependencies inside the sandbox when
the first session starts. The bridge package depends on @opencode-ai/sdk and
opencode-ai.

contents.heading: import
contents.content: openCode is equivalent to createOpenCode() with its default configuration.

contents.heading: basic-usage
contents.content:

Vercel Sandbox, and one of the variables listed under authentication
for OpenCode.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Use createOpenCode() to configure the runtime:

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Settings:

contents.heading: adapter-settings

or an isolated authentication environment.

credentialForwarding: optional synchronous or asynchronous callback that
customizes each credential immediately before the harness adapter forwards it
into a sandbox process. It receives the credential value that would otherwise
be forwarded (either the real credential or a masked value) and the
environment variable name used to expose it. This callback only controls the
value forwarded into the sandbox process. It does not restrict which
credentials the harness adapter can discover, read, or otherwise access in
the host process.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: mcpServers: MCP server definitions keyed by server name.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
openCodeConfig: additional native OpenCode configuration. Adapter-managed
settings take precedence. Agent-local permission and deprecated tools
settings are ignored so they cannot bypass harness permissions or built-in
tool filtering.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: provider: provider id to use when model on HarnessAgent is unprefixed.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
reasoningVariant: OpenCode reasoning/thinking variant for supported models,
such as low, medium, or high.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: port: bridge port override.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: startupTimeoutMs: maximum time to wait for the bridge to start.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
reconnect: reconnect timing after an established bridge WebSocket
connection drops. maxElapsedMs controls the total retry window, including
connection establishment and backoff delays, and defaults to 30 seconds.
initialDelayMs defaults to 50 milliseconds, and maxDelayMs defaults to
2 seconds. These retries use exponential backoff and are separate from
startupTimeoutMs. They cannot recover when the sandbox, bridge process, or
bridge endpoint is permanently unavailable.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
mintBridgeToken: synchronous function that receives the sandbox id and
returns the bridge authentication token. By default, the adapter generates a
random 32-byte token. Custom implementations must return a suitably secret

The adapter uses OpenCode's json_schema prompt format and returns the
validated structured result as JSON text.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:

metadata.title: Pi
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Pi harness adapter.

contents.content:
The Pi harness adapter connects HarnessAgent to
@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent. Pi runs in the host Node.js process and uses
the sandbox as a remote filesystem and shell. It does not install a bridge
inside the sandbox.

Harness packages are experimental. Expect breaking changes between
releases as this early API gets further refined.

contents.heading: import
contents.content: pi is equivalent to createPi() with its default configuration.

contents.heading: basic-usage
contents.content:
To use this agent, ensure environment variables include VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN for
Vercel Sandbox, and one of the variables listed under authentication
for Pi.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Use createPi() to configure the runtime:

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: Settings:

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
auth: authentication mode (auto, openai, anthropic, custom, or
ai-gateway) or an isolated authentication environment.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
cacheRetention: default prompt cache retention for model requests (none,
short, or long). For Anthropic models, long uses the 1-hour cache
instead of the 5-minute default.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
credentials: application-owned Pi credential storage. This replaces the
file-backed auth.json store and supports persistent database-backed
credentials.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
extensionFactories: trusted inline Pi extension factories that run in the
host Node.js process.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
fileToolPathPolicy: extra sandbox roots Pi's native file tools can read,
and roots they must refuse. See File Tool Paths.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: mcpServers: MCP server definitions keyed by server name.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
mcpSettings: settings for the MCP adapter that serves mcpServers, applied
over the package defaults. toolPrefix (mcp, server, short, or none)
sets how MCP tool names are prefixed and defaults to mcp; only
mcp-prefixed tool calls are reported as provider-executed dynamic tools
with parsed JSON results. outputGuard defaults to true; the adapter then
truncates tool results over 50 KiB or 2,000 lines and writes the full text to
the host temp directory, which Pi's sandbox file tools cannot read. Set it to
false to return results in full.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content: providers: explicit Pi provider configurations for custom models.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
reattachInProcess: whether a suspended turn can reuse its live Pi session
in the current process. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: adapter-settings
contents.content:
thinkingLevel: Pi thinking level (off, minimal, low, medium,
high, xhigh, or max).

contents.heading: file-tool-paths
contents.content:
By default, Pi's native file tools (read, write, edit, ls, find, and
grep) are limited to the session workspace, and the read-only tools can also
read the harness skill directory. Use fileToolPathPolicy to change what they
can reach:

contents.heading: file-tool-paths
contents.content:
readableRoots: absolute sandbox directories that read, ls, find, and
grep can reach in addition to the defaults. They do not become writable.

contents.heading: file-tool-paths
contents.content:
deniedRoots: absolute sandbox directories that every native file tool
refuses, even inside the workspace or a readable root. Both requested paths
and denied roots are resolved in the sandbox, so symlinks pointing to or from
a denied root are refused. Denied roots are resolved when the Pi session
starts; start a new session if a denied symlink changes target. find and
grep skip denied roots when they search a parent directory. grep skips
them by directory name, so it also skips other directories with the same
name under the searched directory.

contents.heading: file-tool-paths
contents.content:
When the setting is present, a leading ~ in a tool path expands to the
sandbox home directory.

contents.heading: file-tool-paths
contents.content:
The policy applies to Pi's native file tools only. The bash tool is not
restricted by it, so do not treat deniedRoots as a security boundary for
commands the agent runs.

contents.heading: inline-extensions
contents.content:
Use extensionFactories to load trusted inline Pi extensions for each harness
session:

contents.heading: inline-extensions
contents.content:
Routine resource refreshes between turns reuse the active extension runtime and
do not reinitialize factories. If the underlying Pi session is rebuilt, the
factories initialize again for the new Pi runtime.

contents.heading: inline-extensions
contents.content:
Extension factories execute in the host Node.js process with access to the host
environment, so only pass factories you trust. This setting enables only the
factories you explicitly provide. Filesystem extension discovery remains
disabled, including user, project, and settings-based extensions. Themes and
prompt templates also remain disabled.

contents.heading: session-reattachment
contents.content:
By default, Pi keeps a suspended turn alive for an efficient continuation in
the same process when the incoming request has compatible settings and runtime
resources. Changed request-scoped settings or sandbox handles cause a cold
restore from persisted lifecycle state.

contents.heading: session-reattachment
contents.content:
For stateless or multi-replica applications, disable in-process reattachment so
every continuation restores the persisted lifecycle state with the current
request's settings:

contents.heading: session-reattachment
contents.content:
An incoming completed resume-session state always takes precedence over an
older live suspended turn in the process.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: The auth setting selects which credentials Pi reads from the host environment:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
auto (default): use AI Gateway credentials when available, then fall back
to all provider credentials found in the environment.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: openai: use OPENAI_API_KEY and the optional OPENAI_BASE_URL.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
anthropic: use ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and the optional
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: custom: register all providers configured through environment variables.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
ai-gateway: use AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY or VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN and the
optional AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
If no applicable credential environment variable is set, the adapter attempts
to resolve a native subscription from the host system unless AI Gateway
authentication is selected.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
Pass an authentication environment to use programmatically resolved
credentials without reading process.env:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
The supplied record replaces the host environment for authentication
discovery. Pi parses provider API keys and base URLs from that record.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
For credentials managed outside environment variables or files, inject an
application-owned credential store. Pi performs credential reads, refreshes,
and updates through this interface:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
credentials replaces Pi's auth.json storage. In request-scoped or
multi-replica deployments, pair it with reattachInProcess: false so each
continuation constructs a model runtime from the current request.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
With custom, standard providers use environment variables such as

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Other providers use a <PREFIX>_API_KEY and matching

contents.content:
Authentication variables do not identify a provider's API protocol or models.
Register that metadata explicitly when using a custom model:

Pi needs a sandbox session but does not require exposed ports. You can create a

metadata.title: AI Gateway
metadata.description: Learn how to use the AI Gateway provider with the AI SDK.

title.children: Vercel Access Token Authentication for Model Requests
Usage Tracking with User and Tags

contents.content: The AI Gateway provider connects you to models from multiple AI providers through a single interface. Instead of integrating with each provider separately, you can access OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI, and other providers and their models.

contents.heading: features
contents.content: Access models from multiple providers without having to install additional provider modules/dependencies

contents.heading: features
contents.content: Use the same code structure across different AI providers

contents.heading: features
contents.content: Switch between models and providers easily

contents.heading: features
contents.content: Automatic authentication when deployed on Vercel

contents.heading: features
contents.content: View pricing information across providers

contents.heading: features
contents.content: Observability for AI model usage through the Vercel dashboard

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Vercel AI Gateway provider is part of the AI SDK.

contents.heading: basic-usage
contents.content: For most use cases, you can use the AI Gateway directly with a model string:

contents.heading: basic-usage
contents.content: The AI SDK automatically uses the AI Gateway when you pass a model string in the creator/model-name format.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The gateway provider instance is available from the ai package in version
5.0.36 and later.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can also import the default provider instance gateway from ai:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You may want to create a custom provider instance when you need to:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Set custom configuration options (API key, Vercel access token, base URL, headers)

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Use the provider in a provider registry

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Wrap the provider with middleware

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Use different settings for different parts of your application

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: To create a custom provider instance, import createGateway from ai:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the AI Gateway provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: batchResultDownloads object

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Settings for downloading JSON Lines batch results.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: maxLineBytes number

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Maximum UTF-8 bytes per row, excluding the LF delimiter. Defaults to 64 MiB
(67,108,864 bytes). Must be a positive safe integer. Oversized rows throw a
DownloadError and cancel the download.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Use a different URL prefix for API calls. The default prefix is https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v4/ai.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key or Vercel access token that is being sent using the Authorization
header. It defaults to the AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY environment variable.
Supports AI Gateway API keys, Vercel personal access tokens, and Vercel app
access tokens.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: teamIdOrSlug string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Vercel team ID or slug used to scope model requests when authenticating with
multi-team Vercel access tokens.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: metadataCacheRefreshMillis number

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: How frequently to refresh the metadata cache in milliseconds. Defaults to 5 minutes (300,000ms).

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: The Gateway provider supports the following authentication methods:

contents.heading: api-key-authentication
contents.content: Set your API key via environment variable:

contents.heading: api-key-authentication
contents.content: Or pass it directly to the provider:

contents.heading: vercel-access-token-authentication-for-model-requests
contents.content:
For dynamic runtime authentication of model requests, pass a Vercel personal
access token or Vercel app access token to a custom Gateway provider instance:

contents.heading: vercel-access-token-authentication-for-model-requests
contents.content: apiKey takes precedence over AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and OIDC.

contents.heading: vercel-access-token-authentication-for-model-requests
contents.content:
Vercel access tokens with teamIdOrSlug are supported for model requests.
Gateway helper methods such as getCredits, getSpendReport, and
getGenerationInfo require an AI Gateway API key or OIDC authentication.

contents.heading: oidc-authentication-vercel-deployments
contents.content:
When deployed to Vercel, the AI Gateway provider supports authenticating model
requests using OIDC (OpenID Connect) tokens
without API Keys.

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: In Production/Preview Deployments:

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: OIDC authentication is automatically handled

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: No manual configuration needed

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: Tokens are automatically obtained and refreshed

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: In Local Development:

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: First, install and authenticate with the Vercel CLI

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: Run vercel env pull to download your project's OIDC token locally

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: For automatic token management:

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: Use vercel dev to start your development server - this will handle token refreshing automatically

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: For manual token management:

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: If not using vercel dev, note that OIDC tokens expire after 12 hours

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: You'll need to run vercel env pull again to refresh the token before it expires

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content:
If an API key or Vercel access token is present (either passed directly or via
environment), it will always be used instead of OIDC, even if invalid.

contents.heading: how-oidc-authentication-works
contents.content: Read more about using OIDC tokens in the Vercel AI Gateway docs.

contents.heading: bring-your-own-key-byok
contents.content: You can connect your own provider credentials to use with Vercel AI Gateway. This lets you use your existing provider accounts and access private resources.

contents.heading: bring-your-own-key-byok
contents.content: To set up BYOK, add your provider credentials in your Vercel team's AI Gateway settings. Once configured, AI Gateway automatically uses your credentials. No code changes are needed.

contents.heading: bring-your-own-key-byok
contents.content: For providers like Azure where you can use custom deployment names, you can configure model mappings to map gateway model slugs to your deployment names. See model mappings for details.

contents.heading: bring-your-own-key-byok
contents.content: Learn more in the BYOK documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can create language models using a provider instance. The first argument is the model ID in the format creator/model-name:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: AI Gateway language models can also be used in the streamText function and support structured data generation with Output (see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
When an upstream provider reports a well-formed error after streaming has
started, AI SDK Core exposes it as a
StreamProviderError.
Use its type, code, statusCode, and isRetryable metadata to classify
the failure without inspecting the Gateway's serialized error payload.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content: Batch support is experimental and the API may change in patch releases.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content:
AI Gateway supports durable text batches through experimental_startBatch,
experimental_getBatchStatus, experimental_getBatchResults, and experimental_cancelBatch. See
Batch for the provider-agnostic workflow,
and the AI Gateway batch processing guide
for supported models, limits, and Gateway-specific behavior.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content: Pass a publicly reachable HTTPS webhookUrl when starting a batch to receive a terminal notification instead of polling. AI Gateway sends batch.completed, batch.failed, or batch.cancelled. The event contains terminal status information but not batch results. Completion webhooks are an AI Gateway capability; direct Anthropic and OpenAI batch providers return an unsupported warning when this option is provided.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content: The signing secret is returned only in the start response. Reserve the callback token before submitting the batch, then persist the secret and minimal batch reference before the process exits. The stable providerOptions.gateway.idempotencyKey makes retrying an ambiguous start safe. Reuse the reserved token when retrying; do not generate a new one. Delete the reservation after a definitive start failure. While the reservation is still pending, the receiver should return a retryable response so an early delivery is sent again after setup completes.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content: The receiver must verify the x-ai-gateway-signature header against a bounded raw request body before trusting the event:

contents.heading: batch
contents.content: The signature header has the form t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex digest>, where v1 is the HMAC-SHA256 digest of "<t>.<raw body>". Verify a size-limited raw request body rather than a re-serialized object, use a timing-safe comparison, reject stale timestamps, and reject events whose data.jobId does not match the persisted batch.id.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content: AI Gateway expects a 2xx response within 10 seconds and retries failed deliveries. It does not follow redirects, so the callback endpoint itself must return the 2xx response. Retries carry the same x-ai-gateway-idempotency-key value (<jobId>-<status>), which receivers can use for deduplication. After verification, pass the persisted batch reference to experimental_getBatchStatus and experimental_getBatchResults. Delivery is best-effort, so periodically reconcile persisted batches by status as a fallback for a notification that exhausts its retries.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content:
Each request specifies its type and model. AI Gateway currently requires
every text request in a batch to use the same model and throws before submission
when the models differ.

contents.heading: cancelling-a-batch
contents.content: Pass the batch reference returned by experimental_startBatch to request cancellation:

contents.heading: cancelling-a-batch
contents.content: Cancellation is asynchronous. Continue checking experimental_getBatchStatus until the batch is terminal, then read experimental_getBatchResults for any partial results. A batch may finish before cancellation takes effect, and successful requests remain billable. Cancellation returns acknowledgement metadata, not confirmation that provider execution has stopped.

contents.heading: reranking-models
contents.content: You can create reranking models using the rerankingModel method on the provider instance:

contents.heading: reranking-models
contents.content: Reranking models are useful for improving search results in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines by re-scoring candidate documents after an initial retrieval step.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content: Realtime support is experimental and the API may change in patch releases.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content: You can create realtime models for bidirectional audio/text WebSocket sessions using the experimental_realtime method on the provider instance. The first argument is the model ID in the format creator/model-name:

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content: The Gateway normalizes realtime the same way it normalizes every other modality: your client speaks the normalized AI SDK realtime protocol and the Gateway translates to and from the upstream provider server-side. This means the same client code works regardless of which provider backs the model.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content: Realtime sessions run in the browser and require a short-lived Gateway client secret created on your server with gateway.experimental_realtime.getToken(). The method uses your Gateway credential (apiKey, AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, or Vercel OIDC token) to mint a vcst_ client secret and returns the WebSocket URL for the model.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
Use the matching Gateway realtime model in the browser. Creating the model is
safe in browser code; only getToken() is server-side.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
Do not expose your Gateway API key or OIDC token to browser clients. Only return
the short-lived setup response from getToken().

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
The Gateway WebSocket route transports the short-lived auth token via the
versioned Sec-WebSocket-Protocol subprotocol and the model id via the
?ai-model-id= query - the WebSocket transport of the Authorization and
ai-model-id headers the HTTP routes use. Subprotocol values must fit the
WebSocket token grammar, and the complete Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header
should stay compact (under an 8 KiB safe header budget).

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Gateway provider options — tags, user, byok, compliance flags, and so on — are set under providerOptions.gateway in the session configuration, mirroring how they ride the request body on the non-realtime routes. Include them in the session configuration you send to the Gateway, and the Gateway applies them server-side:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The GatewayProviderOptions type is exported from @ai-sdk/gateway for stable client-facing fields. The type also accepts service-owned option keys so the Gateway service can add or change server-side options without requiring an SDK release for every schema change. Runtime validation is owned by the Gateway service.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Provider options are sent in the initial session update after the socket
opens, so connect-time options such as byok and quota selection require a
Gateway that resolves them from that update. Routing knobs like order /
only do not apply to realtime, where the Gateway selects the
WebSocket-capable provider.

contents.heading: available-models
contents.content: The AI Gateway supports models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI, Mistral, DeepSeek, Amazon Bedrock, Cohere, Perplexity, Alibaba, and other providers.

contents.heading: available-models
contents.content: For the complete list of available models, see the AI Gateway documentation.

contents.heading: dynamic-model-discovery
contents.content: You can discover available models programmatically:

contents.heading: credit-usage
contents.content: You can check your team's current credit balance and usage:

contents.heading: credit-usage
contents.content: The getCredits() method returns your team's credit information based on the authenticated API key or OIDC token:

contents.heading: credit-usage
contents.content: balance number - Your team's current available credit balance

contents.heading: credit-usage
contents.content: total_used number - Total credits consumed by your team

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: Look up detailed information about a specific generation by its ID, including cost, token usage, latency, and provider details. Generation IDs are available in providerMetadata.gateway.generationId on both generateText and streamText responses.

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: When streaming, the generation ID is injected on the first content chunk, so you can capture it early in the stream without waiting for completion. This is especially useful in cases where a network interruption or mid-stream error could prevent you from receiving the final response — since the gateway records the final status server-side, you can use the generation ID to look up the results (including cost, token usage, and finish reason) later via getGenerationInfo().

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: With streamText, you can capture the generation ID from the first chunk via stream:

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content:
You can also capture the generation ID for every completed model call with
onLanguageModelCallEnd. The callback runs before client-side tools execute,
so the metadata remains available even if the operation is later aborted while
a tool is running:

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: The getGenerationInfo() method accepts:

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: id string - The generation ID to look up (format: gen_<ulid>, required)

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: It returns a GatewayGenerationInfo object with the following fields:

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: id string - The generation ID

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: totalCost number - Total cost in USD

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: upstreamInferenceCost number - Upstream inference cost in USD (relevant for BYOK)

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: usage number - Usage cost in USD (same as totalCost)

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: createdAt string - ISO 8601 timestamp when the generation was created

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: model string - Model identifier used

contents.heading: generation-lookup

contents.heading: provider-executed-tools
contents.content: Some providers offer tools that are executed by the provider itself, such as OpenAI's web search tool. To use these tools through AI Gateway, import the provider to access the tool definitions:

contents.heading: provider-executed-tools
contents.content:
Some provider-executed tools require account-specific configuration (such as
Claude Agent Skills) and may not work through AI Gateway. To use these tools,
you must bring your own key (BYOK) directly to the provider.

contents.heading: gateway-tools
contents.content: The AI Gateway provider includes built-in tools that are executed by the gateway itself. These tools can be used with any model through the gateway.

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: The Perplexity Search tool enables models to search the web using Perplexity's search API. This tool is executed by the AI Gateway and returns web search results that the model can use to provide up-to-date information.

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: You can also configure the search with optional parameters:

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: The Perplexity Search tool supports the following optional configuration options:

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: maxResults number

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: The maximum number of search results to return (1-20, default: 10).

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: maxTokensPerPage number

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: The maximum number of tokens to extract per search result page (256-2048, default: 2048).

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: maxTokens number

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: The maximum total tokens across all search results (default: 25000, max: 1000000).

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: searchLanguageFilter string[]

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: Filter search results by language using ISO 639-1 language codes (e.g., ['en'] for English, ['en', 'es'] for English and Spanish).

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: country string

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: Filter search results by country using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (e.g., 'US' for United States, 'GB' for United Kingdom).

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: searchDomainFilter string[]

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: Limit search results to specific domains (e.g., ['reuters.com', 'bbc.com']). This is useful for restricting results to trusted sources.

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: searchRecencyFilter 'day' | 'week' | 'month' | 'year'

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: Filter search results by relative time period. Useful for always getting recent results (e.g., 'week' for results from the last week).

contents.heading: perplexity-search
contents.content: The tool works with both generateText and streamText:

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: The Exa Search tool enables models to search the web using Exa's Search API. This tool is executed by the AI Gateway and returns token-efficient web excerpts for agent workflows.

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: You can also configure the search with optional parameters:

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: The Exa Search tool supports the following optional configuration options:

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: type 'auto' | 'fast' | 'instant'

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: Search mode. 'auto' is the default balance of speed and quality.

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: numResults number

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: Maximum number of results to return (1-100, default: 10).

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: category 'company' | 'people' | 'research paper' | 'news' | 'personal site' | 'financial report'

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: Focus results on a specific content type.

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: includeDomains / excludeDomains string[]

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: Restrict or exclude search results by domain.

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: startPublishedDate / endPublishedDate string

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: Filter results by ISO 8601 publication date.

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: contents object

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: Control result extraction and freshness:

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: text - Return full page text, optionally capped with maxCharacters

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: highlights - Return token-efficient excerpts

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: maxAgeHours - Control cached content freshness

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: livecrawlTimeout - Livecrawl timeout in milliseconds

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: subpages / subpageTarget - Crawl related subpages

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: extras.links / extras.imageLinks - Extract links from pages

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content: The tool works with both generateText and streamText.

contents.heading: exa-search
contents.content:
This initial Gateway integration supports Exa's plain Search modes and
token-efficient content controls. Deep synthesis modes and generated summaries
are intentionally not exposed yet because they have separate pricing from
standard Search.

contents.heading: browserbase-search
contents.content: The Browserbase Search tool enables models to search the web using Browserbase's Search API. It is executed by AI Gateway and returns fast, structured search results without opening a browser session.

contents.heading: browserbase-search
contents.content: You can configure the maximum number of results returned by each search:

contents.heading: browserbase-search
contents.content: The Browserbase Search tool supports this optional configuration option:

contents.heading: browserbase-search
contents.content: numResults number

contents.heading: browserbase-search
contents.content: Maximum number of search results to return (1-25, default: 10).

contents.heading: browserbase-search
contents.content: The tool works with both generateText and streamText.

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: The Browserbase Fetch tool enables models to retrieve page content using Browserbase's Fetch API. It is a lightweight option for pages that do not require JavaScript execution or browser interaction, and it supports raw, Markdown, and schema-driven JSON output.

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: You can configure the output format and request behavior. For example, use JSON extraction to return content matching a JSON Schema:

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: The Browserbase Fetch tool supports these optional configuration options:

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: format 'raw' | 'markdown' | 'json'

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: Output format for the fetched content. raw returns the upstream response body unchanged and is the default. markdown converts the page to Markdown. json performs structured extraction and requires schema.

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: schema object

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: JSON Schema describing the desired structured content. Only used when format is json.

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: allowRedirects boolean

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: Follow HTTP redirects. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: proxies boolean

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: Route the request through Browserbase's proxy network. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: allowInsecureSsl boolean

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: Bypass TLS certificate verification. Defaults to false; only enable it for trusted hosts.

contents.heading: browserbase-fetch
contents.content: The Fetch API does not execute JavaScript. Use a browser session for interactive or JavaScript-rendered pages. The tool works with both generateText and streamText.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: The Tako Search tool enables models to search the web and Tako's curated knowledge graph in a single call using Tako's Search API. This tool is executed by the AI Gateway and returns token-efficient web excerpts, plus knowledge-graph results that carry structured data, premium source attribution, and an embed-ready visualization.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: Configure the search with effort, source selection, and localization defaults. These defaults override values the model includes in a tool call:

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: The Tako Search tool supports these optional configuration options:

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: effort 'fast' | 'instant' | 'deep' - Search effort. 'fast' is the balanced default, 'instant' favors cached low-latency results, and 'deep' broadens retrieval with reranking at higher cost and latency.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: sources object - Omit to search both curated Tako data and the live web. When set, only source keys present are searched.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: sources.web object - Configure web results:

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: count number - Maximum web results, 1-20.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: category 'finance' | 'news' | 'sports' - Restrict web results to one category.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: includeDomains / excludeDomains string[] - Only return, or drop, results from these bare domains. Up to 20 each.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: publishedAfter / publishedBefore string - Keep results published on or after, or on or before, this YYYY-MM-DD date.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: snippetMaxChars number - Character cap on each result's text excerpt. Defaults to 4,000; maximum 20,000.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: highlights boolean - Return query-relevant passages as each result's snippet instead of the opening text of the page. The snippet can hold multiple passages joined by ' ... ', and a page with no highlight returns snippet: null. Defaults to true in the AI Gateway.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: includeContents boolean - Inline each page's extracted full text in content. articleContentMaxChars caps it, defaulting to 30,000 characters (maximum 1,000,000).

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: sources.data object - Configure data results:

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: count number - Maximum data results, 1-20. Defaults to 5.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: includeContents boolean - Inline each card's underlying rows in content.dataset as typed, unit-labeled columns. This adds a data surcharge based on the row count and dataset source. To estimate cost, first search with includeContents: false and inspect cards.content.export_pricing. Because this applies to every returned card, use count and maxRows to control cost.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: contentFormat 'json_compact' | 'json_records' | 'csv' | 'card_json' - Serialization for inlined card data. Defaults to 'json_compact'.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: maxRows number - Row cap per result. Omit to use the allowance in cards.content.export_pricing. A data surcharge applies per 1,000 exported rows; lower values reduce cost.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: nodeIds string[] - Data Graph node IDs to prioritize. Up to 20.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: strict boolean - Only return cards matching nodeIds. Requires at least one nodeIds value.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: location object - End-user { latitude, longitude } coordinates for localized results.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: countryCode string - ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as 'US'.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: locale string - BCP-47 locale, such as 'en-US'.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: timezone string - IANA timezone, such as 'America/New_York'.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: outputSettings object - Card rendering controls. forceRefresh is available only with 'instant' effort.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: includeRelated number - Number of related search suggestions to include (1-20).

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: For precise entity matching, quote a phrase in the query and optionally append a label: "Tesla":PRODUCT price. Tako treats the quoted phrase as one entity before searching.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: The tool works with both generateText and streamText:

contents.heading: parallel-search
contents.content: The Parallel Search tool enables models to search the web using Parallel AI's Search API. This tool is optimized for LLM consumption, returning relevant excerpts from web pages that can replace multiple keyword searches with a single call.

contents.heading: parallel-search

contents.heading: parallel-search

contents.heading: parallel-search

contents.heading: parallel-search

contents.heading: parallel-search

contents.heading: parallel-search
