During streaming, each Anthropic message_start event is exposed as an
anthropic.message_start custom stream part containing the message ID, model,
and raw initial token usage. No provider option is required.

contents.heading: message-start-events
contents.content:
Initial usage may be incomplete; use result.usage for final token counts.
Like other custom parts, this event is included in response content and forwarded
to UI message streams. It is ignored when replaying conversation history to Anthropic.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Anthropic models:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: disableParallelToolUse boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Optional. Disables the use of parallel tool calls. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: When set to true, the model will only call one tool at a time instead of potentially calling multiple tools in parallel.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: sendReasoning boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Optional. Include reasoning content in requests sent to the model. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
If you are experiencing issues with the model handling requests involving
reasoning content, you can set this to false to omit them from the request.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: effort "low" | "medium" | "high" | "xhigh" | "max"

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Optional. See Effort section for more details.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: taskBudget object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Optional. See Task Budgets section for more details.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: speed "fast" | "standard"

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Optional. See Fast Mode section for more details.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: inferenceGeo "us" | "global"

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Optional. See Data Residency section for more details.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinking object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Optional. See Reasoning section for more details.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: toolStreaming boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Whether to enable tool streaming (and structured output streaming). Default to true.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: structuredOutputMode "outputFormat" | "jsonTool" | "auto"

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Determines how structured outputs are generated. Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: "outputFormat": Use the output_format parameter to specify the structured output format.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: "jsonTool": Use a special "json" tool to specify the structured output format.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: "auto": Use "outputFormat" when supported, otherwise fall back to "jsonTool" (default).

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: metadata object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Optional. Metadata to include with the request. See the Anthropic API documentation for details.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: userId string - An external identifier for the end-user. Should be a UUID, hash, or other opaque identifier. Must not contain PII.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content: Batch support is experimental and the API may change in patch releases.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content:
Anthropic language models support asynchronous text generation through the
Message Batches API.
Pass the Anthropic provider to the AI SDK's Batch
API for the complete workflow, including polling, persistence, and result handling.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content:
Each request specifies its type and model. Anthropic supports using
different text models within the same batch.

contents.heading: batch-limitations
contents.content:
Anthropic Message Batches do not support the speed option or completion
webhooks. Explicit anthropicBeta values must be configured when starting the
batch rather than on an individual request. When you provide a webhookUrl,
the provider returns an unsupported warning and starts the batch without a
webhook.

contents.heading: structured-outputs-and-tool-input-streaming
contents.content:
Tool call streaming is enabled by default. You can opt out by setting the
toolStreaming provider option to false.

contents.heading: structured-outputs-and-tool-input-streaming
contents.content:
For claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5, and claude-fable-5-1, the
default "auto" mode uses native structured outputs through
output_config.format. These models reject forced tool use, so the
"jsonTool" mode cannot be used with them. If you
request "jsonTool" anyway, the provider falls back to "outputFormat" and
emits a warning. Likewise, a required or named toolChoice is downgraded to
auto with a warning; instruct the model to use the tool in your prompt and
verify that a tool call was made.

contents.heading: effort
contents.content: Anthropic introduced an effort option with claude-opus-4-5 that affects thinking, text responses, and function calls. Effort defaults to high and you can set it to medium or low to save tokens and to lower time-to-last-token latency (TTLT). claude-opus-4-7, claude-opus-4-8, claude-opus-5, claude-opus-5-5, claude-fable-5, claude-fable-5-1, claude-sonnet-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, and claude-haiku-5-5 additionally support xhigh for maximum reasoning effort.

contents.heading: effort
contents.content: On claude-opus-5 and claude-haiku-5-5, thinking can only be disabled at effort levels up to and including high. When you combine thinking: { type: 'disabled' } with effort: 'xhigh' or effort: 'max', the AI SDK lowers the effort to high and emits a warning instead of sending a request that the API would reject.

contents.heading: effort
contents.content:
claude-haiku-5-5 is the first Haiku model with effort levels and supports all
five of them. It uses adaptive thinking and does not support thinking token
budgets: the AI SDK converts thinking: { type: 'enabled', budgetTokens } to
{ type: 'adaptive' } and emits a warning. Use effort to control how much it
thinks. Unlike claude-sonnet-5-5, thinking can still be turned off with
thinking: { type: 'disabled' }, but only at low, medium, and high effort.
Start at medium effort and test other levels rather than carrying over the
settings you used on claude-haiku-4-5.

contents.heading: effort
contents.content:
On claude-opus-5-5, thinking is always adaptive and cannot be disabled, so
effort is the main control for latency and cost. The API default effort for
claude-opus-5-5 is medium. Start there and test other levels rather than
carrying over the setting you used on claude-opus-5. Set maxOutputTokens
with room for thinking as well as the reply; thinking counts toward the limit
even when its content is not returned.

contents.heading: effort
contents.content:
On claude-sonnet-5-5, thinking cannot be turned off either, and the API
default effort is high. Its effort levels are not equivalent to those of
claude-sonnet-5, so test several levels rather than carrying over your
current setting. For agentic coding and other multi-step tool use, start at
medium for well-specified tasks and move to high for harder ones. The
lowest thinking setting, between_tools, is only
accepted at low, medium, and high effort. When you combine it with
effort: 'xhigh' or effort: 'max', the AI SDK lowers the effort to high
and emits a warning.

contents.heading: fast-mode
contents.content: Anthropic supports a speed option for claude-opus-4-6 that enables faster inference with approximately 2.5x faster output token speeds.

contents.heading: fast-mode
contents.content: The speed option accepts 'fast' or 'standard' (default behavior).

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: claude-opus-4-7 supports a taskBudget option that informs the model of the total token budget available for an agentic turn. The model uses this information to prioritize work, plan ahead, and wind down gracefully as the budget is consumed.

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: Task budgets are advisory — they do not enforce a hard token limit. The model will attempt to stay within budget, but actual usage may vary.

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: For long-running agents that compact and restart context, you can carry the remaining budget forward using the remaining field:

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: The taskBudget object accepts:

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: type "tokens" - Budget type. Currently only "tokens" is supported.

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: total number - Total task budget for the agentic turn. Minimum 20,000.

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: remaining number - Budget left after prior compacted-away contexts. Must be between 0 and total. Defaults to total if omitted.

contents.heading: data-residency
contents.content: Anthropic supports an inferenceGeo option that controls where model inference runs for a request.

contents.heading: data-residency
contents.content: The inferenceGeo option accepts 'us' (US-only infrastructure) or 'global' (default, any available geography).

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: Claude Fable 5 has safeguards that limit its performance in certain areas like cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry, and automated safety checks are run on every request.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: Claude Haiku 5.5 has the same biology safeguards as Claude Sonnet 5 and 5.5, plus safeguards that prevent cyber misuse.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: Claude Sonnet 5.5 also has safety classifiers enabled, including for cybersecurity, biology, and reasoning extraction. Requests that ask the model to reproduce its internal reasoning in the response text can be declined with the reasoning_extraction category; use thinking: { type: 'adaptive', display: 'summarized' } and read the reasoning parts instead.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: When one of these checks blocks a request, the API does not answer it. Instead it returns a classifier block: a 200 response with a refusal stop reason and an optional stop_details object describing the category that triggered the block. The AI SDK surfaces this as a content-filter finish reason, with the details available on providerMetadata.anthropic.stopDetails.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: A classifier block looks like this:

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: Branch on the finish reason rather than on the presence of stop_details — the API may return a refusal with no details at all.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: To avoid receiving a classifier block, pass the fallbacks option. When the primary model's classifiers block a turn, the API automatically retries it server-side on a fallback model and returns that model's answer. The required beta header is added for you.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: The recommended configuration is fallbacks: 'default', which lets the API route the retry to Anthropic's recommended fallback model based on the refusal category and removes the need to migrate when a fallback model is deprecated:

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: You can also pin an explicit fallback chain:

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: Each fallback entry requires a model and may additionally override max_tokens, thinking, output_config, and speed for that attempt only.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: When a fallback serves the turn, it is recorded in the per-model usage breakdown (usage.iterations) as a fallback_message entry. The AI SDK exposes this breakdown on providerMetadata.anthropic.iterations, so you can detect whether a fallback ran:

contents.heading: dangerous-tool-use-safeguard
contents.content: The safeguards option asks the API to run additional server-side checks as part of the request. The dangerous_tool_use safeguard classifies every tool_use block in the response for dangerous actions, such as destructive shell commands or data exfiltration, and returns a verdict per tool call. This is the check that Claude Code's auto mode relies on. The dangerous-tool-use-2026-09-03 beta header is added for you.

contents.heading: dangerous-tool-use-safeguard
contents.content: The verdicts are available on providerMetadata.anthropic.safeguardResults, one entry per requested safeguard, in the API's wire shape:

contents.heading: dangerous-tool-use-safeguard
contents.content: status.type is available when the classifier ran; unsupported means the API key is not enabled for the beta. Inside status.tool_uses, each tool call id maps to evaluated (with an outcome of not_flagged or flagged, the latter with an explanation such as [Data Exfiltration]), skipped, or unavailable (a transient classifier failure). When streaming, the verdicts arrive on the final message_delta event and are exposed on the finish part's provider metadata.

contents.heading: dangerous-tool-use-safeguard
contents.content: Anthropic's platform reference does not document the beta yet; the feature is described from the client side in the Claude Code auto mode classifier and gateway compatibility guides.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Anthropic models support extended thinking, where Claude shows its reasoning process before providing a final answer.

contents.heading: adaptive-thinking
contents.content:
For newer models (claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-6, and later), use adaptive thinking.
Claude automatically determines how much reasoning to use based on the complexity of the prompt.

contents.heading: adaptive-thinking
contents.content: You can combine adaptive thinking with the effort option to control how much reasoning Claude uses:

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content:
claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5, claude-fable-5, and
claude-fable-5-1 always run adaptive thinking. The API rejects
thinking: { type: 'disabled' } and budget-based
thinking: { type: 'enabled' } for these models. To keep existing code
working, the provider:

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content: removes thinking: { type: 'disabled' } and emits a warning,

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content: converts thinking: { type: 'enabled', budgetTokens } to { type: 'adaptive' } and emits a warning,

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content: maps the top-level reasoning: 'none' option to effort: 'low' and emits a warning.

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content:
On claude-sonnet-5-5, which supports
between_tools thinking, the provider instead
replaces thinking: { type: 'disabled' } with thinking: { type: 'between_tools' }
(with a warning) and maps reasoning: 'none' to between_tools thinking.

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content:
Use effort to control how much these models think. On claude-opus-5-5, set
effort: 'low' when time to first token matters, and move to medium if
quality drops:

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content:
Responses from adaptive-only models can begin with a thinking block. Read the
response by content type (text, reasoning, tool-call) rather than
assuming the first part is text. Under the default display: 'omitted'
setting, thinking blocks are returned with empty text.

contents.heading: between-tools-thinking
contents.content:
claude-sonnet-5-5 supports thinking: { type: 'between_tools' }, its lowest
thinking setting. The model does no upfront thinking, but the short progress
notes it writes between tool calls are still returned as thinking blocks, each
with a short summary. They are available as reasoning parts and are sent back
unchanged on the next step. between_tools accepts no other thinking options
(such as display or blockBinding) and is only accepted at low, medium,
and high effort. Per-message effort changes via
mid-conversation system messages are not
supported with between_tools.

contents.heading: thinking-display-opus-47
contents.content: Starting with claude-opus-4-7, thinking content is omitted from the response by default — thinking blocks are present in the stream but their text is empty. To receive reasoning output, set display: 'summarized':

contents.heading: thinking-display-opus-47
contents.content:
If you stream reasoning to users with claude-opus-4-7, the default
"omitted" display will cause a long pause before output begins. Set
display: "summarized" to restore visible progress during thinking.

contents.heading: thinking-updates
contents.content:
Use display: 'updates' with claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5, or
claude-fable-5-1 to stream thinking summaries between tool calls. These models
return progress notes between tool calls as thinking blocks rather than text, so
without this setting a long tool-calling turn can look silent. The provider adds
the required thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18 beta header automatically:

contents.heading: thinking-binding-controls
contents.content:
Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, and Sonnet 5.5 can recover from a thinking-block prefix
mismatch by dropping the mismatched block. Set
blockBinding.prefixMismatchBehavior to drop_block, or set it to error to
reject the request. You can provide block binding by itself to preserve the
model's default thinking mode, or combine it with adaptive thinking. Block
binding is not available with between_tools thinking; keep the message
history append-only instead.

contents.heading: thinking-binding-controls
contents.content:
Dropped blocks are reported in
providerMetadata.anthropic.inputTransformations with their type, path, and
reason.

contents.heading: budget-based-thinking
contents.content:
For earlier models (claude-opus-4-20250514, claude-sonnet-4-20250514, claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929),
use type: 'enabled' with an explicit token budget:

contents.heading: budget-based-thinking
contents.content:
Anthropic's max_tokens limit includes both thinking and final text. To reserve
room for both, the provider adds budgetTokens to maxOutputTokens when
setting max_tokens. For known models, the combined value is capped at the
model's maximum output token limit.

contents.heading: budget-based-thinking
contents.content:
See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details
on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: context-management
contents.content: Anthropic's Context Management feature allows you to automatically manage conversation context by clearing tool uses or thinking content when certain conditions are met. This helps optimize token usage and manage long conversations more efficiently.

contents.heading: context-management
contents.content: You can configure context management using the contextManagement provider option:

contents.heading: context-editing
contents.content: Context editing strategies selectively remove specific content types from earlier in the conversation to reduce token usage without losing the overall conversation flow.

contents.heading: clear-tool-uses
contents.content: The clear_tool_uses_20250919 edit type removes old tool call/result pairs from the conversation history:

contents.heading: clear-tool-uses
contents.content: trigger - Condition that triggers the clearing (e.g., { type: 'input_tokens', value: 10000 } or { type: 'tool_uses', value: 10 })

contents.heading: clear-tool-uses
contents.content: keep - How many recent tool uses to preserve (e.g., { type: 'tool_uses', value: 5 })

contents.heading: clear-tool-uses
contents.content: clearAtLeast - Minimum amount to clear (e.g., { type: 'input_tokens', value: 1000 })

contents.heading: clear-tool-uses
contents.content: clearToolInputs - Whether to clear tool input parameters (boolean)

contents.heading: clear-tool-uses
contents.content: excludeTools - Array of tool names to never clear

contents.heading: clear-thinking
contents.content: The clear_thinking_20251015 edit type removes thinking/reasoning blocks from earlier turns, keeping only the most recent ones:

contents.heading: clear-thinking
contents.content: keep - How many recent thinking turns to preserve (e.g., { type: 'thinking_turns', value: 2 }) or 'all' to keep everything

contents.heading: on-demand-compaction
contents.content:
Use the compaction provider option to ask Anthropic to summarize the supplied
conversation immediately. The provider automatically adds the
compact-2026-09-04 beta header.

contents.heading: on-demand-compaction
contents.content:
Anthropic returns the summary as a text part whose
providerMetadata.anthropic.type is compaction. Its opaque signature is
available as providerMetadata.anthropic.signature. Response messages copy
that metadata to providerOptions, so passing
summary.finalStep.response.messages back to the AI SDK preserves the signed
block and automatically adds the beta header on the continuation request.

contents.heading: on-demand-compaction
contents.content:
Check rawFinishReason before reading the response block. Anthropic can return
a successful HTTP response without a summary when summarization ends for
another reason, such as max_tokens, model_context_window_exceeded,
tool_use, refusal, or end_turn. In that case, keep the existing history
and retry later; the unsuccessful summarization is still included in
providerMetadata.anthropic.iterations.

contents.heading: on-demand-compaction
contents.content:
Send exactly one signed compaction block on continuation requests. It must be
the first content block in messages and must be replayed without changing its
text or signature. Remove the messages it summarizes before continuing. Keep
the same system prompt and tool definitions on the compaction request that you
use for the conversation, especially when preserving later thinking blocks.

contents.heading: on-demand-compaction
contents.content:
Before requesting compaction, resolve any unfinished tool call from the last
assistant turn. Do not combine compaction with contextManagement,
stopSequences, structured output, a required or named toolChoice, or a
taskBudget.remaining value. Also omit taskBudget.remaining from later
requests that carry the signed block.

contents.heading: on-demand-compaction
contents.content:
On-demand compaction usage is reported in
providerMetadata.anthropic.iterations. Sum the iteration usage when
calculating the tokens consumed by the summarization request.

contents.heading: on-demand-compaction
contents.content:
On-demand compaction can also be initiated in a Message Batch. Configure the
compaction provider option on the individual batch request; the provider
automatically adds compact-2026-09-04 to the batch beta header.

contents.heading: on-demand-compaction
contents.content:
For more details, see
Anthropic's on-demand compaction documentation.

contents.heading: threshold-compaction
contents.content: The compact_20260112 edit type automatically summarizes earlier conversation context when token limits are reached. This is useful for long-running conversations where you want to preserve the essence of earlier exchanges while staying within token limits.

contents.heading: threshold-compaction
contents.content: Configuration:

contents.heading: threshold-compaction
contents.content: trigger - Condition that triggers compaction (e.g., { type: 'input_tokens', value: 50000 })

contents.heading: threshold-compaction
contents.content: instructions - Custom instructions for how the model should summarize the conversation. Use this to guide the compaction summary towards specific aspects of the conversation you want to preserve.

contents.heading: threshold-compaction
contents.content: pauseAfterCompaction - When true, the model will pause after generating the compaction summary, allowing you to inspect or process it before continuing. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: threshold-compaction
contents.content: When compaction occurs, the model generates a summary of the earlier context. This summary appears as a text block with special provider metadata.

contents.heading: detecting-compaction-in-streams
contents.content: When using streamText, you can detect compaction summaries by checking the providerMetadata on text-start events:

contents.heading: compaction-in-ui-applications
contents.content: When using useChat or other UI hooks, compaction summaries appear as regular text parts with providerMetadata. You can style them differently in your UI:

contents.heading: applied-edits-metadata
contents.content: After generation, you can check which edits were applied in the provider metadata:

contents.heading: applied-edits-metadata
contents.content: For more details, see Anthropic's Context Management documentation.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content:
In the messages and message parts, you can use the providerOptions property to set cache control breakpoints.
You need to set the anthropic property in the providerOptions object to { cacheControl: { type: 'ephemeral' } } to set a cache control breakpoint.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content:
Cache read and cache write (creation) token counts are returned on the standard
usage object for both generateText and streamText. You can access them at
result.usage.inputTokenDetails.cacheReadTokens and
result.usage.inputTokenDetails.cacheWriteTokens.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content: You can also use cache control on system messages by providing multiple system messages at the head of your messages array:

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content: Cache control for tools:

contents.heading: longer-cache-ttl
contents.content: Anthropic also supports a longer 1-hour cache duration.

contents.heading: longer-cache-ttl
contents.content: Here's an example:

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: The minimum cacheable prompt length is:

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: 4096 tokens for Claude Opus 4.5

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: 1024 tokens for Claude Opus 4.1, Claude Opus 4, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4, Claude Sonnet 3.7, and Claude Opus 3

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: 4096 tokens for Claude Haiku 4.5

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: 2048 tokens for Claude Haiku 3.5 and Claude Haiku 3

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: Shorter prompts cannot be cached, even if marked with cacheControl. Any requests to cache fewer than this number of tokens will be processed without caching.

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: For more on prompt caching with Anthropic, see Anthropic's Cache Control documentation.

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content:
Because the UIMessage type (used by AI SDK UI hooks like useChat) does not
support the providerOptions property, you can use convertToModelMessages
first before passing the messages to functions like generateText or
streamText. For more details on providerOptions usage, see
here.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content:
The Bash Tool allows running bash commands. By default, the tool executes
commands through the experimental_sandbox that you pass to generateText or streamText:

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: command (string): The bash command to run. Required unless the tool is being restarted.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: restart (boolean, optional): Specifying true will restart this tool.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content:
Two versions are available: bash_20250124 (recommended) and bash_20241022.
Only certain Claude versions are supported.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content:
You can also provide a custom execute function when you want to handle bash
execution directly instead of using the request experimental sandbox.

contents.heading: memory-tool
contents.content:
The Memory Tool allows Claude to use a local memory, e.g. in the filesystem.
Here's how to create it:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: The Text Editor Tool provides functionality for viewing and editing text files.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: Different models support different versions of the tool:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: textEditor_20250728 - For Claude Sonnet 4, Opus 4, and Opus 4.1 (recommended)

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: textEditor_20250124 - For Claude Sonnet 3.7

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: textEditor_20241022 - For Claude Sonnet 3.5

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: Note: textEditor_20250429 is deprecated. Use textEditor_20250728 instead.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: command ('view' | 'create' | 'str_replace' | 'insert' | 'undo_edit'): The command to run. Note: undo_edit is only available in Claude 3.5 Sonnet and earlier models.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: path (string): Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. /repo/file.py or /repo.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: file_text (string, optional): Required for create command, with the content of the file to be created.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: insert_line (number, optional): Required for insert command. The line number after which to insert the new string.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: new_str (string, optional): New string for str_replace command.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: insert_text (string, optional): Required for insert command, containing the text to insert.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: old_str (string, optional): Required for str_replace command, containing the string to replace.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: view_range (number[], optional): Optional for view command to specify line range to show.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: The Computer Tool enables control of keyboard and mouse actions on a computer:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content:
Use computerToolset_20260801 for Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 (required),
Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Fable 5.1, and Opus 4.8. Use computer_20251124
for Claude Opus 4.5 through Opus 4.7, which support the zoom action. Use
computer_20250124 for Claude Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.1, Sonnet 4, Opus
4, and Sonnet 3.7.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content:
Newer models use the computer toolset instead of a versioned computer tool.
claude-sonnet-5-5 and claude-opus-5-5 accept computer use only through the
toolset and reject the older computer_* tool types with a 400. The toolset
does not require a beta header and has no display size parameters: coordinates
are always in the pixel space of the screenshots you return. Zoom is enabled by default, and Claude can
return several actions in one turn, each as its own tool call.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content:
The API returns each action as a separate tool_use block with
toolset_name: 'computer'. The AI SDK maps every action to the toolset tool and
passes the action name as action, so execute receives the same input shape
as the older computer tools:

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: action ('screenshot' | 'zoom' | 'left_click' | 'right_click' | 'middle_click' | 'double_click' | 'triple_click' | 'left_click_drag' | 'mouse_move' | 'left_mouse_down' | 'left_mouse_up' | 'cursor_position' | 'scroll' | 'type' | 'key' | 'hold_key' | 'wait'): The member tool that Claude invoked.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: coordinate (number[], optional): The (x, y) pixel coordinates for click, move, and scroll actions.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: start_coordinate (number[], optional): Where a left_click_drag starts.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: region (number[], optional): [x1, y1, x2, y2] for the zoom action.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: text (string, optional): Text to type, the key combination for key and hold_key, or modifier keys to hold during click and scroll actions.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: repeat (number, optional): How many times to press the key for key.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: duration (number, optional): Seconds for hold_key and wait.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: scroll_direction ('up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right', optional) and scroll_amount (number, optional): For the scroll action.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: configs (object, optional): Per-action settings keyed by action name. Each entry accepts enabled (default true) and deferLoading (default false, for tool search).

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content:
Tool calls and results of the toolset are serialized with toolset_name when
you pass the message history back. Keep the toolset tool in tools on
follow-up requests, or the provider falls back to the toolsetName provider
metadata on the tool calls of previous responses. Do not declare the toolset
together with an older computer_* tool.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: action ('key' | 'type' | 'mouse_move' | 'left_click' | 'left_click_drag' | 'right_click' | 'middle_click' | 'double_click' | 'screenshot' | 'cursor_position' | 'zoom'): The action to perform. For versioned computer tools, the zoom action is only available with computer_20251124. It is also available with computerToolset_20260801, where it is enabled by default.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: coordinate (number[], optional): Required for mouse_move and left_click_drag actions. Specifies the (x, y) coordinates.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: text (string, optional): Required for type and key actions.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: region (number[], optional): Required for zoom action. Specifies [x1, y1, x2, y2] coordinates for the area to inspect.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: displayWidthPx (number): The width of the display in pixels.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: displayHeightPx (number): The height of the display in pixels.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: displayNumber (number, optional): The display number for X11 environments.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: enableZoom (boolean, optional): Enable the zoom action. Only available with computer_20251124. Default: false.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: Anthropic provides a provider-defined web search tool that gives Claude direct access to real-time web content, allowing it to answer questions with up-to-date information beyond its knowledge cutoff.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: You can enable web search using the provider-defined web search tool:

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content:
Web search must be enabled in your organization's Console
settings.

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content:
Use webSearch_20260318 for dynamic filtering and response inclusion control.
The older webSearch_20260209 and webSearch_20250305 versions remain
available for applications that need their earlier behavior.

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: The web search tool supports several configuration options:

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: maxUses number

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: Maximum number of web searches Claude can perform during the conversation.

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: allowedDomains string[]

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: Optional list of domains that Claude is allowed to search. If provided, searches will be restricted to these domains.

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: blockedDomains string[]

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: Optional list of domains that Claude should avoid when searching.

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: userLocation object

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: Optional user location information to provide geographically relevant search results.

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: responseInclusion 'full' | 'excluded'

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content:
Available with webSearch_20260318. Controls whether search result blocks
consumed by a completed code execution call in the same turn are included in
the API response. The default is 'full'. Use 'excluded' to omit those
nested call/result pairs and reduce output token usage.

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content:
responseInclusion: 'excluded' only omits results consumed by code execution
calls that complete in the same turn. Results from direct calls and from code
execution calls that pause before completing are always returned in full so
they can be sent back on the next turn.

contents.heading: web-fetch-tool
contents.content: Anthropic provides a provider-defined web fetch tool that allows Claude to retrieve content from specific URLs. This is useful when you want Claude to analyze or reference content from a particular webpage or document.

contents.heading: web-fetch-tool
contents.content: You can enable web fetch using the provider-defined web fetch tool:

contents.heading: advisor-tool
contents.content: Anthropic provides a provider-executed advisor tool that lets an executor model consult a stronger advisor model during generation. This is useful for long-running coding, research, and agentic tasks where a stronger model can provide planning or course correction while the main response is generated by a faster or lower-cost model.

contents.heading: advisor-tool
contents.content: You can enable the advisor tool using anthropic.tools.advisor_20260301:

contents.heading: advisor-tool
contents.content:
The AI SDK automatically sends the required advisor-tool-2026-03-01 beta
header when you include this tool.

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: The advisor tool supports the following configuration options:

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: model string

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: Required. The advisor model ID, such as claude-opus-4-8. The advisor model must be at least as capable as the executor model.

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: maxUses number

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: Optional. Maximum number of advisor calls allowed in a single request. Once the executor reaches this cap, further advisor calls return an advisor_tool_result_error with errorCode: 'max_uses_exceeded', and the executor continues without further advice.

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: maxTokens number

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: Optional. Maximum number of tokens the advisor can generate per call, including thinking and text. The minimum is 1024, and Anthropic recommends starting with 2048. This limit applies independently to each advisor call and is separate from the request-level maxOutputTokens, which controls executor output. Values above the selected advisor model's output limit result in an Anthropic 400 error. When configured, successful advisor results include stopReason; check for stopReason === 'max_tokens' to detect truncated advice. The field is available on both plaintext and redacted advisor result variants and is preserved across follow-up turns.

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: caching object

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: Optional. Enables prompt caching for the advisor's own transcript across calls within a conversation. Use { type: 'ephemeral', ttl: '5m' | '1h' }. This is most useful for longer agent loops where you expect at least three advisor calls.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: The advisor tool is provider-executed, so you do not provide an execute function. When the executor model calls advisor, Anthropic runs a separate server-side inference with the advisor model. The advisor sees the transcript and returns guidance to the executor, which then continues generating within the same request.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: The advisor tool input is always empty. Anthropic constructs the advisor's view from the full transcript automatically.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: For multi-turn conversations, pass the full assistant content, including advisor tool results, back on subsequent turns. If you remove the advisor tool from a later request, also remove previous advisor tool results from the message history; otherwise the Anthropic API returns an invalid request error.

contents.heading: streaming
contents.content: Advisor sub-inferences do not stream. When using streamText, the executor stream pauses while the advisor runs, then the advisor result arrives as a single tool result before executor output resumes.

contents.heading: tool-search
contents.content: Anthropic provides provider-defined tool search tools that enable Claude to work with hundreds or thousands of tools by dynamically discovering and loading them on-demand. Instead of loading all tool definitions into the context window upfront, Claude searches your tool catalog and loads only the tools it needs.

contents.heading: tool-search
contents.content: There are two variants:

contents.heading: tool-search
contents.content: BM25 Search - Uses natural language queries to find tools

contents.heading: tool-search
contents.content: Regex Search - Uses regex patterns (Python re.search() syntax) to find tools

contents.heading: using-regex-search
contents.content: For more precise tool matching, you can use the regex variant:

contents.heading: using-regex-search
contents.content: Claude will construct regex patterns like weather|temperature|forecast to find matching tools.

contents.heading: custom-tool-search
contents.content: You can implement your own tool search logic (e.g., using embeddings or semantic search) by returning tool-reference content blocks via toModelOutput:

contents.heading: custom-tool-search
contents.content: This sends tool_reference blocks to Anthropic, which loads the corresponding deferred tool schemas into Claude's context.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-system-controls
contents.content:
With claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5, and claude-fable-5-1, use an
empty system message to change effort from the next user turn. A separate
system message containing text can provide a turn-scoped reminder with
clearAt: 'next_user_message': its text applies until the next user message. Keep the reminder after a user turn and
before an assistant turn, or at the end of the messages array.
The provider adds the required
mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21 and
mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01 beta headers automatically.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-system-controls
contents.content:
An effort-only system message can use an empty content array at the API level;
in an AI SDK prompt, set content: ''. The provider serializes it as
content: []. These effort-only messages can appear first or later in the
conversation, including consecutively. The provider preserves their order. The new
level applies from the next user turn until a later message changes it.
Initial instruction text is sent in the top-level system field.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-system-controls
contents.content:
Consecutive inline system messages are evaluated as a group. If an effort-only
message is adjacent to a system message containing text, the whole group must
follow Anthropic's content placement rules.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-system-controls
contents.content:
Turn-scoped messages with clearAt support text only. Put effort updates in a
separate message, as in the example above.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-system-controls
contents.content:
clearAt applies only to mid-conversation system messages. On initial system
messages, the provider ignores clearAt and effort attached to non-empty
content and emits a warning. Use an empty system message for an initial
per-message effort setting, or the top-level effort provider option to
configure effort for the full request.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-tool-changes
contents.content: With claude-opus-4-8, you can add or remove tools between turns of a conversation without invalidating the prompt cache. Attach toolChanges to a system message that appears mid-conversation (right before an assistant message or at the end of the messages). The required mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01 beta header is added automatically.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-tool-changes
contents.content: Tools referenced by a tool_addition must be declared in the tools option — typically with deferLoading: true, so they are not loaded into context until the addition surfaces them. A tool_removal removes a previously available tool from the conversation going forward.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-tool-changes
contents.content: To change a tool's definition, remove the old definition at the end of one request, then carry the conversation forward with the updated definition in tools on the next request.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-tool-changes
contents.content:
Tool changes are not supported on the initial system message. The AI SDK
ignores them there and emits a warning — configure the initial tool set via
the tools option instead.

contents.heading: mcp-connectors
contents.content: Anthropic supports connecting to MCP servers as part of their execution.

contents.heading: mcp-connectors
contents.content: You can enable this feature with the mcpServers provider option:

contents.heading: mcp-connectors
contents.content: The tool calls and results are dynamic, i.e. the input and output schemas are not known.

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: The web fetch tool supports several configuration options:

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: maxUses number

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: The maxUses parameter limits the number of web fetches performed.

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: allowedDomains string[]

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: Only fetch from these domains.

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: blockedDomains string[]

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: Never fetch from these domains.

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: citations object

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: Unlike web search where citations are always enabled, citations are optional for web fetch. Set "citations": {"enabled": true} to enable Claude to cite specific passages from fetched documents.

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: maxContentTokens number

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: The maxContentTokens parameter limits the amount of content that will be included in the context.

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: useCache boolean

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content:
Available with webFetch_20260318. Set to false to bypass cached content
and fetch fresh content. The default is true; disabling the cache can
increase latency.

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content: responseInclusion 'full' | 'excluded'

contents.heading: configuration-options-2
contents.content:
Available with webFetch_20260318. Controls whether fetch result blocks
consumed by a completed code execution call in the same turn are included in
the API response. The default is 'full'. Direct results and results from
code execution calls that pause before completing are always returned in full.

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: Web search errors are handled differently depending on whether you're using streaming or non-streaming:

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content:
Non-streaming (generateText):
Web search errors throw exceptions that you can catch:

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content:
Streaming (streamText):
Web search errors are delivered as error parts in the stream:

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: Anthropic provides a provider-defined code execution tool that gives Claude direct access to a real Python environment allowing it to execute code to inform its responses.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: You can enable code execution using the provider-defined code execution tool:

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content:
Three versions are available: codeExecution_20260120 (recommended, does not
require a beta header, supports Claude Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 4.5, and
Opus 4.5), codeExecution_20250825 (supports Python and Bash with enhanced
file operations), and codeExecution_20250522 (supports Bash only).

contents.heading: uploading-files-for-code-execution
contents.content: You can upload files via the Files API and make them available inside the code execution sandbox. First upload the file, then reference it in your message using containerUpload: true in the provider options:

contents.heading: uploading-files-for-code-execution
contents.content: Supported file types include CSV, Excel, JSON, XML, images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP), and text files.

contents.heading: error-handling-1
contents.content: Code execution errors are handled differently depending on whether you're using streaming or non-streaming:

contents.heading: error-handling-1
contents.content:
Non-streaming (generateText):
Code execution errors are delivered as tool result parts in the response:

contents.heading: error-handling-1
contents.content:
Streaming (streamText):
Code execution errors are delivered as error parts in the stream:

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content: Programmatic Tool Calling allows Claude to write code that calls your tools programmatically within a code execution container, rather than requiring round trips through the model for each tool invocation. This reduces latency for multi-tool workflows and decreases token consumption.

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content: To enable programmatic tool calling, use the allowedCallers provider option on tools that you want to be callable from within code execution:

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content: In this flow:

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content: Claude writes Python code that calls your getWeather tool multiple times in parallel

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content: The SDK automatically executes your tool and returns results to the code execution container

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content: Claude processes the results in code and generates the final response

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content:
Programmatic tool calling requires claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-sonnet-4-5,
claude-opus-4-6, or claude-opus-4-5 models and uses the
code_execution_20260120 or code_execution_20250825 tool.

contents.heading: pruning-programmatic-tool-history
contents.content:
When pruning removes a code execution call but keeps a tool call that references
it through caller.toolId, the provider omits the dangling caller metadata from
history before a subsequent user message and emits a warning. The retained tool
calls and results are still sent to Anthropic; the removed code execution history
is not restored.

contents.heading: pruning-programmatic-tool-history
contents.content:
Tool-result messages do not end a turn. Caller metadata in an active tool
continuation is preserved, so keep the source code execution call when returning
programmatic tool results.

contents.heading: container-persistence
contents.content: When using programmatic tool calling across multiple steps, you need to preserve the container ID between steps using prepareStep. You can use the forwardAnthropicContainerIdFromLastStep helper function to do this automatically. The container ID is available in providerMetadata.anthropic.container.id after each step completes.

contents.heading: agent-skills
contents.content: Anthropic Agent Skills enable Claude to perform specialized tasks like document processing (PPTX, DOCX, PDF, XLSX) and data analysis. Skills run in a sandboxed container and require the code execution tool to be enabled.

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: Anthropic provides several built-in skills:

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: pptx - Create and edit PowerPoint presentations

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: docx - Create and edit Word documents

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: pdf - Process and analyze PDF files

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: xlsx - Work with Excel spreadsheets

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: To use skills, you need to:

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: Enable the code execution tool

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: Specify the container with skills in providerOptions

contents.heading: custom-skills
contents.content: You can also use custom skills by specifying type: 'custom':

contents.heading: custom-skills
contents.content:
Skills use progressive context loading and execute within a sandboxed
container with code execution capabilities.

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content:
Anthropic Claude models support reading PDF files.
You can pass PDF files as part of the message content using the file type:

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content: Option 1: URL-based PDF document

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content: Option 2: Base64-encoded PDF document

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content:
The model will have access to the contents of the PDF file and
respond to questions about it.
The PDF file should be passed using the data field,
and the mediaType should be set to 'application/pdf'.

contents.heading: decision-models
contents.content:
Create an experimental decision model with anthropic.decisionModel(modelId).
It uses the Messages API's structured-output support for Choice, Score, and Boolean
questions. claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 is one supported model.

contents.heading: decision-models
contents.content:
Choice labels are preserved exactly, and Scores are finite fractional positions
on the ordered rubric. Anthropic does not support numeric bounds in its native
output schema, so the adapter describes them in the prompt and validates them
after parsing. Invalid answers, refusals, and truncation fail the entire call.

contents.heading: decision-models
contents.content:
The adapter returns no probability distributions for Choice or Score. Boolean
answers contain prompted estimates of P(true), validated to be finite and in
[0, 1]. These estimates are not guaranteed to be calibrated. Apply thresholds
in application code, for example answers.requestsRefund.probability >= 0.5.
It respects
createAnthropic configuration and forwards providerOptions.anthropic, including
structuredOutputMode. Supported models use native structured output by default;
jsonTool uses the existing Messages JSON-tool fallback. Usage, warnings,
response information, and provider metadata are preserved.
See Decisions.

contents.heading: decision-models
contents.content:
Decision models can also be accessed through customProvider aliases or
createProviderRegistry().decisionModel('provider:model'). Direct string IDs
use Gateway by default, or an explicitly configured default provider with an
decisionModel method. See
model aliases and registries.

metadata.title: AssemblyAI
metadata.description: Learn how to use the AssemblyAI provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content: The AssemblyAI provider contains transcription model support for the AssemblyAI transcription API.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The AssemblyAI provider is available in the @ai-sdk/assemblyai module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance assemblyai from @ai-sdk/assemblyai:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createAssemblyAI from @ai-sdk/assemblyai and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the AssemblyAI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the AssemblyAI transcription API
using the .transcription() factory method.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id, e.g. universal-3-5-pro.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The best model is a deprecated legacy model, sent using AssemblyAI's
deprecated speech_model request parameter. It still works, but using it emits a
deprecation warning — prefer universal-3-5-pro. The older nano model has been
removed by AssemblyAI and is no longer available. All newer models are sent using
the speech_models
request parameter, which the provider selects automatically based on the model id.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
universal-3-pro and universal-2 are fully supported and continue to work, but
using them emits an informational warning (not a deprecation) suggesting
universal-3-5-pro, AssemblyAI's latest flagship model.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying the contentSafety option will enable content safety filtering.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: audioEndAt number

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
End time of the audio in milliseconds.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: audioStartFrom number

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Start time of the audio in milliseconds.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: autoChapters boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to automatically generate chapters for the transcription.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: autoHighlights boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to automatically generate highlights for the transcription.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: boostParam enum

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Boost parameter for wordBoost.
Allowed values: 'low', 'default', 'high'.
Deprecated — only applies to the deprecated wordBoost; use keytermsPrompt instead.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: contentSafety boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to enable content safety filtering.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: contentSafetyConfidence number

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Confidence threshold for content safety filtering (25-100).
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: customSpelling array of objects

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Custom spelling rules for the transcription.
Each object has from (array of strings) and to (string) properties.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: disfluencies boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to include disfluencies (um, uh, etc.) in the transcription.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: domain string

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Enable a domain-specific model for specialized terminology.
Currently supports 'medical-v1' (Medical Mode).

contents.heading: speaker-diarization-and-audio-intelligence-results
contents.content:
The AI SDK's transcribe result exposes text, segments, language, and
durationInSeconds. AssemblyAI's richer results — speaker diarization and
audio-intelligence features — don't fit that shape, so they are surfaced in two
places:

contents.heading: speaker-diarization-and-audio-intelligence-results
contents.content:
providerMetadata.assemblyai — structured results for the features you
enabled: utterances (speaker-diarized segments, when speakerLabels is set),
entities, sentimentAnalysisResults, contentSafetyLabels,
iabCategoriesResult, and autoHighlightsResult.

contents.heading: speaker-diarization-and-audio-intelligence-results
contents.content:
response.body — the complete, raw AssemblyAI transcript response, so any
field not surfaced above (e.g. chapters, word-level speaker labels) is
still available.

contents.heading: speaker-diarization-and-audio-intelligence-results
contents.content:
Note: timings inside providerMetadata and response.body (e.g.
utterances[].start) are in milliseconds, matching the AssemblyAI API —
whereas the top-level segments use seconds.

contents.heading: speaker-diarization-and-audio-intelligence-results
contents.content:
The following AssemblyAI features are deprecated by the API and not surfaced
in providerMetadata (their output remains on the raw response.body if
enabled): Summarization, Auto Chapters, and Custom Topics. Note also that some
features are language-gated (e.g. sentiment analysis is English-centric); see
AssemblyAI's documentation for per-language availability.
