contents.heading: image-input-options
contents.content: referenceImages string[]

contents.heading: image-input-options
contents.content:
Array of reference image URLs for multi-reference image-to-video generation.
The model extracts key features from each image and reproduces them in the
video. Use [Image 1], [Image 2], etc. in your prompt to reference
specific images.

contents.heading: media-reference-options
contents.content: referenceVideos string[]

contents.heading: media-reference-options
contents.content: Array of reference video URLs (up to 3 videos, max 15 seconds each) for reference-guided video generation. The model uses the referenced videos to guide style, motion, or composition. Supported by Seedance 2.0.

contents.heading: media-reference-options
contents.content: referenceAudio string[]

contents.heading: media-reference-options
contents.content: Array of reference audio URLs (up to 3, max 15 seconds each) for audio-guided video generation. The model uses the referenced audio as background music or synchronized sound. Supports data URIs (e.g., data:audio/wav;base64,...). Supported by Seedance 2.0.

contents.heading: polling-options
contents.content:
ByteDance video generation is task-based: the provider creates a task and the AI
SDK polls it until it completes. Configure polling with the top-level poll
option of generateVideo():

contents.heading: polling-options
contents.content:
The configured ByteDance API origin is trusted for the first status request,
while every redirect to another origin is validated before it is followed.

contents.heading: polling-options
contents.content:
The pollIntervalMs and pollTimeoutMs provider options are deprecated and
ignored. Passing either emits a warning. Video generation can take several
minutes, so raise poll.timeoutMs above the 10 minute default for long jobs.

contents.content: The Cerebras provider offers access to powerful language models through the Cerebras API, including their high-speed inference capabilities powered by Wafer-Scale Engines and CS-3 systems.
API keys can be obtained from the Cerebras Platform.

contents.heading: provider-options

contents.heading: provider-options

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Controls request priority. Availability depends on your account and endpoint.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'none' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Controls the amount of reasoning performed by supported models. Supported values and defaults depend on the model.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: reasoningFormat 'none' | 'parsed' | 'text_parsed' | 'raw' | 'hidden'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Controls how reasoning content appears in the response. Format support depends on the model.

contents.heading: provider-options

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Supplies predicted output that can accelerate requests where most of the response is already known.

contents.heading: provider-options

contents.heading: provider-options

contents.heading: provider-options

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Whether to use strict JSON schema validation. When true, the model uses constrained decoding to guarantee schema compliance. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: embedding-models

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: embeddingType 'float' | 'int8' | 'uint8' | 'binary' | 'ubinary'

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
Selects one embedding format per call. Defaults to float, preserving the
existing behavior. Non-float formats require Embed v3.0 or newer. For example:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
The selected format is returned in embedding (or embeddings for
embedMany) as number arrays. The provider returns the values without
converting or unpacking them. binary and ubinary contain packed bytes:
each number represents eight dimensions. Use a binary-aware vector database
or unpack the bits before comparing vectors; do not pass packed bytes directly
to cosineSimilarity. Compressed formats can affect retrieval quality, and
compact storage requires an appropriate database representation.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: inputType 'search_document' | 'search_query' | 'classification' | 'clustering'

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Specifies the type of input passed to the model. Default is search_query.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: search_document: Used for embeddings stored in a vector database for search use-cases.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: search_query: Used for embeddings of search queries run against a vector DB to find relevant documents.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: classification: Used for embeddings passed through a text classifier.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: clustering: Used for embeddings run through a clustering algorithm.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
The number of dimensions of the output embedding. Available for Embed v4.0
and newer models. Embed v4.0 supports 256, 512, 1024, and 1536
(default). Embed v5.0 Pro and Fast also support 768 and 2048 (default).
When omitted, the API uses the model's default dimension.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: truncate 'NONE' | 'START' | 'END'

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
Specifies how the API will handle inputs longer than the maximum token length.
Default is END.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: NONE: If selected, when the input exceeds the maximum input token length will return an error.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: START: Will discard the start of the input until the remaining input is exactly the maximum input token length for the model.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: END: Will discard the end of the input until the remaining input is exactly the maximum input token length for the model.

metadata.description: Learn how to use the Deepgram provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content: The Deepgram provider contains language model support for the Deepgram transcription and speech generation APIs.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Deepgram provider is available in the @ai-sdk/deepgram module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance deepgram from @ai-sdk/deepgram:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createDeepgram from @ai-sdk/deepgram and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Deepgram provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the DEEPGRAM_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Deepgram text-to-speech API
using the .speech() factory method.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
The first argument is the voice family ID: aura-2 (current generation) or
aura (Aura-1). The voice and language are selected with the
generateSpeech voice and language options — the provider composes the
upstream Deepgram model ID as <family>-<voice>-<language> (language
defaults to en):

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Full voice model IDs (e.g. deepgram.speech('aura-2-helena-en')) still pass
through, but the family ID + voice/language form above is the recommended
path — it matches voice selection in the other speech providers.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: encoding string

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Encoding type for the audio output.
Supported values: 'linear16', 'mulaw', 'alaw', 'mp3', 'opus', 'flac', 'aac'.
Optional.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: container string

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Container format for the output audio.
Supported values: 'wav', 'ogg', 'none'.
Optional.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: sampleRate number

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Sample rate for the output audio in Hz.
Supported values depend on the encoding: 8000, 16000, 24000, 32000, 48000.
Optional.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: bitRate number | string

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Bitrate of the audio in bits per second.
For mp3: 32000 or 48000.
For opus: 4000 to 650000.
For aac: 4000 to 192000.
Optional.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: callback string

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
URL to which Deepgram will make a callback request with the audio.
Optional.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: callbackMethod enum

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
HTTP method for the callback request.
Allowed values: 'POST', 'PUT'.
Optional.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: mipOptOut boolean

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Opts out requests from the Deepgram Model Improvement Program.
Optional.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: tag string | array of strings

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Label your requests for identification during usage reporting.
Optional.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Speech results include Deepgram response details in
providerMetadata.deepgram: modelName (the resolved upstream model),
modelUuid, additionalModelUuids, charCount (the billed character
count), breaksApplied, pronunciationsApplied,
pronunciationWarnings (when present), and requestId.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
The generateSpeech speed option is passed through to Deepgram's speed
parameter. Deepgram accepts speeds in the 0.7–1.5 range and rejects
out-of-range values with a 400 error; speed is not supported for all
languages. instructions is not supported and is ignored with a warning.

metadata.title: DeepSeek
metadata.description: Learn how to use DeepSeek's models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: The DeepSeek provider offers access to powerful language models through the DeepSeek API.
API keys can be obtained from the DeepSeek Platform.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The DeepSeek provider is available via the @ai-sdk/deepseek module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance deepSeek from @ai-sdk/deepseek:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: For custom configuration, you can import createDeepSeek and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the DeepSeek provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls.
The default prefix is https://api.deepseek.com.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header. It defaults to
the DEEPSEEK_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom fetch implementation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can create language models using a provider instance:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can also use the .chat() or .languageModel() factory methods:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
DeepSeek language models can be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
DeepSeek retired the deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner aliases on July 24, 2026. Use deepseek-flash (the alias for the current V4.x Flash release), deepseek-v4-flash, or deepseek-v4-pro for the current API. Custom
and legacy model IDs remain accepted as strings for compatibility with custom
endpoints.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for DeepSeek models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: logprobs boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Returns log probabilities for generated content and reasoning
tokens in providerMetadata.deepseek.logprobs.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: topLogprobs number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Returns the specified number of most likely tokens at each token
position. Accepts values from 0 through 20 and automatically enables
logprobs.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: userId string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. An opaque end-user identifier that DeepSeek uses for content-safety
tracing, KV-cache isolation, and scheduling isolation. The value must match
^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ and contain at most 512 characters. Do not include names,
email addresses, or other private user information.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinking object

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Controls thinking mode (chain-of-thought reasoning) for DeepSeek V4 models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: type: 'enabled' | 'disabled' - Enable or disable thinking mode. See DeepSeek's thinking mode docs.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'low' | 'high' | 'max'

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Controls thinking strength for DeepSeek V4 reasoning models. When
using the top-level reasoning setting, minimal is sent as low,
medium is sent as high, xhigh is sent as max, and max is sent
directly. A compatibility warning is returned whenever the requested value
is mapped.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
For backwards compatibility, legacy provider options supplied at runtime are
also mapped to documented values: thinking.type: 'adaptive' becomes
'enabled', reasoningEffort: 'medium' becomes 'high', and
reasoningEffort: 'xhigh' becomes 'max'. Each mapping returns a compatibility
warning so callers can migrate to a canonical value.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
DeepSeek has deprecated the top-level frequencyPenalty and presencePenalty
settings. The provider omits these settings and returns a deprecation warning
when they are used. temperature and topP have no effect while thinking is
enabled, including the default thinking mode for DeepSeek V4 models, so the
provider omits them with an unsupported warning. Explicitly set
thinking.type to 'disabled' to use temperature and topP.

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
DeepSeek supports optional participant names on system, user, and assistant
messages. Set providerOptions.deepseek.name on each message that should
include a name:

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content: The same message option works with streamText:

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
Names are omitted when the option is not set. The name value must be a
string. DeepSeek does not support names on tool messages, so the provider
ignores that placement and returns an unsupported-feature warning. Avoid
including unnecessary personal or identifying information in message names.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: DeepSeek V4 models support reasoning. The reasoning is exposed through streaming:

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details
on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: chat-prefix-completion
contents.content:
DeepSeek's beta chat prefix completion
continues the content of a final assistant message. Create a provider with a
beta base URL and set prefix: true in that assistant message's provider
options:

contents.heading: chat-prefix-completion
contents.content:
The prefixed message must be an assistant message and the final message in the
prompt. The configured baseURL must end in /beta, including when using a
proxy. Invalid placement or a non-beta base URL causes the request to fail
before it is sent.

contents.heading: chat-prefix-completion
contents.content: Chat prefix completion is a DeepSeek beta feature and its behavior may change.

contents.heading: strict-tool-calls
contents.content:
DeepSeek's strict tool-call mode is a beta feature. Create the provider with a
beta base URL and set strict: true on every function tool in the request:

contents.heading: strict-tool-calls
contents.content:
Strict tools fail locally when the base URL does not end in /beta. When any
function tool is strict, every function tool in the same request must set
strict: true.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
DeepSeek exposes the response system fingerprint and context cache usage through
the providerMetadata property:

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: The metadata includes:

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: systemFingerprint: The backend configuration fingerprint for the response

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: promptCacheHitTokens: Number of input tokens that were cached

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: promptCacheMissTokens: Number of input tokens that were not cached

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
For streamed responses, the latest non-null fingerprint from the response
chunks is returned.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
For more details about DeepSeek's caching system, see the DeepSeek caching
documentation.

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
DeepSeek preserves provider-specific response fields in
providerMetadata.deepseek for generated and streamed responses:

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: responseObject: chat.completion or chat.completion.chunk

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: choiceIndex: the selected response choice index

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: messageRole: the response message role, when supplied

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: toolCallTypes: the tool-call type for each returned call

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
These fields remain in provider metadata because they are specific to
DeepSeek's Chat Completions response rather than shared AI SDK result fields.

contents.heading: file-uploads
contents.content:
For inline images or image URLs, use file-part provider options to select the
image processing detail. DeepSeek supports low, high, original, and
auto:

contents.heading: file-uploads
contents.content:
Set fileData: true on an inline image file part to use DeepSeek's
file_data content-part representation. This preserves the file part's
filename. fileData cannot be used with image URLs or imageDetail.

contents.heading: file-uploads
contents.content:
DeepSeek accepts JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP image inputs. HTTP image URLs can be
at most 8,192 characters.

contents.heading: file-uploads
contents.content: You can upload images using the DeepSeek Files API and pass the returned provider reference to deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp. This avoids sending the image bytes again in each request.

contents.heading: file-uploads
contents.content: The optional expiresAfter setting specifies the lifetime in seconds. DeepSeek accepts values from 3,600 seconds (one hour) through 2,592,000 seconds (30 days). Files are permanent when no expiration is specified.

contents.heading: file-uploads
contents.content:
The provider requires a valid file ID in successful upload responses. It also
validates returned object and purpose discriminators and numeric metadata.
Other response metadata remains optional for compatibility with incomplete
responses; omitted values are not included in providerMetadata, and an
omitted response filename falls back to the filename supplied to uploadFile.

contents.heading: file-uploads
contents.content:
DeepSeek file uploads support JPEG (.jpg and .jpeg), PNG, GIF, and WebP
images. Each file can be at most 64 MiB, and filenames can contain at most 512
characters. The AI SDK validates these constraints before sending the upload
request. The image/jpg media type alias is accepted, and a supported filename
extension is used as a fallback when the media type is generic (for example,
application/octet-stream). Recognizable non-image content is rejected even
when its declared media type or filename indicates a supported image format.

metadata.title: ElevenLabs
metadata.description: Learn how to use the ElevenLabs provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content: The ElevenLabs provider contains language model support for the ElevenLabs transcription and speech generation APIs.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The ElevenLabs provider is available in the @ai-sdk/elevenlabs module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance elevenLabs from @ai-sdk/elevenlabs:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createElevenLabs from @ai-sdk/elevenlabs and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the ElevenLabs provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the xi-api-key header.
It defaults to the ELEVENLABS_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: webSocket WebSocketConstructor

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom WebSocket implementation for realtime transcription. A
header-capable implementation is required in runtimes whose native WebSocket
constructor cannot send the xi-api-key authentication header.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the ElevenLabs speech API
using the .speech() factory method.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. eleven_multilingual_v2.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
The voice argument can be set to a voice ID from the ElevenLabs Voice Library.
You can find voice IDs by selecting a voice in the library and copying its ID.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: languageCode string or nullOptional. Language code (ISO 639-1) used to enforce a language for the model. Currently, only Turbo v2.5 and Flash v2.5 support language enforcement. For other models, providing a language code will result in an error.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: voiceSettings object or nullOptional. Voice settings that override stored settings for the given voice. These are applied only to the current request.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: stability double or nullOptional. Determines how stable the voice is and the randomness between each generation. Lower values introduce broader emotional range; higher values result in a more monotonous voice.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: useSpeakerBoost boolean or nullOptional. Boosts similarity to the original speaker. Increases computational load and latency.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: similarityBoost double or nullOptional. Controls how closely the AI should adhere to the original voice.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: style double or nullOptional. Amplifies the style of the original speaker. May increase latency if set above 0.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: pronunciationDictionaryLocators array of objects or nullOptional. A list of pronunciation dictionary locators to apply to the text, in order. Up to 3 locators per request.Each locator object:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: pronunciationDictionaryId string (required)The ID of the pronunciation dictionary.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: versionId string or null (optional)The version ID of the dictionary. If not provided, the latest version is used.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: seed integer or nullOptional. If specified, the system will attempt to sample deterministically. Must be between 0 and 4294967295. Determinism is not guaranteed.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: previousText string or nullOptional. The text that came before the current request's text. Can improve continuity when concatenating generations or influence current generation continuity.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: nextText string or nullOptional. The text that comes after the current request's text. Can improve continuity when concatenating generations or influence current generation continuity.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: previousRequestIds array of strings or nullOptional. List of request IDs for samples generated before this one. Improves continuity when splitting large tasks. Max 3 IDs. If both previousText and previousRequestIds are sent, previousText is ignored.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: nextRequestIds array of strings or nullOptional. List of request IDs for samples generated after this one. Useful for maintaining continuity when regenerating a sample. Max 3 IDs. If both nextText and nextRequestIds are sent, nextText is ignored.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: applyTextNormalization enumOptional. Controls text normalization.Allowed values: 'auto' (default), 'on', 'off'.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: 'auto': System decides whether to apply normalization (e.g., spelling out numbers).

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: 'on': Always apply normalization.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: 'off': Never apply normalization.For eleven_turbo_v2_5 and eleven_flash_v2_5, can only be enabled with Enterprise plans.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: applyLanguageTextNormalization booleanOptional. Defaults to false. Controls language text normalization, which helps with proper pronunciation in some supported languages (currently only Japanese). May significantly increase latency.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: enableLogging booleanOptional. Whether to enable request logging for this API call. Defaults to the account-level setting.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the ElevenLabs transcription API
using the .transcription() factory method.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. scribe_v2.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 (e.g. en) format can sometimes improve transcription performance if known beforehand.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: languageCode string

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
An ISO-639-1 or ISO-639-3 language code corresponding to the language of the audio file.
Can sometimes improve transcription performance if known beforehand.
Defaults to null, in which case the language is predicted automatically.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: tagAudioEvents boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to tag audio events like (laughter), (footsteps), etc. in the transcription.
Defaults to true.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: numSpeakers integer

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The maximum amount of speakers talking in the uploaded file.
Can help with predicting who speaks when.
The maximum amount of speakers that can be predicted is 32.
Defaults to null, in which case the amount of speakers is set to the maximum value the model supports.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: timestampsGranularity enum

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The granularity of the timestamps in the transcription.
Defaults to 'word'.
Allowed values: 'none', 'word', 'character'.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: diarize boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to annotate which speaker is currently talking in the uploaded file.
Defaults to true.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: fileFormat enum

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The format of input audio.
Defaults to 'other'.
Allowed values: 'pcm_s16le_16', 'other'.
For 'pcm_s16le_16', the input audio must be 16-bit PCM at a 16kHz sample rate, single channel (mono), and little-endian byte order.
Latency will be lower than with passing an encoded waveform.

Scribe v2 Realtime supports live transcription through
experimental_streamTranscribe. It accepts raw PCM audio at 8, 16, 22.05, 24,
44.1, or 48 kHz, or 8 kHz mu-law audio.

contents.heading: streaming-transcription-models
contents.content:
The ElevenLabs realtime endpoint authenticates with a WebSocket header. Use a
header-capable WebSocket implementation, such as ws, in runtimes whose native

contents.heading: streaming-transcription-models
contents.content:
The streaming provider options mirror ElevenLabs' realtime transcription
settings: commitStrategy, enableLogging, filterBackgroundAudio,
includeLanguageDetection, includeTimestamps, keyterms,
minSilenceDurationMs, minSpeechDurationMs, noVerbatim, previousText,
secondaryLanguages, vadSilenceThresholdSecs, and vadThreshold.

contents.heading: streaming-transcription-models
contents.content:
ElevenLabs delivers detected language on its timestamp-bearing committed event.
When includeLanguageDetection is enabled, the provider requests that event
internally, but only returns timestamp segments when includeTimestamps is also
enabled. filterBackgroundAudio cannot be combined with either option.

streaming transcription.

contents.heading: provider-options

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: imageUrl - Reference image URL for image-to-image generation (deprecated, use prompt.images instead)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: strength - Controls how much the output differs from the input image

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: guidanceScale - Controls adherence to the prompt (range: 1-20)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: numInferenceSteps - Number of denoising steps (range: 1-50)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: enableSafetyChecker - Enable/disable safety filtering

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: outputFormat - Output format: 'jpeg' or 'png'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: syncMode - Wait for completion before returning response

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: acceleration - Speed of generation: 'none', 'regular', or 'high'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: safetyTolerance - Content safety filtering level (1-6, where 1 is strictest)

contents.heading: provider-options

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:

guidance_scale) are deprecated and will be removed in a future version.

Optional.

Optional.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
For models that support reasoning effort, use the top-level reasoning parameter.
Fireworks maps 'minimal' to 'low' and 'xhigh' or 'max' to 'high', returning
a compatibility warning whenever it coerces the effort. Streaming calls include
the warning in the stream-start event. Explicit
providerOptions.fireworks.reasoningEffort takes precedence over the top-level
setting.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Fireworks exposes the thinking of deepseek-r1 in the generated text using the <think> tag.
You can use the extractReasoningMiddleware to extract this reasoning and expose it as a reasoning property on the result:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: You can then use that enhanced model in functions like generateText and streamText.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Fireworks chat models support additional provider options that are not part of
the standard call settings. You can pass them in the providerOptions argument:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Fireworks chat models:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: promptCacheKey string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
A stable, opaque key that improves prompt cache hit rates by routing requests
with shared prompt prefixes to the same Fireworks replica. Reuse the same key
for all steps and calls in one conversation, and use different keys for
unrelated conversations.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: serviceTier 'priority'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Uses the Fireworks Priority serving path for higher reliability during peak
traffic. The provider sends it as Fireworks' service_tier request field.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinking object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Configuration for thinking/reasoning models like Kimi K2.6.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: type 'enabled' | 'disabled'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Whether to enable thinking mode.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: budgetTokens number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Maximum number of tokens for thinking (minimum 1024).

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: reasoningHistory 'disabled' | 'interleaved' | 'preserved'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Controls how reasoning history is handled in multi-turn conversations:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: 'disabled': Remove reasoning from history

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: 'interleaved': Include reasoning between tool calls within a single turn

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: 'preserved': Keep all reasoning in history

contents.heading: prompt-cache-affinity
contents.content:
Fireworks prompt caching
is automatic, but cached prefixes are local to a replica. Set
promptCacheKey to an opaque session or conversation identifier to improve
cache affinity. The provider sends it as Fireworks'
prompt_cache_key
request field.

contents.heading: prompt-cache-affinity
contents.content:
The AI SDK reuses the same provider options for every model step in a
multi-step generateText or streamText call, so one key covers the complete
tool loop:

contents.heading: prompt-cache-affinity
contents.content:
For a reusable ToolLoopAgent, use call options to supply a key for each
conversation. Pass the same key again for later agent calls that continue that
conversation:

contents.heading: prompt-cache-affinity
contents.content:
Use non-identifying values for cache keys rather than email addresses or other
personal information.

contents.heading: priority-service-tier
contents.content:
Fireworks Priority tier
prioritizes supported models above Standard traffic. Set serviceTier to
'priority' to send Fireworks' service_tier request field:

metadata.title: Fish Audio
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Fish Audio provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content:
The Fish Audio provider contains speech generation (S1 and
S2 models) and speech-to-text transcription support.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Fish Audio provider is available in the @ai-sdk/fish-audio module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance fishAudio from @ai-sdk/fish-audio:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createFishAudio from @ai-sdk/fish-audio and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Fish Audio provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the FISH_AUDIO_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Base URL for the API calls.
Defaults to https://api.fish.audio.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Fish Audio text-to-speech API
using the .speech() factory method.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
The voice option selects a Fish Audio voice model ID (reference_id), either
from the Fish Audio voice library or one of your own
uploaded models. Omit it to use the default voice.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Voice listing is not part of the AI SDK speech model specification, so browse
voices with the Fish Audio list-models
endpoint
directly:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: Add self=true to list only your own uploaded models, or language=en / tag=narration to filter.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: referenceId string | array of strings

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Voice model ID(s). A single ID selects one speaker; an array enables
multi-speaker dialogue (S2-Pro models). Takes precedence over the top-level
voice option.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: sampleRate number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Output sample rate in Hz. Falls back to the format default when unset
(44100 Hz for wav/pcm/mp3, 48000 Hz for opus).
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: mp3Bitrate 64 | 128 | 192

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Bitrate in kbps for mp3 output. Ignored for other formats.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Bitrate in bps for opus output, where -1000 selects automatic. Ignored for
other formats.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: latency 'low' | 'normal' | 'balanced'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Latency/quality tradeoff. normal gives the best quality, balanced reduces
latency, and low is the fastest.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: volume number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Volume offset in dB. Negative values are quieter.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: normalizeLoudness boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Loudness normalization. Supported by the S2 family (s2-pro and
s2.1-pro). Fish Audio accepts it on s1 but ignores it, so the provider
drops it and emits a warning in that case.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: temperature number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Governs expressiveness (0 to 1). Higher values are more varied.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: topP number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Controls diversity via nucleus sampling (0 to 1).
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: chunkLength number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Text segment size for processing (100 to 300).
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options

contents.heading: provider-options

contents.heading: output-formats

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content:
Whether to skip precise timestamps. Mirrors the Fish Audio

Optional.

result.language reports the detected language as an ISO-639-1 code (e.g. en).
It is always a two-letter code, never a locale such as en-US, and is
undefined when Fish Audio detects no language.

contents.heading: provider-options-1

The provider metadata language is a display name intended for presentation.
Its exact form is not guaranteed, so avoid matching or branching on it — use
result.language for anything programmatic.

contents.heading: provider-options-1

contents.content: GMI Cloud's edge reports a generic banner in error.message on rejections and nests the backend engine's diagnostic in error.details. metadata.title: Google Vertex AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Google Vertex AI provider.

contents.content: The Google Vertex provider for the AI SDK contains language model support for the Google Vertex AI APIs. This includes support for Google's Gemini models, Anthropic's Claude partner models, xAI's Grok partner models, and MaaS (Model as a Service) open models.

The Google Vertex provider is compatible with both Node.js and Edge runtimes.
The Edge runtime is supported through the @ai-sdk/google-vertex/edge
sub-module. More details can be found in the Google Vertex Edge
Runtime, Google Vertex Anthropic Edge
Runtime, and Google Vertex MaaS Edge
Runtime sections below.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Google Vertex, Google Vertex Anthropic, Google Vertex xAI, and Google Vertex MaaS providers are available in the @ai-sdk/google-vertex module. You can install it with

contents.heading: google-vertex-provider-usage
contents.content: The Google Vertex provider instance is used to create model instances that call the Vertex AI API. The models available with this provider include Google's Gemini models. If you're looking to use Anthropic's Claude models, see the Google Vertex Anthropic Provider section below.

contents.heading: google-vertex-provider-usage
contents.content:
Vertex Gemini models share the Google provider's forward-compatible model
classification. Unrecognized gemini-* IDs and -latest aliases use the
newest supported Gemini request behavior, while known legacy IDs keep their
generation-specific tool, reasoning, function-response, and thought-signature
handling. The selected Vertex model must still support each requested feature.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance googleVertex from @ai-sdk/google-vertex:

contents.heading: provider-instance

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Google Vertex supports multiple authentication methods depending on your runtime environment and requirements.

contents.heading: nodejs-runtime
contents.content: The Node.js runtime is the default runtime supported by the AI SDK. It supports all standard Google Cloud authentication options through the google-auth-library. Typical use involves setting a path to a json credentials file in the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable. The credentials file can be obtained from the Google Cloud Console.

consistent low-latency performance at a premium, or 'flex' for a 50%
discount with longer expected latency. Both are supported only on the
global endpoint and on a subset of Gemini models.

contents.heading: language-models

By default — with Provisioned Throughput allocated and requestType unset
— the request consumes Provisioned Throughput quota first and only falls
back to the chosen shared tier if PT capacity is exhausted. To bypass
Provisioned Throughput entirely, also set requestType: 'shared'.

The served tier is reported back on

and Flex PayGo

the request through shared PayGo capacity. See

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can use Google Vertex language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Google Vertex language models can also be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: tuned-models
contents.content:
Tuned models
are served from a deployed endpoint and are addressed by their endpoint id rather
than a published model name. Pass the endpoint resource with the endpoints/
prefix and the provider will route the request to the deployed endpoint
(.../locations/{location}/endpoints/{ENDPOINT_ID}) instead of the base model
path (.../publishers/google/models/{MODEL_ID}):

contents.heading: tuned-models
contents.content:
Use the deployed endpoint id, not the tuned model id (a tuned model has both a
models/... resource and a separate endpoints/... resource; only the endpoint
is callable for inference). The request and response format is identical to the
base model, so all standard call settings and provider options continue to work.

contents.heading: tuned-models
contents.content:
Tuned models require standard Google Cloud credentials and the
project/location of the deployed endpoint (via GOOGLE_VERTEX_PROJECT /
GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION or createGoogleVertex). Express
Mode API keys are not supported for tuned models.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: With Code Execution, certain Gemini models on Vertex AI can generate and execute Python code. This allows the model to perform calculations, data manipulation, and other programmatic tasks to enhance its responses.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: You can enable code execution by adding the code_execution tool to your request.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: The response will contain tool-call and tool-result parts for the executed code.

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: URL Context allows Gemini models to retrieve and analyze content from URLs. Supported models: Gemini 2.0 and newer.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Google Search enables Gemini models to access real-time web information. Supported models: Gemini 2.0 and newer.

contents.heading: enterprise-web-search
contents.content: Enterprise Web Search provides grounding using a compliance-focused web index designed for highly-regulated industries such as finance, healthcare, and the public sector. Unlike standard Google Search grounding, Enterprise Web Search does not log customer data and supports VPC service controls. Supported models: Gemini 2.0 and newer.

contents.heading: google-maps
contents.content: Google Maps grounding enables Gemini models to access Google Maps data for location-aware responses. Supported models: Gemini 2.0 and newer.

contents.heading: google-maps
contents.content: The optional retrievalConfig.latLng provider option provides location context for queries about nearby places. This configuration applies to any grounding tools that support location context.

contents.heading: streaming-function-call-arguments
contents.content:
For Gemini 3 Pro and later models on Vertex AI, you can stream function call
arguments as they are generated by setting streamFunctionCallArguments to
true. This reduces perceived latency when functions need to be called, as
tool-input-delta events arrive incrementally instead of waiting for the
complete arguments. This option defaults to false.

contents.heading: streaming-function-call-arguments
contents.content:
This feature is only available on the Vertex AI API. It is not supported on
the Gemini API. When used with the Google provider, a warning will be emitted
and the option will be ignored.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: Google Vertex AI, through its support for Gemini models, can also emit "thinking" tokens, representing the model's reasoning process. The AI SDK exposes these as reasoning information.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: To enable thinking tokens for compatible Gemini models via Vertex, set includeThoughts: true in the thinkingConfig provider option. These options are passed through providerOptions.vertex:

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: When includeThoughts is true, parts of the API response marked with thought: true will be processed as reasoning.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: In generateText, these contribute to the reasoningText (string) and reasoning (array) fields.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: In streamText, these are emitted as reasoning stream parts.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content:
Refer to the Google Vertex AI documentation on
"thinking"
for model compatibility and further details.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: The Google Vertex provider supports file inputs, e.g. PDF files.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content:
The AI SDK will automatically download URLs if you pass them as data, except
for gs:// URLs. You can use the Google Cloud Storage API to upload larger
files to that location.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: See File Parts for details on how to use files in prompts.

contents.heading: tool-result-files
contents.content:
For Gemini 3 and later models, tool results can include Google Cloud Storage
(gs://) file URLs. Vertex receives these references directly as
functionResponse.parts[].fileData, without downloading the files into the SDK
process. The supported MIME types are image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp,
application/pdf, and text/plain. Specify the full MIME type; a top-level type
such as image is not sufficient for GCS tool results.

contents.heading: tool-result-files
contents.content: Use a file part in the tool's toModelOutput result:

contents.heading: tool-result-files
contents.content:
Include originalUrl when URL parsing changes an opaque GCS URI, such as a path
containing spaces, so Vertex receives the exact object reference. The Vertex
caller must have access to the referenced object.

contents.heading: tool-result-files
contents.content:
HTTP(S) tool-result files are downloaded and sent as inline data, subject to
toolResultDownloads.maxBytes. Direct GCS tool-result forwarding is not supported
for older Gemini models or MIME types outside the list above.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content:
You can create Gemini image models using the .image() factory method. These
models provide image output through the language model :generateContent API.
For more on image generation with the AI SDK see
generateImage().

contents.heading: gemini-image-models
contents.content: Gemini image models (e.g. gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview) are multimodal output language models that can be used with generateImage() for a simpler image generation experience. Internally, the provider calls the language model API with responseModalities: ['IMAGE'].

contents.heading: gemini-image-models
contents.content: Gemini image models also support image editing by providing input images:

contents.heading: gemini-image-models
contents.content:
Input images must be provided as Buffer, ArrayBuffer, Uint8Array, or
base64-encoded strings. URL inputs, including HTTP and gs:// URLs, are not
supported by generateImage() with Google Vertex image models.

contents.heading: gemini-image-models
contents.content:
Gemini image models do not support the size or n parameters. Use
aspectRatio instead of size. Mask-based inpainting is also not supported.

contents.heading: gemini-image-models
contents.content:
Gemini image models are multimodal output models that can generate both text
and images. For more advanced use cases where you need both text and image
outputs, or want more control over the generation process, you can use them
directly with generateText().

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
You can transcribe audio with Google Cloud Speech-to-Text models using the
.transcription() factory method together with
transcribe().

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The provider supports Chirp
models chirp_2 and chirp_3, plus telephony for phone-call audio.
Speech-to-Text uses standard Google Cloud credentials (OAuth, Application Default
Credentials, or a service account) and calls the Cloud Speech-to-Text API.
Express Mode API keys are not supported for transcription models. Set
GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION (or providerOptions.googleVertex.region) to a
Speech-to-Text region. For Chirp, chirp_2 is available in us-central1,
europe-west4, and asia-southeast1; chirp_3 in the us and eu
multi-regions. Chirp is not available in the global Speech-to-Text location,
and these regions differ from Vertex AI regions. telephony availability
depends on the selected Speech-to-Text region and language.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The synchronous API transcribes audio up to one minute or 10 MB, whichever is
reached first. The spoken language is auto-detected by default; pass
languageCodes to restrict it. For telephony, pass a supported language code
such as ['en-US'].

language. Defaults to ['auto']. Multiple explicit language codes require a
multi-region Speech-to-Text endpoint such as us or eu.

contents.heading: transcription-models

true. Google notes that enabling word-level timestamps can reduce
transcription quality and speed.

location.

contents.content: The Google Vertex Anthropic provider for the AI SDK offers support for Anthropic's Claude models through the Google Vertex AI APIs. This section provides details on how to set up and use the Google Vertex Anthropic provider.

contents.heading: provider-instance-1

contents.heading: nodejs-runtime-1
contents.content: For Node.js environments, the Google Vertex Anthropic provider supports all standard Google Cloud authentication options through the google-auth-library. You can customize the authentication options by passing them to the createVertexAnthropic function:

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings-3
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Google Vertex Anthropic provider instance:

(including the standard Google Auth library) are not compatible.

contents.heading: tools

contents.heading: tools

Setting strict: true on a tool will be ignored and a warning will be
emitted.

Currently, this means Gemini 3 request behavior for provider-defined and mixed
tools, thinkingLevel reasoning, multimodal function responses, and thought
signatures. Known legacy Gemini model IDs keep their generation-specific
request behavior. This SDK default controls request serialization; the
selected model must still support each feature in the Google API.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Google also supports some model specific settings that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Google models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: cachedContent string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. The name of the cached content used as context to serve the prediction.
Format: cachedContents/{cachedContent}

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Enable structured output. Default is true.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can disable structured outputs when a schema is not supported or exceeds
Google's schema complexity limits. The model will still be instructed to
return JSON, but the schema will not be sent to Google.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: See Troubleshooting: Schema Limitations for more details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: safetySettings Array<{ category: string; threshold: string }>

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Safety settings for the model.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: category string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The category of the safety setting. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_UNSPECIFIED

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_CIVIC_INTEGRITY

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: threshold string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The threshold of the safety setting. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_BLOCK_THRESHOLD_UNSPECIFIED

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_NONE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: OFF

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
responseModalities string[]
The modalities to use for the response. The following modalities are supported: TEXT, IMAGE. When not defined or empty, the model defaults to returning only text.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinkingConfig { thinkingLevel?: 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'; thinkingBudget?: number; includeThoughts?: boolean }

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Configuration for the model's thinking process. Only supported by specific Google models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinkingLevel 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Controls the thinking depth for Gemini 3 and later models. Gemini 3.1 Pro supports 'low', 'medium', and 'high', Gemini 3 Pro supports 'low' and 'high', while Gemini 3 Flash supports all four levels: 'minimal', 'low', 'medium', and 'high'.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinkingBudget number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Gives the model guidance on the number of thinking tokens it can use when generating a response. Setting it to 0 disables thinking, if the model supports it.
For more information about the possible value ranges for each model see Google thinking documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
This option is for Gemini 2.5 models. Gemini 3 and later models should use
thinkingLevel instead.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: includeThoughts boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. If set to true, thought summaries are returned, which are synthesized versions of the model's raw thoughts and offer insights into the model's internal reasoning process.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: imageConfig { aspectRatio?: string, imageSize?: string }

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Configuration for the models image generation. Only supported by specific Google models.

contents.heading: language-models

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Model defaults to generate 1:1 squares, or to matching the output image size to that of your input image. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: imageSize string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Controls the output image resolution. Defaults to 1K. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models

contents.heading: language-models

Optional. Enables timestamp understanding for audio-only files.
See Google Cloud audio understanding documentation.

contents.heading: language-models

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. If specified, the media resolution specified will be used. Can be one of the following:

Optional. Defines labels used in billing reports. Available on Vertex AI only.
See Google Cloud labels documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. The service tier to use for the request.
Set to 'flex' for 50% cheaper processing at the cost of increased latency.
Set to 'priority' for ultra-low latency at a 75-100% price premium over 'standard'.

contents.content:
Because Priority can be gracefully downgraded to Standard under load, the

result.providerMetadata.google.serviceTier. See
Priority inference
and Flex inference.

contents.heading: thinking
contents.content: The Gemini 2.5 and Gemini 3-and-later series models use an internal "thinking process" that significantly improves their reasoning and multi-step planning abilities, making them highly effective for complex tasks such as coding, advanced mathematics, and data analysis. For more information see Google thinking documentation.

contents.heading: gemini-3-and-later-models
contents.content: For Gemini 3 and later models, use the thinkingLevel parameter to control the depth of reasoning:

contents.heading: gemini-25-models
contents.content: For Gemini 2.5 models, use the thinkingBudget parameter to control the number of thinking tokens:

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: The Google provider supports file inputs, e.g. PDF files.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: You can also use YouTube URLs directly:

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content:
The AI SDK will automatically download URLs if you pass them as data, except
for https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/files/ and YouTube
URLs. You can use the Google Generative AI Files API to upload larger files to
that location. YouTube URLs (public or unlisted videos) are supported directly

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: you can specify one YouTube video URL per request.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: See File Parts for details on how to use files in prompts.

contents.heading: cached-content
contents.content: Google supports both explicit and implicit caching to help reduce costs on repetitive content.

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Gemini models automatically provide cache cost savings without needing to create an explicit cache. When you send requests that share common prefixes with previous requests, you'll receive a 75% token discount on cached content.

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: To maximize cache hits with implicit caching:

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Keep content at the beginning of requests consistent

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Add variable content (like user questions) at the end of prompts

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Ensure requests meet minimum token requirements:

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Gemini 3 series: 4096 tokens minimum

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Gemini 2.5 series: 2048 tokens minimum

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content:
Usage metadata was added to providerMetadata in @ai-sdk/google@1.2.23. If
you are using an older version, usage metadata is available in the raw HTTP
response body returned as part of the return value from generateText.

contents.heading: explicit-caching
contents.content: For guaranteed cost savings, you can still use explicit caching with Gemini 2.5 and 3 series models. See the models page to check if caching is supported for the used model:

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: With Code Execution, certain models can generate and execute Python code to perform calculations, solve problems, or provide more accurate information.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: You can enable code execution by adding the code_execution tool to your request.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: The response will contain the tool calls and results from the code execution.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content:
With Google Search grounding,
the model has access to the latest information using Google Search.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: The googleSearch tool accepts the following optional configuration options:

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: searchTypes object

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Enables specific search types. Both can be combined.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: webSearch: Enable web search grounding (pass {} to enable). This is the default.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: imageSearch: Enable image search grounding (pass {} to enable).

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: timeRangeFilter object

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Restricts search results to a specific time range. Both startTime and endTime are required.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: startTime: Start time in ISO 8601 format (e.g. '2025-01-01T00:00:00Z').

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: endTime: End time in ISO 8601 format (e.g. '2025-12-31T23:59:59Z').

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: When Google Search grounding is enabled, the model will include sources in the response.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Additionally, the grounding metadata includes detailed information about how search results were used to ground the model's response. Here are the available fields:

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: webSearchQueries (string[] | null)

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Array of search queries used to retrieve information

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Example: ["What's the weather in Chicago this weekend?"]

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: searchEntryPoint ({ renderedContent: string } | null)

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Contains the main search result content used as an entry point

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: The renderedContent field contains the formatted content

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: groundingSupports (Array of support objects | null)

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Contains details about how specific response parts are supported by search results

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Each support object includes:

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: segment: Information about the grounded text segment

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: text: The actual text segment

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: startIndex: Starting position in the response

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: endIndex: Ending position in the response

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: groundingChunkIndices: References to supporting search result chunks

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: confidenceScores: Confidence scores (0-1) for each supporting chunk

contents.content: Example response:

contents.heading: enterprise-web-search
contents.content:
With Enterprise Web Search,
the model has access to a compliance-focused web index designed for highly-regulated industries such as finance, healthcare, and public sector.

contents.heading: enterprise-web-search
contents.content:
Enterprise Web Search is only available on Vertex AI. You must use the Google
Vertex provider (@ai-sdk/google-vertex) instead of the standard Google
provider (@ai-sdk/google) to use this feature. Requires Gemini 2.0 or newer
models.

contents.heading: enterprise-web-search
contents.content: Enterprise Web Search provides the following benefits:

contents.heading: enterprise-web-search
contents.content: Does not log customer data

contents.heading: enterprise-web-search
contents.content: Supports VPC service controls

contents.heading: enterprise-web-search
contents.content: Compliance-focused web index for regulated industries

contents.heading: file-search
contents.content: The File Search tool lets Gemini retrieve context from your own documents that you have indexed in File Search stores. The provider enables this tool for Gemini 2.5 and Gemini 3-and-later model IDs, including unrecognized future Gemini IDs.

contents.heading: file-search
contents.content: File Search responses include citations via the normal sources field and expose raw grounding metadata in providerMetadata.google.groundingMetadata.

contents.heading: file-search
contents.content:
Custom metadata attached to the indexed documents is available in
groundingMetadata.groundingChunks[].retrievedContext.customMetadata.

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: Google provides a provider-defined URL context tool.

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: The URL context tool allows you to provide specific URLs that you want the model to analyze directly in from the prompt.

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: The URL context metadata includes detailed information about how the model used the URL context to generate the response. Here are the available fields:

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: urlMetadata ({ retrievedUrl: string; urlRetrievalStatus: string; }[] | null)

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: Array of URL context metadata

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: Each object includes:

contents.heading: url-context

contents.heading: url-context

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content:
The URL context tool is only supported for Gemini 2.0 Flash models and above.
Check the supported models for URL context
tool.

contents.heading: combine-url-context-with-search-grounding
contents.content: You can combine the URL context tool with search grounding to provide the model with the latest information from the web.

contents.heading: google-maps-grounding
contents.content:
With Google Maps grounding,
the model has access to Google Maps data for location-aware responses. This enables providing local data and geospatial context, such as finding nearby restaurants.

contents.heading: google-maps-grounding
contents.content: The optional retrievalConfig.latLng provider option provides location context for queries about nearby places. This configuration applies to any grounding tools that support location context, including Google Maps and Google Search.

contents.heading: google-maps-grounding
contents.content: When Google Maps grounding is enabled, the model's response will include sources pointing to Google Maps URLs. The grounding metadata includes maps chunks with place information:

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content:
With RAG Engine Grounding,
the model has access to your custom knowledge base using the Vertex RAG Engine.
This enables the model to provide answers based on your specific data sources and documents.

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content:
RAG Engine Grounding is only supported with Vertex Gemini models. You must use
the Google Vertex provider (@ai-sdk/google-vertex) instead of the standard
Google provider (@ai-sdk/google) to use this feature.

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: When RAG Engine Grounding is enabled, the model will include sources from your RAG corpus in the response.

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: Additionally, the grounding metadata includes detailed information about how RAG results were used to ground the model's response. Here are the available fields:

contents.content: Each support object includes:

contents.content: text: The actual text segment

contents.content: startIndex: Starting position in the response

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: groundingChunkIndices: References to supporting RAG result chunks

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding

contents.heading: image-outputs
contents.content: Gemini models with image generation capabilities (e.g. gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview) support generating images as part of a multimodal response. Images are exposed as files in the response.

contents.heading: image-outputs
contents.content:
If you primarily want to generate images without text output, you can also use
Gemini image models with the generateImage() function. See Gemini Image

contents.heading: schema-limitations
contents.content:
The Google Generative AI API supports a subset of JSON Schema. Google notes that
very large or deeply nested schemas may be rejected.
When a schema exceeds Google's complexity limit, the API may return the following
generic error:

contents.heading: schema-limitations
contents.content: Request contains an invalid argument.

contents.heading: schema-limitations
contents.content:
You can work around this by simplifying the schema sent to Google. For example,
remove unnecessary constraints or reduce nesting while preserving the fields
and types the model needs to generate. If you need stricter client-side
validation than the schema sent to Google, use jsonSchema
with a custom validation function or validate the generated output separately.

contents.heading: schema-limitations
contents.content:
By default, structured outputs are enabled (and for tool calling they are required).
You can also disable provider-enforced structured outputs for object generation:

contents.heading: schema-limitations
contents.content:
When structuredOutputs is false, Google still receives the JSON response MIME type
but not the schema. Describe the required schema in your prompt. AI SDK
will still validate the response against the schema in Output.object.
