contents.heading: batch
contents.content: Batch support is experimental and the API may change in patch releases.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content:
The Google provider supports asynchronous text generation through the Gemini
Batch API. Pass the Google
provider to the AI SDK's Batch
API for the complete workflow, including polling, persistence, and result handling.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content:
Each request specifies its type and model. Google requires every text
request in a batch to use the same model and throws before submission when the
models differ.

contents.heading: webhooks
contents.content: You can pass a webhookUrl to receive a notification when the batch reaches a terminal state:

contents.heading: webhooks
contents.content: Google sends a thin event to the webhook URL. After receiving and verifying the event, use the persisted batch reference with getBatchStatus or getBatchResults. Your application is responsible for handling the webhook and verifying Google's dynamic webhook signature.

contents.heading: large-batches
contents.content: When the serialized batch creation body is under 20 MB, the provider sends the requests inline. At 20 MB or more, it uploads a JSONL input file through the Gemini Files API.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Gemini Live API
using the .experimental_realtime() factory method.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
Realtime sessions run in the browser and require a short-lived token created on
your server with google.experimental_realtime.getToken():

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
Google realtime models may require provider-specific audio formats, depending
on the model and modality. See Realtime for the
complete setup and tool calling pattern.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
Gemini lifecycle signals that do not have provider-neutral equivalents are
emitted as custom events. Inspect rawType for goAway,
sessionResumptionUpdate, and generationComplete and use the event's raw
payload for provider-specific details.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
With input audio transcription enabled, parseServerEvent emits
input-transcription-completed events with a stable itemId for each user
utterance. Each transcript contains the accumulated text so far. If you consume
these events directly, replace the text for that itemId with transcript on
each event. The realtime session handles this automatically.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
Google's finished transcription marker ends an utterance even when the marker
contains no text. For payloads without this marker, response completion and
interruption provide fallback boundaries. These fallback boundaries cannot
unambiguously associate all delayed transcription fragments. Input item IDs use
their own sequence and need not match the model's response IDs.

contents.heading: live-translation
contents.content:
Use gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview for low-latency speech-to-speech
translation. Configure the target language with
providerOptions.google.translationConfig in the realtime session config you
use when creating the token:

contents.heading: live-translation
contents.content:
Set targetLanguageCode to a BCP-47 language code (defaults to en). When
echoTargetLanguage is true, input audio already in the target language is
echoed instead of producing silence.

contents.heading: live-translation
contents.content:
Gemini Live Translation accepts audio input and produces translated audio
output. Text input, tools, and custom instructions are not supported by this
model.

contents.heading: gemini-38-live
contents.content:
gemini-3.8-live and gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking are audio-only
realtime models: request outputModalities: ['audio'], and add
outputAudioTranscription: {} if you want the assistant's transcript as
audio-transcript-delta events. Server-side voice activity detection and
proactive audio are always on.

contents.heading: gemini-38-live
contents.content:
gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking reasons in the background while streaming
audio. Google requires exactly one of thinkingLevel (low, medium, high)
or thinkingBudget for it; the provider sends thinkingLevel: 'low' when you
set neither. Override it through providerOptions.google.thinkingConfig:

contents.heading: gemini-38-live
contents.content:
Tools declared in the session config run asynchronously (NON_BLOCKING) by
default on these models, so the model keeps talking while a tool call is in
flight. Set providerOptions.google.defaultToolBehavior: 'BLOCKING' on
gemini-3.8-live to make it wait for the result instead.

contents.heading: gemini-38-live
contents.content:
On the extended thinking model, turnComplete (the response-done event) does
not mean the model is idle. Watch the interactionStatus custom event: its
raw.interactionStatus is IN_PROGRESS, IDLE, or WAITING_FOR_INPUT. A
waitingForInput custom event is emitted when the model has stopped and needs
user input to continue.

contents.heading: translation-models
contents.content:
For server-side streaming translation, you can create models that call the
Gemini Live API using the
.translation() factory method. Translation models are streaming-only and are
used with
experimental_streamTranslate.

contents.heading: translation-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview.

contents.heading: translation-models
contents.content:
The Gemini Live API auto-detects the source language (sourceLanguage is not
supported) and always outputs 24kHz 16-bit PCM audio (outputAudioFormat is
not supported). Unsupported settings surface as call warnings.

contents.heading: translation-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: translation-models
contents.content:
echoTargetLanguage boolean
Whether input audio already in the target language should be echoed instead
of producing silence.
Optional.

contents.heading: interactions-api
contents.content:
The Gemini Interactions API
(POST /v1beta/interactions) is a separate Google endpoint with server-side
state, unified content blocks, first-class built-in tools, agent presets,
managed agents that run in a sandboxed Linux environment, and native
multimodal image and video output. It is reached via the
google.interactions(...) factory:

contents.heading: interactions-api
contents.content:
google.interactions(...) accepts a model ID string (e.g.
'gemini-3.8-flash', 'gemini-3.1-pro-preview'), { agent: <name> } to use
a Gemini agent preset, or { managedAgent: <name> } to
invoke a managed agent you created on Google's side.
The returned model can be passed to generateText and streamText like
any other AI SDK language model.

contents.heading: interactions-api
contents.content:
Use google(...) for the standard :generateContent /
:streamGenerateContent endpoints, and google.interactions(...) for the new
Interactions endpoint. Pick one per model instance — they target different
request bodies and SSE event vocabularies.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
The Interactions model reads its options from the shared
providerOptions.google.* namespace. Validate them with the
GoogleLanguageModelInteractionsOptions type:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: previousInteractionId string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Server-side interaction id from a prior turn. When set, the server pulls
prior context from its own state and only the new user message is sent on
the wire. Pair with the default store: true to chain stateful
conversations. See Stateful chaining.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: store boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether the server should persist the interaction. Defaults to true.
Set to false for stateless multi-turn conversations where the full
message history is re-sent on every turn.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: agent string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Name of a Gemini agent preset (e.g. 'deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025').

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Prefer the factory form google.interactions({ agent: '...' }) over
setting agent in provider options — the factory is type-checked
against the supported agent names.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: agentConfig object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Per-agent configuration. Currently supports { type: 'dynamic' } and
{ type: 'deep-research', thinkingSummaries?, visualization?, collaborativePlanning? }.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinkingLevel 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Controls reasoning depth for thinking-enabled models. Mapped onto the
Interactions request's thinking_level.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinkingSummaries 'auto' | 'none'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether the model returns synthesized thought summaries on reasoning
parts. Defaults to the API default.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: responseFormat Array<ResponseFormatEntry>

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Output-format entries that map directly to the API's response_format
array. Entries have the following shape:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Use this for fine-grained control over image, audio, video, or non-JSON
text outputs. Video entries can control aspect ratio, resolution, duration,
and inline or URI delivery; set gcsUri when delivering to Google Cloud
Storage. Inline videos are returned in result.files by generateText and
emitted as file parts by streamText.
The AI SDK call-level responseFormat: { type: 'json', schema } still
drives JSON-mode automatically and prepends a matching text entry;
entries listed here are appended.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: imageConfig { aspectRatio?: string; imageSize?: '1K' | '2K' | '4K' | '512' } (deprecated)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Use responseFormat with a { type: 'image', ... } entry instead.
Retained for backwards compatibility; the SDK translates imageConfig
into a matching response_format image entry and emits a warning when
set. Ignored when responseFormat already supplies an image entry.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: mediaResolution 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'ultra_high'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Media resolution applied to image inputs / outputs.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: serviceTier 'flex' | 'standard' | 'priority'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Service tier for the request. Mirrored back on
result.providerMetadata.google.serviceTier for observability.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: systemInstruction string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Alternative to the AI SDK system message. If both are set, the AI SDK
system message wins and a warning is emitted.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: background boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Run the interaction in the background. Required for agents whose
server-side workflow cannot complete within a single request/response;
rejected by agents that only support synchronous calls. When true,
the POST returns a non-terminal status and the SDK polls
GET /interactions/{id} until the work completes.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: environment string | object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Sandbox environment configuration for managed agents.
Pass 'remote' to provision a fresh sandbox, an environment_id
string to reuse an existing one, or an object of the form
{ type: 'remote', sources?, network? } to preload files and/or
constrain outbound traffic. Only applies to agent calls.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: pollingTimeoutMs number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Maximum time, in milliseconds, to poll a background interaction before
giving up. Defaults to 30 minutes (1,800,000 ms). Long-running agents
may need longer.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
result.providerMetadata.google (typed via GoogleInteractionsProviderMetadata)
exposes:

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: interactionId string

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
Server-side interaction id. Pass this back as previousInteractionId on
the next turn to chain.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: serviceTier string

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: Service tier the request actually ran on.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: signature string

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
Per-block signature hash, set by the SDK on output reasoning and
tool-call or agentic video processing parts. Round-tripped automatically on
the next turn.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: Agentic video custom parts additionally expose:

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: processingId string

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
ID of an agentic video processing_call. Present on
google.processing_call custom parts.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: processingCallId string

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
ID of the matching agentic video processing call. Present on
google.processing_result custom parts.

contents.heading: stateful-chaining
contents.content:
With the default store: true, the server retains the prior turn so the
next request only needs to send the new user message and the
previousInteractionId:

contents.heading: stateful-chaining
contents.content:
For stateless multi-turn conversations, set store: false and re-send the
full message history on every turn (no previousInteractionId):

contents.heading: agentic-video-understanding
contents.content:
Gemini 3.7 Flash, 3.6 Flash, and 3.5 Flash Lite support agentic video
understanding through the Interactions API. Instead of sampling the entire
video at a fixed frame rate, the model dynamically navigates the timeline and
loads the transcripts, frames, or audio needed for the prompt.

contents.heading: agentic-video-understanding
contents.content:
Set processing: 'agentic' in the Google provider options of an individual
video file part. You can validate the per-file options with
GoogleInteractionsVideoOptions:

contents.heading: agentic-video-understanding
contents.content: Agentic navigation is exposed as custom content parts:

contents.heading: agentic-video-understanding
contents.content:
google.processing_call marks a request by the model to inspect part of the
video. Its providerMetadata.google.processingId contains the processing ID.

contents.heading: agentic-video-understanding
contents.content:
google.processing_result marks completion of that request. Its
providerMetadata.google.processingCallId links it to the processing call.

contents.heading: agentic-video-understanding
contents.content:
These parts are informational and do not require a tool response. They are
available from both generateText and streamText.

contents.heading: agentic-video-understanding
contents.content:
For static processing, use 'static' or provide clipping and frame-rate
options. startOffset and endOffset are measured in seconds:

contents.heading: agentic-video-understanding
contents.content:
With stateful conversations, pass the returned interactionId as
previousInteractionId; Gemini retains the video context server-side. With
store: false, append result.responseMessages and re-send the full history.
The processing custom parts and their signatures are then round-tripped as
native processing_call and processing_result steps so the video context is
preserved.

Add a { type: 'image' } entry to responseFormat on a Gemini

the response. No tool wrapping is required, and the entry doubles as the
place to set aspectRatio, imageSize, and mimeType.

contents.heading: image-output-via-interactions
contents.content:
To control aspect ratio, image size, or output mime type, add those
fields to the same image entry:

contents.heading: image-output-via-interactions

contents.heading: image-output-via-interactions

contents.heading: agent-presets
contents.content:
Pass { agent: <name> } to target a Gemini agent preset. The factory
type-checks the agent name against the supported set:

contents.heading: agent-presets
contents.content:
Whether an agent runs synchronously or in the background depends on the
agent. Long-running presets (such as the deep-research-* family)
require background: true — the POST returns a non-terminal status and
the SDK polls GET /interactions/{id} internally until the interaction
completes. Other agents accept synchronous calls only and will reject
background: true. Set the flag explicitly via
providerOptions.google.background.

contents.heading: agent-presets
contents.content:
The default polling timeout is 30 minutes; raise it via
pollingTimeoutMs for slower agents:

contents.heading: agent-presets
contents.content: Agents also chain through previousInteractionId like model-id calls.

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content:
Managed agents run inside a
sandboxed Linux environment provisioned per interaction. Pass the environment
provider option to control how the sandbox is set up; the option is only
accepted on agent calls.

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content: The simplest form provisions a fresh sandbox:

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content: environment accepts three shapes:

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content: 'remote' — provision a fresh sandbox for this call.

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content:
any other string — an environment_id to reuse, forking the previous
sandbox so its filesystem and installed packages persist.

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content:
an object — provision a fresh sandbox and optionally preload sources
and/or constrain outbound traffic via network:

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content:
Three source types are supported: inline (write a string into the
sandbox at target), repository (clone a git repository — pass the
URL as source), and gcs (mount a Google Cloud Storage prefix).

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content:
The network field accepts the string 'disabled' to block all
outbound traffic, or an object with an allowlist array whose entries
each carry a domain plus an optional transform array of header
objects to inject into matching requests.

contents.heading: custom-managed-agents
contents.content:
For user-defined agents that you created on Google's side via the
Gemini API's /v1beta/agents endpoint, pass the agent's name through the dedicated
managedAgent factory shape instead of agent (which only accepts
known preset names):

contents.heading: streaming
contents.content:
streamText is supported. The stream's finish part exposes
interactionId on providerMetadata.google so callers can chain.

The following Gemma models are available:

contents.heading: gemma-models
contents.content: Gemma models don't natively support the systemInstruction parameter, but the provider automatically handles system instructions by prepending them to the first user message. This allows you to use system instructions with Gemma models seamlessly:

contents.heading: gemma-models
contents.content: The system instruction is automatically formatted and included in the conversation, so Gemma models can follow the guidance without any additional configuration.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Google Generative AI embeddings API
using the .embedding() factory method.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: The Google provider sends API calls to the right endpoint based on the type of embedding:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Single embeddings: When embedding a single value with embed(), the provider uses the single :embedContent endpoint, which typically has higher rate limits compared to the batch endpoint.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Batch embeddings: When embedding multiple values with embedMany() or multiple values in embed(), the provider uses the :batchEmbedContents endpoint.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Google embedding models support additional settings. You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: When using embedMany, provide per-value multimodal content via the content option. Each entry corresponds to a value at the same index; use null for text-only entries:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Google embedding models:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: outputDimensionality: number

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Optional reduced dimension for the output embedding. If set, excessive values in the output embedding are truncated from the end.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: taskType: string

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Optional. Specifies the task type for generating embeddings. Supported task types include:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY: Optimized for text similarity.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: CLASSIFICATION: Optimized for text classification.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: CLUSTERING: Optimized for clustering texts based on similarity.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT: Optimized for document retrieval.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: RETRIEVAL_QUERY: Optimized for query-based retrieval.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: QUESTION_ANSWERING: Optimized for answering questions.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: FACT_VERIFICATION: Optimized for verifying factual information.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY: Optimized for retrieving code blocks based on natural language queries.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: content: array

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Optional. Per-value multimodal content parts for embedding non-text content (images, video, PDF, audio). Each entry corresponds to the embedding value at the same index — its parts are merged with the text value in the request. Use null for entries that are text-only. The array length must match the number of values being embedded. Each non-null entry is an array of parts, where each part can be { text: string }, { inlineData: { mimeType: string, data: string } } for inline base64 data, or { fileData: { fileUri: string, mimeType: string } } to reference remote content via HTTP URL or Google Cloud Storage URI (gs://...). Supported by gemini-embedding-2-preview.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content:
You can create image models that call the Google Generative AI API using the .image() factory method.
For more on image generation with the AI SDK see generateImage().

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content:
The .image() factory supports Gemini multimodal language models with image
output capabilities through the :generateContent API.

contents.heading: gemini-image-models
contents.content: Gemini image models (e.g. gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview) are technically multimodal output language models, but they can be used with the generateImage() function for a simpler image generation experience. Internally, the provider calls the language model API with responseModalities: ['IMAGE'].

contents.heading: gemini-image-models
contents.content: Gemini image models also support image editing by providing input images:

contents.heading: gemini-image-models
contents.content: You can also use URLs for input images:

contents.heading: gemini-image-models
contents.content:
Gemini image models do not support the size or n parameters. Use
aspectRatio instead of size. Mask-based inpainting is also not supported.

contents.heading: gemini-image-models
contents.content:
For more advanced use cases where you need both text and image outputs, or
want more control over the generation process, you can use Gemini image models
directly with generateText(). See Image Outputs for
details.

contents.content: Gemini image models support Google Search grounding through providerOptions.google.googleSearch. The value matches the args of google.tools.googleSearch(...); pass {} to enable with defaults, or { searchTypes: { imageSearch: {} } } to ground on reference photos.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Gemini text-to-speech API
using the .speech() factory method.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
The first argument is the model ID, such as gemini-3.8-flash-tts or
gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts. Speech generation uses the generateContent API.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
The voice argument can be set to one of Gemini's 30 prebuilt voices
e.g. Kore, Puck, Zephyr, or Charon. Voice names are case-sensitive.
The default voice is Kore. Custom voice IDs and replication keys are not supported.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
By default the generated audio is returned as a playable WAV file
(result.audio.mediaType is audio/wav). Gemini 3.8 returns a complete WAV file;
the provider passes those bytes through unchanged. Older models return raw PCM,
which the provider wraps in a WAV container. Write result.audio.uint8Array
directly to disk without adding another WAV header.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Gemini 2.5 and 3.1 model IDs retain the legacy request format. Other model IDs,
including custom aliases, use the structured speech format.

contents.heading: speech-directions-in-gemini-38
contents.content:
Gemini 3.8 treats text as a verbatim transcript. The provider sends instructions
as speechMetadata.style, leaving the text unchanged. You can also supply
providerOptions.google.speechMetadata with style and speaker fields.
An explicit style overrides instructions, including an empty style string.

contents.heading: speech-directions-in-gemini-38
contents.content:
Put sustained delivery directions such as whispering, speaking slowly, or being
out of breath in metadata. Keep momentary vocal events and pauses such as
<laugh>, <sigh>, <cough>, <breath>, and <short pause> in the transcript.
Avoid sound-effect tags such as applause or thuds. The provider preserves inline
tags as written.

contents.heading: speech-directions-in-gemini-38
contents.content:
For Gemini 3.1 and earlier, the provider retains the existing behavior of
prepending instructions to single-speaker text. It ignores instructions with a
warning for older multi-speaker requests. Structured turns and speechMetadata
require Gemini 3.8.

contents.heading: multi-speaker-audio
contents.content:
For Gemini 3.8 dialogue, pass multiSpeakerVoiceConfig and turns through
providerOptions.google. Every turn must include speechMetadata.speaker
matching a configured speaker; missing or unknown speakers produce an error
before the request is sent. Speaker labels belong in metadata, not the text.

contents.heading: multi-speaker-audio
contents.content:
The turns array replaces the top-level text, so pass text: ''. The combined
turn text must be non-empty. Passing
nonempty top-level text with turns produces a warning. Put metadata on each turn
instead of combining turns with top-level speechMetadata. Each turn's style
overrides instructions; turns without a style inherit instructions.

contents.heading: multi-speaker-audio
contents.content:
multiSpeakerVoiceConfig overrides the top-level voice. Each voiceConfig
uses prebuiltVoiceConfig: { voiceName: 'Kore' }. Google supports up to two
prebuilt voices in a multi-speaker request.

contents.heading: multi-speaker-audio
contents.content:
Older models continue to use labelled transcripts, such as
text: 'Joe: How are you? Jane: Doing great, thanks!', with
multiSpeakerVoiceConfig and without turns.

contents.heading: multi-speaker-audio
contents.content:
Gemini TTS models do not support the speed or language options; passing
them adds a warning to result.warnings. Language is detected automatically
from the input text.

contents.heading: decision-models
contents.content:
Create an experimental decision model with google.decisionModel(modelId).
It uses Gemini structured output for Choice, Score, and Boolean questions. Choose a model
that supports structured output, such as gemini-3.5-flash-lite.

contents.heading: decision-models
contents.content:
The factory respects createGoogle settings and forwards providerOptions.google,
including thinking configuration. Thinking controls depend on the selected model;
use options supported by that model. The existing Gemini implementation sends the
answer schema as generationConfig.responseJsonSchema.

contents.heading: decision-models
contents.content:
Choice labels are returned exactly, and Scores are finite fractional positions
within the ordered rubric. The adapter validates complete answers after parsing
and rejects safety-blocked, truncated, or invalid output. It preserves usage
(including reasoning tokens), warnings, response data, and provider metadata.

contents.heading: decision-models
contents.content:
Choice and Score answers do not include probability distributions. Boolean
answers contain prompted estimates of P(true), validated to be finite and in
[0, 1]. These estimates are not guaranteed to be calibrated. Apply thresholds
in application code, for example answers.requestsRefund.probability >= 0.5. See Decisions.

contents.heading: decision-models
contents.content:
Decision models can also be accessed through customProvider aliases or

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Groq offers reasoning models such as qwen/qwen3.6-27b and openai/gpt-oss-120b.
You can configure how the reasoning is exposed in the generated text by using the reasoningFormat option.
It supports the options parsed, hidden, and raw.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Groq language models:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: reasoningFormat 'parsed' | 'raw' | 'hidden'

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Controls how reasoning is exposed in the generated text. Supported by reasoning models such as qwen/qwen3.6-27b; available formats depend on the model.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: For a complete list of reasoning models and their capabilities, see Groq's reasoning models documentation.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'none' | 'default'

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Controls the level of effort the model will put into reasoning.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: qwen/qwen3.6-27b

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Supported values:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: none: Disable reasoning. The model will not use any reasoning tokens.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: default: Enable reasoning.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: openai/gpt-oss-20b and openai/gpt-oss-120b

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Supported values:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: low: Use a low level of reasoning effort.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: medium: Use a medium level of reasoning effort.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: high: Use a high level of reasoning effort.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Defaults to default for qwen/qwen3.6-27b.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Whether to use structured outputs.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Defaults to true.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: When enabled, object generation will use the json_schema format instead of json_object format, providing more reliable structured outputs.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: strictJsonSchema boolean

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Whether to use strict JSON schema validation. When true, the model uses constrained decoding to guarantee schema compliance.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Defaults to true.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Only used when structuredOutputs is enabled and a schema is provided. See Groq's Structured Outputs documentation for details on strict mode limitations.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help with monitoring and abuse detection.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: serviceTier 'on_demand' | 'performance' | 'flex' | 'auto'

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Service tier for the request. Defaults to 'on_demand'.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: 'on_demand': Default tier with consistent performance and fairness

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: 'performance': Prioritized tier for latency-sensitive workloads

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: 'flex': Higher throughput tier (10x rate limits) optimized for workloads that can handle occasional request failures

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: 'auto': Uses on_demand rate limits first, then falls back to flex tier if exceeded

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: For more details about service tiers and their benefits, see Groq's service tiers documentation.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Structured outputs are enabled by default for Groq models.
You can disable them by setting the structuredOutputs option to false.

contents.heading: browser-search-tool
contents.content: Groq provides a browser search tool that offers interactive web browsing capabilities. Unlike traditional web search, browser search navigates websites interactively, providing more detailed and comprehensive results.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Groq transcription API
using the .transcription() factory method.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. whisper-large-v3.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 (e.g. en) format will improve accuracy and latency.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
timestampGranularities string[]
The granularity of the timestamps in the transcription.
Defaults to ['segment'].
Possible values are ['word'], ['segment'], and ['word', 'segment'].
Note: There is no additional latency for segment timestamps, but generating word timestamps incurs additional latency.
Important: Requires responseFormat to be set to 'verbose_json'.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
responseFormat string
The format of the response. Set to 'verbose_json' to receive timestamps for audio segments and enable timestampGranularities.
Set to 'text' to return only the transcribed text.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
language string
The language of the input audio. Supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 format (e.g. 'en') will improve accuracy and latency.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
prompt string
An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment. The prompt should match the audio language.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
temperature number
The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use log probability to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.
Defaults to 0.
Optional.

metadata.title: Kling AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Kling AI provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content: The Kling AI provider contains support for Kling AI's video generation models, including text-to-video, image-to-video, motion control, and multi-shot video generation.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Kling AI provider is available in the @ai-sdk/klingai module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance klingai from @ai-sdk/klingai:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createKlingAI from @ai-sdk/klingai and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Kling AI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Kling AI API key. Defaults to the KLINGAI_API_KEY environment variable.
Create one in the Kling AI developer console.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: accessKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Kling AI access key. Defaults to the KLINGAI_ACCESS_KEY environment variable.
Legacy authentication — prefer apiKey.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: secretKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Kling AI secret key. Defaults to the KLINGAI_SECRET_KEY environment variable.
Legacy authentication — prefer apiKey.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://api-singapore.klingai.com.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: Kling AI supports two authentication schemes:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
API key (recommended). A single key that is sent as a bearer token. Create
one in the Kling AI developer console and set
it as KLINGAI_API_KEY, or pass it via the apiKey setting.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
Access key / secret key (legacy). A key pair that the provider uses to
sign a short-lived JWT for each request. Set KLINGAI_ACCESS_KEY and
KLINGAI_SECRET_KEY, or pass the accessKey and secretKey settings.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
Credentials are resolved in this order, with explicit settings taking
precedence over environment variables:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: The apiKey setting

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: The accessKey and secretKey settings

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: The KLINGAI_API_KEY environment variable

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: The KLINGAI_ACCESS_KEY and KLINGAI_SECRET_KEY environment variables

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
You can create Kling AI video models using the .video() factory method.
For more on video generation with the AI SDK see generateVideo().

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content: This provider currently supports four video generation modes: text-to-video, image-to-video, reference-to-video (multi-image), and motion control.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
Not all options are supported by every model version and mode combination. See
the KlingAI Capability
Map
for detailed compatibility across models.

contents.heading: text-to-video
contents.content: Generate videos from text prompts:

contents.heading: image-to-video
contents.content: Generate videos from a start frame image with an optional text prompt. The popular start+end frame feature is available via the imageTail option:

contents.heading: multi-shot-video-generation
contents.content: Generate videos with multiple storyboard shots, each with its own prompt and duration (Kling v3.0+):

contents.heading: multi-shot-video-generation
contents.content: Multi-shot also works with image-to-video by combining a start frame image with per-shot prompts.

contents.heading: reference-to-video-multi-image
contents.content: Generate a video that combines reference images using the top-level inputReferences option.

contents.heading: motion-control
contents.content: Generate video by transferring motion from a reference video to a character image:

contents.heading: caller-managed-callbacks
contents.content:
For text-to-video, image-to-video, multi-image-to-video, and motion control,
use experimental_startVideo({ model, prompt, webhookUrl }) to register an
application-owned callback receiver. The SDK forwards webhookUrl as
callback_url, taking precedence over providerOptions.klingai.callback_url.
When webhookUrl is omitted, a raw callback_url is passed through unchanged.

contents.heading: caller-managed-callbacks
contents.content:
KlingAI sends progress notifications (task_status: 'submitted' or
'processing') as well as terminal notifications ('succeed' or 'failed').
Your receiver must filter progress notifications and correlate callbacks with
the task. Use experimental_getVideoStatus(model, { operation }) with the
operation returned by experimental_startVideo to check status and retrieve
the result after a terminal notification.

contents.heading: caller-managed-callbacks
contents.content:
These models deliberately do not expose handleWebhookOption because their
callback protocol requires a progress-aware receiver. Core
generateVideo({ webhook })
falls back to polling without calling the webhook factory. Plain
generateVideo() also polls. Workflow's existing native webhook capability
check rejects these direct provider models for webhook-based generation;
use the explicit start/status flow for caller-managed callbacks.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
The following provider options are available via providerOptions.klingai. Options vary by mode — see the
KlingAI Capability Map for per-model support.

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: mode 'std' | 'pro'

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content:
Video generation mode. 'std' is cost-effective. 'pro' produces higher quality
but takes longer.

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: pollIntervalMs number

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: Polling interval in milliseconds for checking task status. Defaults to 5000.

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: pollTimeoutMs number

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: Maximum wait time in milliseconds for video generation. Defaults to 600000 (10 minutes).

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: watermarkEnabled boolean

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: Whether to generate watermarked results simultaneously.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: negativePrompt string

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: A description of what to avoid in the generated video (max 2500 characters).

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: sound 'on' | 'off'

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Whether to generate audio simultaneously. Only V2.6 and subsequent models support this, and requires mode: 'pro'.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: cfgScale number

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Flexibility in video generation. Higher values mean stronger prompt adherence. Range: [0, 1]. Not supported by V2.x models.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: cameraControl object

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Camera movement control with a type preset ('simple', 'down_back', 'forward_up', 'right_turn_forward', 'left_turn_forward') and optional config with horizontal, vertical, pan, tilt, roll, zoom values (range: [-10, 10]).

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: multiShot boolean

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Enable multi-shot video generation (Kling v3.0+). When true, the video is split into up to 6 storyboard shots with individual prompts and durations.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: shotType 'customize' | 'intelligence'

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Storyboard method for multi-shot generation. 'customize' uses multiPrompt for user-defined shots. 'intelligence' lets the model auto-segment based on the main prompt. Required when multiShot is true.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: multiPrompt Array<{index, prompt, duration}>

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Per-shot details for multi-shot generation. Each shot has an index (number), prompt (string, max 512 characters), and duration (string, in seconds). Shot durations must sum to the total duration. Required when multiShot is true and shotType is 'customize'.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: voiceList Array<{voice_id: string}>

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Voice references for voice control (Kling v3.0+). Up to 2 voices. Reference via <<<voice_1>>> template syntax in the prompt. Requires sound: 'on'. Cannot coexist with elementList on the I2V endpoint.

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: imageTail string

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: End frame image for start+end frame control. Accepts an image URL or raw base64-encoded data. Requires mode: 'pro' for most models.

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: staticMask string

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: Static brush mask image for motion brush. Accepts an image URL or raw base64-encoded data.

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: dynamicMasks Array

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: Dynamic brush configurations for motion brush. Up to 6 groups, each with a mask (image URL or base64) and trajectories (array of {x, y} coordinates).

contents.heading: image-to-video-and-motion-control-options
contents.content: elementList Array<{element_id: number}>

contents.heading: image-to-video-and-motion-control-options
contents.content: Reference elements for element control (Kling v3.0+). Supports video character elements and multi-image elements. Up to 3 elements for I2V (cannot coexist with voiceList). Up to 1 element for motion control.

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content: videoUrl string (required)

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content: URL of the reference motion video. Supports .mp4/.mov, max 100MB, duration 3–30 seconds.

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content: characterOrientation 'image' | 'video' (required)

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content:
Orientation of the characters in the generated video.
'image' matches the reference image orientation (max 10s video).
'video' matches the reference video orientation (max 30s video).

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content: keepOriginalSound 'yes' | 'no'

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content: Whether to keep the original sound from the reference video. Defaults to 'yes'.

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content:
Video generation is an asynchronous process that can take several minutes.
Consider setting pollTimeoutMs to at least 10 minutes (600000ms) for
reliable operation. Status polls trust the configured Kling AI API origin for
the first request and validate every redirect to another origin before
following it.

metadata.title: Luma
metadata.description: Learn how to use Luma AI models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: Luma AI provides state-of-the-art image generation models through their Dream Machine platform. Their models offer ultra-high quality image generation with superior prompt understanding and unique capabilities like character consistency and multi-image reference support.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Luma provider is available via the @ai-sdk/luma module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance luma from @ai-sdk/luma:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createLuma and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Luma provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://api.lumalabs.ai.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the LUMA_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content:
You can create Luma image models using the .image() factory method.
For more on image generation with the AI SDK see generateImage().

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: You can customize the generation behavior with optional settings:

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: Since Luma processes images through an asynchronous queue system, these settings allow you to tune the polling behavior:

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: maxImagesPerCall number

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: Override the maximum number of images generated per API call. Defaults to 1.

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: pollIntervalMillis number

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content:
Control how frequently the API is checked for completed images while they are
being processed. Defaults to 500ms.

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: maxPollAttempts number

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content:
Limit how long to wait for results before timing out, since image generation
is queued asynchronously. Defaults to 120 attempts.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Luma offers two main models:

contents.heading: model-capabilities

metadata.title: MiniMax
metadata.description: Learn how to use MiniMax models with the AI SDK.

contents.content:
The MiniMax provider offers access to the MiniMax-M
series of language models through the MiniMax API, including models with
reasoning capabilities, as well as video generation with the MiniMax-H series.
API keys can be obtained from the MiniMax Platform.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The MiniMax provider is available via the @ai-sdk/minimax module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance minimax from @ai-sdk/minimax:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: For custom configuration, you can import createMiniMax and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the MiniMax provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls. This provider speaks MiniMax's
Anthropic-compatible protocol, so the default prefix is
https://api.minimax.io/anthropic/v1 — not the OpenAI-compatible
https://api.minimax.io/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: videoBaseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for video generation API calls. The video API uses
the MiniMax V2 native endpoint (not the Anthropic-compatible endpoint).
The default prefix is https://api.minimax.io.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key for the MiniMax API. It defaults to the MINIMAX_API_KEY environment
variable. Language models send it in the x-api-key header (the
Anthropic-compatible protocol); video models send it as
Authorization: Bearer.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom fetch implementation

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can create language models using a provider instance:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can also use the .chat() or .languageModel() factory methods:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
MiniMax language models can be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
MiniMax-M models can produce intermediate reasoning ("thinking") before their
final response. You control this behavior through provider options. The reasoning
output is streamed through the standard AI SDK reasoning parts.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for MiniMax language models:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinking object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Controls the model's reasoning ("thinking") behavior.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: type 'adaptive' | 'disabled'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: 'adaptive': the model decides when to reason (deep reasoning enabled)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
'disabled': the model responds directly without reasoning, for higher
throughput and lower latency

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: When omitted, the model uses its provider-side default.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Thinking control is only supported on minimax-m3. The M2.x models always
think, so 'disabled' has no effect on them.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
You can generate videos with the MiniMax-H3 and MiniMax-H3-Max models using
the experimental_generateVideo
function. MiniMax-H3-Max is the faster variant: it renders at lower resolutions
and serves every mode except reference-to-video.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
Both models generate one video per call. Generation is asynchronous — by default,
the model creates a task and polls until it completes, then returns the resulting
MP4 URL.
Status polls trust the configured MiniMax API origin for the first request and
validate every redirect to another origin before following it.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
duration accepts a whole number of seconds and defaults to 5. MiniMax-H3
supports 4 to 15 seconds; MiniMax-H3-Max supports 5 to 15 seconds. A fractional
value is rounded and an out-of-range value is clamped, each with a warning.
MiniMax-H3 supports 768P and 2K output, while MiniMax-H3-Max supports 480P
and 768P.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
The API takes a named tier rather than a frame size, so a top-level resolution
is matched against a fixed table of one frame size per tier per aspect ratio:

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content: Tier

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content: Accepted resolution values

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content: 2K

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
Anything outside the table, or a tier the selected model does not support, warns
and falls back to the model default. providerOptions.minimax.resolution names
the tier exactly and wins over the top-level value, which is reported as ignored.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
For text-to-video, aspectRatio defaults to 16:9 when omitted. The MiniMax
API requires a concrete ratio for text-only requests and does not accept
adaptive. For reference-to-video, the API default is adaptive when
aspectRatio is omitted. For image-to-video with frame images, the aspect
ratio follows the input image.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
Result URLs are time-limited. Download and persist the video to your own
storage promptly after generation.

contents.heading: asynchronous-generation
contents.content: To let the SDK manage the start/status flow, pass poll to generateVideo:

contents.heading: asynchronous-generation
contents.content:
Without poll or webhook, generation continues to use the provider's
pollIntervalMs and pollTimeoutMs options. With poll, the SDK's polling
settings apply instead.

contents.heading: asynchronous-generation
contents.content:
MiniMax does not implement the generic webhook hook. Passing webhook to
generateVideo falls back to SDK polling without invoking the factory. MiniMax's
challenge handshake and progress notifications require a protocol-aware receiver
and are incompatible with the generic SDK and Workflow webhook receivers.

contents.heading: asynchronous-generation
contents.content:
For caller-managed scheduling, use experimental_startVideo to submit one task
without polling and experimental_getVideoStatus to check it once, returning
pending, completed, or error. Persist the complete JSON-serializable
operation from experimental_startVideo and pass it unchanged to
experimental_getVideoStatus on a model with the same configuration.
Its resolvedInputs contains imageCount and referenceVideoIndices: zero-based
positions of accepted URL-video references in the original mixed inputReferences
array. Inline videos count toward the cap but are omitted from the indices;
duplicate references keep separate indices. Neither the operation nor status
metadata retains input URLs, prompts, inline data, or API credentials.
Status metadata uses these indices instead of referenceVideoUrls; ordinary
generateVideo calls without poll or webhook retain the existing URL metadata.
See the
start/status example.

contents.heading: asynchronous-generation
contents.content:
For application-managed callbacks, pass an explicit webhookUrl to
experimental_startVideo:

contents.heading: asynchronous-generation
contents.content:
Your application hosts the callback endpoint and handles MiniMax's callback
protocol; the adapter only forwards webhookUrl as MiniMax's callback_url.
The endpoint must echo the verification challenge unchanged within 3 seconds
and filter out queued/running progress updates. Handle terminal notifications
when task.status is succeeded, failed, or cancelled, then use
getVideoStatus with the persisted operation to retrieve the outcome. Neither
the challenge nor a progress update signals completion. See the
MiniMax V2 API reference
for the callback contract.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content: The generation mode is inferred from the inputs you pass:

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content: Text-to-video — prompt only.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
First-frame image-to-video — pass image (or a frameImages entry with
frameType: 'first_frame') to animate a starting image.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
First-to-last keyframes — pass frameImages with both a first_frame and
a last_frame to control the transition.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
Reference-to-video (MiniMax-H3 only) — pass inputReferences (images
and/or videos, routed by media type) to keep a subject/style or follow motion.
Frame images and references are mutually exclusive. MiniMax-H3-Max does not
support reference-to-video inputs.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
When a frame image is supplied, the aspect ratio follows the image and any
explicit aspectRatio is ignored.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for MiniMax video models:

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: resolution '480P' | '768P' | '2K'

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Output resolution. MiniMax-H3 supports '768P' and '2K' (the default).
MiniMax-H3-Max supports '480P' and '768P' (the default).

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Aspect ratio of the generated video. Overrides the top-level aspectRatio.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: referenceAudioUrls string[]

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Reference audio URLs (or mm_file:// handles) for MiniMax-H3
reference-to-video generation. Must be paired with at least one reference
image or video. Up to 3. MiniMax-H3-Max does not support reference audio.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: aigcWatermark boolean

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Whether to embed an AIGC watermark in the output. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: pollIntervalMs number

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Interval in milliseconds between task status polls. Default: 10000.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: pollTimeoutMs number

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Maximum time in milliseconds to poll before timing out. Default: 600000.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
MiniMax mm_file:// handles are only forwarded as-is for
referenceAudioUrls. They cannot be used for image, frameImages, or
inputReferences: those inputs go through the AI SDK's file handling, which
base64-decodes any string that is not an http(s):// or data: URL. Pass
those inputs as public URLs, data URIs, or binary data instead.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: MiniMax video results include providerMetadata.minimax:

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: taskId string

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: ID of the MiniMax generation task.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: videoUrl string

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: The MiniMax-hosted MP4 URL (the same URL as video). Time-limited.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: resolvedInputs object

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content:
The inputs that were actually sent, after the caps and rejections H3 imposes
(warnings report that an input was dropped, but not how many survived).

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content:
imageCount number — number of images sent (frame images or reference
images).

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content:
referenceVideoUrls string[] — the URLs of the reference videos sent.
Inline video data is omitted, since it is sent as a data URI.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: duration number

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: Duration of the generated video in seconds, when reported by the API.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: ratio string

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: Aspect ratio of the generated video, when reported by the API.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: resolution string

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: Resolution tier of the generated video, when reported by the API.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: usage object

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content:
Billed seconds, when reported by the API: totalSeconds, inputSeconds,
and outputSeconds.

metadata.title: Mistral AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use Mistral.

contents.content:
The Mistral AI provider contains language model,
embedding model, speech model, and transcription model support for Mistral
APIs.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Mistral provider is available in the @ai-sdk/mistral module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance mistral from @ai-sdk/mistral:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
If you need a customized setup, you can import createMistral from @ai-sdk/mistral
and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Mistral provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://api.mistral.ai/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the MISTRAL_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Mistral chat API using a provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. mistral-large-latest.
Some Mistral chat models support tool calls.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Mistral chat models also support additional model settings that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them as an options argument and utilize MistralLanguageModelChatOptions for typing:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Mistral models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: safePrompt boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to inject a safety prompt before all conversations.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to false.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: documentImageLimit number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Maximum number of images to process in a document.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: documentPageLimit number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Maximum number of pages to process in a document.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: strictJsonSchema boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to use strict JSON schema validation for structured outputs. Only applies when a schema is provided and only sets the strict flag in addition to using Custom Structured Outputs, which is used by default if a schema is provided.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to false.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to use structured outputs. When enabled, tool calls and object generation will be strict and follow the provided schema.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to true.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use. When set to false, the model will use at most one tool per response.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to true.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: promptCacheKey string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: A stable identifier used to improve cache affinity for requests that share a prompt prefix.

contents.heading: prompt-cache-affinity
contents.content:
Mistral prompt caching
reuses shared prompt prefixes. Set promptCacheKey to a stable workflow,
session, or conversation identifier to improve cache affinity. The provider
sends it as Mistral's prompt_cache_key request field:

contents.heading: prompt-cache-affinity
contents.content:
Use the same key for requests with the same stable prefix. Multi-step
generateText and streamText calls reuse their provider options for every
step, so a single key applies across the complete tool loop. Prompt cache
affinity is best-effort and does not guarantee a cache hit.

contents.heading: prompt-cache-affinity
contents.content:
Treat cache keys as opaque identifiers. Do not include API keys, secrets, email
addresses, or other sensitive personal data.

contents.heading: document-ocr
contents.content:
Mistral chat models support document OCR for PDF files.
You can optionally set image and page limits using the provider options.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Mistral offers reasoning models that provide step-by-step thinking capabilities:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: magistral-small-latest: Smaller reasoning model for efficient step-by-step thinking

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: magistral-medium-latest: More powerful reasoning model balancing performance and cost

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: These models return structured reasoning content that the AI SDK extracts automatically. The reasoning is available via the reasoningText property in the result:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: The SDK automatically parses Mistral's native reasoning format and provides separate reasoningText and text properties in the result. No middleware is needed.

contents.heading: configurable-reasoning
contents.content:
Some Mistral models support configurable reasoning, which you can control via the reasoning parameter.
You can use the AI SDK's top-level reasoning setting to control reasoning effort:

contents.heading: configurable-reasoning
contents.content: So far, Mistral only supports 'high' and 'none' as effort levels.

contents.heading: example
contents.content: You can use Mistral language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: example
contents.content:
Mistral language models can also be used in the streamText function
and support structured data generation with Output
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Mistral chat models support structured outputs using JSON Schema. You can use generateText or streamText with Output
and Zod, Valibot, or raw JSON Schema. The SDK sends your schema via Mistral's response_format: { type: 'json_schema' }.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: You can enable strict JSON Schema validation using a provider option:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
When using structured outputs, the SDK no longer injects an extra "answer with
JSON" instruction. It relies on Mistral's native json_schema/json_object
response formats instead. You can customize the schema name/description via
the standard structured-output APIs.

contents.heading: conversations-api
contents.content:
Use mistral.conversation(modelId) to create a model that calls Mistral's
Conversations API (/v1/conversations). It supports generateText and
streamText, including Mistral's built-in web search tools.

contents.heading: web-search
contents.content: The provider offers two tools:

contents.heading: web-search
contents.content: mistral.tools.webSearch(): searches the web.

contents.heading: web-search
contents.content:
mistral.tools.webSearchPremium(): searches the web and accesses news articles
through Mistral's integrated news providers.

contents.heading: web-search
contents.content:
Mistral executes these tools on the server. No execute function is needed.
Search calls and results are available in result.toolCalls and
result.toolResults, and URL citations are available in result.sources.

contents.heading: web-search
contents.content:
Replace mistral.tools.webSearch() with mistral.tools.webSearchPremium() to use
premium search.

contents.heading: web-search
contents.content:
Web search requires mistral.conversation(). The default mistral() factory
and mistral.chat() use the Chat Completions API, which does not support
these tools. See Mistral's web search
documentation.

contents.heading: web-search
contents.content: You can also stream the answer and access citations after the stream completes:

contents.heading: multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
Pass the previous user messages and responseMessages into the next call.
Keep the complete response history, including search calls and results, so
follow-up questions can use the retrieved information. The model does not
retain conversation history between calls.

contents.heading: multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
For streamText, consume the stream before appending
await result.responseMessages to your message history.

transcription-models
contents.content: Use Mistral transcription models with transcribe:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Mistral transcription models support additional provider options. Pass them
through providerOptions.mistral and use
MistralTranscriptionModelOptions for type checking:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: language string

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The language of the audio, such as en. Providing it can improve accuracy.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: temperature number

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The sampling temperature for the transcription.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: timestampGranularities Array<'segment' | 'word'>

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Timestamp granularities to include in the response. Mistral does not support

InvalidArgumentError when both are provided.

contents.heading: transcription-models

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: Whether to identify speakers in the transcription.

contents.heading: transcription-models

contents.heading: transcription-models
transcription-models
contents.content:
The normalized result includes transcript text, language, timed segments, and
duration when returned by Mistral. Mistral token and prompt-audio usage is
available under result.providerMetadata.mistral.usage. Segment scores and
speaker IDs from diarization are available under
result.providerMetadata.mistral.segments.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Audio is uploaded to Mistral for processing. This integration supports batch
transcription only; Mistral realtime transcription is not exposed by this
model.

contents.content:
You can create models that call the
Mistral speech API using
the .speech() factory method:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: Use a preset or saved voice ID with generateSpeech:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
The Mistral speech model maps voice to Mistral's voice_id. It supports
mp3, wav, pcm, flac, and opus output formats and defaults to mp3.
The instructions, speed, and language settings are not supported and
produce warnings when provided.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Mistral also supports one-off voice cloning with base64-encoded reference
audio. Pass it through providerOptions.mistral.refAudio and use
MistralSpeechModelOptions for type checking:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
When refAudio is provided, it takes precedence over voice. Reference audio
is redacted from request metadata and API call errors returned by the provider.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Only use reference audio with the speaker's explicit consent. Follow Mistral's
voice cloning usage policy and disclose AI-generated audio when required. This
provider integration supports non-streaming speech generation; Mistral's
streaming speech API is not exposed through SpeechModelV4.

contents.heading: model-capabilities-2
contents.content: Model

contents.heading: model-capabilities-2
