metadata.title: Moonshot AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use Moonshot AI models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: The Moonshot AI provider offers access to powerful language models through the Moonshot API, including the Kimi series of models with reasoning capabilities.
API keys can be obtained from the Kimi API Platform.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Moonshot AI provider is available via the @ai-sdk/moonshotai module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance moonshotai from @ai-sdk/moonshotai:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: For custom configuration, you can import createMoonshotAI and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Moonshot AI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls.
The default prefix is https://api.moonshot.ai/v1

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header. It defaults to
the MOONSHOT_API_KEY environment variable

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom fetch implementation

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can create language models using a provider instance:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can also use the .chatModel() or .languageModel() factory methods:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Moonshot AI language models can be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Moonshot V1 models support the standard temperature, topP,
presencePenalty, and frequencyPenalty settings. Kimi models use fixed
sampling parameters; the provider omits those settings for Kimi requests and
returns an unsupported-setting warning when they are supplied.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Kimi K3 supports toolChoice: 'required'. Kimi K2.6 and the Kimi K2.7 Code
models reject that setting, so the provider omits it and returns an unsupported
warning for those model IDs. Other tool choice modes are passed through
unchanged.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Native structured outputs are enabled for Kimi K models and the official
Moonshot V1 text, auto, and vision models.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
The provider normalizes schemas to Moonshot's supported JSON Schema subset and
enables strict schema validation by default.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For unknown custom model IDs, object generation falls back to JSON mode instead
of schema-constrained decoding.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: For best reliability, it is strongly recommended to include your schema requirements in your prompt in addition to passing the schema through Output.

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
Moonshot AI supports optional participant names on system, user, and assistant
messages. Set providerOptions.moonshotai.name on each message that should
include a name:

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
The same option works with streamText. Names are omitted when unset. The
provider ignores a name on a tool message and returns an unsupported warning.
Avoid including unnecessary personal or identifying information in message
names.

contents.heading: partial-mode
contents.content:
Moonshot AI's Partial Mode
continues the content of a final assistant message. Set partial: true in that
assistant message's provider options:

contents.heading: partial-mode
contents.content:
The partial message must be the final assistant message in the prompt. Moonshot
returns only the continuation, so concatenate the prefix and generated text
when you need the complete response.

contents.heading: partial-mode
contents.content:
Partial Mode cannot be combined with Moonshot's json_object response format.
The provider rejects that combination before sending the request. A supported
json_schema response remains available, but structured-output parsing
validates only the returned continuation.

contents.heading: kimi-k3-dynamic-tool-loading
contents.content:
Kimi K3 can load complete function tool definitions at arbitrary positions in
a conversation. Add tools to the Moonshot provider options of an empty system
message. The provider sends { role: 'system', tools: [...] } without a
content field and applies the same Moonshot Flavored JSON Schema normalization
used for top-level tools.

contents.heading: kimi-k3-dynamic-tool-loading
contents.content:
Each entry must include its complete function definition. Top-level tools and
dynamically loaded tools can be used in the same request. Known unsupported
official models omit the dynamic message and return an unsupported warning;
custom model IDs retain it for forward compatibility.

contents.heading: kimi-k3-dynamic-tool-loading
contents.content:
Keep dynamic system messages in trusted server-side state. Tool names,
descriptions, and schemas are sent to Moonshot and consume context. Dynamic
declarations are request-local, so retain earlier declarations in later
requests while those tools should remain available. Appending messages also
preserves prompt-cache prefixes better than rewriting earlier declarations.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Kimi K3 always reasons and supports low, high, and max reasoning effort.
The default is max. You can configure the effort through provider options or
the generic reasoning setting:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Kimi K2.5 and K2.6 can enable or disable thinking. Kimi K2.7 always has
thinking and preserved reasoning enabled. Keep reasoning history in multi-turn
Kimi K2.7 conversations. The reasoning output is exposed through the standard
AI SDK reasoning parts.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: log-probabilities
contents.content:
Moonshot AI can return token log probabilities for Chat Completions. Set
logprobs to request token probabilities, or set topLogprobs to request the
most likely alternatives at each token position. Setting topLogprobs
automatically enables logprobs.

contents.heading: log-probabilities
contents.content:
For generateText, log probabilities are available at
providerMetadata.moonshotai.logprobs. For streamText, the accumulated log
probabilities are included in the final finish part under the same metadata
path.

contents.heading: log-probabilities
contents.content:
Moonshot documents the request options and OpenAI Chat Completions
compatibility, but does not separately specify the log probability response
schema. The provider therefore preserves the OpenAI-compatible content
entries, including each token's logprob, nullable bytes, and
top_logprobs.

contents.heading: log-probabilities
contents.content:
Token probabilities and alternatives can significantly increase response size.
Request them only when needed, and avoid forwarding or persistently logging
provider metadata unless your application requires it.

contents.heading: video-input
contents.content: Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7 Code, Kimi K2.6, and Kimi K2.5 support video input. Pass the video as a file content part with a video media type:

contents.heading: video-input
contents.content: You can also pass a URL. Since Moonshot AI does not fetch external URLs, the AI SDK downloads the video and inlines it as base64 before sending:

contents.heading: video-input
contents.content:
Supported image media types are image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif,
image/webp, image/bmp, image/heic, and image/heif. Supported video
media types are video/mp4, video/mpeg, video/mov, video/avi,
video/x-flv, video/mpg, video/webm, video/wmv, and video/3gpp. Other
image and video media types are rejected before a request is sent.

contents.heading: video-input
contents.content:
Moonshot AI recommends videos up to 1080p. For larger videos, or videos you
reuse across many requests, upload them with the Moonshot Files
API instead. Audio and PDF inputs
are not supported by Moonshot AI chat completions.

contents.heading: file-references-and-text-files
contents.content:
Images and videos uploaded through the Moonshot Files API can be passed as
provider references. Prefix the uploaded file ID with ms:// and use an image
or video media type:

contents.heading: file-references-and-text-files
contents.content: Inline text file data is sent as a native text content part:

contents.heading: predicted-outputs
predicted-outputs
contents.content: The content can also be an array of text parts:

contents.heading: predicted-outputs
contents.content:
Predicted content is sent to Moonshot AI as part of the request. Avoid
including sensitive or proprietary text unless you intend to share it with the
provider.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Moonshot AI language models:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: strictJsonSchema boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether to use strict JSON schema validation for structured outputs. Defaults
to true.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: logprobs boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether to return log probabilities for generated tokens. Results are
available in providerMetadata.moonshotai.logprobs.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: topLogprobs number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Number of most likely tokens to return at each token position. Accepts
integer values from 0 through 20 and automatically enables logprobs.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'low' | 'high' | 'max'

contents.heading: provider-options
provider-options
contents.content: prediction { type: 'content'; content: string | Array<{ type: 'text'; text: string }> }

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Supplies static predicted output that can accelerate requests where most of
the response is already known.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinking object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Configuration for Kimi K2.5 and K2.6. Kimi K2.7 accepts only enabled
because its thinking cannot be disabled. Kimi K3 does not accept this field.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: type 'enabled' | 'disabled'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether to enable thinking mode. For Kimi K2.7 Code, only 'enabled' is
accepted.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: budgetTokens number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Deprecated. Moonshot Chat Completions does not support thinking budgets.
The provider omits this value and returns a warning. It remains accepted
for backwards compatibility.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: reasoningHistory 'disabled' | 'interleaved' | 'preserved'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Controls preserved reasoning behavior in multi-turn conversations:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
'disabled' and 'interleaved' are retained for compatibility. They do
not change the request, so the model's server-default behavior applies.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
'preserved' maps to thinking.keep: 'all' for Kimi K2.6. Kimi K2.7 and
K3 preserve reasoning by default.

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
Moonshot AI preserves provider-specific response fields in
providerMetadata.moonshotai for generated and streamed responses:

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: responseObject: chat.completion or chat.completion.chunk

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: choiceIndex: the selected response choice index

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: messageRole: the response message role, when supplied

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: toolCallTypes: the tool-call type for each returned call

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
These fields remain in provider metadata because they are specific to
Moonshot's Chat Completions response rather than shared AI SDK result fields.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content:
The Moonshot V1 series and Kimi K2.5 are unavailable to newly registered users
and are scheduled for full platform sunset on August 31, 2026. They remain
listed because they are still part of the Chat Completions API model surface,
but new applications should use Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7 Code, or Kimi K2.6.

metadata.title: Open Responses
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Open Responses provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content:
The Open Responses provider connects AI SDK
Core to language model servers that implement an Open Responses-compatible
POST endpoint. Open Responses is an open specification based on the OpenAI
Responses API.

Use @ai-sdk/open-responses for third-party or self-hosted endpoints that
implement this protocol, such as LM Studio. If you call OpenAI directly and
need OpenAI-specific provider options or built-in tools, use the
@ai-sdk/openai provider instead.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Open Responses provider is available in the @ai-sdk/open-responses module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Create an Open Responses provider instance using createOpenResponses:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: The name and url options are required:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: name string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Provider name. Used in the model's provider identifier and as the key for
provider options.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: url string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Full URL for the Open Responses API POST endpoint. Pass the endpoint URL,
such as http://localhost:1234/v1/responses, not only its base URL.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Open Responses provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: API key that is sent as a bearer token in the Authorization header.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string> | () => Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom headers to include in requests. Pass a function when headers must be
resolved lazily for each request.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: failedResponseHandler ResponseHandler<APICallError>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom handler for non-successful HTTP responses. Use this when an endpoint
returns an error envelope that differs from the default OpenAI-compatible
{ error: { message, type, param, code } } shape.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: getResponseErrorMetadata function

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Extracts optional statusCode and isRetryable metadata from a response error
object, including endpoint-specific fields. Applies to generation failures and
streaming response.failed and error events. The standard Open Responses
error fields are code and message; endpoint-specific status fields require
this callback. When only a status code is supplied, the SDK derives retryability
from it. HTTP failures are handled separately by failedResponseHandler.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: strictResponseInput boolean

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Serializes assistant history using strict OpenAI Responses input schemas.
Assistant messages without an item ID are sent as easy input messages, while
messages with a genuine provider item ID are sent as complete output items.
Defaults to false.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: customToolId ${string}.${string}

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Provider-tool ID used by provider.tools.customTool. Defaults to
open-responses.custom.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Whether JSON response formats are sent to the endpoint. When false,
structured-output requests are omitted with an unsupported warning.
Defaults to true.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: userAgentSuffix string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Overrides the default ai-sdk-open-responses/<version> user-agent suffix.

contents.heading: endpoint-examples
contents.content: For a local LM Studio server that does not require authentication:

contents.heading: endpoint-examples
contents.content: For the OpenAI Responses API:

contents.heading: endpoint-examples
contents.content:
You can use the same setup with another compatible service by changing the
name, url, authentication, and model ID.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The Open Responses provider instance is a function that you can invoke to create a language model:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The model ID is passed to the endpoint unchanged.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can use Open Responses models with the generateText and streamText functions,
and they support structured data generation with Output
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: reasoning-and-provider-options
contents.content:
Use the top-level reasoning setting to control
reasoning effort. The provider maps supported values to the Open Responses
reasoning.effort field.

contents.heading: reasoning-and-provider-options
contents.content:
The provider also supports reasoningEffort and reasoningSummary through
providerOptions. The provider option key must match the name passed to
createOpenResponses:

contents.heading: reasoning-and-provider-options
contents.content:
reasoningEffort accepts any string and is passed through unchanged to the
endpoint's reasoning.effort field. Use it for endpoint-native values that are
not part of the top-level reasoning setting, such as 'max'. When both are
set, providerOptions reasoningEffort takes precedence over the top-level
reasoning value.

contents.heading: reasoning-and-provider-options
contents.content:
reasoningSummary accepts 'auto', 'concise', or 'detailed' and can be
combined with either reasoning effort setting. Reasoning support and accepted
effort values depend on the endpoint and model; unsupported values may be
rejected or ignored by the endpoint.

contents.heading: custom-tools
contents.content:
Endpoints with OpenAI-compatible custom-tool support can call tools with raw
string inputs, optionally constrained by a regex or Lark grammar. These tools
execute in your application:

contents.heading: custom-tools
contents.content:
The endpoint must support the OpenAI-compatible custom tool,
custom_tool_call, and custom_tool_call_output wire types, as OpenAI and
QuiverAI do. These are compatibility extensions, not part of the Open Responses
2026-04-24 specification. Custom-tool results can include text, images, and files
when supported by the endpoint.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content:
The provider supports image and non-image file inputs in user messages. Images
are sent as input_image parts, while other media types, such as PDFs, are
sent as input_file parts.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: You can provide a file as inline data:

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content:
You can also set data to a URL. The endpoint and model must support the
file's media type. Provider file references, such as OpenAI file IDs, and
file data in { type: 'text', text: '...' } format are not supported by this
provider.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
Open Responses implementations can add namespaced tools, items, and streaming
events. Use Experimental_OpenResponsesExtension to encode and decode an
implementation's extension wire formats. Unregistered provider tools are
omitted from requests with an unsupported warning.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content: This API is experimental and may change in a future release.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
The AI SDK provider-tool ID uses dot notation (acme.document_search), while
Open Responses wire types use colon notation (acme:document_search). The
namespace in id must match the namespace in every registered wire type.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
Some Responses-compatible implementations document non-namespaced extension
discriminators, such as web_search, web_search_call, or
response.custom_tool_call_input.delta. These are not portable Open Responses
types. Register each exact value through the dedicated bare fields to opt in:

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
Set allowBareTypes: true when using bareToolType, bareItemTypes, or
bareEventTypes. These fields accept only non-namespaced values. They do not
enable unknown JSON passthrough: a bare discriminator is handled only when it
exactly matches a registered value. Core Open Responses discriminators and
duplicate registrations are rejected.
Use the normal namespaced fields whenever the implementation supports them.
Experimental_OpenResponsesExtension remains the namespaced interface;
use Experimental_OpenResponsesBareExtension only for this compatibility
mode.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
Set providerExecuted on each decoded tool-call or tool-input-start part.
It can vary by item or event.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content: An extension codec can define:

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
encodeTool: Encodes a provider tool. Returning undefined omits the tool
with an unsupported warning. A toolChoice that selects the omitted tool is
also omitted.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
encodeToolChoice: Encodes a specific toolChoice. The default is
an object containing the registered toolType or bareToolType.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
decodeItem: Maps a completed item to AI SDK content parts. mode is either
'generate' or 'stream'.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
encodeInputItem: Encodes tool-call or tool-result history when the original
wire item is unavailable. Returned items must include id, status, and a
type registered through itemTypes or bareItemTypes.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
decodeEvent: Maps a streaming event to AI SDK stream parts. Its state map
lasts for one response stream.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
Tool, item, and event capabilities are independent. An item-only extension, for
example, defines itemTypes (or bareItemTypes) and decodeItem without a
tool type or encodeTool. Capability fields must be provided in pairs.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
Each decoded item adds an open-responses.extension-replay custom part that
stores the original JSON in provider metadata. Other decoded parts reference
that custom part instead of copying the item. Passing result.response.messages
to a later call replays the original item once, including opaque fields. This
also preserves items that decode only to response-only source parts.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
The adapter validates only the extension discriminator fields. Validate other
item and event fields in the codec before returning AI SDK parts. The original
item is stored in provider metadata and may appear in persisted messages,
telemetry, logs, or UI payloads.

contents.heading: experimental-extensions
contents.content:
Extension callbacks cannot be serialized across workflow step boundaries.
Create the provider inside the workflow step. Serializing a model configured
with extensions throws a SerializationError.

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: Stop sequences, topK, and seed are not supported and are ignored with warnings.

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content:
The provider supports language models only. It does not provide embedding or
image generation models.

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content:
AI SDK function tools and registered Open Responses extensions are supported.
Other provider-specific tools and options require a dedicated provider
implementation.

metadata.title: OpenAI
metadata.description: Learn how to use the OpenAI provider for the AI SDK.

title.children: Typed providerMetadata in Source Document Parts

contents.content: The OpenAI provider contains language model support for the OpenAI responses, chat, and completion APIs, as well as embedding model support for the OpenAI embeddings API.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The OpenAI provider is available in the @ai-sdk/openai module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance openai from @ai-sdk/openai:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createOpenAI from @ai-sdk/openai and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the OpenAI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: batchResultDownloads object

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Settings for downloading JSON Lines batch results.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: maxLineBytes number

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Maximum UTF-8 bytes per row, excluding the LF delimiter. Defaults to 64 MiB
(67,108,864 bytes). Must be a positive safe integer. Oversized rows throw a
DownloadError and cancel the download.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
It defaults to the OPENAI_BASE_URL environment variable, and then to
https://api.openai.com/v1.
The default OpenAI model factory (openai('model-id')) uses the Responses
API. If your custom base URL only supports the Chat Completions API, create
chat models with openai.chat('model-id') instead, or use the
OpenAI-compatible provider.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: name string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The provider name. You can set this when using OpenAI compatible providers
to change the model provider property. Defaults to openai.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: organization string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: OpenAI Organization.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: project string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: OpenAI project.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The OpenAI provider instance is a function that you can invoke to create a language model:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
It automatically selects the correct API based on the model id.
You can also pass additional settings in the second argument:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
The available options depend on the API that's automatically chosen for the model (see below).
If you want to explicitly select a specific model API, you can use .responses, .chat, or .completion.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Since AI SDK 5, the OpenAI responses API is called by default (unless you
specify e.g. 'openai.chat')

contents.heading: example
contents.content: You can use OpenAI language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: example
contents.content:
OpenAI language models can also be used in the streamText function
and support structured data generation with Output
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: You can use the OpenAI responses API with the openai(modelId) or openai.responses(modelId) factory methods. It is the default API that is used by the OpenAI provider (since AI SDK 5).

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
Further configuration can be done using OpenAI provider options.
You can validate the provider options using the OpenAILanguageModelResponsesOptions type.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
parallelToolCalls boolean
Whether to use parallel tool calls. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: store boolean

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: Whether to store the generation. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: passThroughUnsupportedFiles boolean

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: Whether to pass through non-image file types as generic input files. Defaults to false, which restricts inline file inputs to images and PDFs. Enable this when the target OpenAI Responses model supports additional file media types.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
maxToolCalls integer
The maximum number of total calls to built-in tools that can be processed in a response.
This maximum number applies across all built-in tool calls, not per individual tool.
Any further attempts to call a tool by the model will be ignored.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
metadata Record<string, string>
Additional metadata to store with the generation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
conversation string
The ID of the OpenAI Conversation to continue.
You must create a conversation first via the OpenAI API.
Cannot be used in conjunction with previousResponseId.
Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
previousResponseId string
The ID of the previous response. You can use it to continue a conversation. Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
instructions string
Instructions for the model.
They can be used to change the system or developer message when continuing a conversation using the previousResponseId option.
Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
logprobs boolean | number
Return the log probabilities of the tokens. Including logprobs will increase the response size and can slow down response times. However, it can be useful to better understand how the model is behaving. Setting to true returns the log probabilities of the tokens that were generated. Setting to a number (1-20) returns the log probabilities of the top n tokens that were generated.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
user string
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse. Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningEffort 'none' | 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max'
Reasoning effort for reasoning models. Defaults to medium. If you use providerOptions to set the reasoningEffort option, this model setting will be ignored.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
Supported reasoning efforts vary by model. GPT-5.6, GPT-6 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna
support 'none', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', and 'max'. GPT-6
Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol do not support 'none'.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
GPT-6 and later models do not support temperature, topP, logprobs, or
the legacy promptCacheRetention option. The provider removes these settings
and returns a warning. Use the Responses API for GPT-6 tool calling.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningEffortUpdate 'none' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max'
Updates the reasoning effort for GPT-6 and later models starting with the
current response without changing the request-level effort. Use this with
previousResponseId to preserve the original prompt prefix for caching.
Configuration updates require standard, single-agent mode and cannot be
combined with automatic compaction or automatic truncation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
The SDK checks effort values against the selected model for both request-level
and message-level updates. For example, GPT-6 Sol and Luna support none,
while GPT-6 Astra does not.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningMode 'standard' | 'pro'
Controls how much model work GPT-5.6 performs before returning a final answer. 'standard' is the default. Use 'pro' for difficult tasks where quality matters more than latency and token usage.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningContext 'auto' | 'current_turn' | 'all_turns'
Controls which available reasoning items GPT-5.6 can reuse. 'auto' uses the model default, 'current_turn' excludes reasoning from earlier turns, and 'all_turns' makes compatible earlier reasoning available. The effective context is returned as providerMetadata.openai.reasoningContext.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningSummary 'auto' | 'detailed' | null
Controls whether the model returns its reasoning process. Set to 'auto' for a condensed summary, 'detailed' for more comprehensive reasoning, or null to omit reasoning summaries. Defaults to 'detailed' when reasoningEffort is set to a value other than 'none', and to no reasoning summaries otherwise. When enabled, reasoning summaries appear in the stream as events with type 'reasoning' and in non-streaming responses within the reasoning field.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
strictJsonSchema boolean
Whether to use strict JSON schema validation. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
OpenAI structured outputs have several
limitations,
in particular around the supported
schemas,
and are therefore opt-in. For example, optional schema properties are not
supported. You need to change Zod .nullish() and .optional() to
.nullable().

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
serviceTier 'auto' | 'flex' | 'priority' | 'fast' | 'ultrafast' | 'default'
Service tier for the request. Set to 'flex' for 50% cheaper processing
at the cost of increased latency (available for o3, o4-mini, and gpt-5 models).
Set to 'priority' for faster processing with Enterprise access (available for gpt-4, gpt-5, gpt-5-mini, o3, o4-mini; gpt-5-nano is not supported).
'fast' is OpenAI's newer name for the 'priority' tier; the two are interchangeable, and responses from
gpt-5.6 and earlier report serviceTier: 'priority' for either.
Set to 'ultrafast' for access-controlled Ultrafast processing (available only for gpt-5.6-sol).

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: Defaults to 'auto'.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
textVerbosity 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'
Controls the verbosity of the model's response. Lower values result in more concise responses,
while higher values result in more verbose responses. Defaults to 'medium'.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
include Array<string>
Specifies additional content to include in the response. Supported values:
['file_search_call.results'] for including file search results in responses.
['message.output_text.logprobs'] for logprobs.
Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
truncation string
The truncation strategy to use for the model response.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: Auto: If the input to this Response exceeds the model's context window size, the model will truncate the response to fit the context window by dropping items from the beginning of the conversation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: disabled (default): If the input size will exceed the context window size for a model, the request will fail with a 400 error.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
promptCacheKey string
A cache key for manual prompt caching control. Used by OpenAI to cache responses for similar requests to optimize your cache hit rates.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
promptCacheOptions object
Configures prompt caching for GPT-5.6 and later models. mode can be 'implicit' or 'explicit', and ttl currently only supports '30m'. In explicit mode, only content blocks marked with a prompt cache breakpoint are cached.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
promptCacheRetention 'in_memory' | '24h'
The legacy retention policy for models before GPT-5.6. Set to '24h' to enable extended prompt caching on supported models. For GPT-5.6 and later models, use promptCacheOptions.ttl instead.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
safetyIdentifier string
A stable identifier used to help detect users of your application that may be violating OpenAI's usage policies. The IDs should be a string that uniquely identifies each user.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
systemMessageMode 'system' | 'developer' | 'remove'
Controls the role of the system message when making requests. By default (when omitted), for models that support reasoning the system message is automatically converted to a developer message. Setting systemMessageMode to system passes the system message as a system-level instruction; developer passes it as a developer message; remove omits the system message from the request.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
forceReasoning boolean
Force treating this model as a reasoning model. This is useful for "stealth" reasoning models (e.g. via a custom baseURL) where the model ID is not recognized by the SDK's allowlist. When enabled, the SDK applies reasoning-model parameter compatibility rules and defaults systemMessageMode to developer unless overridden.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
contextManagement Array<object>
Enable server-side context management (compaction). When configured, the server automatically compresses conversation context when token usage crosses a specified threshold. Each object in the array should have:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: type: 'compaction'

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: compactThreshold: number — the token count at which compaction is triggered

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
compactionTrigger boolean
Request explicit server-side compaction. When true, the provider appends a terminal { type: 'compaction_trigger' } item to the Responses input. Support depends on the configured Responses-compatible endpoint and model.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The OpenAI responses provider also returns provider-specific metadata:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: For Responses models, you can type this metadata using OpenaiResponsesProviderMetadata:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The following OpenAI-specific metadata may be returned:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
responseId string | null | undefined
The ID of the response. Can be used to continue a conversation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
logprobs (optional)
Log probabilities of output tokens (when enabled).

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
serviceTier (optional)
Service tier information returned by the API.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningContext (optional)
Effective persisted-reasoning context returned by GPT-5.6 ('current_turn' or 'all_turns').

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
You can increase reasoning effort for difficult work or reduce it for routine
follow-ups while preserving the conversation prefix for prompt caching:

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
Set the initial effort with request-level reasoning and keep that setting
unchanged throughout the conversation.

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
For later changes, add a message-level reasoningEffortUpdate before the next
user message, following
OpenAI's configuration update guidance.

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
The new effort applies until another update changes it. When sending conversation
history in messages, include earlier effort updates along with the other messages.

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
Represent an update as an empty system message with
providerOptions.openai.reasoningEffortUpdate.

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content: You must set allowSystemInMessages: true to allow these trusted system messages.

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
In this example, the conversation starts at low effort and switches to high
effort for the follow-up. Both requests keep reasoning: 'low'.

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
The OpenAI Responses provider sends each message-level effort update as a
configuration_update input item.

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content: Message-level updates also work with streamText and previousResponseId.

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content: Effort updates are supported on GPT-6-family models with these settings:

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content: Setting

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content: Required value

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content: reasoningMode

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content: 'standard' (default)

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content: contextManagement

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content: Omitted

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content: truncation

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content: 'disabled' (default)

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content: Each update must use exactly content: ''.

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content:
Updates cannot be consecutive, even with the same effort. This also applies
across the boundary with history referenced by previousResponseId or
conversation.

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content: Requests that violate these restrictions are rejected.

contents.heading: restrictions
contents.content:
Effort update messages are sent even if systemMessageMode is set to
remove.

contents.heading: compaction
contents.content:
Effort updates are incompatible with automatic compaction through
providerOptions.openai.contextManagement or compaction through OpenAI's
/responses/compact endpoint.

contents.heading: compaction
contents.content:
To compact conversations containing effort updates, use explicit
compaction with
providerOptions.openai.compactionTrigger.

contents.heading: compaction
contents.content:
After compaction, add a fresh effort update before the next user message,
as OpenAI recommends. Keep request-level reasoning unchanged.

contents.heading: request-level-update-option
contents.content:
The request-level providerOptions.openai.reasoningEffortUpdate option is a
convenience that prepends a configuration update to the input. When using
message-level updates, omit this option.

contents.heading: request-level-update-option
contents.content:
The request-level option continues to warn and omit updates for unsupported
models or configurations.

contents.heading: reasoning-output
contents.content: For reasoning models like gpt-6-astra, you can enable reasoning summaries to see the model's thought process. Different models support different summarizers—for example, o4-mini supports detailed summaries. Set reasoningSummary: "auto" to automatically receive the richest level available. When reasoningEffort is set to a value other than 'none', the OpenAI Responses provider defaults reasoningSummary to 'detailed'; set reasoningSummary: null to omit reasoning summaries.

contents.heading: reasoning-output
contents.content: For non-streaming calls with generateText, the reasoning summaries are available in the reasoning field of the response:

contents.heading: reasoning-output
contents.content: Learn more about reasoning summaries in the OpenAI documentation.

contents.heading: websocket-transport
contents.content:
OpenAI's WebSocket API keeps a persistent connection open, which can significantly
reduce Time-to-First-Byte (TTFB) in agentic workflows with many tool calls.
After the initial connection, subsequent requests skip TCP/TLS/HTTP negotiation entirely.

contents.heading: websocket-transport
contents.content:
The ai-sdk-openai-websocket-fetch
package provides a drop-in fetch replacement that routes streaming requests
through a persistent WebSocket connection.

contents.heading: websocket-transport
contents.content: Pass the WebSocket fetch to createOpenAI via the fetch option:

contents.heading: websocket-transport
contents.content:
The first request will be slower because it must establish the WebSocket connection
(DNS + TCP + TLS + WebSocket upgrade). After that, subsequent steps in a
multi-step tool-calling loop reuse the open connection, resulting in lower TTFB
per step.

contents.heading: websocket-transport
contents.content:
The WebSocket transport only routes streaming requests to the OpenAI Responses
API (POST /responses with stream: true) through the WebSocket. All other
requests (non-streaming, embeddings, etc.) fall through to the standard
fetch implementation.

contents.heading: websocket-transport
contents.content:
You can see a live side-by-side comparison of HTTP vs WebSocket streaming performance
in the demo app.

contents.heading: verbosity-control
contents.content: You can control the length and detail of model responses using the textVerbosity parameter:

contents.heading: verbosity-control
contents.content: The textVerbosity parameter scales output length without changing the underlying prompt:

contents.heading: verbosity-control
contents.content: 'low': Produces terse, minimal responses

contents.heading: verbosity-control
contents.content: 'medium': Balanced detail (default)

contents.heading: verbosity-control
contents.content: 'high': Verbose responses with comprehensive detail

contents.heading: namespaced-function-calls
contents.content:
OpenAI supports grouping related function tools into
namespaces.
When the Responses API returns a function_call with a namespace, the OpenAI provider
exposes this value on the generated tool-call part as
providerMetadata.openai.namespace.

contents.heading: namespaced-function-calls
contents.content:
When using streamText, the namespace is available on the tool-input-end event and on
the final tool-call event:

contents.heading: namespaced-function-calls
contents.content:
If you persist or reconstruct messages for later turns, preserve the OpenAI provider
metadata on tool-call parts. The SDK uses providerMetadata.openai.namespace or
providerOptions.openai.namespace to round-trip the namespace back to OpenAI on
subsequent requests.

contents.heading: async-tool-calling
contents.content:
GPT-6 Astra and later Responses models support
async tool calling.
An async tool lets the model continue generating independent output after issuing
the call instead of waiting for its result. Your application still executes the
tool and sends its result in a later request using the original tool call ID.

contents.heading: async-tool-calling
contents.content: Enable async calling on a function tool with providerOptions.openai.async:

contents.heading: async-tool-calling
contents.content:
The generated tool call exposes the provider marker as
providerMetadata.openai.async. Use providerMetadata.openai.responseId as the
next request's previousResponseId, and submit the result in a tool message with
the original toolCallId.

contents.heading: async-tool-calling
contents.content:
With streamText, OpenAI can continue streaming text after the completed
tool-call part. Use the tool's onInputAvailable callback to start work as soon
as that part arrives. If execute returns the same already-running promise, tool
execution overlaps the rest of the model stream. Omit execute when the job
should outlive the current generation and submit its result in a later request.

contents.heading: async-tool-calling
contents.content:
Async calling applies to directly called function and custom tools. It does not
apply to hosted tools and should not be combined with programmatic tool calling.

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content:
OpenAI Programmatic Tool Calling lets supported Responses models generate and run
hosted JavaScript that coordinates client-side function tools. Add the hosted tool
with openai.tools.programmaticToolCalling(), then opt each eligible function into
programmatic calls with allowedCallers.

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content: allowedCallers supports:

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content: ['direct'] (or omitted): only direct model tool calls

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content: ['programmatic']: only calls from hosted JavaScript

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content: ['direct', 'programmatic']: both invocation modes

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content:
Use outputSchema to describe the JSON value returned by the function. This schema
is sent to OpenAI as output_schema so generated JavaScript can safely use the
returned fields. It does not replace the tool's AI SDK output validation or execution
logic.

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content:
The provider preserves program code, replay fingerprints, program outputs, and nested
function caller metadata across the generateText and streamText tool loops,
including stateless requests with store: false. Programmatic invocation is
currently supported for AI SDK function tools; other OpenAI tool types remain
direct-only through this integration.

contents.heading: programmatic-tool-calling
contents.content:
Treat generated programs and tool arguments as untrusted. Enforce authorization and
approval inside every tool, avoid programmatic access to side-effecting tools unless
the operation is idempotent, and set explicit step limits.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: The OpenAI responses API supports web search through the openai.tools.webSearch tool.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: The web search tool supports the following configuration options:

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: externalWebAccess boolean - Whether to use external web access for fetching live content. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: searchContextSize 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' - Controls the amount of context used for the search. Higher values provide more comprehensive results but may have higher latency and cost.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: userLocation - Optional location information to provide geographically relevant results. Includes type (always 'approximate'), country, city, region, and timezone.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: filters - Optional filter configuration to restrict search results.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: allowedDomains string[] - Up to 100 allowed domains for the search.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: blockedDomains string[] - Up to 100 blocked domains for the search.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: Omit the HTTP or HTTPS prefix from domain filters. Subdomains of configured domains are automatically included or excluded.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: For detailed information on configuration options see the OpenAI Web Search Tool documentation.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: The OpenAI responses API supports file search through the openai.tools.fileSearch tool.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: You can force the use of the file search tool by setting the toolChoice parameter to { type: 'tool', toolName: 'file_search' }.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: The file search tool supports filtering with both comparison and compound filters:

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: Comparison filters - Filter by a single attribute:

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: eq - Equal to

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: ne - Not equal to

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: gt - Greater than

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: gte - Greater than or equal to

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: lt - Less than

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: lte - Less than or equal to

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: in - Value is in array

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: nin - Value is not in array

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: Compound filters - Combine multiple filters with and or or:

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
OpenAI's Responses API supports multi-modal image generation as a provider-defined tool.
Availability is restricted to specific models (for example, gpt-5 variants).

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content: You can use the image tool with either generateText or streamText:

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
When you set store: false, then previously generated images will not be
accessible by the model. We recommend using the image generation tool without
setting store: false.

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
To use xhigh or max quality, select gpt-image-2.5-flare or
gpt-image-2.5-sunburst as the image generation tool's model:

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
For complete details on model availability, image quality controls, supported sizes, and tool-specific parameters,
refer to the OpenAI documentation:

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content: Image generation overview and models: OpenAI Image Generation

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content: Image generation tool parameters (background, size, quality, format, etc.): Image Generation Tool Options

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content:
The OpenAI responses API supports the code interpreter tool through the openai.tools.codeInterpreter tool.
This allows models to write and execute Python code.

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content: The code interpreter tool can be configured with:

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content: container: Either a container ID string or an object with fileIds to specify uploaded files that should be available to the code interpreter

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content:
When working with files generated by the Code Interpreter, reference
information can be obtained from both annotations in Text
Parts and providerMetadata in
Source Document Parts.

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: The OpenAI responses API supports connecting to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers through the openai.tools.mcp tool. This allows models to call tools exposed by remote MCP servers or service connectors.

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: The MCP tool can be configured with:

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: serverLabel string (required)

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: A label to identify the MCP server. This label is used in tool calls to distinguish between multiple MCP servers.

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: serverUrl string (required if connectorId is not provided)

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: The URL for the MCP server. Either serverUrl or connectorId must be provided.

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: connectorId string (required if serverUrl is not provided)

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: Identifier for a service connector. Either serverUrl or connectorId must be provided.

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: serverDescription string (optional)

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: Optional description of the MCP server that helps the model understand its purpose.

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: allowedTools string[] | object (optional)

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: Controls which tools from the MCP server are available. Can be:

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: An array of tool names: ['tool1', 'tool2']

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: An object with filters:

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: authorization string (optional)

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: OAuth access token for authenticating with the MCP server or connector.

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: headers Record<string, string> (optional)

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: Optional HTTP headers to include in requests to the MCP server.

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: requireApproval 'always' | 'never' | object (optional)

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: Controls which MCP tool calls require user approval before execution. Can be:

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: 'always': All MCP tool calls require approval

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: 'never': No MCP tool calls require approval (default)

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: An object with filters:

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content: When approval is required, the model will return a tool-approval-request content part that you can use to prompt the user for approval. See Human in the Loop for more details on implementing approval workflows.

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content:
When requireApproval is not set, tool calls are approved by default. Be sure
to connect to only trusted MCP servers, who you trust to share your data with.

contents.heading: mcp-tool
contents.content:
The OpenAI MCP tool is different from the general MCP client approach
documented in MCP Tools. The OpenAI MCP tool is
a built-in provider-defined tool that allows OpenAI models to directly connect
to MCP servers, while the general MCP client requires you to convert MCP tools
to AI SDK tools first.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content:
The OpenAI Responses API supports the GA computer tool through
openai.tools.computer. The model returns an ordered batch of browser or
desktop actions for your application to execute, and your application returns
an updated screenshot.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: The execute callback receives:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content:
actions - An ordered array of click, double_click, drag,
keypress, move, screenshot, scroll, type, and wait actions.
Execute every action in order before capturing the next screenshot.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content:

Computer calls and computer_call_output screenshot results are carried
