contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create xAI models using a provider instance. The
first argument is the model id, e.g. grok-4.7.

contents.heading: example
contents.content: You can use xAI language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: example
contents.content:
xAI language models can also be used in the streamText function
and support structured data generation with Output
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: reasoning-effort
contents.content:
For models with configurable reasoning, you can control how much effort the
model spends thinking before responding via
providerOptions.xai.reasoningEffort.

contents.heading: reasoning-effort
contents.content: The AI SDK option accepts these values, but each xAI model supports a subset:

contents.heading: reasoning-effort
contents.content:
'none' — Disables reasoning entirely; no thinking tokens are used. Best
for simple use cases that need a near-instant response.

contents.heading: reasoning-effort
contents.content:
'low' — Uses some reasoning tokens, but still fast. Good for general
agentic use and tool calling.

contents.heading: reasoning-effort
contents.content:
'medium' — More thinking for less-latency-sensitive applications such as
complex data analysis and long-context reasoning.

contents.heading: reasoning-effort
contents.content:
'high' — More reasoning tokens for deeper thinking. Suited for very
challenging problems, complex math, multi-step logic, and competition-level
tasks.

contents.heading: reasoning-effort
contents.content:
'xhigh' — Uses the most reasoning tokens for the most challenging tasks.
This level is only supported by grok-4.6.

contents.heading: reasoning-effort
contents.content:
Support and defaults are model-specific. grok-4.3 supports 'none',
'low', 'medium', and 'high'. grok-4.5 supports 'low', 'medium',
and 'high', defaults to 'high', and cannot disable reasoning. grok-4.6
supports 'low', 'medium', 'high', and 'xhigh', and defaults to
'high'. The grok-4.20-reasoning and grok-4.20-non-reasoning variants do
not accept this option. For grok-4.20-multi-agent, 'low', 'medium', and
'high' control the number of agents instead of reasoning depth. See xAI's
reasoning
docs and
Grok 4.6 model page for
current details.

contents.heading: priority-processing
contents.content:
providerOptions.xai.serviceTier requests higher scheduling priority, which
typically lowers time-to-first-token and speeds up inter-token latency.

contents.heading: priority-processing
contents.content:
Priority requests are billed at a premium per-token rate, and xAI only charges
that rate when the response confirms the priority tier — so read the applied
tier back from providerMetadata.xai.serviceTier rather than assuming the
request you sent is the tier you got. Omitting the option is equivalent to
'default'. See xAI's priority processing
docs.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the xAI Realtime API
using the .experimental_realtime() factory method.

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
Realtime sessions run in the browser and require a short-lived token created on
your server with xai.experimental_realtime.getToken():

contents.heading: realtime-models
contents.content:
See Realtime for the complete setup and tool
calling pattern.

contents.heading: responses-api-agentic-tools
contents.content: The xAI Responses API is the default when using xai(modelId) (since AI SDK 7). You can also use xai.responses(modelId) explicitly. This enables the model to autonomously orchestrate tool calls and research on xAI's servers.

contents.heading: responses-api-agentic-tools
contents.content: The Responses API provides server-side tools that the model can autonomously execute during its reasoning process:

contents.heading: responses-api-agentic-tools
contents.content: web_search: Real-time web search and page browsing

contents.heading: responses-api-agentic-tools
contents.content: x_search: Search X (Twitter) posts, users, and threads

contents.heading: responses-api-agentic-tools
contents.content: code_execution: Execute Python code for calculations and data analysis

contents.heading: responses-api-agentic-tools
contents.content: view_image: View and analyze images

contents.heading: responses-api-agentic-tools
contents.content: view_x_video: View and analyze videos from X posts

contents.heading: responses-api-agentic-tools
contents.content: mcp_server: Connect to remote MCP servers and use their tools

contents.heading: responses-api-agentic-tools
contents.content: file_search: Search through documents in vector stores (collections)

contents.heading: vision
contents.content: The Responses API supports image input with vision models:

contents.heading: vision
contents.content:
You can control the resolution at which the model processes an image with
the imageDetail provider option on the image part:

contents.heading: vision
contents.content: The following image detail values are supported:

contents.heading: vision
contents.content: low: processes the image at reduced resolution and consumes fewer input tokens.

contents.heading: vision
contents.content: high: processes the image at full resolution.

contents.heading: vision
contents.content: auto: lets the xAI API decide.

contents.heading: vision
contents.content: When not set, the image is processed at full resolution.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: The web search tool enables autonomous web research with optional domain filtering and image understanding:

contents.heading: web-search-parameters
contents.content: allowedDomains string[]

contents.heading: web-search-parameters
contents.content: Only search within specified domains (max 5). Cannot be used with excludedDomains.

contents.heading: web-search-parameters
contents.content: excludedDomains string[]

contents.heading: web-search-parameters
contents.content: Exclude specified domains from search (max 5). Cannot be used with allowedDomains.

contents.heading: web-search-parameters
contents.content: enableImageSearch boolean

contents.heading: web-search-parameters
contents.content: Allow the model to perform image search as a separate Web Search mode when images are useful for the answer. The model can choose between regular web search and image search; responses can include Markdown image embeds when relevant.

contents.heading: web-search-parameters
contents.content: enableImageUnderstanding boolean

contents.heading: web-search-parameters
contents.content: Enable the model to view and analyze images found during search. Increases token usage. To allow explicitly searching for images, use enableImageSearch.

contents.heading: x-search-tool
contents.content: The X search tool enables searching X (Twitter) for posts, with filtering by handles and date ranges:

contents.heading: x-search-parameters

contents.heading: x-search-parameters

contents.heading: x-search-parameters

contents.content: Exclude posts from specified X handles (max 20). Cannot be used with allowedXHandles.

contents.heading: x-search-parameters

contents.heading: x-search-parameters
contents.content: Start date for posts in ISO8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

contents.heading: x-search-parameters

contents.heading: x-search-parameters
contents.content: End date for posts in ISO8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

contents.heading: x-search-parameters
contents.content: enableImageUnderstanding boolean

contents.heading: x-search-parameters
contents.content: Enable the model to view and analyze images in X posts.

contents.heading: x-search-parameters
contents.content: enableVideoUnderstanding boolean

contents.heading: x-search-parameters
contents.content: Enable the model to view and analyze videos in X posts.

contents.heading: code-execution-tool
contents.content: The code execution tool enables the model to write and execute Python code for calculations and data analysis:

contents.content: The view image tool enables the model to view and analyze images:

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content: The image generation tool lets the model create and edit images with Grok Imagine as part of a conversation. The model decides when to call the tool, writes the image prompt, and returns the finished image alongside its text response:

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content: The tool result also contains the prompt that the model wrote for the image model, which is useful for understanding and debugging what was generated.

contents.heading: image-generation-parameters
contents.content: action 'auto' | 'generate' | 'edit'

contents.heading: image-generation-parameters
contents.content: Restricts what the tool can do. Defaults to 'auto'.

contents.heading: image-generation-parameters
contents.content: 'auto': the model can generate and edit images.

contents.heading: image-generation-parameters
contents.content: 'generate': text-to-image generation only.

contents.heading: image-generation-parameters
contents.content: 'edit': image editing only (edits images already in the conversation, including images the model generated earlier).

contents.heading: image-generation-parameters
contents.content:
The tool takes no size or format parameters; the model picks an aspect ratio
for each call. To control it, ask in your prompt (e.g. "in a 9:16 vertical
aspect ratio").

File search requires grok-4 family models (including grok-4.20) and the

contents.content: You can combine multiple server-side tools for comprehensive research:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The Responses API supports the following provider options:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'none' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Control the reasoning effort for supported models. See Reasoning Effort for model-specific values and defaults.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: logprobs boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Return log probabilities for output tokens. This is silently ignored by grok-4.20 and newer models.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: topLogprobs number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Number of most likely tokens to return per token position (0-8). When set, logprobs is automatically enabled. This is silently ignored by grok-4.20 and newer models.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: minP number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Set the min-p sampling threshold between 0 and 1. Tokens whose probability is below minP times the most likely token's probability are excluded. Unlike the standard AI SDK topK option, minP is xAI-specific and must be set in providerOptions.xai.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: maxTurns number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Set the maximum number of assistant/server-side tool turns xAI may perform within one API request. This limits xAI's internal loop for provider-executed tools such as web search; it is separate from AI SDK's stopWhen, which limits the outer loop of AI SDK steps and API requests.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Allow the model to call tools in parallel. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: promptCacheKey string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Route requests with shared prompt prefixes to improve cache reuse.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: safetyIdentifier string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Provide a stable, preferably hashed end-user identifier for safety monitoring.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Provide an end-user identifier for abuse monitoring.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: include Array<'file_search_call.results' | 'web_search_call.action.sources' | 'code_interpreter_call.outputs' | 'reasoning.encrypted_content' | 'no_inline_citations'>

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Include file-search results, web-search sources, code-interpreter outputs, or encrypted reasoning content, or disable inline citations.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: store boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Whether to store the input message(s) and model response for later retrieval. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: previousResponseId string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The ID of the previous response from the model. You can use it to continue a conversation.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: serviceTier 'default' | 'priority'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Scheduling priority for the request. 'priority' buys lower time-to-first-token and faster inter-token latency at a premium per-token price. The tier xAI actually applied comes back on providerMetadata.xai.serviceTier, and is 'default' when priority capacity was unavailable. See Priority Processing.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
The Responses API only supports server-side tools. You cannot mix server-side
tools with client-side function tools in the same request.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content: Batch support is experimental and the API may change in patch releases.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content:
The xAI provider supports asynchronous text generation through the Batch
API. Pass the xAI
provider to the AI SDK's Batch API
for the complete workflow, including polling, persistence, and result handling.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content:
Each request specifies its type and model. xAI supports using different
text models within the same batch.

contents.heading: batch
contents.content:
The xAI Batch API does not support per-batch webhooks. When you provide a
webhookUrl, the provider returns an unsupported warning and starts the batch
without a webhook.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the xAI Text to Speech API
using the .speech() factory method. xAI's text-to-speech endpoint does not
require a model identifier.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: Use xAI speech models with the generateSpeech function:

contents.heading: supported-parameters
contents.content: text string (required)

contents.heading: supported-parameters
contents.content:
Text to synthesize. You can include xAI speech tags such as [pause],
[laugh], or <whisper>...</whisper> directly in the text.

contents.heading: supported-parameters
contents.content: voice string

contents.heading: supported-parameters
contents.content:
The xAI voice ID. Defaults to 'eve'. Built-in voice IDs are 'eve',
'ara', 'rex', 'sal', and 'leo'; custom voice IDs are also accepted.

contents.heading: supported-parameters
contents.content: language string

contents.heading: supported-parameters
contents.content:
A BCP-47 language code or 'auto' for automatic detection. Defaults to
'auto' when omitted.

contents.heading: supported-parameters
contents.content: speed number

contents.heading: supported-parameters
contents.content: Speech rate multiplier from 0.7 to 1.5.

contents.heading: supported-parameters
contents.content: outputFormat string

contents.heading: supported-parameters
contents.content:
The audio codec to generate. Supported values are 'mp3', 'wav', 'pcm',
'mulaw', and 'alaw'. Defaults to 'mp3'.

contents.heading: supported-parameters
contents.content:
xAI does not expose a separate instructions field for text-to-speech. Use
speech tags in text to control expressive delivery.

contents.heading: provider-options-1

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content: Sample rate of the output audio in Hz.

contents.content:
MP3 bit rate in bits per second. Only applies when outputFormat is

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content: optimizeStreamingLatency 0 | 1 | 2

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content:
Latency optimization level. Higher values reduce time to first audio with a
quality tradeoff at chunk boundaries.

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content: textNormalization boolean

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content: Whether to normalize written-form input text before synthesizing speech.

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content: withTimestamps boolean

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content:
Return character-level timing metadata alongside the audio. The timing data
and total duration are exposed via providerMetadata.xai (see below).

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content: replace Record<string, string>

contents.heading: provider-options-1

Map of phrases to spoken substitutions applied before synthesis. Values may
be respellings ({ 'Acme Mobile': 'Acme Mobull' }) or IPA phonetics
({ nginx: '/ˈɛndʒɪn ˈɛks/' }).

per-character alignment data (only with withTimestamps). graphChars[i]
is the character spoken during the [start, end] interval
graphTimes[i], in seconds.

Input audio encoding for raw, headerless audio (pcm, mulaw, alaw).
Container formats such as Ogg/Opus are auto-detected, so do not set
audioFormat for them. opus is supported for streaming transcription only:
each audio chunk must be exactly one raw Opus packet (not Ogg), and an

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content: You can create xAI image models using the .image() factory method. For more on image generation with the AI SDK see generateImage().

The xAI image model does not support the size parameter. Use aspectRatio
instead. Supported aspect ratios: 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 3:2,
2:3, 2:1, 1:2, 19.5:9, 9:19.5, 20:9, 9:20, and auto.

contents.heading: image-editing
contents.content: xAI supports image editing through the grok-imagine-image model. Pass input images via prompt.images to transform or edit existing images.

contents.heading: image-editing
contents.content:
xAI image editing does not support masks. Editing is prompt-driven - describe
what you want to change in the text prompt.

contents.heading: basic-image-editing
contents.content: Transform an existing image using text prompts:

contents.heading: multi-image-editing
contents.content: Combine or reference multiple input images in the prompt:

contents.heading: style-transfer
contents.content: Apply artistic styles to an image:

contents.heading: style-transfer
contents.content:
Input images can be provided as Buffer, ArrayBuffer, Uint8Array, or
base64-encoded strings.

contents.heading: image-provider-options
contents.content: You can customize the image generation behavior with provider-specific settings via providerOptions.xai:

contents.heading: image-provider-options
contents.content: resolution '1k' | '1.5k' | '2k'

contents.heading: image-provider-options
contents.content:
Output resolution: 1k (default, ~1024×1024), 1.5k (~1408×1408), or 2k
(~2048×2048). Actual dimensions vary based on aspect ratio.
grok-imagine-image does not support 1.5k.

contents.heading: image-provider-options
contents.content: quality 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'auto'

contents.heading: image-provider-options
contents.content:
Image quality level. Only supported by grok-imagine-image-2.0, which accepts
low, medium, and auto. auto is the default when omitted: it serves
low for generation and medium for editing, billed at the quality served.
high is not documented by xAI but is still accepted by older models, and is
kept for backward compatibility.

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Model

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
You can create xAI video models using the .video() factory method.
For more on video generation with the AI SDK see generateVideo().

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content: This provider supports standard video generation from text prompts or image input, plus explicit video editing, video extension, and reference-to-video (R2V) operations.

contents.heading: text-to-video
contents.content: Generate videos from text prompts:

contents.heading: generation-with-image-input
contents.content: Generate videos using an image as the starting frame with an optional text prompt. This uses the standard generation path rather than a separate provider mode:

contents.heading: generation-with-image-input
contents.content: You can also pass the starting frame via the top-level frameImages option using the first_frame role. This is provider-agnostic and accepts file data (e.g. a Buffer) or a { type: 'url', url } object:

contents.heading: generation-with-image-input
contents.content:
grok-imagine-video-1.5 supports first-last-frame interpolation. Earlier
models ignore a last_frame entry with a warning. Use extend-video when you
want to continue an existing video rather than pin its final frame.

contents.heading: video-editing
contents.content: Edit an existing video using a text prompt by providing a source video URL via provider options:

contents.heading: video-editing
contents.content:
Video editing accepts input videos up to 8.7 seconds long. The duration,
aspectRatio, and resolution parameters are not supported for editing - the
output matches the input video's properties (capped at 720p).

contents.heading: chaining-and-concurrent-edits
video-extension
contents.content: Extend an existing video from its last frame. The duration controls the length of the extension only, not the total output. The output inherits aspectRatio and resolution from the source video.

contents.heading: video-extension
contents.content:
Video extension does not support custom aspectRatio or resolution — the
output inherits those from the source video. duration is supported and
controls how long the extension is (not the total video length).

contents.heading: reference-to-video-r2v
contents.content: Provide reference images to guide the video's style and content. Unlike image-to-video, reference images are not used as the first frame — the model incorporates their visual elements into the generated video. Each reference image can be a public HTTPS URL or a base64 data URI.

contents.heading: reference-to-video-r2v
contents.content: Use <IMAGE_1>, <IMAGE_2>, etc. in your prompt to reference specific images. Up to 7 reference images are supported per request.

contents.heading: reference-to-video-r2v
contents.content: Alternatively, use the provider-agnostic top-level inputReferences option. Providing it automatically selects reference-to-video mode, and it accepts file data (e.g. a Buffer) or { type: 'url', url } objects:

contents.heading: reference-to-video-r2v
contents.content:
inputReferences accepts image and audio references. Audio references must
declare an audio media type and can be supplied alone or together with images;
they are sent through reference_audios. A reference with no media type is
treated as an image. Video references are ignored with a warning.

contents.heading: reference-audio
contents.content:
Reference-to-video can also give the subject a voice. Use inputReferences for
caller-supplied audio clips, or referenceVoiceIds for up to 3 xAI preset voice
ids. Reference them from the prompt with <AUDIO_0>, <AUDIO_1>, and
<AUDIO_2>, in the order they are passed.

contents.heading: reference-audio
contents.content:
Valid voice ids come from the xAI
text-to-speech voice roster.
Ids are case-insensitive, and an unknown id returns a 400 response listing the
available voices. referenceVoiceIds is ignored with a warning when the
resolved operation is not reference-to-video.

contents.heading: reference-audio
contents.content:
Preset voices are generally available. Caller-supplied voice clips are
available to trusted partners on request. xAI accepts at most three audio
references per request.

contents.heading: reference-audio
contents.content:
Reference-to-video supports duration, aspectRatio, and resolution. Use
mode to select the operation — each mode is mutually exclusive.
inputReferences takes precedence over the legacy referenceImageUrls
provider option and can be combined with pinned frames. Reference-to-video is
supported by the grok-imagine-video and grok-imagine-video-1.5 models;
native 1080p requires grok-imagine-video-1.5.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
The following provider options are available via providerOptions.xai.
You can validate the provider options using the XaiVideoModelOptions type.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: pollIntervalMs number

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Polling interval in milliseconds for checking task status. Defaults to 5000.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: pollTimeoutMs number

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Maximum wait time in milliseconds for video generation. Defaults to 600000 (10 minutes).

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: resolution '480p' | '720p' | '1080p'

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Video resolution. When using the SDK's standard resolution parameter,
1920x1080 maps to 1080p, 1280x720 maps to 720p, and 854x480 maps
to 480p. Use this provider option to pass the native format directly.
1080p requires the grok-imagine-video-1.5 model and is available for
text-to-video and image-to-video; reference-to-video is capped at 720p
(a 1080p request is downgraded with a warning).

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Optional identifier for the end user responsible for the request. xAI uses
this value for abuse monitoring. It is sent unchanged for video generation
(including reference-to-video) and video editing requests, and is omitted
when not configured. It is not sent for video extension requests. Use an
opaque stable identifier and avoid sending unnecessary personal information.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: mode 'edit-video' | 'extend-video' | 'reference-to-video'

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Selects the explicit video operation. Each mode is mutually exclusive:

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: 'edit-video' — edit an existing video (requires videoUrl)

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: 'extend-video' — extend a video from its last frame (requires videoUrl)

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: 'reference-to-video' — generate from reference images (requires referenceImageUrls)

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: When omitted, standard generation is used. Legacy inputs are still auto-detected from fields for backward compatibility.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: videoUrl string

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
URL of a source video. Used with mode: 'edit-video' for video editing
and mode: 'extend-video' for video extension.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: referenceImageUrls string[]

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Array of reference image URLs (1–7 images) or base64 data URIs for
reference-to-video (R2V) generation. The model incorporates visual
elements from these images without using them as the first frame. Use
<IMAGE_1>, <IMAGE_2>, etc. in the prompt to reference specific
images. Used with mode: 'reference-to-video'.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: referenceVoiceIds string[]

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Up to 3 xAI preset voice ids that give the subject a voice in
reference-to-video (R2V) generation. Preset voices only — audio clips
cannot be uploaded. Ids are case-insensitive and come from the
text-to-speech voice roster;
an unknown id returns a 400 listing the available voices. Use <AUDIO_0>,
<AUDIO_1>, and <AUDIO_2> tags in the prompt to reference the voices.
Ignored with a warning outside reference-to-video. Reference audio is
documented as US-only and limited to trusted partners.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: storageOptions object

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Stores the generated video in the xAI Files API. Set filename and
optionally expiresAfter (up to 30 days) and publicUrl. Stored-file
details and storage errors are returned in providerMetadata.xai.fileOutput
and providerMetadata.xai.storageError.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: keyframes Array<{ imageUrl: string; timestampSeconds: number }>

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Up to four mid-video image anchors. Each timestamp must fall strictly inside
the video duration. Keyframes are supported by grok-imagine-video-1.5 and
are ignored with a warning for editing and extension operations.

contents.heading: audio-and-frame-controls
contents.content:
Use the provider-neutral generateAudio option to request or disable generated
audio. Use frameImages for exact endpoint frames:

contents.heading: audio-and-frame-controls
contents.content:
last_frame is supported only by grok-imagine-video-1.5. The provider emits
an unsupported-feature warning and omits the field for other model IDs. A
first_frame is sent as xAI's standard image input.

contents.heading: audio-and-frame-controls
contents.content:
Video generation is an asynchronous process that can take several minutes.
Consider setting pollTimeoutMs to at least 10 minutes (600000ms) for
reliable operation. Generated video URLs are ephemeral and should be
downloaded promptly.

contents.heading: aspect-ratio-and-resolution
contents.content:
For text-to-video, you can specify both aspectRatio and resolution.
The default aspect ratio is 16:9 and the default resolution is 480p. The
grok-imagine-video-1.5 model additionally supports native 1080p for
text-to-video and image-to-video.

contents.heading: aspect-ratio-and-resolution
contents.content:
For image-to-video, the output defaults to the input image's aspect ratio.
If you specify aspectRatio, it will override this and stretch the image to the
desired ratio.

contents.heading: aspect-ratio-and-resolution
contents.content:
For video editing, the output matches the input video's aspect ratio and
resolution. Custom duration, aspectRatio, and resolution are not
supported — the output resolution is capped at 720p (e.g., a 1080p input
will be downsized to 720p).

contents.heading: aspect-ratio-and-resolution
contents.content:
For video extension, the output inherits aspectRatio and resolution
from the source video. duration is supported and controls only the
extension length.

contents.heading: aspect-ratio-and-resolution
contents.content:
For reference-to-video (R2V), you can specify duration, aspectRatio,
and resolution. Unlike text-to-video, R2V is capped at 720p — a 1080p
request is downgraded to 720p with a warning.

metadata.title: ACP (Agent Client Protocol)

The ACP provider bridges ACP agents (like Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, and many more) to the AI SDK by communicating with them via the Agent Client Protocol and exposing them through the LanguageModel interface, enabling you to build web applications and Node.js services with ACP agents.

metadata.title: Writing a Custom Provider
metadata.description: Learn how to write a custom provider for the AI SDK

title.children: Step 1: Create the Provider Entry Point

contents.content: The AI SDK provides a Language Model Specification that enables you to create custom providers compatible with the AI SDK. This specification ensures consistency across different providers.

contents.heading: publishing-your-provider
contents.content: Please publish your custom provider in your own GitHub repository and as an NPM package. You are responsible for hosting and maintaining your provider. Once published, you can submit a PR to the AI SDK repository to add your provider to the Community Providers documentation section. Use the OpenRouter provider documentation as a template for your documentation.

contents.heading: why-the-language-model-specification
contents.content: The Language Model Specification V4 is a standardized specification for interacting with language models that provides a unified abstraction layer across all AI providers. This specification creates a consistent interface that works seamlessly with different language models, ensuring that developers can interact with any provider using the same patterns and methods. It enables:

contents.heading: why-the-language-model-specification
contents.content:
If you open-source a provider, we'd love to promote it here. Please send us a
PR to add it to the Community Providers
section.

contents.heading: understanding-the-v4-specification
contents.content: The Language Model Specification V4 creates a robust abstraction layer that works across all current and future AI providers. By establishing a standardized interface, it provides the flexibility to support emerging LLM capabilities while ensuring your application code remains provider-agnostic and future-ready.

contents.heading: architecture
contents.content: The V4 specification includes the following interfaces:

contents.heading: architecture
contents.content: ProviderV4: The top-level interface that serves as a factory for different model types

contents.heading: architecture
contents.content: LanguageModelV4: The primary interface for text generation models

contents.heading: architecture
contents.content: EmbeddingModelV4 and ImageModelV4: Interfaces for embeddings and image generation

contents.heading: providerv4
contents.content: The ProviderV4 interface acts as the entry point:

contents.heading: languagemodelv4
contents.content: The LanguageModelV4 interface defines the methods your provider must implement:

contents.heading: languagemodelv4
contents.content: Key aspects:

contents.heading: languagemodelv4
contents.content: specificationVersion: Must be 'v4'

contents.heading: languagemodelv4
contents.content: supportedUrls: Declares which URLs (for file parts) the provider can handle natively

contents.heading: languagemodelv4
contents.content: doGenerate/doStream: methods for non-streaming and streaming generation

contents.heading: understanding-input-vs-output
contents.content: Before diving into the details, it's important to understand the distinction between two key concepts in the V4 specification:

contents.heading: understanding-input-vs-output
contents.content: LanguageModelV4Content: The specification for what the models generate

contents.heading: understanding-input-vs-output
contents.content: LanguageModelV4Prompt: The specification for what you send to the model

contents.heading: languagemodelv4content
contents.content: The V4 specification supports five distinct content types that models can generate, each designed for specific use cases:

contents.heading: text-content
contents.content: The fundamental building block for all text generation:

contents.heading: text-content
contents.content: This is used for standard model responses, system messages, and any plain text output.

contents.heading: tool-calls
contents.content: Enable models to invoke functions with structured arguments:

contents.heading: tool-calls
contents.content: The toolCallId is crucial for correlating tool results back to their calls, especially in streaming scenarios.

contents.heading: file-generation
contents.content: Support for multimodal output generation:

contents.heading: file-generation
contents.content: This enables models to generate images, audio, documents, and other file types directly.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Dedicated support for chain-of-thought reasoning (essential for models like OpenAI's o1):

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Reasoning content is tracked separately from regular text, allowing for proper token accounting and UI presentation.

contents.heading: languagemodelv4prompt
contents.content: The V4 prompt format (LanguageModelV4Prompt) is designed as a flexible message array that supports multimodal inputs:

contents.heading: message-roles
contents.content: Each message has a specific role with allowed content types:

contents.heading: message-roles
contents.content: System: Model instructions (text only)

contents.heading: message-roles
contents.content: User: Human inputs supporting text and files

contents.heading: message-roles
contents.content: Assistant: Model outputs with full content type support

contents.heading: message-roles
contents.content: Tool: Results from tool executions

contents.heading: prompt-parts
contents.content: Prompt parts are the building blocks of messages in the prompt structure. While LanguageModelV4Content represents the model's output content, prompt parts are specifically designed for constructing input messages. Each message role supports different types of prompt parts:

contents.heading: prompt-parts
contents.content: System messages: Only support text content

contents.heading: prompt-parts
contents.content: User messages: Support text and file parts

contents.heading: prompt-parts
contents.content: Assistant messages: Support text, file, reasoning, and tool call parts

contents.heading: prompt-parts
contents.content: Tool messages: Only support tool result parts

contents.heading: prompt-parts
contents.content: Let's explore each prompt part type:

contents.heading: text-parts
contents.content: The most basic prompt part, containing plain text content:

contents.heading: reasoning-parts
contents.content: Used in assistant messages to capture the model's reasoning process:

contents.heading: file-parts
contents.content: Enable multimodal inputs by including files in prompts:

contents.heading: file-parts
contents.content: The data field offers flexibility:

contents.heading: file-parts
contents.content: Uint8Array: Direct binary data

contents.heading: file-parts
contents.content: string: Base64-encoded data

contents.heading: file-parts
contents.content: URL: Reference to external content (if supported by provider via supportedUrls)

contents.heading: tool-call-parts
contents.content: Represent tool calls made by the assistant:

contents.heading: tool-result-parts
contents.content: Contain the results of executed tool calls:

contents.heading: tool-result-parts
contents.content: The optional content field enables rich tool results including images, providing more flexibility than the basic result field.

contents.heading: stream-parts
contents.content: The streaming system uses typed events for different stages:

contents.heading: stream-parts
contents.content: Stream Lifecycle Events:

contents.heading: stream-parts
contents.content: stream-start: Initial event with any warnings about unsupported features

contents.heading: stream-parts
contents.content: response-metadata: Model information and response headers

contents.heading: stream-parts
contents.content: finish: Final event with usage statistics and finish reason

contents.heading: stream-parts
contents.content: error: Error events that can occur at any point

contents.heading: stream-parts
contents.content: Content Events:

contents.heading: stream-parts
contents.content: All content types (text, file, reasoning, source, tool-call) stream directly

contents.heading: stream-parts
contents.content: tool-call-delta: Incremental updates for tool call arguments

contents.heading: stream-parts
contents.content: reasoning-part-finish: Explicit marker for reasoning section completion

contents.heading: stream-parts
contents.content: Example stream sequence:

contents.heading: usage-tracking
contents.content: Enhanced usage information:

contents.heading: tools
contents.content: The V4 specification supports two types of tools:

contents.heading: function-tools
contents.content: Standard user-defined functions with JSON Schema validation:

contents.heading: provider-defined-client-tools
contents.content: Native provider capabilities exposed as tools:

contents.heading: provider-defined-client-tools
contents.content: Tool choice can be controlled via:

contents.heading: native-url-support
contents.content: Providers can declare URLs they can access directly:

contents.heading: native-url-support
contents.content: The AI SDK checks these patterns before downloading any URL-based content.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The specification includes a flexible system for provider-specific features without breaking the standard interface:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Provider options can be specified at multiple levels:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Call level: In LanguageModelV4CallOptions

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Message level: On individual messages

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Part level: On specific content parts (text, file, etc.)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: This layered approach allows fine-grained control while maintaining compatibility.

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: The V4 specification emphasizes robust error handling:

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: Streaming Errors: Can be emitted at any point via { type: 'error', error: unknown }

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: Warnings: Non-fatal issues reported in stream-start and response objects

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: Finish Reasons: Clear indication of why generation stopped:

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: 'stop': Natural completion

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: 'length': Hit max tokens

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: 'content-filter': Safety filtering

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: 'tool-calls': Stopped to execute tools

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: 'error': Generation failed

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: 'other': Provider-specific reasons

contents.content: To implement a custom language model provider, you'll need to install the required packages:

contents.heading: provider-implementation-guide
contents.content: Implementing a custom language model provider involves several steps:

contents.heading: provider-implementation-guide
contents.content: Creating an entry point

contents.content: Start by creating a provider.ts file that exports a factory function and a default instance:

contents.heading: step-2-implement-the-language-model
contents.content: Create a custom-chat-language-model.ts file that implements LanguageModelV4:

contents.heading: step-6-add-workflow-serialization-support
contents.content: To make your provider compatible with Workflow DevKit, model instances need to be serializable when they cross workflow step boundaries. The AI SDK provides helpers that make this straightforward.

contents.heading: step-6-add-workflow-serialization-support
contents.content: First, make headers optional in your config type so deserialized models work without pre-configured auth:

contents.heading: step-6-add-workflow-serialization-support
contents.content: Then add the static serialization methods to your model class:

contents.heading: step-6-add-workflow-serialization-support
contents.content: serializeModel() automatically extracts only serializable config properties (strings, numbers, booleans), filtering out functions like headers, fetch, and generateId.

contents.heading: step-6-add-workflow-serialization-support
contents.content: Since headers are not serialized, update any call sites to use optional chaining:

contents.heading: step-6-add-workflow-serialization-support
contents.content:
The deserialized model will not have auth headers. In a workflow context,
authentication is typically handled through environment variables or
request-level options available in the step execution environment.

metadata.title: Helicone
metadata.description: Helicone Provider for the AI SDK

contents.content: The Helicone AI Gateway provides you with access to hundreds of AI models, as well as tracing and monitoring integrated directly through our observability platform.
Unified model access: Use one API key to access hundreds of models from leading providers like Anthropic, Google, Meta, and more.
Smart provider selection: Always hit the cheapest provider, enabling fallbacks for provider uptimes and rate limits.
Simplified tracing: Monitor your LLM's performance and debug applications with Helicone observability by default, including OpenTelemetry support for logs, metrics, and traces.
Improve performance and cost: Cache responses to reduce costs and latency.
Prompt management: Handle prompt versioning and playground directly from Helicone, so you no longer depend on engineers to make changes.
Learn more about Helicone's capabilities in the Helicone Documentation.

metadata.title: Hindsight
metadata.description: Learn how to use Hindsight persistent memory with the AI SDK.

contents.content: Hindsight is a persistent memory service for AI agents. The @vectorize-io/hindsight-ai-sdk package provides five AI SDK-compatible tools that give your agents long-term memory across conversations.
Features include:
Five memory tools: retain, recall, reflect, getMentalModel, and getDocument
Works with generateText, streamText, and ToolLoopAgent
Infrastructure options (budget, tags, async mode) configured at tool creation — semantic choices left to the model
Multi-user memory isolation via bankId
Full TypeScript support

contents.content: Hindsight can be run locally with Docker or used as a cloud service.

contents.heading: multi-user-memory

metadata.title: MCP Sampling AI Provider
metadata.description: Learn how to use the MCP Sampling AI Provider.

title.children: Client Sampling (for clients without native support)

contents.content: The MCP Sampling AI Provider allows MCP servers to use AI models through the AI SDK by leveraging your existing client subscriptions (like VS Code Copilot). This transforms your MCP server into an agentic tool that can reason and make decisions, without requiring separate API keys or subscriptions.
The provider implements LanguageModelV4 by forwarding requests through MCP's sampling feature to the MCP client, offering unique advantages:
Server-Side AI Integration: Enable MCP servers to call language models directly through AI SDK's standard interface
No Direct Model Management: Forward AI requests to MCP clients, eliminating the need for multiple API keys
Model Flexibility: Let MCP clients decide which model to use based on preferences (cost, speed, intelligence)
Seamless AI SDK Compatibility: Support for generateText, streamText, structured output with Output, and experimental tool calling
Client Sampling Support: Add sampling capability to any MCP client with built-in helpers
Agentic Tools: Transform simple MCP tools into intelligent agents that can reason and make decisions
Learn more about MCP Sampling in the MCP Specification.

metadata.title: Neon AI Gateway
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Neon AI Gateway provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content: Neon AI Gateway is a model gateway built into Neon. A branch-scoped Neon credential gives you access to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Alibaba, and other providers. The Neon provider for the AI SDK routes each model to the gateway endpoint it needs.

It supports text generation, streaming, tool calls, structured output, and image input. Models are referenced by short IDs such as gpt-5-mini or gemini-3-5-flash regardless of who hosts them, and every request is scoped to your Neon branch.

Neon AI Gateway is in beta. To use it, you need a paid Neon plan and a project
in the AWS US East (Ohio) region (aws-us-east-2). Inference is free during
the beta. Neon documents the current availability and pricing on the AI
Gateway overview.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Neon provider is available in the @neon/ai-sdk-provider package. It requires Node.js 22 or later. Install it alongside AI SDK 7 with:

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: In the Neon Console, open your branch and create a credential with the ai_gateway:invoke scope. Set the branch's AI Gateway URL and credential in your environment:

contents.heading: setup

contents.heading: setup

contents.heading: setup

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The model ID determines which endpoint the provider uses. OpenAI models use the Responses API, Anthropic models use the Messages API, and other models use Neon's unified OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The provider accepts canonical model IDs as well as the legacy databricks- prefixed form (for example databricks-gpt-5).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Neon updates the model catalog as availability changes. Check the Neon model catalog before choosing a model ID. The catalog is also published as the neon provider on models.dev.

contents.content: For OpenAI models that support image generation, neon.tools.imageGeneration exposes the Responses API image_generation tool. Use streamText to receive generated images as tool results:

contents.content: Neon binds each gateway URL to a branch. A credential works on the branch where it was created and on branches descended from it. For example, preview branches forked from main can use a credential created on main. An unrelated branch cannot.

metadata.title: Nia
metadata.description: Learn how to use Nia with the AI SDK.

contents.content: Nia by Nozomio Labs is an API for technical, up-to-date context. It lets you index docs, repos, PDFs, and datasets, then search them with AI so your agent gets real answers instead of hallucinations. The @nozomioai/nia-ai-sdk package integrates Nia with the AI SDK through tools, middleware, and direct streaming helpers.
It is designed for workflows where you want to:
Call Nia Tracer as a tool for public GitHub and documentation research
Call Nia Oracle as a tool for grounded research over indexed repositories, docs, PDFs, and datasets
Call Nia Document Agent as a tool for deep document analysis and structured extraction
Augment an existing AI SDK model with Nia-backed middleware
Stream Tracer, Oracle, or Document Agent events directly in your app
Learn more in the Nia documentation.

accurate transcription. • It is mandatory for the saarika:v1 model (this
model does not support unknown). • It is optional for the saarika:v2
model. • Use unknown when the language is not known; in that case, the API
will auto‑detect it. Available options: unknown, hi-IN, bn-IN, kn-IN,

contents.heading: document-indexing
contents.content: Before you can use the vectorstores provider, you need to define an index for your documents. An index stores document embeddings in a vector database, enabling semantic search over your content.

contents.heading: document-indexing
contents.content: An easy way to create an index is by using the VectorStoreIndex.fromDocuments function from the @vectorstores/core package. This function will automatically chunk your documents into smaller chunks, embed them, and store them in the vector database.

contents.content: To be able to embed the documents, you need an embedding model. You can use the vercelEmbedding function (see Utilities) to use any AI SDK embedding model.

contents.heading: document-indexing
contents.content: Once you have an index, you can use a retriever to find the most relevant documents based on similarity to a given query.

contents.heading: vercelembedding
contents.content: The vercelEmbedding function adapts any AI SDK embedding model for use with vectorstores. This enables you to use embedding providers like OpenAI or Cohere within the vectorstores ecosystem.

contents.content:
You can create models that call the Voyage embeddings API

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: You can use Voyage embedding models to generate embeddings with the embed or embedMany function:

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: Voyage embedding models support additional provider options that can be passed via providerOptions.voyage:

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: inputType 'query' | 'document' | 'null'

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: Specifies the type of input passed to the model. Defaults to 'null'.

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: 'null': When inputType is 'null', the embedding model directly converts the inputs into numerical vectors.

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: For retrieval/search purposes it is recommended to use 'query' or 'document'.

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: 'query': The input is a search query, e.g., "Represent the query for retrieving supporting documents: ...".

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: 'document': The input is a document to be stored in a vector database, e.g., "Represent the document for retrieval: ...".

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: outputDimension number

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: The number of dimensions for the resulting output embeddings. Default is 'null'.

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: For example, voyage-code-3 and voyage-3-large support: 2048, 1024 (default), 512, and 256.

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: Refer to the model documentation for supported values.

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: outputDtype 'float' | 'int8' | 'uint8' | 'binary' | 'ubinary'

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: The data type for the output embeddings. Defaults to 'float'.

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: 'float': 32-bit floating-point numbers (supported by all models).

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: 'int8', 'uint8': 8-bit integer types (supported by voyage-3-large, voyage-3.5, voyage-3.5-lite, and voyage-code-3).

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: 'binary', 'ubinary': Bit-packed, quantized single-bit embedding values (voyage-3-large, voyage-3.5, voyage-3.5-lite, and voyage-code-3). The returned list length is 1/8 of outputDimension. 'binary' uses offset binary encoding.

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: See FAQ: Output Data Types for more details.

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: truncation boolean

contents.heading: text-embedding-models
contents.content: Whether to truncate the input texts to fit within the model's context length. If not specified, defaults to true.

contents.content:
If you get an image URL not found error, convert the image to base64 and pass the
base64 data URL in the image array. The value should be a Base64-encoded image in the
data URL format data:[mediatype];base64,<data>. Supported media types: image/png,

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: The following constraints apply to the values list:

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: The list must not contain more than 1,000 values.

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: Each image must not contain more than 16 million pixels or be larger than 20 MB in size.

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: With every 560 pixels of an image being counted as a token, each input in the list must not exceed 32,000 tokens, and the total number of tokens across all inputs must not exceed 320,000.

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: Voyage multimodal embedding models support additional provider options that can be passed via providerOptions.voyage:

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: Specifies the type of input passed to the model. Defaults to 'query'.

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: When inputType is specified as 'query' or 'document', Voyage automatically prepends a prompt to your inputs before vectorizing them, creating vectors tailored for retrieval/search tasks:

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: 'query': Prepends "Represent the query for retrieving supporting documents: "

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: 'document': Prepends "Represent the document for retrieval: "

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: outputEncoding 'base64'

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: The data encoding for the resulting output embeddings. Defaults to null (list of 32-bit floats).

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: If null, embeddings are returned as a list of floating-point numbers (float32).

contents.heading: example-1-embed-multiple-texts-and-images-as-single-embedding
contents.content: If 'base64', embeddings are returned as a Base64-encoded NumPy array of single-precision floats.

contents.content: See FAQ: Output Data Types for more details.

metadata.title: Confident AI
metadata.description: Trace and monitor your AI SDK applications with Confident AI

contents.content: Confident AI is an LLM observability and evaluation platform for teams building reliable AI applications in development and production.

confident-trace, Confident AI's OpenTelemetry-native tracing SDK, traces AI SDK applications without changing your calls — every generateText and streamText call shows up in the Observatory as a trace with agent, step, model, and tool spans, so you can see which tools your app chose, what each model call cost, and run evaluations on the result.
Confident AI integrates with the AI SDK to provide:
Traces with the full agent, step, model, and tool hierarchy
Token usage and cost on every model call
Threads that group a conversation's turns into one unit
Online evaluations that score traces as they are ingested

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: Tracing requires Node.js 22 or later and AI SDK >=7.0.93 <8.

contents.heading: set-your-api-key

contents.heading: set-your-api-key

For users in the EU region set
CONFIDENT_OTEL_ENDPOINT="https://eu.otel.confident-ai.com/v1/traces"

contents.heading: register-the-telemetry-integration
contents.content:
The createVercelAITracer() function returns a tracer that maps AI SDK spans onto
Confident AI's span types. Pass it to OpenTelemetry and register that once at
application startup, before any AI SDK call. init() sets up the exporter that
ships the spans to your project:

contents.heading: register-the-telemetry-integration
contents.content:
In Next.js, put this in instrumentation.ts at your project root — Next.js calls
register() for you. For Node.js applications without Next.js, run the same two
lines at the top level of your entry file:

contents.heading: register-the-telemetry-integration
contents.content: Your AI SDK calls stay exactly as they are. Every span carries the Vercel AI SDK integration label, nests under whatever span is active when the call is made, and captures:

contents.heading: register-the-telemetry-integration
contents.content: Agent and step spans — one span for the overall generateText or streamText call, plus one span per step in a multi-step run.

contents.heading: register-the-telemetry-integration
contents.content: Model calls — LLM spans with the model name, token usage, finish reason, and normalized input/output messages, including the tool calls the model requested.

contents.heading: register-the-telemetry-integration
contents.content: Tool calls — tool spans with the tool name, its input, and its result, nested under the step that ran them.

contents.heading: register-the-telemetry-integration
contents.content: Content — prompt and response text, captured by default with no size limit unless you configure one, and subject to the content policy.

contents.heading: register-the-telemetry-integration
contents.content:
Reasoning and binary content parts are marked but not exported, and raw
request headers, arbitrary SDK metadata, and exception messages are left out.
Embeddings, reranking, and the image and audio APIs are outside this
integration's scope.

contents.heading: register-the-telemetry-integration
contents.content:
Initialize once, shut down once. In a long-running server, call init() at
startup and runtime.shutdown() during graceful shutdown, after in-flight
requests and streams finish — never per request. In a serverless function,
call runtime.flush() at the end of the handler instead, once any stream has
finished, so spans are exported before the function freezes.

contents.heading: online-evals
contents.content: You can configure what happens to your incoming traces on Confident AI's workflows page.

contents.heading: online-evals
contents.content: Here's the workflows you can configure:

contents.heading: online-evals
contents.content: Evaluation rules — evaluate incoming traces against a metric collection.

contents.heading: online-evals
contents.content: Classifiers — label your traces by issue, sentiment, or any dimension you define, which lets you group or filter them later on.

contents.heading: online-evals
contents.content: Queue ingestion — route your production traces into annotation queues for your internal review team to annotate them by hand.

contents.heading: online-evals
contents.content: Dataset ingestion — ingest your production traces into datasets to reuse as test cases and iterate on results to improve over time.

contents.heading: online-evals
contents.content: You can create custom workflows for different data models like traces, spans, and threads individually as per your needs.

contents.heading: online-evals
contents.content: To evaluate a component or trace manually, pass a metric collection via updateTrace — see online evaluations.

contents.heading: trace-properties
contents.content: Use a trace context to attach attributes you know before the call starts. It creates no extra span — the trace started by generateText() inherits everything you pass:

contents.heading: group-traces-into-threads
contents.content: confident-trace provides a turn() method you can use to group sequential AI SDK calls into one turn. Reuse the same thread ID on later turns to group them into one thread you can view and evaluate on Confident AI:

contents.heading: troubleshooting
contents.content: No traces at all: confirm registerTelemetry() runs before the first AI SDK call. In Next.js, that means instrumentation.ts at the project root, not inside a route. Registering no telemetry integration disables AI SDK telemetry entirely.

contents.heading: troubleshooting
contents.content: Traces stop partway through a run: the process exited before the export queue drained. Call runtime.shutdown() at exit, or runtime.flush() at the end of a serverless handler.

contents.heading: troubleshooting
contents.content: Streamed calls arrive incomplete: finish consuming or abort the stream before flushing or shutting down.

contents.heading: troubleshooting
contents.content: Traces are missing content: check AI SDK's recordInputs and recordOutputs, and captureContent on init().

contents.heading: troubleshooting
contents.content: For anything else, see Confident AI's troubleshooting guide.

metadata.description: Monitor AI SDK calls and agent traces with Sentry

contents.content:

AI SDK v7 through the native Node.js telemetry channel, so you do not need

metadata.title: OpenAI Compatible Providers
metadata.description: Use OpenAI compatible providers with the AI SDK.

contents.content: You can use the OpenAI Compatible Provider package to use language model providers that implement the OpenAI API.
Below we focus on the general setup and provider instance creation. You can also write a custom provider package leveraging the OpenAI Compatible package.
We provide detailed documentation for the following OpenAI compatible providers:
LM Studio
NIM
ModelRush
Cheaper Inference
Heroku
Clarifai
NEAR AI Cloud
The general setup and provider instance creation is the same for all of these providers.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The OpenAI Compatible provider is available via the @ai-sdk/openai-compatible module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: To use an OpenAI compatible provider, you can create a custom provider instance with the createOpenAICompatible function from @ai-sdk/openai-compatible:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Set the URL prefix for API calls.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key for authenticating requests. If specified, adds an Authorization
header to request headers with the value Bearer <apiKey>. This will be added
before any headers potentially specified in the headers option.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional custom headers to include in requests. These will be added to request headers
after any headers potentially added by use of the apiKey option.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: queryParams Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Optional custom url query parameters to include in request urls.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: includeUsage boolean

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Include usage information in streaming responses. When enabled, usage data will be included in the response metadata for streaming requests. Defaults to undefined (false).

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: supportsStructuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Set to true if the provider supports structured outputs. Only relevant for provider(), provider.chatModel(), and provider.languageModel().

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: supportsMultiPartToolContent boolean

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Set to true if the provider supports multi-part content arrays in tool
results. When enabled, tool outputs with type: 'content' can contain text,
images, video, audio, and PDF content parts. Defaults to false. Only
relevant for provider(), provider.chatModel(), and
provider.languageModel().

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: supportedUrls () => Record<string, RegExp[]>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Defines URLs that chat models can access directly, grouped by media type.
Matching URLs are passed to the provider instead of being downloaded by the
AI SDK.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: transformRequestBody (args: Record<string, any>, warnings?: SharedV4Warning[]) => Record<string, any>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional function to transform the request body before sending it to the API.
This is useful for proxy providers that may require a different request format
than the official OpenAI API.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The optional second argument is the call's warning collection. Append
SharedV4Warning entries to report compatibility coercions or other transformations.
These warnings are returned by doGenerate and included in the stream-start
event for doStream. Existing callbacks that accept only the body continue to work.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: metadataExtractor MetadataExtractor

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional metadata extractor to capture provider-specific metadata from API responses.
See Custom Metadata Extraction for details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create provider models using a provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. model-id.

contents.content: Reasoning content - Support for models that return reasoning/thinking tokens (e.g., DeepSeek R1)

contents.heading: supported-capabilities
contents.content: System messages - Support for system prompts

contents.heading: supported-capabilities
contents.content: Multi-modal inputs - Support for images and other content types (provider-dependent)

contents.content:

contents.content:
OpenAI-compatible providers that accept the non-standard video_url content

contents.content:
To pass a hosted video URL through without downloading it first, configure

contents.content:
video_url is an OpenAI-compatible provider extension, not an official OpenAI

title.children: Start With a Growing Agent Loop
Use the Same Pattern With Core Functions

contents.content: In this guide, you will learn how to compact an agent's context by returning a new messages array from prepareStep.

The example uses pruneMessages, a built-in helper that removes selected messages and message parts. You can use any compaction logic you want. The core behavior is that prepareStep can mutate the message state that later steps receive.

contents.heading: start-with-a-growing-agent-loop
contents.content: Agents that call tools can build up large message histories. Each tool call and tool result becomes part of the context for the next step.

contents.heading: start-with-a-growing-agent-loop
contents.content: This example uses a tool that returns long results:

contents.heading: start-with-a-growing-agent-loop
contents.content: This works, but the message list grows after each tool call. If the agent reads several large documents, later steps may send old tool results that the model no longer needs in full.

contents.heading: add-a-compaction-trigger

contents.heading: add-a-compaction-trigger
contents.content: This example uses a simple token estimate:

contents.heading: add-a-compaction-trigger
contents.content: Use a real tokenizer or provider usage data if you need tighter accounting. The exact trigger does not matter for the pattern.

contents.heading: compact-messages-in-preparestep
contents.content: prepareStep runs before each model step. It receives the messages that will be sent to the model for that step.

contents.heading: compact-messages-in-preparestep
contents.content: When you return a new messages array, the SDK uses it for the current step and as the base for following steps.

contents.heading: compact-messages-in-preparestep
contents.content: pruneMessages is only one way to compact. You can replace it with your own logic when you need a different message shape.

contents.heading: understand-what-persists
contents.content: The messages parameter is the loop's current message state. If prepareStep returns messages, that changed list persists into later steps. New assistant and tool response messages are appended as the loop continues.

metadata.description: Learn how to extend your agent with specialized capabilities loaded at runtime with Agent Skills.

title.children: Step 4: Create the Load Skill Tool

contents.content: In this guide, you will learn how to extend your agent with Agent Skills, a lightweight, open format for adding specialized knowledge and workflows that load at runtime from markdown files.
At its core, a skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file with metadata and instructions that tell an agent how to perform a specific task.

contents.heading: how-skills-work
contents.content: Skills use progressive disclosure to manage context efficiently:

contents.heading: how-skills-work
contents.content: Discovery: At startup, agents load only the name and description of each available skill (just enough to know when it might be relevant)

contents.heading: how-skills-work
contents.content: Activation: When a task matches a skill's description, the agent reads the full SKILL.md instructions into context

contents.heading: how-skills-work
contents.content: Execution: The agent follows the instructions, optionally loading referenced files or executing bundled code as needed

contents.heading: how-skills-work
contents.content: This approach keeps agents fast while giving them access to more context on demand.

contents.heading: the-skillmd-file
contents.content: Every skill starts with a SKILL.md file containing YAML frontmatter and Markdown instructions:

contents.content: The frontmatter requires:

contents.heading: the-skillmd-file

contents.heading: the-skillmd-file
contents.content: The Markdown body contains the actual skill content with no restrictions on structure or content.
