contents.heading: maximum-output-tokens
contents.content: The maxTokens parameter has been renamed to maxOutputTokens for clarity.

contents.heading: converttocoremessages--converttomodelmessages
contents.content:
For more information about model messages, see the Model Message
reference.

contents.heading: content--parts-array
contents.content: For UIMessages (previously called Message), the .content property has been replaced with a parts array structure.

contents.heading: data-role-removed
contents.content: The data role has been removed from UI messages.

contents.heading: uimessage-reasoning-structure
contents.content: The reasoning property on UI messages has been moved to parts.

contents.heading: reasoning-part-property-rename
contents.content: The reasoning property on reasoning UI parts has been renamed to text.

contents.heading: file-part-changes
contents.content: File parts now use .url instead of .data and .mimeType.

contents.heading: stream-data-removal
contents.content: The StreamData class has been completely removed and replaced with UI message streams for custom data.

contents.heading: custom-data-streaming-writemessageannotationwritedata-removed
contents.content: The writeMessageAnnotation and writeData methods from DataStreamWriter have been removed. Instead, use custom data parts with the new UIMessage stream architecture.

contents.heading: custom-data-streaming-writemessageannotationwritedata-removed
contents.content:
For more detailed information about streaming custom data in v5, see the
Streaming Data guide.

contents.heading: provider-metadata--provider-options
contents.content: The providerMetadata input parameter has been renamed to providerOptions. Note that the returned metadata in results is still called providerMetadata.

contents.heading: tool-definition-changes-parameters--inputschema
contents.content: Tool definitions have been updated to use inputSchema instead of parameters and error classes have been renamed.

contents.heading: tool-result-content-experimental_totoolresultcontent--tomodeloutput
contents.content: The experimental_toToolResultContent option has been renamed to toModelOutput and is no longer experimental.

contents.heading: tool-property-changes-argsresult--inputoutput
contents.content: Tool call and result properties have been renamed for better consistency with schemas.

contents.heading: tool-execution-error-handling
contents.content: The ToolExecutionError class has been removed. Tool execution errors now appear as tool-error content parts in the result steps, enabling automated LLM roundtrips in multi-step scenarios.

contents.heading: tool-execution-error-handling
contents.content: For streaming scenarios, tool execution errors appear as tool-error parts in the stream, while other errors appear as error parts.

contents.heading: tool-call-streaming-now-default-toolcallstreaming-removed
contents.content: The toolCallStreaming option has been removed in AI SDK 5.0. Tool call streaming is now always enabled by default.

contents.heading: tool-part-type-changes-uimessage
contents.content: In v5, UI tool parts use typed naming: tool-${toolName} instead of generic types.

contents.heading: dynamic-tools-support
contents.content: AI SDK 5.0 introduces dynamic tools for handling tools with unknown types at development time, such as MCP tools without schemas or user-defined functions at runtime.

contents.heading: new-dynamictool-helper
contents.content: The new dynamicTool helper function allows you to define tools where the input and output types are not known at compile time.

contents.heading: mcp-tools-without-schemas
contents.content: MCP tools that don't provide schemas are now automatically treated as dynamic tools:

contents.heading: type-safe-handling-with-mixed-tools
contents.content: When using both static and dynamic tools together, use the dynamic flag for type narrowing:

contents.heading: new-dynamic-tool-ui-part
contents.content: UI messages now include a dynamic-tool part type for rendering dynamic tool invocations:

contents.heading: breaking-change-type-narrowing-required-for-tool-calls-and-results
contents.content: When iterating over toolCalls and toolResults, you now need to check the dynamic flag first for proper type narrowing:

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: Tool UI parts now use more granular states that better represent the streaming lifecycle and error handling.

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: State Changes:

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: partial-call → input-streaming (tool input being streamed)

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: call → input-available (tool input complete, ready to execute)

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: result → output-available (tool execution successful)

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: New: output-error (tool execution failed)

contents.heading: rendering-tool-invocations-catch-all-pattern
contents.content: In v4, you typically rendered tool invocations using a catch-all tool-invocation type. In v5, the recommended approach is to handle each tool specifically using its typed part name (e.g., tool-getWeather). However, if you need a catch-all pattern for rendering all tool invocations the same way, you can use the isToolUIPart and getToolName helper functions as a fallback.

contents.heading: media-type-standardization
contents.content: mimeType has been renamed to mediaType for consistency. Both image and file types are supported in model messages.

contents.heading: reasoning-text-property-rename
contents.content: The .reasoning property has been renamed to .reasoningText for multi-step generations.

contents.heading: generate-text-reasoning-property-changes
contents.content: In generateText() and streamText() results, reasoning properties have been renamed.

contents.heading: continuation-steps-removal
contents.content: The experimental_continueSteps option has been removed from generateText().

contents.heading: image-generation-changes
contents.content: Image model settings have been moved to providerOptions.

contents.heading: step-type-removal
contents.content: The stepType property has been removed from step results.

contents.heading: step-control-maxsteps--stopwhen
contents.content: For core functions like generateText and streamText, the maxSteps parameter has been replaced with stopWhen, which provides more flexible control over multi-step execution. The stopWhen parameter defines conditions for stopping the generation when the last step contains tool results. When multiple conditions are provided as an array, the generation stops if any condition is met.

contents.heading: step-control-maxsteps--stopwhen
contents.content: Common stopping patterns:

contents.heading: step-control-maxsteps--stopwhen
contents.content: Important: The stopWhen conditions are only evaluated when the last step contains tool results.

contents.heading: usage-vs-total-usage
contents.content: Usage properties now distinguish between single step and total usage.

contents.heading: ai-sdkrsc-package-extraction
contents.content: The ai/rsc export has been extracted to a separate package @ai-sdk/rsc.

contents.heading: react-ui-hooks-moved-to-ai-sdkreact
contents.content: The deprecated ai/react export has been removed in favor of @ai-sdk/react.

contents.heading: react-ui-hooks-moved-to-ai-sdkreact
contents.content: Don't forget to install the new package: npm install @ai-sdk/react

contents.heading: usechat-changes
contents.content: The useChat hook has undergone significant changes in v5, with new transport architecture, removal of managed input state, and more.

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content: The maxSteps parameter has been removed from useChat. You should now use server-side stopWhen conditions for multi-step tool execution control, and manually submit tool results and trigger new messages for client-side tool calls.

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content:
Important: When using sendAutomaticallyWhen, don't use await with
addToolOutput inside onToolCall as it can cause deadlocks. The await is
useful when you're not using automatic submission and need to ensure the
messages are updated before manually calling sendMessage().

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content: This change provides more flexibility for handling tool calls and aligns client behavior with server-side multi-step execution patterns.

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content: For more details on the new tool submission approach, see the Tool Result Submission Changes section below.

contents.heading: initial-messages-renamed
contents.content: The initialMessages option has been renamed to messages.

contents.heading: sharing-chat-instances
contents.content: In v4, you could share chat state between components by using the same id parameter in multiple useChat hooks.

contents.heading: sharing-chat-instances
contents.content: In v5, you need to explicitly share chat instances by passing a shared Chat instance.

contents.heading: sharing-chat-instances
contents.content: For a complete example of sharing chat state across components, see the Share Chat State Across Components recipe.

contents.heading: chat-transport-architecture
contents.content: Configuration is now handled through transport objects instead of direct API options.

contents.heading: removed-managed-input-state
contents.content: The useChat hook no longer manages input state internally. You must now manage input state manually.

contents.heading: message-sending-append--sendmessage
contents.content: The append function has been replaced with sendMessage and requires structured message format.

contents.heading: message-regeneration-reload--regenerate
contents.content: The reload function has been renamed to regenerate with enhanced functionality.

contents.heading: onresponse-removal
contents.content: The onResponse callback has been removed from useChat and useCompletion.

contents.heading: send-extra-message-fields-default
contents.content: The sendExtraMessageFields option has been removed and is now the default behavior.

contents.heading: keep-last-message-on-error-removal
contents.content: The keepLastMessageOnError option has been removed as it's no longer needed.

contents.heading: chat-request-options-changes
contents.content: The data and allowEmptySubmit options have been removed from ChatRequestOptions.

contents.heading: request-options-type-rename
contents.content: RequestOptions has been renamed to CompletionRequestOptions.

contents.heading: addtoolresult-renamed-to-addtooloutput
contents.content: The addToolResult method has been renamed to addToolOutput. Additionally, the result parameter has been renamed to output for consistency with other tool-related APIs.

contents.heading: addtoolresult-renamed-to-addtooloutput
contents.content:
addToolResult is still available but deprecated. It will be removed in
version 6.

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: The automatic tool result submission behavior has been updated in useChat and the Chat component. You now have more control and flexibility over when tool results are submitted.

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: onToolCall no longer supports returning values to automatically submit tool results

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: You must explicitly call addToolOutput to provide tool results

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: Use sendAutomaticallyWhen with lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls helper for automatic submission

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: Important: Don't use await with addToolOutput inside onToolCall to avoid deadlocks

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: The maxSteps parameter has been removed from the Chat component and useChat hook

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: For multi-step tool execution, use server-side stopWhen conditions instead (see maxSteps Removal)

contents.heading: loading-state-changes
contents.content: The deprecated isLoading helper has been removed in favor of status.

contents.heading: resume-stream-support
contents.content: The resume functionality has been moved from experimental_resume to resumeStream.

contents.heading: dynamic-body-values
contents.content: In v4, the body option in useChat configuration would dynamically update with component state changes. In v5, the body value is only captured at the first render and remains static throughout the component lifecycle.

contents.heading: dynamic-body-values
contents.content: For more details on request configuration, see the Chatbot guide.

contents.heading: usage-information
contents.content: In v4, usage information was directly accessible through the onFinish callback's options parameter. In v5, usage data is attached as metadata to individual messages using the messageMetadata function in toUIMessageStreamResponse.

contents.heading: usage-information
contents.content: Then, on the client, you can access the message-level metadata.

contents.heading: usage-information
contents.content: You can also access your metadata from the onFinish callback of useChat:

contents.heading: request-body-preparation-experimental_preparerequestbody--preparesendmessagesrequest
contents.content: The experimental_prepareRequestBody option has been replaced with prepareSendMessagesRequest in the transport configuration.

contents.heading: ai-sdkvue-changes
contents.content: The Vue.js integration has been completely restructured, replacing the useChat composable with a Chat class.

contents.heading: message-structure-changes
contents.content: Messages now use a parts array instead of a content string.

contents.heading: ai-sdksvelte-changes
contents.content: The Svelte integration has also been updated with new constructor patterns and readonly properties.

contents.heading: properties-made-readonly
contents.content: Properties are now readonly and must be updated using setter methods.

contents.heading: removed-managed-input
contents.content: Like React and Vue, input management has been removed from the Svelte integration.

contents.heading: ai-sdkui-utils-package-removal
contents.content: The @ai-sdk/ui-utils package has been removed and its exports moved to the main ai package.

contents.heading: ai-sdkui-utils-package-removal
contents.content: Note: processDataStream was removed entirely in v5.0. Use readUIMessageStream instead for processing UI message streams, or use the more configurable Chat/useChat APIs for most use cases.

contents.heading: usecompletion-changes
contents.content: The data property has been removed from the useCompletion hook.

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content: The useAssistant hook has been removed.

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content:
The useAssistant hook was specific to the OpenAI Assistants API. OpenAI has
deprecated that API in favor of the Responses API. Configure useChat for your
route as shown above, then return a UI message stream from the route:

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content:
For persistent conversation state and built-in tools, see the
OpenAI Responses API guide.

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content:
If you need to connect useChat to another backend, see the
transport documentation and
stream protocol. For migrating existing
OpenAI Assistants data and API calls, see OpenAI's
Assistants migration guide.

contents.heading: attachments--file-parts
contents.content: The experimental_attachments property has been replaced with the parts array.

contents.heading: attachments--file-parts
contents.content:
Some models do not support text files (text/plain, text/markdown, text/csv,
etc.) as file parts. For text files, you can read and send the context as a text part
instead:

contents.heading: provider-options-for-embeddings
contents.content: Embedding model settings now use provider options instead of model parameters.

contents.heading: raw-response--response
contents.content: The rawResponse property has been renamed to response.

contents.heading: parallel-requests-in-embedmany
contents.content: embedMany now makes parallel requests with a configurable maxParallelCalls option.

contents.heading: langchain-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdklangchain
contents.content: The LangChainAdapter has been moved to @ai-sdk/langchain and the API has been updated to use UI message streams.

contents.heading: langchain-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdklangchain
contents.content: Don't forget to install the new package: npm install @ai-sdk/langchain

contents.heading: llamaindex-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdkllamaindex
contents.content: The LlamaIndexAdapter has been extracted to a separate package @ai-sdk/llamaindex and follows the same UI message stream pattern.

contents.heading: llamaindex-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdkllamaindex
contents.content: Don't forget to install the new package: npm install @ai-sdk/llamaindex

contents.heading: streaming-architecture
contents.content: The streaming architecture has been completely redesigned in v5 to support better content differentiation, concurrent streaming of multiple parts, and improved real-time UX.

contents.heading: stream-protocol-single-chunks--startdeltaend-pattern
contents.content: The fundamental streaming pattern has changed from single chunks to a three-phase pattern with unique IDs for each content block.

contents.heading: reasoning-streaming-pattern
contents.content: Reasoning content now follows the same start/delta/end pattern:

contents.heading: tool-input-streaming
contents.content: Tool inputs can now be streamed as they're being generated:

contents.heading: onchunk-callback-changes
contents.content: The onChunk callback now receives the new streaming chunk types with IDs and the start/delta/end pattern.

contents.heading: file-stream-parts-restructure
contents.content: File parts in streams have been flattened.

contents.heading: source-stream-parts-restructure
contents.content: Source stream parts have been flattened.

contents.heading: finish-event-changes
contents.content: Stream finish events have been renamed for consistency.

contents.heading: proprietary-protocol---server-sent-events
contents.content: The data stream protocol has been updated to use Server-Sent Events.

contents.heading: data-stream-response-helper-functions-renamed
contents.content: The streaming API has been completely restructured from data streams to UI message streams.

contents.heading: stream-transform-function-renaming
contents.content: Various stream-related functions have been renamed for consistency.

contents.heading: error-handling-geterrormessage--onerror
contents.content: The getErrorMessage option in toDataStreamResponse has been replaced with onError in toUIMessageStreamResponse, providing more control over error forwarding to the client.

contents.heading: error-handling-geterrormessage--onerror
contents.content: By default, error messages are NOT sent to the client to prevent leaking sensitive information. The onError callback allows you to explicitly control what error information is forwarded to the client.

contents.heading: id-generation-changes
contents.content: The createIdGenerator() function now requires a size argument.

contents.heading: idgenerator--idgenerator
contents.content: The type name has been updated.

contents.heading: language-model-v2-import
contents.content: LanguageModelV3 must now be imported from @ai-sdk/provider.

contents.heading: middleware-rename
contents.content: LanguageModelV1Middleware has been renamed and moved.

contents.heading: usage-token-properties
contents.content: Token usage properties have been renamed for consistency.

contents.heading: stream-part-type-changes
contents.content: The LanguageModelV3StreamPart type has been expanded to support the new streaming architecture with start/delta/end patterns and IDs.

contents.heading: raw-response--response-1
contents.content: Provider response objects have been updated.

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: The experimental_prepareStep option has been promoted and no longer requires the experimental prefix.

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: The prepareStep function receives { steps, stepNumber, model } and can return:

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: model: Different model for this step

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: activeTools: Which tools to make available

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: toolChoice: Tool selection strategy

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: system: System message for this step

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: undefined: Use default settings

contents.heading: temperature-default-removal
contents.content: Temperature is no longer set to 0 by default.

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content:
If you have persisted messages in a database, see the Data Migration
Guide for comprehensive
guidance on migrating your stored message data to the v5 format.

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content: In v4, you would typically use helper functions like appendResponseMessages or appendClientMessage to format messages in the onFinish callback of streamText:

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content: In v5, message persistence is now handled through the toUIMessageStreamResponse method, which automatically formats response messages in the UIMessage format:

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content:
Important: When using toUIMessageStreamResponse, you should always
provide both originalMessages and generateMessageId parameters. Without
these, you may experience duplicate or repeated assistant messages in your UI.
For more details, see Troubleshooting: Repeated Assistant
Messages.

contents.heading: message-id-generation
contents.content: The experimental_generateMessageId option has been moved from streamText configuration to toUIMessageStreamResponse, as it's designed for use with UIMessages rather than ModelMessages.

contents.heading: message-id-generation
contents.content: For more details on message IDs and persistence, see the Chatbot Message Persistence guide.

contents.heading: using-createuimessagestream
contents.content: For more complex scenarios, especially when working with data parts, you can use createUIMessageStream:

contents.heading: default-provider-instance-uses-responses-api
contents.content: In AI SDK 5, the default OpenAI provider instance uses the Responses API, while AI SDK 4 used the Chat Completions API. The Chat Completions API remains fully supported and you can use it with openai.chat(...).

contents.heading: default-provider-instance-uses-responses-api
contents.content:
The Responses and Chat Completions APIs have different behavior and defaults.
If you depend on the Chat Completions API, switch your model instance to
openai.chat(...) and audit your configuration.

contents.heading: strict-schemas-strictschemas-with-responses-api
contents.content: In AI SDK 4.0, you could set the strictSchemas option on Responses models (which defaulted to true). This option has been renamed to strictJsonSchema in AI SDK 5.0 and now defaults to false.

contents.heading: strict-schemas-strictschemas-with-responses-api
contents.content: If you call openai.chat(...) to use the Chat Completions API directly, you can type it with OpenAIChatLanguageModelOptions. AI SDK 5 adds the same strictJsonSchema option there as well.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: The structuredOutputs option is now configured using provider options rather than as a setting on the model instance.

contents.heading: compatibility-option-removal
contents.content: The compatibility option has been removed; strict compatibility mode is now the default.

contents.heading: legacy-function-calls-removal
contents.content: The useLegacyFunctionCalls option has been removed.

contents.heading: simulate-streaming
contents.content: The simulateStreaming model option has been replaced with middleware.

contents.heading: search-grounding-is-now-a-provider-defined-tool
contents.content: Search Grounding is now called "Google Search" and is now a provider defined tool.

contents.heading: snake-case--camel-case
contents.content: Provider options have been updated to use camelCase.

contents.heading: provider-utils-changes
contents.content: Deprecated CoreTool* types have been removed.

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: If you experience TypeScript server crashes, slow type checking, or errors like "Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite" when using Zod with AI SDK 5.0:

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: First, ensure you're using Zod 4.1.8 or later - this version includes a fix for module resolution issues that cause TypeScript performance problems.

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: If the issue persists, update your tsconfig.json to use moduleResolution: "nodenext":

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: This resolves the TypeScript performance issues while allowing you to continue using the standard Zod import. If this doesn't resolve the issue, you can try using a version-specific import path as an alternative solution. For detailed troubleshooting steps, see TypeScript performance issues with Zod.

metadata.title: Versioning
metadata.description: Understand how the AI SDK approaches versioning.

contents.content: Each version number follows the format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
Major: Breaking API updates that require code changes.
Minor: Blog post that aggregates new features and improvements into a public release that highlights benefits.
Patch: New features and bug fixes.

contents.heading: api-stability
contents.content: We communicate the stability of our APIs as follows:

contents.heading: stable-apis
contents.content: All APIs without special prefixes are considered stable and ready for production use. We maintain backward compatibility for stable features and only introduce breaking changes in major releases.

contents.heading: experimental-apis
contents.content: APIs prefixed with experimental_ or Experimental_ (e.g. experimental_generateImage()) are in development and can change in any releases. To use experimental APIs safely:

contents.heading: experimental-apis
contents.content: Test them first in development, not production

contents.heading: experimental-apis
contents.content: Review release notes before upgrading

contents.heading: experimental-apis
contents.content: Prepare for potential code updates

contents.heading: experimental-apis
contents.content:
If you use experimental APIs, make sure to pin your AI SDK version number
exactly (avoid using ^ or ~ version ranges) to prevent unexpected breaking
changes.

contents.heading: deprecated-apis
contents.content: APIs marked as deprecated will be removed in future major releases. You can wait until the major release to update your code. To handle deprecations:

contents.heading: deprecated-apis
contents.content: Switch to the recommended alternative API

contents.heading: deprecated-apis
contents.content: Follow the migration guide (released alongside major releases)

contents.heading: deprecated-apis
contents.content:
For major releases, we provide automated codemods where possible to help
migrate your code to the new version.

metadata.title: Agent (Interface)
metadata.description: API Reference for the Agent interface.

contents.content: The Agent interface defines a contract for agents that can generate or stream AI-generated responses in response to prompts. Agents may encapsulate advanced logic such as tool usage, multi-step workflows, or prompt handling, enabling both simple and autonomous AI agents.

Implementations of the Agent interface—such as ToolLoopAgent—fulfill the same contract and integrate seamlessly with all SDK APIs and utilities that expect an agent. This design allows users to supply custom agent classes or wrappers for third-party chains, while maximizing compatibility with AI SDK features.

metadata.title: cosineSimilarity
metadata.description: Calculate the cosine similarity between two vectors (API Reference)

contents.content:
When you want to compare the similarity of embeddings, standard vector similarity metrics
like cosine similarity are often used.

cosineSimilarity calculates the cosine similarity between two vectors.
A high value (close to 1) indicates that the vectors are very similar, while a low value (close to -1) indicates that they are different.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: A number between -1 and 1 representing the cosine similarity between the two vectors.

metadata.title: createAgentUIStreamResponse
metadata.description: API Reference for the createAgentUIStreamResponse utility.

contents.content: The createAgentUIStreamResponse function executes an Agent, runs its streaming output as a UI message stream, and returns an HTTP Response object whose body is the live, streaming UI message output. This is designed for API routes that deliver real-time agent results, such as chat endpoints or streaming tool-use operations.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: A Promise<Response> whose body is a streaming UI message output from the agent. Use this as the return value of API/server handlers in serverless, Next.js, Express, Hono, or edge runtime contexts.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: UI Message Validation: Validates the incoming uiMessages array according to the agent's specified tools and requirements.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Model Message Conversion: Converts validated UI messages into the internal model message format for the agent.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Streaming Agent Output: Invokes the agent’s .stream({ prompt, ... }) to get a stream of chunks (steps/UI messages).

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: HTTP Response Creation: Wraps the output stream as a readable HTTP Response object that streams UI message chunks to the client.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Your agent must implement .stream({ prompt, ... }) and define a tools property (even if it's just {}) to work with this function.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Server Only: This API should only be called in backend/server-side contexts (API routes, edge/serverless/server route handlers, etc.). Not for browser use.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Additional options (headers, status, UI stream options, transforms, etc.) are available for advanced scenarios.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: This leverages ReadableStream so your platform/client must support HTTP streaming consumption.

metadata.title: createAgentUIStream
metadata.description: API Reference for the createAgentUIStream utility.

contents.content: The createAgentUIStream function executes an Agent, consumes an array of UI messages, and streams the agent's output as UI message chunks via an async iterable. This enables real-time, incremental rendering of AI assistant output with full access to tool use, intermediate reasoning, and interactive UI features in your own runtime—perfect for building chat APIs, dashboards, or bots powered by agents.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: A Promise<AsyncIterableStream<UIMessageChunk>>, where each yielded chunk is a UI message output from the agent (see UIMessage). This can be consumed with any async iterator loop, or piped to a streaming HTTP response, socket, or any other sink.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: UI Message Validation: The input uiMessages array is validated and normalized using the agent's tools definition. Any invalid messages cause an error.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Conversion to Model Messages: The validated UI messages are converted into model-specific message format, as required by the agent.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Agent Streaming: The agent's .stream({ prompt, ... }) method is invoked with the converted model messages, optional call options, abort signal, and any experimental transforms.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: UI Message Stream Building: The result stream is converted and exposed as a streaming async iterable of UI message chunks for you to consume.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The agent must implement the .stream({ prompt, ... }) method and define its supported tools property.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: This utility returns an async iterable for maximal streaming flexibility. For HTTP responses, see createAgentUIStreamResponse (Web) or pipeAgentUIStreamToResponse (Node.js).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The uiMessages parameter is named uiMessages, not just messages.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: You can provide advanced options via UIMessageStreamOptions (for example, to include sources or usage).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: To cancel the stream, pass an AbortSignal via the abortSignal parameter.

metadata.title: embedMany
metadata.description: API Reference for embedMany.

contents.content: Embed several values using an embedding model.

embedMany automatically splits large requests into smaller chunks when the
model has a limit on either the number of embeddings or the UTF-8 input bytes
that can be processed in a single call. Providers can use a conservative byte
budget to keep requests below aggregate token limits without adding a tokenizer
to the AI SDK core package. An individual value larger than the byte budget is
sent in its own call because splitting it would change the resulting embedding.

metadata.title: embed
metadata.description: API Reference for embed.

contents.content: Generate an embedding for a single value using an embedding model.
This is ideal for use cases where you need to embed a single value to e.g. retrieve similar items or to use the embedding in a downstream task.

jsonSchema is a helper function that creates a JSON schema object that is compatible with the AI SDK.
It takes the JSON schema and an optional validation function as inputs, and can be typed.

See Language Model Middleware for more information.

metadata.title: isLoopFinished
metadata.description: API Reference for isLoopFinished.

contents.content: Creates a stop condition that never triggers, letting the agent loop run until it naturally finishes (i.e., the model stops making tool calls).

By default, ToolLoopAgent uses stepCountIs(20) as a safety measure to prevent runaway loops that could result in excessive API calls and costs. If you are confident that your agent will terminate naturally or you are less concerned about costs, isLoopFinished() removes that limit and lets the agent run until the model is truly done.

contents.content: The pipeAgentUIStreamToResponse function runs an Agent and streams the resulting UI message output directly to a Node.js ServerResponse object. This is ideal for building real-time streaming API endpoints (for chat, tool use, etc.) in Node.js-based frameworks like Express, Hono, or custom Node servers.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: A Promise<void>. The function completes when the UI message stream has been fully sent to the provided ServerResponse.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Runs the Agent: Calls the agent’s .stream method with the provided UI messages and options, converting them into model messages as needed.

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Streams UI Message Output: Pipes the agent output as a UI message stream to the ServerResponse, sending data via streaming HTTP responses (including appropriate headers).

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: Abort Signal Handling: If abortSignal is supplied, streaming is cancelled as soon as the signal is triggered (such as on client disconnect).

contents.heading: how-it-works
contents.content: No Response Return: Unlike Edge/serverless APIs that return a Response, this function writes bytes directly to the ServerResponse and does not return a response object.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Abort Handling: For best robustness, use an AbortSignal (for example, wired to Express/Hono client disconnects) to ensure quick cancellation of agent computation and streaming.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Node.js Only: Only works with Node.js ServerResponse objects (e.g., in Express, Hono’s node adapter, etc.), not Edge/serverless/web Response APIs.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Streaming Support: Make sure your client (and any proxies) correctly support streaming HTTP responses for full effect.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Parameter Names: The property for input messages is uiMessages (not messages) for consistency with SDK agent utilities.

metadata.title: zodSchema
metadata.description: Helper function for creating Zod schemas

contents.content:
zodSchema is a helper function that converts a Zod schema into a JSON schema object that is compatible with the AI SDK.
It takes a Zod schema and optional configuration as inputs, and returns a typed schema.
You can use it to generate structured data and in tools.

You can also pass Zod objects directly to the AI SDK functions. Internally,
the AI SDK will convert the Zod schema to a JSON schema using zodSchema().
However, if you want to specify options such as useReferences, you can pass
the zodSchema() helper function instead.

When using .meta() or .describe() to add metadata to your Zod schemas,
make sure these methods are called at the end of the schema chain.

metadata is attached to a specific schema
instance, and most schema methods (.min(), .optional(), .extend(), etc.)
return a new schema instance that does not inherit metadata from the previous one.
Due to Zod's immutability, metadata is only included in the JSON schema output
if .meta() or .describe() is the last method in the chain.

metadata.title: AI_UIMessageStreamError
metadata.description: Learn how to fix AI_UIMessageStreamError

contents.content: This error occurs when a UI message stream contains invalid or out-of-sequence chunks.
Common causes:
Receiving a text-delta chunk without a preceding text-start chunk
Receiving a text-end chunk without a preceding text-start chunk
Receiving a reasoning-delta chunk without a preceding reasoning-start chunk
Receiving a reasoning-end chunk without a preceding reasoning-start chunk
Receiving a tool-input-delta chunk without a preceding tool-input-start chunk
Attempting to access a tool invocation that doesn't exist
This error often surfaces when an upstream request fails before any tokens are streamed and a custom transport tries to write an inline error message to the UI stream without the proper start chunk.

contents.heading: properties
contents.content: chunkType: The type of chunk that caused the error (e.g., text-delta, reasoning-end, tool-input-delta)

contents.heading: properties
contents.content: chunkId: The ID associated with the failing chunk (part ID or toolCallId)

contents.heading: properties
contents.content: message: The error message with details about what went wrong

contents.heading: checking-for-this-error
contents.content: You can check if an error is an instance of AI_UIMessageStreamError using:

contents.heading: common-solutions
contents.content: Ensure proper chunk ordering: Always send a *-start chunk before any *-delta or *-end chunks for the same ID:

contents.heading: common-solutions
contents.content: Verify IDs match: Ensure the id used in *-delta and *-end chunks matches the id used in the corresponding *-start chunk.

contents.heading: common-solutions
contents.content: Handle error paths correctly: When writing error messages in custom transports, ensure you emit the full start/delta/end sequence:

contents.heading: common-solutions
contents.content: Check stream producer logic: Review your streaming implementation to ensure chunks are sent in the correct order, especially when dealing with concurrent operations or merged streams.

metadata.title: AI SDK Errors
metadata.description: Reference for AI SDK error classes and typed error handling.

contents.content:
The AI SDK exposes typed errors so applications can handle expected failure
modes without matching error message strings.

contents.heading: importing-errors
contents.content:
The application package is named ai, not @ai-sdk/ai. It re-exports common
provider-level errors from @ai-sdk/provider together with the higher-level
errors raised by AI SDK Core:

contents.heading: importing-errors
contents.content:
Provider implementations that depend directly on @ai-sdk/provider can import
its provider-level errors from that package instead:

contents.heading: migrating-to-typed-error-handling
contents.content:
Replace message matching or an unconditionally generic catch block with the
most specific static isInstance guard available. Check AISDKError last when
you need a fallback for any AI SDK error:

contents.heading: migrating-to-typed-error-handling
contents.content:
Prefer ErrorClass.isInstance(error) over error instanceof ErrorClass when
the class provides it. The static guard also works when multiple AI SDK package
versions are loaded.

metadata.title: Abort and resumable streams
metadata.description: Troubleshooting abort and stop behavior with resumable streams

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using useChat with resume: true for stream resumption, client-side aborts are treated as disconnects. Closing a tab, refreshing the page, navigating away, or calling stop() closes the current HTTP connection, but it should not cancel the underlying generation.

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: If your application passes the request abort signal through to the model call, disconnects can cancel the work that stream resumption expects to keep running. If your stop button only calls stop(), the server-side generation can continue and the client may reconnect to the same active stream.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: Stream resumption lets the client reconnect to an active stream after the original connection closes. To support that, the server needs to keep the stream producer running even when no client is currently connected.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: This means route cleanup, page unloads, and network disconnects should be handled as resumable disconnects. Explicit user cancellation needs a separate server-side signal that cancels the active producer and clears the stored active stream reference.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Use resume: true for reconnecting after disconnects, and add a dedicated stop endpoint for explicit user cancellation.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: The stop endpoint should:

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Load the chat and read its active stream ID

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Persist the latest partial assistant message if the client sends one

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Cancel the work that is producing the stream

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Clear the active stream reference only if it still points to the same stream

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: On the client, call your stop endpoint before stopping the local chat stream:

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Keep navigation separate from stop behavior. Do not call the stop endpoint from route cleanup code, page unload handlers, or component unmount cleanup. Those events are disconnects that should remain resumable.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: If you do not need stream resumption and only want client-side cancellation, disable resume and use stop() directly:

metadata.title: High memory usage when processing many images
metadata.description: Troubleshooting high memory usage when using generateText or streamText with many images

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using generateText or streamText with many images (e.g., in a loop or batch processing), you may notice:

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: Memory usage grows continuously and doesn't decrease

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: Application eventually runs out of memory

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: Memory is not reclaimed even after garbage collection

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: This is especially noticeable when using experimental_download to process images from URLs, or when sending base64-encoded images in prompts.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: By default, the AI SDK includes the full request and response bodies in the step results. When processing images, the request body contains the base64-encoded image data, which can be very large (a single image can be 1MB+ when base64 encoded). If you process many images and keep references to the results, this data accumulates in memory.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: For example, processing 100 images of 500KB each would include ~50MB+ of request body data in memory.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Use the experimental_include option to disable inclusion of request and/or response bodies:

contents.heading: options
contents.content: The experimental_include option accepts:

contents.heading: options
contents.content: requestBody: Set to false to exclude the request body from step results. This is where base64-encoded images are stored. Default: true. Available in both generateText and streamText.

contents.heading: options
contents.content: responseBody: Set to false to exclude the response body from step results. Default: true. Only available in generateText.

contents.heading: when-to-use
contents.content: Batch processing images: When processing many images in a loop

contents.heading: when-to-use
contents.content: Long-running agents: When an agent may process many images over its lifetime

contents.heading: when-to-use
contents.content: Memory-constrained environments: When running in environments with limited memory

contents.heading: trade-offs
contents.content: When you disable body inclusion:

contents.heading: trade-offs
contents.content: You won't have access to result.request.body or result.response.body

contents.heading: trade-offs
contents.content: Debugging may be harder since you can't inspect the raw request/response

contents.heading: trade-offs
contents.content: If you need the bodies for logging or debugging, consider extracting the data you need before the next iteration

metadata.title: Missing Tool Results Error
metadata.description: How to fix the "Tool results are missing for tool calls" error when using the AI SDK.

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: You encounter the error AI_MissingToolResultsError with a message like:

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: Tool results are missing for tool calls: ...

contents.heading: cause
contents.content: This error occurs when you attempt to send a new message to the Large Language Model (LLM) while there are pending tool calls from a previous turn that have not yet been resolved.

contents.heading: cause
contents.content: The AI SDK core logic validates that all tool-call parts in the conversation history are resolved before proceeding. "Resolved" typically means:

contents.heading: cause
contents.content: The tool has been executed and a tool-result has been added to the history.

contents.heading: cause
contents.content: Or, the tool call has triggered a tool-approval-response (if using tool approvals).

contents.heading: cause
contents.content: If a tool call is found without a corresponding result or approval response, this error is thrown to prevent sending an invalid conversation history to the model.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Ensure that every tool call in your conversation history is properly handled.

contents.heading: provide-tool-results
contents.content: For standard tool calls, ensure that you provide the output of the tool execution.

contents.heading: handle-tool-approvals
contents.content: If you are using the tool approval workflow, ensure that you include the tool-approval-response.

metadata.title: Object generation failed with OpenAI
metadata.description: Troubleshooting NoObjectGeneratedError with finish-reason content-filter caused by incompatible Zod schema types when using OpenAI structured outputs

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using structured output generation with OpenAI, you may encounter a NoObjectGeneratedError with the finish reason content-filter. This error occurs when your Zod schema contains incompatible types that OpenAI's structured output feature cannot process.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: OpenAI's structured output generation uses JSON Schema under the hood and has specific requirements for schema compatibility. The Zod methods .nullish() and .optional() generate JSON Schema patterns that are incompatible with OpenAI's implementation, causing the model to reject the schema and return a content-filter finish reason.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Replace .nullish() and .optional() with .nullable() in your Zod schemas when using structured output generation with OpenAI models.

metadata.description: Troubleshooting duplicate assistant messages when using useChat with streamText

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using useChat with streamText on the server, the assistant's messages appear duplicated in the UI - showing both the previous message and the new message, or showing the same message multiple times. This can occur when using tool calls or complex message flows.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: The duplication occurs because toUIMessageStreamResponse generates new message IDs for each new message.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Pass the original messages array to toUIMessageStreamResponse using the originalMessages option. By passing originalMessages, the method can reuse existing message IDs instead of generating new ones, ensuring the client properly updates existing messages rather than creating duplicates.

metadata.title: onFinish not called when stream is aborted
metadata.description: Troubleshooting onFinish callback not executing when streams are aborted with toUIMessageStreamResponse

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using toUIMessageStreamResponse with an onFinish callback, the callback may not execute when the stream is aborted. This happens because the abort handler immediately terminates the response, preventing the onFinish callback from being triggered.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: When a stream is aborted, the response is immediately terminated. Without proper handling, the onFinish callback has no chance to execute, preventing important cleanup operations like saving partial results or logging abort events.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Add consumeStream to the toUIMessageStreamResponse configuration. This ensures that abort events are properly captured and forwarded to the onFinish callback, allowing it to execute even when the stream is aborted.

contents.heading: background

Errors become part of the stream and are not thrown to prevent e.g. servers from crashing.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: To log errors, you can provide an onError callback that is triggered when an error occurs.

metadata.title: TypeScript performance issues with Zod and AI SDK 5
metadata.description: Troubleshooting TypeScript server crashes and slow performance when using Zod with AI SDK 5

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using the AI SDK 5 with Zod, you may experience:

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: TypeScript server crashes or hangs

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: Extremely slow type checking in files that import AI SDK functions

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: Error messages like "Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite"

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: IDE becoming unresponsive when working with AI SDK code

contents.heading: background
contents.content: The AI SDK 5 has specific compatibility requirements with Zod versions. When importing Zod using the standard import path (import { z } from 'zod'), TypeScript's type inference can become excessively complex, leading to performance degradation or crashes.

contents.heading: upgrade-zod-to-418-or-later
contents.content: The primary solution is to upgrade to Zod version 4.1.8 or later, which includes a fix for this module resolution issue:

contents.heading: upgrade-zod-to-418-or-later
contents.content: This version resolves the underlying problem where different module resolution settings were causing TypeScript to load the same Zod declarations twice, leading to expensive structural comparisons.

contents.heading: alternative-update-typescript-configuration
contents.content: If upgrading Zod isn't possible, you can update your tsconfig.json to use moduleResolution: "nodenext":

contents.heading: alternative-update-typescript-configuration
contents.content: This resolves the TypeScript performance issues while allowing you to continue using the standard Zod import.

title.children: Option 1: Request-Level Configuration (Recommended for Dynamic Values)
Option 2: Hook-Level Configuration with Static Values
Option 3: Hook-Level Configuration with Resolvable Functions
Combining Hook and Request Level Options

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using the useChat hook, custom request options like headers, body fields, and credentials configured directly on the hook are not being sent with the request:

contents.heading: background
contents.content: The useChat hook has changed its API for configuring request options. Direct options like headers, body, and credentials on the hook itself are no longer supported. Instead, you need to use the transport configuration with DefaultChatTransport or pass options at the request level.

contents.heading: solution

contents.heading: option-1-request-level-configuration-recommended-for-dynamic-values
contents.content: For dynamic values that change over time, the recommended approach is to pass options when calling sendMessage:

contents.heading: option-1-request-level-configuration-recommended-for-dynamic-values
contents.content: This approach ensures that the most up-to-date values are always sent with each request.

contents.heading: option-2-hook-level-configuration-with-static-values
contents.content: For static values that don't change during the component lifecycle, use the DefaultChatTransport:

contents.heading: option-3-hook-level-configuration-with-resolvable-functions
contents.content: If you need dynamic values at the hook level, you can use functions that return configuration values. However, request-level configuration is generally preferred for better reliability:

contents.heading: option-3-hook-level-configuration-with-resolvable-functions
contents.content:
For component state that changes over time, request-level configuration
(Option 1) is recommended. If using hook-level functions, consider using
useRef to store current values and reference ref.current in your
configuration function.

contents.heading: combining-hook-and-request-level-options
contents.content: Request-level options take precedence over hook-level options:

contents.heading: combining-hook-and-request-level-options
contents.content: For more details on request configuration, see the Request Configuration documentation.

metadata.title: Stale body values with useChat
metadata.description: Troubleshooting stale values when passing information via the body parameter of useChat

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using useChat and passing dynamic information via the body parameter at the hook level, the data remains stale and only reflects the value from the initial component render. This occurs because the body configuration is captured once when the hook is initialized and doesn't update with subsequent component re-renders.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: The hook-level body configuration is evaluated once during the initial render and doesn't re-evaluate when component state changes.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Pass dynamic variables via the second argument of the sendMessage function instead of at the hook level. Request-level options are evaluated on each call and take precedence over hook-level options.

contents.heading: alternative-dynamic-hook-level-configuration
contents.content: If you need hook-level configuration that responds to changes, you can use functions that return configuration values. However, for component state, you'll need to use useRef to access current values:

contents.heading: alternative-dynamic-hook-level-configuration
contents.content: Recommendation: Request-level configuration is simpler and more reliable for component state. Use it whenever you need to pass dynamic values that change during the component lifecycle.

contents.heading: server-side-handling
contents.content: On your server side, retrieve the custom fields by destructuring the request body:

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: Look up detailed information about a specific generation by its ID, including cost, token usage, latency, and provider details. Generation IDs are available in providerMetadata.gateway.generationId on both generateText and streamText responses.

contents.heading: generation-lookup
contents.content: When streaming, the generation ID is injected on the first content chunk, so you can capture it early in the stream without waiting for completion. This is especially useful in cases where a network interruption or mid-stream error could prevent you from receiving the final response — since the gateway records the final status server-side, you can use the generation ID to look up the results (including cost, token usage, and finish reason) later via getGenerationInfo().

contents.heading: perplexity-search

contents.heading: perplexity-search

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: The Tako Search tool enables models to search the web and Tako's curated knowledge graph in a single call using Tako's Search API. This tool is executed by the AI Gateway and returns token-efficient web excerpts, plus knowledge-graph results that carry structured data, premium source attribution, and an embed-ready visualization.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: Configure the search with effort, source selection, and localization defaults. These defaults override values the model includes in a tool call:

contents.heading: tako-search

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: effort 'fast' | 'instant' | 'deep' - Search effort. 'fast' is the balanced default, 'instant' favors cached low-latency results, and 'deep' broadens retrieval with reranking at higher cost and latency.

contents.heading: tako-search

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: includeDomains / excludeDomains string[] - Only return, or drop, results from these bare domains. Up to 20 each.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: publishedAfter / publishedBefore string - Keep results published on or after, or on or before, this YYYY-MM-DD date.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: snippetMaxChars number - Character cap on each result's text excerpt. Defaults to 4,000; maximum 20,000.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: highlights boolean - Return query-relevant passages as each result's snippet instead of the opening text of the page. The snippet can hold multiple passages joined by ' ... ', and a page with no highlight returns snippet: null. Defaults to true in the AI Gateway.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: includeContents boolean - Inline each page's extracted full text in content. articleContentMaxChars caps it, defaulting to 30,000 characters (maximum 1,000,000).

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: sources.data object - Configure data results:

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: count number - Maximum data results, 1-20. Defaults to 5.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: includeContents boolean - Inline each card's underlying rows in content.dataset as typed, unit-labeled columns. This adds a data surcharge based on the row count and dataset source. To estimate cost, first search with includeContents: false and inspect cards.content.export_pricing. Because this applies to every returned card, use count and maxRows to control cost.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: contentFormat 'json_compact' | 'json_records' | 'csv' | 'card_json' - Serialization for inlined card data. Defaults to 'json_compact'.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: maxRows number - Row cap per result. Omit to use the allowance in cards.content.export_pricing. A data surcharge applies per 1,000 exported rows; lower values reduce cost.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: nodeIds string[] - Data Graph node IDs to prioritize. Up to 20.

contents.heading: tako-search

contents.heading: tako-search

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: locale string - BCP-47 locale, such as 'en-US'.

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: timezone string - IANA timezone, such as 'America/New_York'.

contents.heading: tako-search

contents.heading: tako-search
contents.content: includeRelated number - Number of related search suggestions to include (1-20).

contents.heading: tako-search

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The AI Gateway provider accepts provider options that control routing behavior and provider-specific configurations.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: You can use the gateway key in providerOptions to control how AI Gateway routes requests:

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: The following gateway provider options are available:

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: order string[]

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Specifies the sequence of providers to attempt when routing requests. The gateway will try providers in the order specified. If a provider fails or is unavailable, it will move to the next provider in the list.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: order: ['bedrock', 'anthropic'] will attempt Amazon Bedrock first, then fall back to Anthropic.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: only string[]

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Restricts routing to only the specified providers. When set, the gateway will never route to providers not in this list, even if they would otherwise be available.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: only: ['anthropic', 'vertex'] will only allow routing to Anthropic or Vertex AI.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: sort 'cost' | 'ttft' | 'tps'

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Sorts available providers by a performance or cost metric before routing. The gateway will try the best-scoring provider first and fall back through the rest in sorted order. If unspecified, providers are ordered using the gateway's default system ranking.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'cost' — lowest cost first

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'ttft' — lowest time-to-first-token first

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'tps' — highest tokens-per-second first

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: When combined with order, the user-specified providers are promoted to the front while remaining providers follow the sorted order.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: sort: 'ttft' will route to the provider with the fastest time-to-first-token.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: When sort is active, the response's providerMetadata.gateway.routing.sort object contains the sort option used, the resulting execution order, per-provider metric values, and any providers that were deprioritized.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: models string[]

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Specifies fallback models to use when the primary model fails or is unavailable. The gateway will try the primary model first (specified in the model parameter), then try each model in this array in order until one succeeds.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: models: ['openai/gpt-5.4-nano', 'gemini-3-flash-preview'] will try the fallback models in order if the primary model fails.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Optional identifier for the end user on whose behalf the request is being made. This is used for spend tracking and attribution purposes, allowing you to track usage per end-user in your application.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: user: 'user-123' will associate this request with end-user ID "user-123" in usage reports.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: tags string[]

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Optional array of tags for categorizing and filtering usage in reports. Useful for tracking spend by feature, prompt version, or any other dimension relevant to your application.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: tags: ['chat', 'v2'] will tag this request with "chat" and "v2" for filtering in usage analytics.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: byok Record<string, Array<Record<string, unknown>>>

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Request-scoped BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) credentials to use for this request. When provided, any cached BYOK credentials configured in the gateway system are not considered. Requests may still fall back to use system credentials if the provided credentials fail.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Each provider can have multiple credentials (tried in order). The structure is a record where keys are provider slugs and values are arrays of credential objects.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Each credential can optionally include a modelMappings array to map AI Gateway model slugs to your deployment names (for example, custom Azure deployment names). If a BYOK request fails, the gateway falls back to system credentials using the default model name.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Examples:

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Single provider: byok: { 'anthropic': [{ apiKey: 'sk-ant-...' }] }

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Multiple credentials: byok: { 'vertex': [{ project: 'proj-1', googleCredentials: { privateKey: '...', clientEmail: '...' } }, { project: 'proj-2', googleCredentials: { privateKey: '...', clientEmail: '...' } }] }

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Multiple providers: byok: { 'anthropic': [{ apiKey: '...' }], 'bedrock': [{ accessKeyId: '...', secretAccessKey: '...' }] }

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: With model mappings: byok: { 'azure': [{ apiKey: '...', resourceName: '...', modelMappings: [{ gatewayModelSlug: 'openai/gpt-5.4-nano', customModelId: 'my-deployment' }] }] }

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: zeroDataRetention boolean

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Restricts routing to providers with zero data retention agreements with Vercel for AI Gateway. BYOK credentials are skipped by default, since your provider agreements differ from Vercel's. When this filter is on, AI Gateway routes only to providers Vercel has ZDR agreements with for the model. If you have BYOK keys marked as ZDR, those keys are tried first, then AI Gateway falls back to its system credentials. You are responsible for the accuracy of that marking. Applies to both account-wide and request-level ZDR. The request fails if no ZDR-eligible credentials are available. Request-level ZDR is only available for Vercel Pro and Enterprise plans.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: disallowPromptTraining boolean

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Restricts routing requests to providers that have agreements with Vercel for AI Gateway to not use prompts for model training. If there are no providers available for the model that disallow prompt training, the request will fail. BYOK credentials are skipped when disallowPromptTraining is set to true to ensure that requests are only routed to providers that do not train on prompt data.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: quotaEntityId string

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: The unique identifier for the entity against which quota is tracked. Used for quota management and enforcement purposes.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: has Array<'implicit-caching' | 'reasoning' | 'tool-use' | 'vision' | quantization:${string} | !quantization:${string}>

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Restricts routing to provider models that have all of the specified capabilities. Applies to both BYOK and system credentials, since the capability is a property of the model rather than the credential. If no provider model for the requested model satisfies the capabilities, the request fails. Unsupported values are rejected.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Supported capabilities:

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'implicit-caching' — models that perform automatic (implicit) prompt caching.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'reasoning' — models that support reasoning.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'tool-use' — models that support tool calling.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'vision' — models that accept image input.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Weight-format conditions route on the serving provider's recorded weight format: 'quantization:fp8' requires a provider serving fp8 weights, while '!quantization:fp8' excludes fp8 providers. A negated condition also matches providers whose weight format is not recorded, so exclusions remain usable while the catalog is populated.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: has: ['implicit-caching'] will only route to models that support implicit caching. Example: has: ['vision'] will only route to models that accept image input. Example: has: ['tool-use'] will only route to models that support tool calling. Example: has: ['!quantization:fp8'] will only route to providers that do not serve fp8 weights.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: providerTimeouts object

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Per-provider timeouts for BYOK credentials in milliseconds. Controls how long to wait for a provider to start responding before falling back to the next available provider.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: providerTimeouts: { byok: { openai: 5000, anthropic: 2000 } }

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: For full details, see Provider Timeouts.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: serviceTier 'flex' | 'priority'

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content:
Unified service tier intent. The gateway translates it into whichever
per-provider option each provider expects, and overrides any tier
also set in the per-provider options. Leave unset for provider
default. See the OpenAI,
Google Generative AI,
and Google Vertex AI
provider docs for tier semantics, model availability, and graceful
downgrade behavior on each provider.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: You can combine these options to have fine-grained control over routing and tracking:

contents.heading: model-fallbacks-example
contents.content: The models option enables automatic fallback to alternative models when the primary model fails:

contents.heading: zero-data-retention-example
contents.content: Set zeroDataRetention to true to route requests to providers with zero data retention agreements with Vercel for AI Gateway. BYOK credentials are skipped by default, since your provider agreements differ from Vercel's. When this filter is on, AI Gateway routes only to providers Vercel has ZDR agreements with for the model. If you have BYOK keys marked as ZDR, those keys are tried first, then AI Gateway falls back to its system credentials. You are responsible for the accuracy of that marking. Applies to both account-wide and request-level ZDR. The request fails if no ZDR-eligible credentials are available. When zeroDataRetention is false or not specified, there is no enforcement of restricting routing. Request-level ZDR is only available for Vercel Pro and Enterprise plans.

contents.heading: disallow-prompt-training-example
contents.content: Set disallowPromptTraining to true to route requests to providers that have agreements with Vercel for AI Gateway to not use prompts for model training. If there are no providers available for the model that disallow prompt training, the request will fail. When disallowPromptTraining is false or not specified, there is no enforcement of restricting routing. BYOK credentials are skipped when disallowPromptTraining is set to true to ensure that requests are only routed to providers that do not train on prompt data.

contents.heading: quota-entity-id-example
contents.content: Set quotaEntityId to track and enforce quota against a specific entity. This is useful for multi-tenant applications where you need to manage quota at the entity level (e.g., per organization or team).

contents.heading: filtering-by-model-capability
contents.content: Set has to restrict routing to provider models that have the specified capabilities. This applies to both BYOK and system credentials, since the capability is a property of the model rather than the credential. 'implicit-caching' limits routing to models that perform automatic prompt caching, 'vision' limits routing to models that accept image input, 'reasoning' limits routing to models that support reasoning, and 'tool-use' limits routing to models that support tool calling. Weight-format conditions ('quantization:fp8' to require, '!quantization:fp8' to exclude) limit routing by the serving provider's recorded weight format. If no provider model for the requested model satisfies the capabilities, the request fails.

contents.heading: filtering-by-model-capability
contents.content:
Use 'vision' when the request sends image input, so the gateway only routes to
provider models that can accept it:

contents.content: When using provider-specific options through AI Gateway, use the actual provider name (e.g. anthropic, openai, not gateway) as the key:

contents.heading: provider-specific-options
contents.content: This works with any provider supported by AI Gateway. Each provider has its own set of options - see the individual provider documentation pages for details on provider-specific options.
