metadata.title: Alibaba
metadata.description: Learn how to use Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Qwen) models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio provides access to the Qwen model series, including advanced reasoning capabilities.
API keys can be obtained from the Console.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Alibaba provider is available via the @ai-sdk/alibaba module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance alibaba from @ai-sdk/alibaba:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: For custom configuration, you can import createAlibaba and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Alibaba provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers or regional endpoints.
The default prefix is https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: videoBaseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for video generation API calls. The video API uses the DashScope
native endpoint (not the OpenAI-compatible endpoint).
The default prefix is https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: embeddingBaseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for embedding API calls. The embedding API uses the DashScope
native endpoint (not the OpenAI-compatible endpoint).
The default prefix is https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/api/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header. It defaults to
the ALIBABA_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom fetch implementation.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: includeUsage boolean

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Include usage information in streaming responses. When enabled, token usage will be included in the final chunk.
Defaults to true.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can create language models using a provider instance:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can also use the .chatModel() or .languageModel() factory methods:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Alibaba language models can be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Alibaba models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: enableThinking boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Enable thinking/reasoning mode for supported models. When enabled, the model generates reasoning content before the response.
Defaults to false.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinkingBudget number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Maximum number of reasoning tokens to generate. Limits the length of thinking content.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: preserveThinking boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Preserve reasoning from previous assistant messages for supported models.
When enabled, reasoning is sent separately as Alibaba reasoning_content and
preserve_thinking is enabled. Defaults to true for models that support
preserved thinking; set to false to opt out. Append AI SDK responseMessages
unchanged when continuing the conversation. See Alibaba's
preserved-thinking documentation
for the list of supported models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use.
Defaults to true.

contents.heading: thinking-mode
contents.content: Alibaba's Qwen models support thinking/reasoning mode for complex problem-solving:

contents.heading: thinking-mode
contents.content: For models that are thinking-only (like qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507), thinking mode is enabled by default.

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
For models that support preserved thinking, the AI SDK replays reasoning from
previous assistant messages as Alibaba reasoning_content by default, so the
model can build on its earlier thought process:

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
When continuing the conversation, append responseMessages unchanged. If you
rebuild assistant history from visible text only, the reasoning parts are
discarded before the provider can serialize them as reasoning_content. Set
preserveThinking: false to opt out of replay, and note the following caveats:

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
preserveThinking does not enable thinking by itself. Pair it with
enableThinking/thinkingBudget or the top-level reasoning option.

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
It is enabled by default only for models that Alibaba documents as supporting
preserved thinking; for other models, preserve_thinking is not sent unless
you set the option explicitly. See Alibaba's
preserved-thinking documentation
for the current list of supported models.

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
Reasoning from the current tool-call round (after the last user message) is
always sent back with tool results, as Alibaba recommends; the option only
controls reasoning from earlier rounds.

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content: Preserved reasoning increases input token usage and billing.

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
Historical reasoning remains separate from visible assistant text; it is never
merged into content.

contents.heading: tool-calling
contents.content: Alibaba models support tool calling with parallel execution:

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: Alibaba supports both implicit and explicit prompt caching to reduce costs for repeated prompts.

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: Implicit caching works automatically - the provider caches appropriate content without any configuration. For more control, you can use explicit caching by marking specific messages with cacheControl:

contents.heading: multi-part-message-cache-control
contents.content: Note: The minimum content length for a cache block is 1,024 tokens.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
You can create text embedding models using the .embedding() factory method.
For more on embeddings with the AI SDK see embed()
and embedMany().

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: You can use Alibaba embedding models to generate embeddings with the embed function:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
Use embedMany to embed multiple text values. Alibaba text embedding models support
up to 10 values per API call; larger batches are split automatically by embedMany.

contents.heading: embedding-models

providerOptions.alibaba:

contents.heading: embedding-models

contents.heading: embedding-models

Differentiates query text from document text for asymmetric retrieval tasks.
Defaults to document.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: dimension number

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
The dimension of the output embedding vectors. Defaults to 1024.
text-embedding-v4 also supports 1536 and 2048 dimensions.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: outputType 'dense' | 'sparse' | 'dense&sparse'

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
Specifies the output vector type. Defaults to dense.
The AI SDK embedding interface returns dense number[] vectors, so sparse-only
output is not supported and will throw. Use dense&sparse to receive dense
embeddings in embedding/embeddings and sparse vectors in
providerMetadata.alibaba.sparseEmbeddings.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
You can create Wan video models that call the Alibaba Cloud DashScope API
using the .video() factory method. For more on video generation with the AI SDK see generateVideo().

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content: Alibaba supports three video generation modes: text-to-video, image-to-video (first frame), and reference-to-video.

contents.heading: text-to-video
contents.content: Generate videos from text prompts:

contents.heading: text-to-video
contents.content:
wan2.7 models additionally support the aspectRatio option (mapped to the
API's ratio parameter) and always generate audio. Multi-shot structure is
described directly in the prompt instead of the shotType option:

contents.heading: image-to-video
contents.content: Generate videos from a first-frame image and optional text prompt:

contents.heading: image-to-video
contents.content: You can also pass the first frame using the top-level frameImages option:

contents.heading: reference-to-video
contents.content: Generate videos using reference images and/or videos for character consistency.

contents.heading: reference-to-video
contents.content:
For wan2.6 models, use character identifiers (character1, character2, etc.)
in your prompt to reference them. References must be public URLs:

contents.heading: reference-to-video
contents.content:
For wan2.7 models, use Image 1, Image 2, Video 1, etc. in your prompt
(images and videos are counted separately, in reference order). Image references
can be public URLs or inline file data; video references must be public URLs:

contents.heading: reference-to-video
contents.content:
For full control over the wan2.7 media array (e.g. voice references or explicit
media types), use the media provider option, which overrides the automatic
mapping from inputReferences and frameImages:

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: The following provider options are available via providerOptions.alibaba:

contents.content: A description of what to avoid in the generated video (max 500 characters).

contents.content: URL to an audio file for audio-video sync (WAV/MP3, 3-30 seconds, max 15MB).

contents.content: promptExtend boolean

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Enable prompt extension/rewriting for better generation quality. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: shotType 'single' | 'multi'

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Shot type for video generation. 'multi' enables multi-shot cinematic narrative (wan2.6 models only).

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: watermark boolean

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Whether to add a watermark to the generated video. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: audio boolean

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Whether to generate audio (for wan2.6 I2V and R2V models; wan2.7 models always generate audio).

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: referenceUrls string[]

contents.heading: video-provider-options

Array of reference image/video URLs for reference-to-video mode (wan2.6 models). Supports 0-5 images and 0-3 videos, max 5 total.
Prefer the top-level inputReferences option when passing reference images.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: media Array<{ type, url, referenceVoice? }>

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Explicit media array for reference-to-video mode (wan2.7 models). Each item has a type
('reference_image', 'reference_video', or 'first_frame'), a url (public URL, or a
data:{mime};base64,{data} URI for images), and an optional referenceVoice audio URL.
Overrides the automatic mapping from inputReferences and frameImages.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Aspect ratio (wan2.7 text-to-video and reference-to-video models).
The top-level aspectRatio option is mapped to this parameter automatically.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Polling interval in milliseconds for checking task status. Defaults to 5000.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: pollTimeoutMs number

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Maximum wait time in milliseconds for video generation. Defaults to 600000 (10 minutes).

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Video generation is an asynchronous process that can take several minutes.
Consider setting pollTimeoutMs to at least 10 minutes (600000ms) for
reliable operation.

metadata.title: Amazon Bedrock
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Amazon Bedrock provider.

title.children: Using IAM Access Key and Secret Key
Using AWS SDK Credentials Chain (instance profiles, instance roles, ECS roles, EKS Service Accounts, etc.)

contents.content: The Amazon Bedrock provider for the AI SDK contains language model support for the Amazon Bedrock APIs.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Bedrock provider is available in the @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock module. You can install it with

contents.heading: prerequisites
contents.content: Access to Amazon Bedrock foundation models isn't granted by default. In order to gain access to a foundation model, an IAM user with sufficient permissions needs to request access to it through the console. Once access is provided to a model, it is available for all users in the account.

contents.heading: prerequisites
contents.content: See the Model Access Docs for more information.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: The Amazon Bedrock provider supports two authentication methods with automatic fallback: API key authentication (recommended) and AWS SigV4 authentication using IAM credentials or the AWS SDK credentials chain.

contents.heading: using-an-api-key-recommended
contents.content: API key authentication provides a simpler setup compared to AWS SigV4 authentication. When an API key is supplied, it takes precedence over any SigV4 credentials.

contents.heading: using-an-api-key-recommended
contents.content: Generate a bedrock API key from the AWS console, then either set it as the AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK environment variable:

contents.heading: using-an-api-key-recommended
contents.content: or pass it directly to createAmazonBedrock:

contents.heading: using-an-api-key-recommended
contents.content: When apiKey is omitted, the provider falls back to AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, and then to SigV4 authentication if neither is set.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Step 1: Creating AWS Access Key and Secret Key

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: To get started, you'll need to create an AWS access key and secret key. Here's how:

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Login to AWS Management Console

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Go to the AWS Management Console and log in with your AWS account credentials.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Create an IAM User

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Navigate to the IAM dashboard and click on "Users" in the left-hand navigation menu.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Click on "Create user" and fill in the required details to create a new IAM user.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Make sure to select "Programmatic access" as the access type.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: The user account needs the AmazonBedrockFullAccess policy attached to it.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Create Access Key

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Click on the "Security credentials" tab and then click on "Create access key".

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Click "Create access key" to generate a new access key pair.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Download the .csv file containing the access key ID and secret access key.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Step 2: Configuring the Access Key and Secret Key

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Within your project add a .env file if you don't already have one. This file will be used to set the access key and secret key as environment variables. Add the following lines to the .env file:

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content:
Many frameworks such as Next.js load the .env file
automatically. If you're using a different framework, you may need to load the
.env file manually using a package like
dotenv.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Remember to replace YOUR_ACCESS_KEY_ID, YOUR_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and YOUR_REGION with the actual values from your AWS account.

contents.heading: using-aws-sdk-credentials-chain-instance-profiles-instance-roles-ecs-roles-eks-service-accounts-etc
contents.content: When using AWS SDK, the SDK will automatically use the credentials chain to determine the credentials to use. This includes instance profiles, instance roles, ECS roles, EKS Service Accounts, etc. A similar behavior is possible using the AI SDK by not specifying the accessKeyId and secretAccessKey, sessionToken properties in the provider settings and instead passing a credentialProvider property.

contents.heading: using-aws-sdk-credentials-chain-instance-profiles-instance-roles-ecs-roles-eks-service-accounts-etc
contents.content: Usage:

contents.heading: using-aws-sdk-credentials-chain-instance-profiles-instance-roles-ecs-roles-eks-service-accounts-etc
contents.content: @aws-sdk/credential-providers package provides a set of credential providers that can be used to create a credential provider chain.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance bedrock from @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createAmazonBedrock from @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Omitted options use the environment variables below. When both
accessKeyId and secretAccessKey are strings, SigV4 uses a sessionToken
only if you pass one - not AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from the environment - so static
keys are not mixed with workload tokens (e.g. EKS IRSA).

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Amazon Bedrock provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: region string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The AWS region that you want to use for the API calls.
It uses the AWS_REGION environment variable by default.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: accessKeyId string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The AWS access key ID that you want to use for the API calls.
It uses the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID environment variable by default.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: secretAccessKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The AWS secret access key that you want to use for the API calls.
It uses the AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variable by default.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: sessionToken string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional. For temporary credentials. With both access keys set as strings,
pass the token here if needed; AWS_SESSION_TOKEN from the environment is not
used. If either key is taken from the environment, omitting sessionToken
allows AWS_SESSION_TOKEN.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: credentialProvider () => Promise<{ accessKeyId: string; secretAccessKey: string; sessionToken?: string; }>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional. The AWS credential provider chain that you want to use for the API calls.
It uses the specified credentials by default.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional. API key for authenticating requests using Bearer token authentication.
When provided, this will be used instead of AWS SigV4 authentication.
It uses the AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK environment variable by default.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional. Base URL for the Bedrock API calls.
Useful for custom endpoints or proxy configurations.
When omitted, the provider also supports the service-specific
AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME and
AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_AGENT_RUNTIME environment variables, which take
precedence over the global AWS_ENDPOINT_URL environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string, string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Optional. Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional. Custom fetch implementation.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Bedrock API using the provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. meta.llama3-70b-instruct-v1:0.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Amazon Bedrock models also support some model specific provider options that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them in the providerOptions argument:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Documentation for additional settings based on the selected model can be found within the Amazon Bedrock Inference Parameter Documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can use Amazon Bedrock language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Amazon Bedrock language models can also be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For Anthropic models, you can use the structuredOutputMode provider option to
choose how Amazon Bedrock generates structured outputs:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: "outputFormat": Use Bedrock's native output_config.format parameter.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: "jsonTool": Use a special json tool with required tool choice.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
"auto": Use native structured output when supported and otherwise fall
back to the JSON tool. This is the default.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
In "auto" mode, Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Claude Haiku 4.5 use the JSON tool
fallback because native structured output can be unreliable across workloads
and Bedrock accounts. You can set "outputFormat" to opt into native structured
output when it works for your account and workload, or use "jsonTool" to force
the fallback for any model:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For parity with the Anthropic provider,
providerOptions.anthropic.structuredOutputMode is also honored for Anthropic
models on Bedrock. When both are provided, the bedrock value takes precedence.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For an Anthropic application inference profile, prefer the Bedrock Anthropic
provider. It uses Bedrock's native InvokeModel API, which accepts application
inference profile ARNs, and identifies the model as Anthropic automatically:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Use modelFamily: 'anthropic' only when you need to use the generic
@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock provider, which uses Bedrock's Converse API (for
example, when IAM permits Converse but not InvokeModel). Application inference
profile ARNs do not identify their underlying model, so declaring the family
allows Anthropic-specific features, including native structured output:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For an underlying model that does not reliably support native structured
output, set structuredOutputMode to "jsonTool".

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content:
Amazon Bedrock supports file inputs in combination with specific models, e.g.
anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: The Amazon Bedrock provider supports file inputs, e.g. PDF files.

contents.heading: guardrails
contents.content: You can use the bedrock provider options to utilize Amazon Bedrock Guardrails:

contents.heading: guardrails
contents.content: Tracing information will be returned in the provider metadata if you have tracing enabled.

contents.heading: guardrails
contents.content: See the Amazon Bedrock Guardrails documentation for more information.

contents.heading: citations
contents.content: Amazon Bedrock supports citations for document-based inputs across compatible models. When enabled:

contents.heading: citations
contents.content: Some models can read documents with visual understanding, not just extracting text

contents.heading: citations
contents.content: Models can cite specific parts of documents you provide, making it easier to trace information back to its source (Not Supported Yet)

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content:
Amazon Bedrock prompt caching is currently in preview release. To request
access, visit the Amazon Bedrock prompt caching
page.

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content: In messages, you can use the providerOptions property to set cache points. Set the bedrock property in the providerOptions object to { cachePoint: { type: 'default' } } to create a cache point.

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content: You can also specify a TTL (time-to-live) for cache points using the ttl property. Supported values are '5m' (5 minutes, default) and '1h' (1 hour). The 1-hour TTL is only supported by Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, and Claude Sonnet 4.5.

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content:
When using multiple cache points with different TTLs, cache entries with
longer TTL must appear before shorter TTLs (i.e., 1-hour cache entries must
come before 5-minute cache entries).

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content: Cache usage information is returned in the providerMetadata object. See examples below.

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content:
Cache points have model-specific token minimums and limits. For example,
Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 requires at least 1,024 tokens for a cache point and
allows up to 4 cache points. See the Amazon Bedrock prompt caching
documentation
for details on supported models, regions, and limits.

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content: Cache points also work with streaming responses:

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: The following Bedrock-specific metadata may be returned in providerMetadata.bedrock:

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
trace (optional)
Guardrail tracing information (when tracing is enabled).

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
performanceConfig (optional)
Performance configuration, e.g. { latency: 'optimized' }.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
serviceTier (optional)
Service tier information, e.g. { type: 'on-demand' }.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
usage (optional)
Cache token usage details including cacheWriteInputTokens and cacheDetails.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
stopSequence string | null
The stop sequence that triggered the stop, if any.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Amazon Bedrock supports model creator-specific reasoning features:

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Anthropic (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929): enable via the reasoningConfig provider option and specifying a thinking budget in tokens (minimum: 1024, maximum: 64000).

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Amazon (e.g. us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0): enable via the reasoningConfig provider option and specifying a maximum reasoning effort level ('low' | 'medium' | 'high').

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
For Anthropic models, Bedrock's maxTokens limit includes both thinking and
final text. The provider therefore adds budgetTokens to maxOutputTokens
when setting maxTokens. When maxOutputTokens is omitted, the provider adds
budgetTokens to the default of 4096.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details
on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: service-tiers
contents.content: Amazon Bedrock supports selecting an inference service tier per request via the serviceTier provider option.

contents.heading: service-tiers
contents.content: Supported values are:

contents.heading: service-tiers
contents.content: reserved

contents.heading: service-tiers
contents.content: priority

contents.heading: service-tiers
contents.content: default

contents.heading: service-tiers
contents.content: flex

contents.heading: service-tiers
contents.content: See the Amazon Bedrock service tiers documentation for model availability and behavior.

contents.heading: extended-context-window
contents.content: Claude Sonnet 4 models on Amazon Bedrock support an extended context window of up to 1 million tokens when using the context-1m-2025-08-07 beta feature.

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Via Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock provides three provider-defined tools that can be used to interact with external systems:

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Bash Tool: Allows running bash commands.

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Text Editor Tool: Provides functionality for viewing and editing text files.

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Computer Tool: Enables control of keyboard and mouse actions on a computer.

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: They are available via the tools property of the provider instance.

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content:
Amazon Bedrock does not support strict mode on tool definitions. Setting
strict: true on a tool will be ignored and a warning will be emitted.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: The Bash Tool allows running bash commands. Here's how to create and use it:

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: command (string): The bash command to run. Required unless the tool is being restarted.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: restart (boolean, optional): Specifying true will restart this tool.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: The Text Editor Tool provides functionality for viewing and editing text files.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: For Claude 4 models (Opus & Sonnet):

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: For Claude 3.5 Sonnet and earlier models:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: command ('view' | 'create' | 'str_replace' | 'insert' | 'undo_edit'): The command to run. Note: undo_edit is only available in Claude 3.5 Sonnet and earlier models.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: path (string): Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. /repo/file.py or /repo.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: file_text (string, optional): Required for create command, with the content of the file to be created.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: insert_line (number, optional): Required for insert command. The line number after which to insert the new string.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: new_str (string, optional): New string for str_replace command.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: insert_text (string, optional): Required for insert command, containing the text to insert.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: old_str (string, optional): Required for str_replace command, containing the string to replace.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: view_range (number[], optional): Optional for view command to specify line range to show.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: When using the Text Editor Tool, make sure to name the key in the tools object correctly:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: Claude 4 models: Use str_replace_based_edit_tool

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and earlier: Use str_replace_editor

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: The Computer Tool enables control of keyboard and mouse actions on a computer:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: action ('key' | 'type' | 'mouse_move' | 'left_click' | 'left_click_drag' | 'right_click' | 'middle_click' | 'double_click' | 'screenshot' | 'cursor_position'): The action to perform.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: coordinate (number[], optional): Required for mouse_move and left_click_drag actions. Specifies the (x, y) coordinates.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: text (string, optional): Required for type and key actions.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: These tools can be used in conjunction with the anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0 model to enable more complex interactions and tasks.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Bedrock API Bedrock API

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
Bedrock Titan embedding model amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 supports several additional settings.
You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Bedrock Titan embedding models:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: dimensions: number

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: The number of dimensions the output embeddings should have. The following values are accepted: 1024 (default), 512, 256.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: normalize boolean

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Flag indicating whether or not to normalize the output embeddings. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: nova-embedding-models
contents.content: Amazon Nova embedding models support additional provider options:

contents.heading: nova-embedding-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Nova embedding models:

contents.heading: nova-embedding-models
contents.content: embeddingDimension number

contents.heading: nova-embedding-models
contents.content: The number of dimensions for the output embeddings. Supported values: 256, 384, 1024 (default), 3072.

contents.heading: nova-embedding-models
contents.content: embeddingPurpose string

contents.heading: nova-embedding-models
contents.content: The purpose of the embedding. Accepts: GENERIC_INDEX (default), TEXT_RETRIEVAL, IMAGE_RETRIEVAL, VIDEO_RETRIEVAL, DOCUMENT_RETRIEVAL, AUDIO_RETRIEVAL, GENERIC_RETRIEVAL, CLASSIFICATION, CLUSTERING.

contents.heading: nova-embedding-models

contents.heading: nova-embedding-models
contents.content: Truncation behavior when input exceeds the model's context length. Accepts: NONE, START, END (default).

contents.heading: cohere-embedding-models

contents.heading: cohere-embedding-models

contents.heading: cohere-embedding-models

contents.heading: cohere-embedding-models

metadata.title: Claude Platform on AWS
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Claude Platform on AWS provider.

contents.content: The Claude Platform on AWS provider for the AI SDK gives you access to the Anthropic Messages API hosted inside your AWS environment. Anthropic operates the stack, so you get the same API surface and feature set as the first-party Anthropic provider — including streaming, prompt caching, tool use, computer use, Agent Skills, and anthropic-beta headers — with AWS-native authentication and AWS Marketplace billing.

This differs from Amazon Bedrock in two important ways: Claude Platform on AWS uses Anthropic's Messages API directly (not Bedrock's Converse/InvokeModel), and new features are available the same day they launch on the first-party Claude API (no AWS integration delay).

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Claude Platform on AWS provider is available in the @ai-sdk/anthropic-aws module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: prerequisites
contents.content: Before you can use the provider, your AWS account must be subscribed to Claude Platform on AWS through the AWS Marketplace, and outbound web identity federation must be enabled on the account (a one-time setup step):

contents.heading: prerequisites
contents.content: Without this, every request returns Outbound web identity federation is disabled for your account. This is the most common setup error.

contents.heading: prerequisites
contents.content: You'll also need your workspace ID. When you subscribe, AWS provisions an initial workspace for your account in the selected region. You can find the ID in the Claude Console under Workspaces (accessed from the AWS Console via the Claude Platform on AWS service page).

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: The provider supports two authentication methods:

contents.heading: using-aws-sigv4-recommended-for-production
contents.content: SigV4 integrates with your existing AWS IAM policies, roles, and auditing. Configure AWS credentials using any method supported by the AWS default credential provider chain — environment variables, shared credentials file, web identity (IRSA), ECS container credentials, or EC2 instance metadata.

contents.heading: using-aws-sigv4-recommended-for-production
contents.content: Then use the default provider instance:

contents.heading: using-aws-sigv4-recommended-for-production
contents.content: Or instantiate explicitly:

contents.heading: using-aws-sigv4-recommended-for-production
contents.content: For dynamic credentials (e.g., assuming a role at request time):

contents.heading: using-an-api-key
contents.content: For simpler integration paths (local development, scripts, migration from the first-party Claude API), you can authenticate with an API key instead of SigV4. Your Anthropic account representative provisions API keys for Claude Platform on AWS.

contents.heading: using-an-api-key
contents.content: When apiKey is set, it takes precedence over any SigV4 credentials in the environment.

contents.content: Anthropic workspace ID for this AWS account. Sent on every request via the anthropic-workspace-id header. Reads from ANTHROPIC_AWS_WORKSPACE_ID if omitted.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can create models that call the Anthropic Messages API on AWS using the provider instance:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Model IDs are identical to the first-party Anthropic API. See the Anthropic provider docs for the full list of language model options, prompt caching, computer use, web search, code execution, and Agent Skills. All of these work identically here because Claude Platform on AWS uses Anthropic's runtime directly.

contents.heading: iam-permissions
contents.content: Your IAM principal needs permission to call the Claude Platform on AWS actions on your workspace. AWS provides three managed policies:

contents.heading: iam-permissions
contents.content: AnthropicFullAccess — grants aws-external-anthropic:* on all resources.

contents.heading: iam-permissions
contents.content: AnthropicInferenceAccess — grants read actions plus CreateInference, CreateBatchInference, CancelBatchInference, DeleteBatchInference, and CountTokens on all workspaces. This is the minimum for calling models.

contents.heading: iam-permissions
contents.content: AnthropicReadOnlyAccess — grants Get*, List*, and CallWithBearerToken on all workspaces. Insufficient for inference.
