metadata.description: Learn how to use the Azure OpenAI provider for the AI SDK.

title.children: Typed providerMetadata in Source Document Parts

contents.content: The Azure OpenAI provider contains language model support for the Azure OpenAI chat API.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI provider is available in the @ai-sdk/azure module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance azure from @ai-sdk/azure:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createAzure from @ai-sdk/azure and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can also use a complete Microsoft Foundry OpenAI v1 base URL:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
For Microsoft Entra ID authentication, you can provide a token provider.
Install @azure/identity separately if you want to use its credential helpers:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the OpenAI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: resourceName string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Azure resource name.
It defaults to the AZURE_RESOURCE_NAME environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The resource name is used in the assembled URL: https://{resourceName}.openai.azure.com/openai/v1{path}.
You can use baseURL instead to specify the URL prefix.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the api-key header.
It defaults to the AZURE_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: tokenProvider () => Promise<string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Microsoft Entra ID token provider that returns an access token to be sent using the Authorization header.
When provided, this is used instead of apiKey.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiVersion string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Sets a custom api version.
Defaults to v1.
This setting is applied when the provider constructs the v1 path or uses
deployment-based URLs. Complete v1 base URLs are used as-is.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Either this or resourceName can be used.
When a baseURL is provided, the resourceName is ignored.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
For Azure-hosted URLs ending in .openai.azure.com,
.services.ai.azure.com, or .cognitiveservices.azure.com, you can pass
either an unversioned OpenAI prefix such as https://your-resource.services.ai.azure.com/openai
or a complete v1 base URL such as https://your-resource.services.ai.azure.com/openai/v1.
The provider appends /v1 and the configured api-version to unversioned
resource URLs. Complete v1 URLs are used as-is.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Complete Microsoft Foundry project v1 URLs, such as
https://your-resource.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/your-project/openai/v1,
are also used as-is. If /v1 is omitted from a Foundry project URL, the
provider appends it without adding an api-version query parameter.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
With a non-Azure custom gateway baseURL, the resolved URL is {baseURL}{path};
the SDK does not append /v1 or an api-version query parameter in this mode.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: useDeploymentBasedUrls boolean

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use deployment-based URLs for API calls. Set to true to use the legacy deployment format:
{baseURL}/deployments/{deploymentId}{path}?api-version={apiVersion} instead of
{baseURL}/v1{path}?api-version={apiVersion}.
Defaults to false.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
This option is useful for compatibility with certain Azure OpenAI models or deployments
that require the legacy endpoint format.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI provider instance is a function that you can invoke to create a language model:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You need to pass your deployment name as the first argument.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Azure exposes the thinking of DeepSeek-R1 in the generated text using the <think> tag.
You can use the extractReasoningMiddleware to extract this reasoning and expose it as a reasoning property on the result:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: You can then use that enhanced model in functions like generateText and streamText.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
The Azure provider calls the Responses API by default (unless you specify e.g.
azure.chat).

contents.heading: example
contents.content: You can use OpenAI language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: example
contents.content:
OpenAI language models can also be used in the streamText function
and support structured data generation with Output
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: example
contents.content:
Azure OpenAI sends larger chunks than OpenAI. This can lead to the perception
that the response is slower. See Troubleshooting: Azure OpenAI Slow To
Stream

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: When using OpenAI language models on Azure, you can configure provider-specific options using providerOptions.openai. More information on available configuration options are on the OpenAI provider page.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
The URL for calling Azure chat models will be constructed as follows:
https://RESOURCE_NAME.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/chat/completions?api-version=v1

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: You can create models that call the Azure OpenAI chat completions API using the .chat() factory method:

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Azure OpenAI chat models support also some model specific settings that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for OpenAI chat models:

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: logitBias Record<number, number>

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Modifies the likelihood of specified tokens appearing in the completion.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Accepts a JSON object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in
the GPT tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. You
can use this tokenizer tool to convert text to token IDs. Mathematically,
the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling.
The exact effect will vary per model, but values between -1 and 1 should
decrease or increase likelihood of selection; values like -100 or 100
should result in a ban or exclusive selection of the relevant token.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: As an example, you can pass {"50256": -100} to prevent the token from being generated.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: logprobs boolean | number

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Return the log probabilities of the tokens. Including logprobs will increase
the response size and can slow down response times. However, it can
be useful to better understand how the model is behaving.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Setting to true will return the log probabilities of the tokens that
were generated.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Setting to a number will return the log probabilities of the top n
tokens that were generated.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use. Default to true.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to
monitor and detect abuse. Learn more.

contents.heading: deepseek-chat-models
contents.content: You can create Azure-hosted DeepSeek chat models using the .deepseek() factory method:

contents.heading: deepseek-chat-models
contents.content:
Use this factory for Azure DeepSeek models that support DeepSeek's chat
reasoning fields, such as deepseek-v4-pro and deepseek-v4-flash. The
factory parses streamed reasoning_content as AI SDK reasoning parts.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: Azure OpenAI uses responses API as default with the azure(deploymentName) factory method.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
Further configuration can be done using OpenAI provider options.
You can validate the provider options using the OpenAILanguageModelResponsesOptions type.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
In the Responses API, use azure as the provider name in providerOptions
instead of openai. The openai key is still supported for providerOptions
input.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
parallelToolCalls boolean
Whether to use parallel tool calls. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
store boolean
Whether to store the generation. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
metadata Record<string, string>
Additional metadata to store with the generation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
previousResponseId string
The ID of the previous response. You can use it to continue a conversation. Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
instructions string
Instructions for the model.
They can be used to change the system or developer message when continuing a conversation using the previousResponseId option.
Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
user string
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse. Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningEffort 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'
Reasoning effort for reasoning models. Defaults to medium. If you use providerOptions to set the reasoningEffort option, this model setting will be ignored.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
strictJsonSchema boolean
Whether to use strict JSON schema validation. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI provider also returns provider-specific metadata:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: For Responses models (azure(deploymentName)), you can type this metadata using AzureResponsesProviderMetadata:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The following Azure-specific metadata may be returned:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
responseId string | null | undefined
The ID of the response. Can be used to continue a conversation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
logprobs (optional)
Log probabilities of output tokens (when enabled).

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
serviceTier (optional)
Service tier information returned by the API.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
The providerMetadata is only returned with the default responses API, and is
not supported when using 'azure.chat' or 'azure.completion'

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
Azure Responses models support message-level reasoning effort updates through
providerOptions.azure.reasoningEffortUpdate. The openai namespace is also
accepted when the message has no azure options. Use the
OpenAIResponsesSystemMessageOptions type exported from @ai-sdk/azure to
validate these options:

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
Keep the request-level providerOptions.azure.reasoningEffort unchanged throughout the conversation and
retain earlier effort updates when resending message history. These updates
also work with streamText. See the OpenAI reasoning effort
guide
for continuation and configuration restrictions.

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
The SDK infers support for effort updates from the deployment name passed to
azure.responses(). The name must identify a supported GPT-6-or-later model
family, such as gpt-6-astra. A custom name such as production is not
recognized, even when the underlying deployment runs GPT-6. In that case,
message-level updates throw, and request-level updates are omitted with a
warning. Setting forceReasoning: true does not override this capability
check.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI responses API supports web search through the azure.tools.webSearch tool.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: The web search tool supports the following configuration options:

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: externalWebAccess boolean - Whether to use external web access for fetching live content. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: searchContextSize 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' - Controls the amount of context used for the search. Higher values provide more comprehensive results but may have higher latency and cost.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: userLocation - Optional location information to provide geographically relevant results. Includes type (always 'approximate'), country, city, region, and timezone.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: filters - Optional filter configuration to restrict search results.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: allowedDomains string[] - Up to 100 allowed domains for the search.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: blockedDomains string[] - Up to 100 blocked domains for the search.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: Omit the HTTP or HTTPS prefix from domain filters. Subdomains of configured domains are automatically included or excluded.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: For detailed information on configuration options see the Azure OpenAI Web Search Tool documentation.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content:
On Microsoft Foundry environment , Live internet access is not supported. The
parameter externalWebAccess if passed will be ignored.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI provider supports file search through the azure.tools.fileSearch tool.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: You can force the use of the file search tool by setting the toolChoice parameter to { type: 'tool', toolName: 'file_search' }.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content:
The tool must be named file_search when using Azure OpenAI's file search
functionality. This name is required by Azure OpenAI's API specification and
cannot be customized.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content:
The 'file_search' tool is only supported with the default responses API, and
is not supported when using 'azure.chat' or 'azure.completion'

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
Azure OpenAI's Responses API supports multi-modal image generation as a provider-defined tool.
Availability is restricted to specific models (for example, gpt-5 variants).

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
The tool must be named image_generation when using Azure OpenAI's image
generation functionality. This name is required by Azure OpenAI's API
specification and cannot be customized.

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
The 'image_generation' tool is only supported with the default responses API,
and is not supported when using 'azure.chat' or 'azure.completion'

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
To use image_generation, you must first create an image generation model. You
must add a deployment specification to the header
x-ms-oai-image-generation-deployment. Please note that the Responses API
model and the image generation model must be in the same resource.

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
When you set store: false, then previously generated images will not be
accessible by the model. We recommend using the image generation tool without
setting store: false.

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI provider supports the code interpreter tool through the azure.tools.codeInterpreter tool. This allows models to write and execute Python code.

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content: The code interpreter tool can be configured with:

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content: container: Either a container ID string or an object with fileIds to specify uploaded files that should be available to the code interpreter

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content:
The tool must be named code_interpreter when using Azure OpenAI's code
interpreter functionality. This name is required by Azure OpenAI's API
specification and cannot be customized.

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content:
The 'code_interpreter' tool is only supported with the default responses API,
and is not supported when using 'azure.chat' or 'azure.completion'

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content:
When working with files generated by the Code Interpreter, reference
information can be obtained from both annotations in Text
Parts and providerMetadata in
Source Document Parts.

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content:
The Azure OpenAI provider supports reading PDF files.
You can pass PDF files as part of the message content using the file type:

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content:
The model will have access to the contents of the PDF file and
respond to questions about it.
The PDF file should be passed using the data field,
and the mediaType should be set to 'application/pdf'.

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content:
Reading PDF files are only supported with the default responses API, and is
not supported when using 'azure.chat' or 'azure.completion'

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content: When using the Azure OpenAI Responses API, the SDK attaches Azure OpenAI-specific metadata to output parts via providerMetadata.

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content:
This metadata can be used on the client side for tasks such as rendering citations or downloading files generated by the Code Interpreter.
To enable type-safe handling of this metadata, the AI SDK exports dedicated TypeScript types.

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content: For text parts, when part.type === 'text', the providerMetadata is provided in the form of AzureResponsesTextProviderMetadata.

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content: This metadata includes the following fields:

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content: itemIdThe ID of the output item in the Responses API.

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content:
annotations (optional)
An array of annotation objects generated by the model.
If no annotations are present, this property itself may be omitted (undefined).

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content: Each element in annotations is a discriminated union with a required type field. Supported types include, for example:

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content: url_citation

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content: file_citation

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content: container_file_citation

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content: file_path

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content:
These annotations directly correspond to the annotation objects defined by the Responses API and can be used for inline reference rendering or output analysis.
For details, see the official OpenAI documentation:
Responses API – output text annotations.

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-text-parts
contents.content:
When implementing file downloads for files generated by the Code Interpreter,
the container_id and file_id available in providerMetadata can be used
to retrieve the file content. For details, see the Retrieve container file
content
API.

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-reasoning-parts
contents.content:
When using the Azure OpenAI Responses API, reasoning output parts can include provider metadata.
To handle this metadata in a type-safe way, use AzureResponsesReasoningProviderMetadata.

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-reasoning-parts
contents.content: For reasoning parts, when part.type === 'reasoning', the providerMetadata is provided in the form of AzureResponsesReasoningProviderMetadata.

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-reasoning-parts
contents.content: This metadata includes the following fields:

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-reasoning-parts
contents.content: itemIdThe ID of the reasoning item in the Responses API.

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-reasoning-parts
contents.content: reasoningEncryptedContent (optional)Encrypted reasoning content (only returned when requested via include: ['reasoning.encrypted_content']).

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-source-document-parts
contents.content: For source document parts, when part.type === 'source' and sourceType === 'document', the providerMetadata is provided as AzureResponsesSourceDocumentProviderMetadata.

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-source-document-parts
contents.content: This metadata is also a discriminated union with a required type field. Supported types include:

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-source-document-parts
contents.content: file_citation

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-source-document-parts
contents.content: container_file_citation

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-source-document-parts
contents.content: file_path

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-source-document-parts
contents.content: Each type includes the identifiers required to work with the referenced resource, such as fileId and containerId.

contents.heading: typed-providermetadata-in-source-document-parts
contents.content:
Annotations in text parts follow the OpenAI Responses API specification and
therefore use snake_case properties (e.g. file_id, container_id). In
contrast, providerMetadata for source document parts is normalized by the
SDK to camelCase (e.g. fileId, containerId). Fields that depend on the
original text content, such as start_index and end_index, are omitted, as
are fields like filename that are directly available on the source object.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the completions API using the .completion() factory method.
The first argument is the model id.
Currently only gpt-35-turbo-instruct is supported.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
OpenAI completion models support also some model specific settings that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Azure OpenAI completion models:

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: echo: boolean

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: Echo back the prompt in addition to the completion.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: logitBias Record<number, number>

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: Modifies the likelihood of specified tokens appearing in the completion.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
Accepts a JSON object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in
the GPT tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. You
can use this tokenizer tool to convert text to token IDs. Mathematically,
the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling.
The exact effect will vary per model, but values between -1 and 1 should
decrease or increase likelihood of selection; values like -100 or 100
should result in a ban or exclusive selection of the relevant token.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
As an example, you can pass {"50256": -100} to prevent the <|endoftext|>
token from being generated.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: logprobs boolean | number

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
Return the log probabilities of the tokens. Including logprobs will increase
the response size and can slow down response times. However, it can
be useful to better understand how the model is behaving.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
Setting to true will return the log probabilities of the tokens that
were generated.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
Setting to a number will return the log probabilities of the top n
tokens that were generated.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: suffix string

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: The suffix that comes after a completion of inserted text.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to
monitor and detect abuse. Learn more.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Azure OpenAI embeddings API
using the .embedding() factory method.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
Azure OpenAI embedding models support several additional settings.
You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Azure OpenAI embedding models:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: dimensions: number

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
The number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have.
Only supported in text-embedding-3 and later models.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to
monitor and detect abuse. Learn more.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content: You can create models that call the Azure OpenAI image generation API (DALL-E) using the .image() factory method. The first argument is your deployment name for the DALL-E model.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content: Azure OpenAI image models support several additional settings. You can pass them as providerOptions.openai when generating the image:

contents.heading: example-1
contents.content: You can use Azure OpenAI image models to generate images with the generateImage function:

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Azure OpenAI supports DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 models through deployments. The capabilities depend on which model version your deployment is using:

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Model Version

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Sizes

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: DALL-E 3

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: DALL-E 2

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content:
DALL-E models do not support the aspectRatio parameter. Use the size
parameter instead.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content:
When creating your Azure OpenAI deployment, make sure to set the DALL-E model
version you want to use.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can create models that call the Azure OpenAI transcription API using the .transcription() factory method.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. whisper-1.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
If you encounter a "DeploymentNotFound" error with transcription models,
try enabling deployment-based URLs:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
This uses the legacy endpoint format which may be required for certain Azure OpenAI deployments.
When using useDeploymentBasedUrls, the default api-version is not valid. You must set it to 2025-04-01-preview or an earlier value.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 (e.g. en) format will improve accuracy and latency.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
timestampGranularities string[]
The granularity of the timestamps in the transcription.
Defaults to ['segment'].
Possible values are ['word'], ['segment'], and ['word', 'segment'].
Note: There is no additional latency for segment timestamps, but generating word timestamps incurs additional latency.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
language string
The language of the input audio. Supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 format (e.g. 'en') will improve accuracy and latency.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
prompt string
An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment. The prompt should match the audio language.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
temperature number
The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use log probability to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.
Defaults to 0.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
include string[]
Additional information to include in the transcription response.

contents.heading: model-capabilities-1
contents.content: Model

contents.heading: model-capabilities-1
contents.content: Transcription

contents.heading: model-capabilities-1
contents.content: Duration

contents.heading: model-capabilities-1
contents.content: Segments

contents.heading: model-capabilities-1
contents.content: Language

contents.heading: model-capabilities-1
contents.content: whisper-1

contents.heading: model-capabilities-1
contents.content: gpt-4o-mini-transcribe

contents.heading: model-capabilities-1
contents.content: gpt-4o-transcribe

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: You can create models that call the Azure OpenAI speech API using the .speech() factory method.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: The first argument is your deployment name for the text-to-speech model (e.g., tts-1).

contents.heading: example-2
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument:

contents.heading: example-2
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: example-2
contents.content:
instructions string
Control the voice of your generated audio with additional instructions e.g. "Speak in a slow and steady tone".
Does not work with tts-1 or tts-1-hd.
Optional.

contents.heading: example-2
contents.content:
speed number
The speed of the generated audio.
Select a value from 0.25 to 4.0.
Defaults to 1.0.
Optional.

contents.heading: model-capabilities-2
contents.content: Azure OpenAI supports TTS models through deployments. The capabilities depend on which model version your deployment is using:

contents.heading: model-capabilities-2
contents.content: Model Version

contents.heading: model-capabilities-2
contents.content: Instructions

contents.heading: model-capabilities-2
contents.content: tts-1

contents.heading: model-capabilities-2
contents.content: tts-1-hd

metadata.title: Baseten
metadata.description: Learn how to use Baseten models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: Baseten is an inference platform for serving frontier, enterprise-grade opensource AI models via their API.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Baseten provider is available via the @ai-sdk/baseten module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance baseten from @ai-sdk/baseten:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
If you need a customized setup, you can import createBaseten from @ai-sdk/baseten
and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Baseten provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://inference.baseten.co/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header. It defaults to
the BASETEN_API_KEY environment variable. It is recommended you set the environment variable using export so you do not need to include the field every time.
You can grab your Baseten API Key here

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: modelURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom model URL for specific models (chat or embeddings). If not provided,
the default Model APIs will be used.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: performanceClient PerformanceClient constructor

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Opt in to Baseten's native performance client for embeddings, for client-side
batching and request hedging. Pass the PerformanceClient constructor from
@basetenlabs/performance-client, which you install yourself. When omitted,
embeddings use plain HTTP. See
Native performance client.

You can select Baseten models using a provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. 'moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct-0905': The complete supported models under Model APIs can be found here.

contents.heading: example
contents.content: You can use Baseten language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: example

Baseten language models can also be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: dedicated-models
contents.content: Baseten supports dedicated model URLs for both chat and embedding models. You have to specify a modelURL when creating the provider:

contents.heading: openai-compatible-endpoints-syncv1
contents.content: For models deployed with Baseten's OpenAI-compatible endpoints:

contents.content: /predict endpoints are currently NOT supported for chat models. You must use /sync/v1 endpoints for chat functionality.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: You can create models that call the Baseten embeddings API using the .embeddingModel() factory method. Baseten Embeddings Inference deployments are OpenAI-compatible, so embeddings use plain HTTP by default with no extra dependencies.

contents.heading: embedding-models

Important: Embedding models require a dedicated deployment with a custom
modelURL. Unlike chat models, embeddings cannot use Baseten's default Model
APIs and must specify a dedicated model endpoint.

contents.heading: embedding-models

Each request sends at most 128 values. embedMany splits larger inputs into
chunks of that size and runs them in parallel, so you can pass as many values as

Baseten also publishes @basetenlabs/performance-client, a native client that

batching your deployment already does. It is not installed by default: it is
a native addon, so it cannot load in edge runtimes and bundlers cannot resolve

When you opt in, the client handles batching itself, so values are sent in a

metadata.title: Black Forest Labs
metadata.description: Learn how to use Black Forest Labs models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: Black Forest Labs provides a generative image platform for developers with FLUX-based models. Their platform offers fast, high quality, and in-context image generation and editing with precise and coherent results.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Black Forest Labs provider is available via the @ai-sdk/black-forest-labs module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance blackForestLabs from @ai-sdk/black-forest-labs:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createBlackForestLabs and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Black Forest Labs provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use a regional endpoint.
The default prefix is https://api.bfl.ai/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the x-key header.
It defaults to the BFL_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: pollIntervalMillis number

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Interval in milliseconds between polling attempts when waiting for generation to complete.
Defaults to 500ms for image models and 2000ms for video models.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: pollTimeoutMillis number

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Overall timeout in milliseconds for polling before giving up.
Defaults to 60000ms (60 seconds) for image models and 600000ms (10 minutes) for video models.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content:
You can create Black Forest Labs image models using the .image() factory method.
For more on image generation with the AI SDK see generateImage().

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Black Forest Labs offers many models optimized for different use cases. Here are a few popular examples. For a full list of models, see the Black Forest Labs Models Page.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Model

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Description

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: flux-kontext-pro

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: FLUX.1 Kontext [pro] handles both text and reference images as inputs, enabling targeted edits and complex transformations

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: flux-kontext-max

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: FLUX.1 Kontext [max] with improved prompt adherence and typography generation

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: flux-pro-1.1-ultra

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Ultra-fast, ultra high-resolution image creation

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: flux-pro-1.1

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Fast, high-quality image generation from text.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: flux-pro-1.0-fill

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Inpainting model for filling masked regions of images with new content

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Black Forest Labs models support aspect ratios from 3:7 (portrait) to 7:3 (landscape).

contents.heading: image-editing
contents.content: Black Forest Labs Kontext models support powerful image editing capabilities using reference images. Pass input images via prompt.images to transform, combine, or edit existing images.

contents.heading: single-image-editing
contents.content: Transform an existing image using text prompts:

contents.heading: multi-reference-editing
contents.content: Combine multiple reference images for complex transformations. Black Forest Labs supports up to 10 input images:

contents.heading: multi-reference-editing
contents.content:
Input images can be provided as URLs or base64-encoded strings. They support
up to 20MB or 20 megapixels per image.

contents.heading: inpainting
contents.content: The flux-pro-1.0-fill model supports inpainting, which allows you to fill masked regions of an image with new content. Pass the source image via prompt.images and a mask image via prompt.mask:

contents.heading: inpainting
contents.content: The mask image should be a grayscale image where white areas indicate regions to be filled and black areas indicate regions to preserve.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Black Forest Labs image models support flexible provider options through the providerOptions.blackForestLabs object. The supported parameters depend on the used model ID:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: width number - Output width in pixels (256–1920). When set, this overrides any width derived from size.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: height number - Output height in pixels (256–1920). When set, this overrides any height derived from size.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: outputFormat string - Desired format of the output image ("jpeg" or "png").

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: steps number - Number of inference steps. Higher values may improve quality but increase generation time.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: guidance number - Guidance scale for generation. Higher values follow the prompt more closely.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: imagePrompt string - Base64-encoded image to use as additional visual context for generation.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: imagePromptStrength number - Strength of the image prompt influence on generation (0.0 to 1.0).

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: promptUpsampling boolean - If true, performs upsampling on the prompt.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: raw boolean - Enable raw mode for more natural, authentic aesthetics.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: safetyTolerance number - Moderation level for inputs and outputs (0 = most strict, 6 = more permissive).

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: pollIntervalMillis number - Interval in milliseconds between polling attempts (default 500ms).

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: pollTimeoutMillis number - Overall timeout in milliseconds for polling before timing out (default 60s).

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: webhookUrl string - URL for asynchronous completion notification. Must be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: webhookSecret string - Secret for webhook signature verification, sent in the X-Webhook-Secret header.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
To pass reference images for editing, use prompt.images instead of provider
options. This supports up to 10 images as URLs or base64-encoded strings.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: The generateImage response includes provider-specific metadata in providerMetadata.blackForestLabs.images[]. Each image object may contain the following properties:

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: seed number - The seed used for generation. Useful for reproducing results.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: start_time number - Unix timestamp when generation started.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: end_time number - Unix timestamp when generation completed.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: duration number - Generation duration in seconds.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: cost number - Cost of the generation request.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: inputMegapixels number - Input image size in megapixels.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: outputMegapixels number - Output image size in megapixels.

contents.heading: regional-endpoints
contents.content: By default, requests are sent to https://api.bfl.ai/v1. You can select a regional endpoint by setting baseURL when creating the provider instance:

contents.heading: video-models
video-models
contents.content:
FLUX 3 generates one video per call. Generation is asynchronous — the model
submits a job and polls until it completes, then passes the signed MP4 URL to AI
SDK Core. generateVideo downloads it before resolving, so video is a
GeneratedFile. The signed URL remains available in
providerMetadata.blackForestLabs.videos[0].videoUrl.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
Polling is handled by the provider. Configure pollIntervalMillis and
pollTimeoutMillis on a custom createBlackForestLabs provider instance when
the 2-second interval or 10-minute timeout defaults need to be changed.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
duration accepts a whole number of seconds from 5 to 20. A fractional value is
rounded and an out-of-range value is clamped, each with a warning. Omit it to let
FLUX 3 fit the duration to the content.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
Audio is generated by default, so generateAudio only has to be set to turn it
off. fps and seed are not supported by the API and are reported as warnings.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
The URL in provider metadata is time-limited. Persist the returned video
bytes to your own storage.

contents.heading: resolution-and-aspect-ratio
contents.content:
The API takes a named resolution tier, hd or fhd (the default is hd), where
fhd is finished by the video upsampler. The exact frame size depends on the
aspect ratio.

contents.heading: resolution-and-aspect-ratio
contents.content:
The top-level resolution option is {width}x{height}, so it is mapped onto a
tier by its shorter side — 1280x720 becomes hd and 1920x1080 becomes fhd.
Other values map to hd when the shorter side is at most 720 pixels, and to
fhd above 720, with a warning reporting the mapping. Use
providerOptions.blackForestLabs.resolution to set the tier directly.

contents.heading: resolution-and-aspect-ratio
contents.content:
aspectRatio accepts 21:9, 2:1, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, and 9:16. The
API default is auto, which infers the ratio from the prompt and any
conditioning media; because the top-level option must be {width}:{height},
auto can only be requested through
providerOptions.blackForestLabs.aspectRatio.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
FLUX 3 is a single endpoint with a mode discriminator. The mode is inferred
from the inputs you pass:

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content: Text-to-video — prompt only.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
Image-to-video — pass image (or a frameImages entry with
frameType: 'first_frame') to animate a starting image. Adding a last_frame
closes the clip on that image. A last_frame without a first_frame cannot be
expressed, and is dropped with a warning.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
Keyframes — for more than two images, or images pinned to a specific
second, pass providerOptions.blackForestLabs.keyframes. It takes precedence
over image and frameImages.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
Video continuation — pass a video-typed entry in inputReferences to
continue from the final frames of an existing MP4. FLUX 3 accepts a single
video; keyframes and continuation are mutually exclusive.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
Draft enhance — pass providerOptions.blackForestLabs.draftCache. See
Draft mode.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
FLUX 3 has no reference-image input, so an image passed in inputReferences is
ignored with a warning pointing at image, frameImages, or keyframes.

contents.heading: keyframes
contents.content:
Keyframes are positional: one image opens the clip, two open and close it, and
with more the first and last are the endpoints while the others are spaced evenly
between them. Each image is an http(s) URL or a base64 string, and a request
accepts 1 to 10 of them.

contents.heading: keyframes
contents.content:
Three or more untimed keyframes require an explicit duration; the provider
throws an error when it is omitted, because the API rejects that combination.

contents.heading: keyframes
contents.content:
Pass [seconds, image] pairs in chronological order to pin each image to a
second of the clip instead:

contents.heading: draft-mode
contents.content:
Setting draft: true renders a fast, lower-quality preview and leaves behind an
encrypted bundle, reported as
providerMetadata.blackForestLabs.videos[0].draftCache. Passing that bundle back
as draftCache reproduces the same generation at full quality.

contents.heading: draft-mode
contents.content:
The bundle pins the original mode, prompt, seed, and conditioning media, so an
enhance request accepts nothing besides safetyTolerance. Any other option set
on the call is reported as an unsupported warning. generateVideo requires a
prompt argument, so pass an empty string to say there is nothing to add.

contents.heading: draft-mode
contents.content:
A draft and its enhance are two separate generations, and each is billed
separately.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for FLUX 3 video:

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: resolution 'hd' | 'fhd'

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Output resolution tier. Takes precedence over the top-level resolution.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Aspect ratio of the generated video. Takes precedence over the top-level
aspectRatio, and unlike it can be set to auto.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: keyframes Array<string | [number, string]>

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Keyframes for image-to-video generation, for the shapes image and
frameImages cannot express: more than two images, or images pinned to a
specific second. Takes precedence over both.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: safetyTolerance number

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Moderation strictness from 0 (strictest) to 4. Defaults to 2. Sexual content is
capped at 3 and hate content at 2 regardless of the request, and any request
carrying conditioning media is capped at 2.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: draft boolean

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Render a fast, lower-quality preview instead of the finished video. Defaults to
false.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: draftCache string

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Encrypted draft-cache bundle from a prior draft generation, which switches the
request to draft-enhance mode.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: version string

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Model version to pin. Only latest is available today.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content:
FLUX 3 video results include providerMetadata.blackForestLabs.videos[]. Each
video object may contain the following properties:

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: id string - ID of the Black Forest Labs generation request.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: videoUrl string - The signed, time-limited MP4 URL used to download video.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: draftCache string - Download URL for the draft bundle. Present only on a draft generation.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: seed number - The seed used for generation, when reported by the API.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: start_time number - Unix timestamp when generation started.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: end_time number - Unix timestamp when generation completed.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: duration number - Duration reported by the API, in seconds.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: cost number - Cost of the generation request in credits.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: inputMegapixels number - Input size in megapixels.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: outputMegapixels number - Output size in megapixels.

contents.heading: video-model-capabilities
contents.content: Model

contents.heading: video-model-capabilities
contents.content: Description

contents.heading: video-model-capabilities
contents.content: flux-3-video

contents.heading: video-model-capabilities
contents.content: Up to full-HD and 20 seconds, with synchronized audio. Text-to-video, keyframes, and video continuation.

metadata.title: ByteDance
metadata.description: Learn how to use ByteDance Seedance video and Seedream image models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: The ByteDance provider contains support for the Seedance family of video generation models and the Seedream family of image generation models through the BytePlus ModelArk platform. Seedance provides high-quality text-to-video and image-to-video generation capabilities, including audio-video synchronization, first-and-last frame control, and multi-reference image generation (see the video generation API). Seedream provides text-to-image and image-to-image generation, including multi-image blending and batch image generation (see the image generation API).

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The ByteDance provider is available via the @ai-sdk/bytedance module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance byteDance from @ai-sdk/bytedance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createByteDance and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the ByteDance provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://ark.ap-southeast.bytepluses.com/api/v3.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance

API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the ARK_API_KEY environment variable.
You can obtain an API key from the BytePlus console.

contents.heading: provider-instance

Custom fetch implementation.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content:
You can create ByteDance Seedream image models using the .image() factory method.
For more on image generation with the AI SDK see generateImage().

contents.heading: text-to-image
contents.content: Generate images from text prompts:

contents.heading: text-to-image
contents.content:
ByteDance identifies Seedream models by their ModelArk model id (e.g.
seedream-5-0-260128) or an account-specific endpoint id (e.g. ep-...). The
size parameter accepts pixel dimensions ({width}x{height}); resolution
levels such as 2K can be passed via providerOptions.bytedance.size.

contents.heading: image-editing
contents.content:
Pass input images via prompt.images to transform an existing image
(image-to-image):

contents.heading: image-editing
contents.content:
You can also pass multiple images to blend styles and elements from several
references into a single output (multi-image blending). Images may be provided
as binary data, base64 strings, or URLs:

contents.heading: image-editing
contents.content:
Seedream does not support mask-based inpainting. Describe the edit in the
prompt, optionally with markers drawn on the input image (interactive editing,
supported by dola-seedream-5-0-pro-260628).

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content:
The following options are available via providerOptions.bytedance. You can
type them with ByteDanceImageModelOptions.

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content: watermark boolean

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content:
Whether to add an "AI generated" watermark to the bottom-right corner of the
output image.

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content: outputFormat 'png' | 'jpeg'

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content:
Format of the generated image file. Supported by seedream-5-0 and
dola-seedream-5-0-pro; seedream-4-5 / seedream-4-0 always return jpeg.

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content: size string

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content:
A resolution level (e.g. 1K, 2K, 3K, 4K) as an alternative to passing
pixel dimensions via the top-level size parameter. When set, this overrides
the top-level size. Available levels vary by model.

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content: sequentialImageGeneration 'auto' | 'disabled'

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content:
Set to 'auto' to generate a batch of related images (e.g. storyboards or
brand visuals). Defaults to 'disabled' (single image).

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content: maxImages number

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content:
Maximum number of images to generate when sequentialImageGeneration is
'auto'. The number of input reference images plus generated images must not
exceed the model's limit.

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content: optimizePromptMode 'standard' | 'fast'

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content:
Prompt optimization mode. seedream-4-0 supports both standard and fast;
other models support standard only.

contents.heading: image-model-options
contents.content:
Additional ModelArk fields can also be passed through
providerOptions.bytedance and are validated by ModelArk.

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Model

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Model ID

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Capabilities

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Seedream 5.0 Pro

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: dola-seedream-5-0-pro-260628

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Text-to-image, single/multi image-to-image, interactive editing (markers). Sizes: 1K, 2K. Formats: png, jpeg. Up to 10 references.

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Seedream 5.0 Lite

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: seedream-5-0-260128 (alias seedream-5-0-lite-260128)

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Text-to-image, single/multi image-to-image, batch generation. Sizes: 2K, 3K, 4K. Formats: png, jpeg. Up to 14 references.

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Seedream 4.5

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: seedream-4-5-251128

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Text-to-image, single/multi image-to-image, batch generation. Sizes: 2K, 4K. Format: jpeg. Up to 14 references.

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Seedream 4.0

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: seedream-4-0-250828

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content: Text-to-image, single/multi image-to-image, batch generation, fast prompt mode. Sizes: 1K, 2K, 4K. Format: jpeg. Up to 14 references.

contents.heading: image-model-capabilities
contents.content:
You can also pass any model or endpoint id string if needed, e.g. for future
models not yet listed here. Streaming image output is not currently supported
through the AI SDK integration.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
You can create ByteDance video models using the .video() factory method.
For more on video generation with the AI SDK see generateVideo().

contents.heading: text-to-video
contents.content: Generate videos from text prompts:

contents.heading: image-to-video
contents.content: Generate videos from a first-frame image with an optional text prompt:

contents.heading: image-to-video
contents.content:
When the output ratio is dictated by an input — first-frame or
first-and-last-frame image-to-video, video editing, and video extension — pass
aspectRatio: 'adaptive' or omit aspectRatio entirely. Newer Seedance
models reject an explicit ratio on those paths, because the output inherits
the ratio of the input media.

contents.heading: image-to-video-with-audio
contents.content: Seedance 1.5 Pro supports generating synchronized audio alongside the video:

contents.heading: first-and-last-frame-video
contents.content: Generate smooth transitions between a starting and ending keyframe image:

contents.heading: multi-reference-image-to-video
contents.content: Using the Seedance 1.0 Lite I2V model, you can provide multiple reference images (1-4) that the model uses to faithfully reproduce object shapes, colors, and textures:

contents.heading: reference-video
contents.content: Seedance 2.0 supports reference videos that guide the style, motion, or composition of the generated video:

contents.heading: reference-audio
contents.content: Seedance 2.0 supports reference audio that is used as background music or sound for the generated video:

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: The following provider options are available via providerOptions.bytedance:

contents.heading: generation-options
contents.content: watermark boolean

contents.heading: generation-options
contents.content: Whether to add a watermark to the generated video.

contents.heading: generation-options
contents.content: generateAudio boolean

contents.heading: generation-options
contents.content: Whether to generate synchronized audio for the video. Only supported by Seedance 1.5 Pro.

contents.heading: generation-options
contents.content: cameraFixed boolean

contents.heading: generation-options
contents.content: Whether to fix the camera during generation.

contents.heading: generation-options
contents.content: returnLastFrame boolean

contents.heading: generation-options

contents.heading: media-reference-options

contents.content: Array of reference audio URLs (up to 3, max 15 seconds each) for audio-guided video generation. The model uses the referenced audio as background music or synchronized sound. Supports data URIs (e.g., data:audio/wav;base64,...). Supported by Seedance 2.0.

contents.heading: polling-options

contents.heading: polling-options
contents.content:
Video generation is an asynchronous process that can take several minutes.

metadata.title: DeepSeek
metadata.description: Learn how to use DeepSeek's models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: The DeepSeek provider offers access to powerful language models through the DeepSeek API.
API keys can be obtained from the DeepSeek Platform.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The DeepSeek provider is available via the @ai-sdk/deepseek module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance deepseek from @ai-sdk/deepseek:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: For custom configuration, you can import createDeepSeek and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the DeepSeek provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls.
The default prefix is https://api.deepseek.com.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header. It defaults to
the DEEPSEEK_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom fetch implementation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can create language models using a provider instance:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can also use the .chat() or .languageModel() factory methods:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
DeepSeek language models can be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
DeepSeek retired the deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner aliases on July 24,
2026. Use deepseek-flash (the alias for the current V4.x Flash release),
deepseek-v4-flash, or deepseek-v4-pro for the current API. Custom and legacy
model IDs remain accepted as strings for compatibility with custom endpoints.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for DeepSeek models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: logprobs boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Returns log probabilities for generated content and reasoning
tokens in providerMetadata.deepseek.logprobs.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: topLogprobs number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Returns the specified number of most likely tokens at each token
position. Accepts values from 0 through 20 and automatically enables
logprobs.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: userId string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. An opaque end-user identifier that DeepSeek uses for content-safety
tracing, KV-cache isolation, and scheduling isolation. The value must match
^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ and contain at most 512 characters. Do not include names,
email addresses, or other private user information.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinking object

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Controls thinking mode (chain-of-thought reasoning) for DeepSeek V4 models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: type: 'enabled' | 'disabled' - Enable or disable thinking mode. See DeepSeek's thinking mode docs.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'low' | 'high' | 'max'

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Controls thinking strength for DeepSeek V4 reasoning models.
medium is sent as high, and xhigh is sent as max. A compatibility
warning is returned whenever the requested value is mapped.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
For backwards compatibility, legacy provider options supplied at runtime are
also mapped to documented values: thinking.type: 'adaptive' becomes
'enabled', reasoningEffort: 'medium' becomes 'high', and
reasoningEffort: 'xhigh' becomes 'max'. Each mapping returns a compatibility
warning so callers can migrate to a canonical value.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
DeepSeek has deprecated the top-level frequencyPenalty and presencePenalty
settings. The provider omits these settings and returns a deprecation warning
when they are used. temperature and topP have no effect while thinking is
enabled, including the default thinking mode for DeepSeek V4 models, so the
provider omits them with an unsupported warning. Explicitly set
thinking.type to 'disabled' to use temperature and topP.

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
DeepSeek supports optional participant names on system, user, and assistant
messages. Set providerOptions.deepseek.name on each message that should
include a name:

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content: The same message option works with streamText:

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
Names are omitted when the option is not set. The name value must be a
string. DeepSeek does not support names on tool messages, so the provider
ignores that placement and returns an unsupported-feature warning. Avoid
including unnecessary personal or identifying information in message names.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: DeepSeek V4 models support reasoning. The reasoning is exposed through streaming:

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details
on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: chat-prefix-completion
contents.content:
DeepSeek's beta chat prefix completion
continues the content of a final assistant message. Create a provider with a
beta base URL and set prefix: true in that assistant message's provider
options:

contents.heading: chat-prefix-completion
contents.content:
The prefixed message must be an assistant message and the final message in the
prompt. The configured baseURL must end in /beta, including when using a
proxy. Invalid placement or a non-beta base URL causes the request to fail
before it is sent.

contents.heading: chat-prefix-completion
contents.content: Chat prefix completion is a DeepSeek beta feature and its behavior may change.

contents.heading: strict-tool-calls
contents.content:
DeepSeek's strict tool-call mode is a beta feature. Create the provider with a
beta base URL and set strict: true on every function tool in the request:

contents.heading: strict-tool-calls
contents.content:
Strict tools fail locally when the base URL does not end in /beta. When any
function tool is strict, every function tool in the same request must set
strict: true.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
DeepSeek exposes the response system fingerprint and context cache usage through
the providerMetadata property:

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: The metadata includes:

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: systemFingerprint: The backend configuration fingerprint for the response

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: promptCacheHitTokens: Number of input tokens that were cached

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: promptCacheMissTokens: Number of input tokens that were not cached

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
For streamed responses, the latest non-null fingerprint from the response
chunks is returned.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
For more details about DeepSeek's caching system, see the DeepSeek caching
documentation.

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
DeepSeek preserves provider-specific response fields in
providerMetadata.deepseek for generated and streamed responses:

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: responseObject: chat.completion or chat.completion.chunk

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: choiceIndex: the selected response choice index

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: messageRole: the response message role, when supplied

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: toolCallTypes: the tool-call type for each returned call

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
These fields remain in provider metadata because they are specific to
DeepSeek's Chat Completions response rather than shared AI SDK result fields.

contents.heading: vision-file-parts
contents.content:
For inline images or image URLs, use file-part provider options to select the
image processing detail. DeepSeek supports low, high, original, and
auto:

contents.heading: vision-file-parts
contents.content:
Set fileData: true on an inline image file part to use DeepSeek's
file_data content-part representation. This preserves the file part's
filename. fileData cannot be used with image URLs or imageDetail.

contents.heading: vision-file-parts
contents.content:
DeepSeek accepts JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP image inputs. HTTP image URLs can be
at most 8,192 characters.
