metadata.title: ElevenLabs
metadata.description: Learn how to use the ElevenLabs provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content: The ElevenLabs provider contains language model support for the ElevenLabs transcription and speech generation APIs.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The ElevenLabs provider is available in the @ai-sdk/elevenlabs module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance elevenlabs from @ai-sdk/elevenlabs:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createElevenLabs from @ai-sdk/elevenlabs and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the ElevenLabs provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the ELEVENLABS_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the ElevenLabs speech API
using the .speech() factory method.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. eleven_multilingual_v2.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
The voice argument can be set to a voice ID from the ElevenLabs Voice Library.
You can find voice IDs by selecting a voice in the library and copying its ID.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: languageCode string or nullOptional. Language code (ISO 639-1) used to enforce a language for the model. Currently, only Turbo v2.5 and Flash v2.5 support language enforcement. For other models, providing a language code will result in an error.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: voiceSettings object or nullOptional. Voice settings that override stored settings for the given voice. These are applied only to the current request.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: stability double or nullOptional. Determines how stable the voice is and the randomness between each generation. Lower values introduce broader emotional range; higher values result in a more monotonous voice.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: useSpeakerBoost boolean or nullOptional. Boosts similarity to the original speaker. Increases computational load and latency.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: similarityBoost double or nullOptional. Controls how closely the AI should adhere to the original voice.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: style double or nullOptional. Amplifies the style of the original speaker. May increase latency if set above 0.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: pronunciationDictionaryLocators array of objects or nullOptional. A list of pronunciation dictionary locators to apply to the text, in order. Up to 3 locators per request.Each locator object:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: pronunciationDictionaryId string (required)The ID of the pronunciation dictionary.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: versionId string or null (optional)The version ID of the dictionary. If not provided, the latest version is used.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: seed integer or nullOptional. If specified, the system will attempt to sample deterministically. Must be between 0 and 4294967295. Determinism is not guaranteed.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: previousText string or nullOptional. The text that came before the current request's text. Can improve continuity when concatenating generations or influence current generation continuity.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: nextText string or nullOptional. The text that comes after the current request's text. Can improve continuity when concatenating generations or influence current generation continuity.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: previousRequestIds array of strings or nullOptional. List of request IDs for samples generated before this one. Improves continuity when splitting large tasks. Max 3 IDs. If both previousText and previousRequestIds are sent, previousText is ignored.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: nextRequestIds array of strings or nullOptional. List of request IDs for samples generated after this one. Useful for maintaining continuity when regenerating a sample. Max 3 IDs. If both nextText and nextRequestIds are sent, nextText is ignored.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: applyTextNormalization enumOptional. Controls text normalization.Allowed values: 'auto' (default), 'on', 'off'.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: 'auto': System decides whether to apply normalization (e.g., spelling out numbers).

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: 'on': Always apply normalization.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: 'off': Never apply normalization.For eleven_turbo_v2_5 and eleven_flash_v2_5, can only be enabled with Enterprise plans.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: applyLanguageTextNormalization booleanOptional. Defaults to false. Controls language text normalization, which helps with proper pronunciation in some supported languages (currently only Japanese). May significantly increase latency.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: enableLogging booleanOptional. Whether to enable request logging for this API call. Defaults to the account-level setting.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the ElevenLabs transcription API
using the .transcription() factory method.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. scribe_v1.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 (e.g. en) format can sometimes improve transcription performance if known beforehand.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: languageCode string

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
An ISO-639-1 or ISO-639-3 language code corresponding to the language of the audio file.
Can sometimes improve transcription performance if known beforehand.
Defaults to null, in which case the language is predicted automatically.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: tagAudioEvents boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to tag audio events like (laughter), (footsteps), etc. in the transcription.
Defaults to true.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: numSpeakers integer

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The maximum amount of speakers talking in the uploaded file.
Can help with predicting who speaks when.
The maximum amount of speakers that can be predicted is 32.
Defaults to null, in which case the amount of speakers is set to the maximum value the model supports.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: timestampsGranularity enum

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The granularity of the timestamps in the transcription.
Defaults to 'word'.
Allowed values: 'none', 'word', 'character'.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: diarize boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to annotate which speaker is currently talking in the uploaded file.
Defaults to true.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: fileFormat enum

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The format of input audio.
Defaults to 'other'.
Allowed values: 'pcm_s16le_16', 'other'.
For 'pcm_s16le_16', the input audio must be 16-bit PCM at a 16kHz sample rate, single channel (mono), and little-endian byte order.
Latency will be lower than with passing an encoded waveform.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Fal image models support flexible provider options through the providerOptions.fal object. You can pass any parameters supported by the specific Fal model's API. Common options include:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: imageUrl - Reference image URL for image-to-image generation (deprecated, use prompt.images instead)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: strength - Controls how much the output differs from the input image

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: guidanceScale - Controls adherence to the prompt (range: 1-20)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: numInferenceSteps - Number of denoising steps (range: 1-50)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: enableSafetyChecker - Enable/disable safety filtering

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: outputFormat - Output format: 'jpeg' or 'png'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: syncMode - Wait for completion before returning response

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: acceleration - Speed of generation: 'none', 'regular', or 'high'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: safetyTolerance - Content safety filtering level (1-6, where 1 is strictest)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: useMultipleImages - When true, converts multiple input images to image_urls array for models that support multiple images (e.g., fal-ai/flux-2/edit)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Deprecation Notice: snake_case parameter names (e.g., image_url,
guidance_scale) are deprecated and will be removed in a future version.
Please use camelCase names (e.g., imageUrl, guidanceScale) instead.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying the batchSize option will increase the number of audio chunks processed in parallel.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
language string
Language of the audio file. Defaults to 'en'. If set to null, the language will be automatically detected.
Accepts ISO language codes like 'en', 'fr', 'zh', etc.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
diarize boolean
Whether to diarize the audio file (identify different speakers).
Defaults to true.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
chunkLevel string
Level of the chunks to return. Either 'segment' or 'word'.
Default value: "segment"
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
version string
Version of the model to use. All models are Whisper large variants.
Default value: "3"
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
batchSize number
Batch size for processing.
Default value: 64
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
numSpeakers number
Number of speakers in the audio file. If not provided, the number of speakers will be automatically detected.
Optional.

Fireworks exposes the thinking of deepseek-r1 in the generated text using the <think> tag.
You can use the extractReasoningMiddleware to extract this reasoning and expose it as a reasoning property on the result:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Fireworks chat models support additional provider options that are not part of
the standard call settings. You can pass them in the providerOptions argument:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Fireworks chat models:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: promptCacheKey string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
A stable, opaque key that improves prompt cache hit rates by routing requests
with shared prompt prefixes to the same Fireworks replica. Reuse the same key
for all steps and calls in one conversation, and use different keys for
unrelated conversations.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: serviceTier 'priority'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Uses the Fireworks Priority serving path for higher reliability during peak
traffic. The provider sends it as Fireworks' service_tier request field.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinking object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Configuration for thinking/reasoning models like Kimi K2.6.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: type 'enabled' | 'disabled'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Whether to enable thinking mode.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: budgetTokens number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Maximum number of tokens for thinking (minimum 1024).

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: reasoningHistory 'disabled' | 'interleaved' | 'preserved'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Controls how reasoning history is handled in multi-turn conversations:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: 'disabled': Remove reasoning from history

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: 'interleaved': Include reasoning between tool calls within a single turn

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: 'preserved': Keep all reasoning in history

contents.heading: prompt-cache-affinity
contents.content:
Fireworks prompt caching
is automatic, but cached prefixes are local to a replica. Set
promptCacheKey to an opaque session or conversation identifier to improve
cache affinity. The provider sends it as Fireworks'
prompt_cache_key
request field.

contents.heading: prompt-cache-affinity
contents.content:
The AI SDK reuses the same provider options for every model step in a
multi-step generateText or streamText call, so one key covers the complete
tool loop:

contents.heading: prompt-cache-affinity
contents.content:
For a reusable ToolLoopAgent, use call options to supply a key for each
conversation. Pass the same key again for later agent calls that continue that
conversation:

contents.heading: prompt-cache-affinity
contents.content:
Use non-identifying values for cache keys rather than email addresses or other
personal information.

contents.heading: priority-service-tier
contents.content:
Fireworks Priority tier
prioritizes supported models above Standard traffic. Set serviceTier to
'priority' to send Fireworks' service_tier request field:

metadata.description: Learn how to use the Fish Audio provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content:
The Fish Audio provider contains speech generation (S1 and
S2 models) and speech-to-text transcription support.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Fish Audio provider is available in the @ai-sdk/fish-audio module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance fishAudio from @ai-sdk/fish-audio:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createFishAudio from @ai-sdk/fish-audio and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Fish Audio provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the FISH_AUDIO_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Base URL for the API calls.
Defaults to https://api.fish.audio.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Fish Audio text-to-speech API
using the .speech() factory method.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
The voice option selects a Fish Audio voice model ID (reference_id), either
from the Fish Audio voice library or one of your own
uploaded models. Omit it to use the default voice.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Voice listing is not part of the AI SDK speech model specification, so browse
voices with the Fish Audio list-models
endpoint
directly:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: Add self=true to list only your own uploaded models, or language=en / tag=narration to filter.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: referenceId string | array of strings

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Voice model ID(s). A single ID selects one speaker; an array enables
multi-speaker dialogue (S2-Pro models). Takes precedence over the top-level
voice option.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: sampleRate number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Output sample rate in Hz. Falls back to the format default when unset
(44100 Hz for wav/pcm/mp3, 48000 Hz for opus).
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: mp3Bitrate 64 | 128 | 192

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Bitrate in kbps for mp3 output. Ignored for other formats.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Bitrate in bps for opus output, where -1000 selects automatic. Ignored for
other formats.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: latency 'low' | 'normal' | 'balanced'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Latency/quality tradeoff. normal gives the best quality, balanced reduces
latency, and low is the fastest.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: volume number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Volume offset in dB. Negative values are quieter.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: normalizeLoudness boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Loudness normalization. Supported by the S2 family (s2-pro and
s2.1-pro). Fish Audio accepts it on s1 but ignores it, so the provider
drops it and emits a warning in that case.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: temperature number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Governs expressiveness (0 to 1). Higher values are more varied.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: topP number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Controls diversity via nucleus sampling (0 to 1).
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: chunkLength number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Text segment size for processing (100 to 300).
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: minChunkLength number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Minimum characters before splitting into a new chunk (0 to 100).
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: normalize boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Text normalization for English and Chinese. Helps stability with numbers.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: maxNewTokens number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Maximum audio tokens to generate per text chunk.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: repetitionPenalty number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Values above 1.0 discourage repeated audio patterns.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: conditionOnPreviousChunks boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Reuse prior audio as context for voice consistency across chunks.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: earlyStopThreshold number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Early-stop threshold used in batch processing (0 to 1).
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: features array of strings

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Request-scoped flags passed through to the inference backend, e.g.
['quality-guard'].
Optional.

contents.heading: multi-speaker-dialogue
contents.content:
S2-Pro models support multi-speaker dialogue. Pass an array of voice model IDs
via referenceId and mark turns in the text with <|speaker:N|>, where N
indexes into that array.

contents.heading: output-formats
contents.content:
Fish Audio supports the wav, pcm, mp3, and opus output formats. Any other
value falls back to mp3 and produces a warning.

contents.heading: output-formats
contents.content:
Fish Audio infers the language from the input text and the selected voice, and
has no language parameter. The language and instructions options are not
supported and produce warnings.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Model

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Multi-Speaker

contents.content: Notes

contents.content: s1

contents.heading: model-capabilities

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Recommended default; supports normalizeLoudness

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: s2.1-pro-free

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Free developer tier; no time-to-first-audio or data-processing guarantees

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content:
Streaming text-to-speech (Fish Audio's TTS-live WebSocket and timestamped
streaming endpoints) is not currently supported, and neither is inline
zero-shot voice cloning via references, which requires a MessagePack request
body. Upload reference audio to Fish Audio and pass its reference_id via
voice or referenceId instead.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Fish Audio speech-to-text API
using the .transcription() factory method.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The Fish Audio speech-to-text endpoint currently exposes no model selector and
serves a single model, so the model ID is optional and defaults to
'transcribe-1'. It is a routing label and is not sent to the API. Fish Audio
expects to add more ASR models and to select them with the model HTTP header,
matching the text-to-speech endpoint.

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content: language string

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content:
Language of the audio. A hint only: Fish Audio passes it to the model, but
auto-detection is authoritative and overrides it, so it changes neither the
transcript nor the reported language.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content: ignoreTimestamps boolean

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content:
Whether to skip precise timestamps. Mirrors the Fish Audio
ignore_timestamps parameter, whose API default is true. This provider
defaults it to false so that segments is populated. Fish Audio documents
an added latency cost for audio shorter than 30 seconds; set this to true to
trade segments for that latency.
Optional.

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content:
result.language reports the detected language as an ISO-639-1 code (e.g. en).
It is always a two-letter code, never a locale such as en-US, and is
undefined when Fish Audio detects no language.

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content:
The human-readable language name (e.g. English) is available as provider
metadata:

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content:
The provider metadata language is a display name intended for presentation.
Its exact form is not guaranteed, so avoid matching or branching on it — use
result.language for anything programmatic.

contents.heading: provider-options-1
contents.content:
Setting ignoreTimestamps to true makes Fish Audio return an empty
segments array. The provider therefore requests timestamps by default.

metadata.title: GMI Cloud
metadata.description: Learn how to use GMI Cloud's models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: The GMI Cloud provider offers access to open-weight language models through GMI Cloud's GPU inference platform, over an OpenAI-compatible API.
API keys can be obtained from the GMI Cloud console.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The GMI Cloud provider is available via the @ai-sdk/gmicloud module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance gmicloud from @ai-sdk/gmicloud:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: For custom configuration, you can import createGmicloud and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the GMI Cloud provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls.
The default prefix is https://api.gmi-serving.com/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header. It defaults to
the GMI_CLOUD_APIKEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch FetchFunction

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom fetch implementation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: GMI Cloud serves an evolving catalog of open-weight models, so model ids are typed as string. Embedding and image models are not supported.

contents.heading: error-diagnostics
contents.content: GMI Cloud's edge reports a generic banner in error.message on rejections and nests the backend engine's diagnostic in error.details. This provider unwraps the nested diagnostic, so AI_APICallError.message carries the engine's reason (e.g. The request is invalid: Invalid max_tokens value, the valid range of max_tokens is [1, 393216].) instead of Backend request failed with status 400.

metadata.title: Google Generative AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use Google Generative AI Provider.

title.children: Combine URL Context with Search Grounding

contents.content:
The Google Generative AI provider contains language and embedding model support for
the Google Generative AI APIs.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Google provider is available in the @ai-sdk/google module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance google from @ai-sdk/google:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createGoogleGenerativeAI from @ai-sdk/google and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Google Generative AI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the x-goog-api-key header.
It defaults to the GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: generateId () => string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional function to generate unique IDs for each request.
Defaults to the SDK's built-in ID generator.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: name string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom provider name.
Defaults to 'google.generative-ai'.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Google Generative AI API using the provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. gemini-2.5-flash.
The models support tool calls and some have multi-modal capabilities.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can use Google Generative AI language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Google Generative AI language models can also be used in the streamText function
and support structured data generation with Output
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
To remain forward-compatible, the provider treats unrecognized gemini-*
model IDs and -latest aliases like the newest supported Gemini generation.
Currently, this means Gemini 3 request behavior for provider-defined and mixed
tools, thinkingLevel reasoning, multimodal function responses, and thought
signatures. Known legacy Gemini model IDs keep their generation-specific
request behavior. This SDK default controls request serialization; the
selected model must still support each feature in the Google API.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Google Generative AI also supports some model specific settings that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Google Generative AI models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: cachedContent string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. The name of the cached content used as context to serve the prediction.
Format: cachedContents/{cachedContent}

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Enable structured output. Default is true.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
This is useful when the JSON Schema contains elements that are
not supported by the OpenAPI schema version that
Google Generative AI uses. You can use this to disable
structured outputs if you need to.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: See Troubleshooting: Schema Limitations for more details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: safetySettings Array<{ category: string; threshold: string }>

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Safety settings for the model.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: category string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The category of the safety setting. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_UNSPECIFIED

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_CIVIC_INTEGRITY

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: threshold string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The threshold of the safety setting. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_BLOCK_THRESHOLD_UNSPECIFIED

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_NONE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: OFF

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
responseModalities string[]
The modalities to use for the response. The following modalities are supported: TEXT, IMAGE. When not defined or empty, the model defaults to returning only text.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinkingConfig { thinkingLevel?: 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'; thinkingBudget?: number; includeThoughts?: boolean }

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Configuration for the model's thinking process. Only supported by specific Google Generative AI models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinkingLevel 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Controls the thinking depth for Gemini 3 and later models. Gemini 3.1 Pro supports 'low', 'medium', and 'high', Gemini 3 Pro supports 'low' and 'high', while Gemini 3 Flash supports all four levels: 'minimal', 'low', 'medium', and 'high'.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinkingBudget number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Gives the model guidance on the number of thinking tokens it can use when generating a response. Setting it to 0 disables thinking, if the model supports it.
For more information about the possible value ranges for each model see Google Generative AI thinking documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
This option is for Gemini 2.5 models. Gemini 3 and later models should use
thinkingLevel instead.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: includeThoughts boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. If set to true, thought summaries are returned, which are synthesized versions of the model's raw thoughts and offer insights into the model's internal reasoning process.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: imageConfig { aspectRatio?: string, imageSize?: string }

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Configuration for the models image generation. Only supported by specific Google Generative AI models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: aspectRatio string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Model defaults to generate 1:1 squares, or to matching the output image size to that of your input image. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: imageSize string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Controls the output image resolution. Defaults to 1K. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: 1K

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: 2K

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: 4K

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: audioTimestamp boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Enables timestamp understanding for audio-only files.
See Google Cloud audio understanding documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: mediaResolution string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. If specified, the media resolution specified will be used. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: MEDIA_RESOLUTION_UNSPECIFIED

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: MEDIA_RESOLUTION_LOW

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: MEDIA_RESOLUTION_MEDIUM

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: MEDIA_RESOLUTION_HIGH

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: See Google API MediaResolution documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: labels Record<string, string>

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Defines labels used in billing reports. Available on Vertex AI only.
See Google Cloud labels documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: serviceTier 'standard' | 'flex' | 'priority'

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. The service tier to use for the request.
Set to 'flex' for 50% cheaper processing at the cost of increased latency.
Set to 'priority' for ultra-low latency at a 75-100% price premium over 'standard'.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Because Priority can be gracefully downgraded to Standard under load, the
tier the request actually ran on is surfaced on
result.providerMetadata.google.serviceTier. See
Priority inference
and Flex inference.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: threshold string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Standalone threshold setting that can be used independently of safetySettings.
Uses the same values as the safetySettings threshold.

contents.heading: thinking
contents.content: The Gemini 2.5 and Gemini 3-and-later series models use an internal "thinking process" that significantly improves their reasoning and multi-step planning abilities, making them highly effective for complex tasks such as coding, advanced mathematics, and data analysis. For more information see Google Generative AI thinking documentation.

contents.heading: gemini-3-and-later-models
contents.content: For Gemini 3 and later models, use the thinkingLevel parameter to control the depth of reasoning:

contents.heading: gemini-25-models
contents.content: For Gemini 2.5 models, use the thinkingBudget parameter to control the number of thinking tokens:

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: The Google Generative AI provider supports file inputs, e.g. PDF files.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: You can also use YouTube URLs directly:

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content:
The AI SDK will automatically download URLs if you pass them as data, except
for https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/files/ and YouTube
URLs. You can use the Google Generative AI Files API to upload larger files to
that location. YouTube URLs (public or unlisted videos) are supported directly

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: you can specify one YouTube video URL per request.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: See File Parts for details on how to use files in prompts.

contents.heading: cached-content
contents.content: Google Generative AI supports both explicit and implicit caching to help reduce costs on repetitive content.

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Gemini 2.5 models automatically provide cache cost savings without needing to create an explicit cache. When you send requests that share common prefixes with previous requests, you'll receive a 75% token discount on cached content.

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: To maximize cache hits with implicit caching:

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Keep content at the beginning of requests consistent

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Add variable content (like user questions) at the end of prompts

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Ensure requests meet minimum token requirements:

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Gemini 2.5 Flash: 1024 tokens minimum

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Gemini 2.5 Pro: 2048 tokens minimum

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content:
Usage metadata was added to providerMetadata in @ai-sdk/google@1.2.23. If
you are using an older version, usage metadata is available in the raw HTTP
response body returned as part of the return value from generateText.

contents.heading: explicit-caching
contents.content: For guaranteed cost savings, you can still use explicit caching with Gemini 2.5 and 2.0 models. See the models page to check if caching is supported for the used model:

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: With Code Execution, certain models can generate and execute Python code to perform calculations, solve problems, or provide more accurate information.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: You can enable code execution by adding the code_execution tool to your request.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: The response will contain the tool calls and results from the code execution.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content:
With Google Search grounding,
the model has access to the latest information using Google Search.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: The googleSearch tool accepts the following optional configuration options:

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: searchTypes object

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Enables specific search types. Both can be combined.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: webSearch: Enable web search grounding (pass {} to enable). This is the default.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: imageSearch: Enable image search grounding (pass {} to enable).

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: timeRangeFilter object

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Restricts search results to a specific time range. Both startTime and endTime are required.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: startTime: Start time in ISO 8601 format (e.g. '2025-01-01T00:00:00Z').

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: endTime: End time in ISO 8601 format (e.g. '2025-12-31T23:59:59Z').

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: When Google Search grounding is enabled, the model will include sources in the response.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Additionally, the grounding metadata includes detailed information about how search results were used to ground the model's response. Here are the available fields:

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: webSearchQueries (string[] | null)

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Array of search queries used to retrieve information

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Example: ["What's the weather in Chicago this weekend?"]

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: searchEntryPoint ({ renderedContent: string } | null)

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Contains the main search result content used as an entry point

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: The renderedContent field contains the formatted content

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: groundingSupports (Array of support objects | null)

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Contains details about how specific response parts are supported by search results

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Each support object includes:

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: segment: Information about the grounded text segment

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: text: The actual text segment

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: startIndex: Starting position in the response

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: endIndex: Ending position in the response

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: groundingChunkIndices: References to supporting search result chunks

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: confidenceScores: Confidence scores (0-1) for each supporting chunk

contents.content:
With Enterprise Web Search,
the model has access to a compliance-focused web index designed for highly-regulated industries such as finance, healthcare, and public sector.

contents.heading: enterprise-web-search
contents.content:
Enterprise Web Search is only available on Vertex AI. You must use the Google
Vertex provider (@ai-sdk/google-vertex) instead of the standard Google

contents.content: The File Search tool lets Gemini retrieve context from your own documents that you have indexed in File Search stores. The provider enables this tool for Gemini 2.5 and Gemini 3-and-later model IDs, including unrecognized future Gemini IDs.

contents.heading: combine-url-context-with-search-grounding

contents.heading: google-maps-grounding
contents.content:
With Google Maps grounding,
the model has access to Google Maps data for location-aware responses. This enables providing local data and geospatial context, such as finding nearby restaurants.

contents.heading: google-maps-grounding
contents.content: The optional retrievalConfig.latLng provider option provides location context for queries about nearby places. This configuration applies to any grounding tools that support location context, including Google Maps and Google Search.

contents.heading: google-maps-grounding
contents.content: When Google Maps grounding is enabled, the model's response will include sources pointing to Google Maps URLs. The grounding metadata includes maps chunks with place information:

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding

This enables the model to provide answers based on your specific data sources and documents.

contents.heading: interactions-api
contents.content:
The Gemini Interactions API
(POST /v1beta/interactions) is a separate Google endpoint with server-side
state, unified content blocks, first-class built-in tools, agent presets,
managed agents that run in a sandboxed Linux environment, and native
multimodal image and video output. It is reached via the
google.interactions(...) factory:

contents.heading: interactions-api
contents.content:
google.interactions(...) accepts a model ID string (e.g.
'gemini-2.5-flash', 'gemini-3-pro-preview'), { agent: <name> } to use
a Gemini agent preset, or { managedAgent: <name> } to
invoke a managed agent you created on Google's side.
The returned model can be passed to generateText and streamText like
any other AI SDK language model.

contents.heading: interactions-api
contents.content:
Use google(...) for the standard :generateContent /
:streamGenerateContent endpoints, and google.interactions(...) for the
new Interactions endpoint. Pick one per model instance — they target
different request bodies and SSE event vocabularies.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
The Interactions model reads its options from the shared
providerOptions.google.* namespace. Validate them with the
GoogleLanguageModelInteractionsOptions type:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: previousInteractionId string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Server-side interaction id from a prior turn. When set, the server pulls
prior context from its own state and only the new user message is sent on
the wire. Pair with the default store: true to chain stateful
conversations. See Stateful chaining.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: store boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether the server should persist the interaction. Defaults to true.
Set to false for stateless multi-turn conversations where the full
message history is re-sent on every turn.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: agent string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Name of a Gemini agent preset (e.g. 'deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025').

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Prefer the factory form google.interactions({ agent: '...' }) over
setting agent in provider options — the factory is type-checked
against the supported agent names.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: agentConfig object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Per-agent configuration. Currently supports { type: 'dynamic' } and
{ type: 'deep-research', thinkingSummaries?, visualization?, collaborativePlanning? }.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinkingLevel 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Controls reasoning depth for thinking-enabled models. Mapped onto the
Interactions request's thinking_level.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinkingSummaries 'auto' | 'none'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether the model returns synthesized thought summaries on reasoning
parts. Defaults to the API default.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: responseFormat Array<ResponseFormatEntry>

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Output-format entries that map directly to the API's response_format
array. Entries have the following shape:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Use this for fine-grained control over image, audio, video, or non-JSON
text outputs. Video entries can control aspect ratio, resolution, duration,
and inline or URI delivery; set gcsUri when delivering to Google Cloud
Storage. Inline videos are returned in result.files by generateText and
emitted as file parts by streamText.
The AI SDK call-level responseFormat: { type: 'json', schema } still
drives JSON-mode automatically and prepends a matching text entry;
entries listed here are appended.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: imageConfig { aspectRatio?: string; imageSize?: '1K' | '2K' | '4K' | '512' } (deprecated)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Use responseFormat with a { type: 'image', ... } entry instead.
Retained for backwards compatibility; the SDK translates imageConfig
into a matching response_format image entry and emits a warning when
set. Ignored when responseFormat already supplies an image entry.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: mediaResolution 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'ultra_high'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Media resolution applied to image inputs / outputs.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: serviceTier 'flex' | 'standard' | 'priority'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Service tier for the request. Mirrored back on
result.providerMetadata.google.serviceTier for observability.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: systemInstruction string

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Alternative to the AI SDK system message. If both are set, the AI SDK
system message wins and a warning is emitted.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: background boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Run the interaction in the background. Required for agents whose
server-side workflow cannot complete within a single request/response;
rejected by agents that only support synchronous calls. When true,
the POST returns a non-terminal status and the SDK polls
GET /interactions/{id} until the work completes.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: environment string | object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Sandbox environment configuration for managed agents.
Pass 'remote' to provision a fresh sandbox, an environment_id
string to reuse an existing one, or an object of the form
{ type: 'remote', sources?, network? } to preload files and/or
constrain outbound traffic. Only applies to agent calls.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: pollingTimeoutMs number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Maximum time, in milliseconds, to poll a background interaction (agent
call) before giving up. Defaults to 30 minutes (1,800,000 ms). Long-running
agents such as deep research may need longer.

contents.content:
result.providerMetadata.google (typed via GoogleInteractionsProviderMetadata)
exposes:

contents.heading: provider-metadata

Server-side interaction id. Pass this back as previousInteractionId on

contents.heading: provider-metadata

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: Service tier the request actually ran on.

contents.heading: provider-metadata

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
Per-block signature hash, set by the SDK on output reasoning and

contents.content:
With the default store: true, the server retains the prior turn so the
next request only needs to send the new user message and the

full message history on every turn (no previousInteractionId):

contents.heading: image-output-via-interactions
contents.content:
Add a { type: 'image' } entry to responseFormat on a Gemini
image-capable model to get images as LanguageModelV4FilePart files in
the response. No tool wrapping is required, and the entry doubles as the
place to set aspectRatio, imageSize, and mimeType.

contents.heading: image-output-via-interactions
contents.content:
To control aspect ratio, image size, or output mime type, add those
fields to the same image entry:

contents.heading: image-output-via-interactions
contents.content:
For multimodal output, list one entry per modality. The model returns
text in result.text and the accompanying image(s) in result.files:

contents.heading: image-output-via-interactions
contents.content:
Iterative image editing pairs naturally with stateful chaining — keep
previousInteractionId set across turns and the model edits its prior

contents.heading: agent-presets
contents.content:
Pass { agent: <name> } to target a Gemini agent preset. The factory
type-checks the agent name against the supported set:

contents.heading: agent-presets
contents.content:
Whether an agent runs synchronously or in the background depends on the
agent. Long-running presets (such as the deep-research-* family)
require background: true — the POST returns a non-terminal status and
the SDK polls GET /interactions/{id} internally until the interaction
completes. Other agents accept synchronous calls only and will reject
background: true. Set the flag explicitly via
providerOptions.google.background.

contents.heading: agent-presets
contents.content:
The default polling timeout is 30 minutes; raise it via
pollingTimeoutMs for slower agents:

contents.heading: agent-presets
contents.content: Agents also chain through previousInteractionId like model-id calls.

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content:
Managed agents run inside a
sandboxed Linux environment provisioned per interaction. Pass the environment
provider option to control how the sandbox is set up; the option is only
accepted on agent calls.

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content: The simplest form provisions a fresh sandbox:

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content: environment accepts three shapes:

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content: 'remote' — provision a fresh sandbox for this call.

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content:
any other string — an environment_id to reuse, forking the previous
sandbox so its filesystem and installed packages persist.

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content:
an object — provision a fresh sandbox and optionally preload sources
and/or constrain outbound traffic via network:

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content:
Three source types are supported: inline (write a string into the
sandbox at target), repository (clone a git repository — pass the
URL as source), and gcs (mount a Google Cloud Storage prefix).

contents.heading: managed-agents
contents.content:
The network field accepts the string 'disabled' to block all
outbound traffic, or an object with an allowlist array whose entries
each carry a domain plus an optional transform array of header
objects to inject into matching requests.

contents.heading: custom-managed-agents
contents.content:
For user-defined agents that you created on Google's side via the
Gemini API's /v1beta/agents endpoint, pass the agent's name through the dedicated
managedAgent factory shape instead of agent (which only accepts
known preset names):

contents.heading: streaming
contents.content:
streamText is supported and consumes the seven Interactions SSE event
types (interaction.start, content.start, content.delta,
content.stop, interaction.status_update, interaction.complete,
error). The stream's finish part exposes interactionId on
providerMetadata.google so callers can chain.

contents.heading: gemma-models
contents.content:
You can use Gemma models with the Google Generative AI API.
The following Gemma models are available:

contents.heading: gemma-models
contents.content: Gemma models don't natively support the systemInstruction parameter, but the provider automatically handles system instructions by prepending them to the first user message. This allows you to use system instructions with Gemma models seamlessly:

contents.heading: gemma-models

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Google Generative AI embeddings API
using the .embedding() factory method.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: The Google Generative AI provider sends API calls to the right endpoint based on the type of embedding:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Single embeddings: When embedding a single value with embed(), the provider uses the single :embedContent endpoint, which typically has higher rate limits compared to the batch endpoint.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Batch embeddings: When embedding multiple values with embedMany() or multiple values in embed(), the provider uses the :batchEmbedContents endpoint.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Google Generative AI embedding models support additional settings. You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: When using embedMany, provide per-value multimodal content via the content option. Each entry corresponds to a value at the same index; use null for text-only entries:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Google Generative AI embedding models:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: outputDimensionality: number

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Optional reduced dimension for the output embedding. If set, excessive values in the output embedding are truncated from the end.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: taskType: string

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Optional. Specifies the task type for generating embeddings. Supported task types include:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY: Optimized for text similarity.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: CLASSIFICATION: Optimized for text classification.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: CLUSTERING: Optimized for clustering texts based on similarity.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT: Optimized for document retrieval.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: RETRIEVAL_QUERY: Optimized for query-based retrieval.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: QUESTION_ANSWERING: Optimized for answering questions.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: FACT_VERIFICATION: Optimized for verifying factual information.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY: Optimized for retrieving code blocks based on natural language queries.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: content: array

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Optional. Per-value multimodal content parts for embedding non-text content (images, video, PDF, audio). Each entry corresponds to the embedding value at the same index — its parts are merged with the text value in the request. Use null for entries that are text-only. The array length must match the number of values being embedded. Each non-null entry is an array of parts, where each part can be { text: string }, { inlineData: { mimeType: string, data: string } } for inline base64 data, or { fileData: { fileUri: string, mimeType: string } } to reference remote content via HTTP URL or Google Cloud Storage URI (gs://...). Supported by gemini-embedding-2-preview.

You can create image models that call the Google Generative AI API using the .image() factory method.
For more on image generation with the AI SDK see generateImage().

contents.heading: image-models

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content: Imagen models: Dedicated image generation models using the :predict API

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content: Gemini image models: Multimodal language models with image output capabilities using the :generateContent API

contents.heading: imagen-models
contents.content: Imagen models are dedicated image generation models.

contents.heading: imagen-models
contents.content: Further configuration can be done using Google provider options. You can validate the provider options using the GoogleImageModelOptions type.

contents.heading: imagen-models

contents.heading: imagen-models
contents.content:
personGeneration allow_adult | allow_all | dont_allow
Whether to allow person generation. Defaults to allow_adult.

contents.heading: imagen-models

Imagen models do not support the size parameter. Use the aspectRatio

Internally, the provider calls the language model API with responseModalities: ['IMAGE'].

contents.heading: gemini-image-models

contents.heading: gemini-image-models

contents.heading: gemini-image-models

For more advanced use cases where you need both text and image outputs, or
want more control over the generation process, you can use Gemini image models
directly with generateText(). See Image Outputs for

contents.content: Gemini image models support Google Search grounding through providerOptions.google.googleSearch. The value matches the args of google.tools.googleSearch(...); pass {} to enable with defaults, or { searchTypes: { imageSearch: {} } } to ground on reference photos.

metadata.title: Google Vertex AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Google Vertex AI provider.

contents.content: The Google Vertex provider for the AI SDK contains language model support for the Google Vertex AI APIs. This includes support for Google's Gemini models, Anthropic's Claude partner models, xAI's Grok partner models, and MaaS (Model as a Service) open models.

The Google Vertex provider is compatible with both Node.js and Edge runtimes.
The Edge runtime is supported through the @ai-sdk/google-vertex/edge
sub-module. More details can be found in the Google Vertex Edge
Runtime, Google Vertex Anthropic Edge
Runtime, and Google Vertex MaaS Edge
Runtime sections below.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Google Vertex, Google Vertex Anthropic, Google Vertex xAI, and Google Vertex MaaS providers are available in the @ai-sdk/google-vertex module. You can install it with

contents.heading: google-vertex-provider-usage
contents.content: The Google Vertex provider instance is used to create model instances that call the Vertex AI API. The models available with this provider include Google's Gemini models. If you're looking to use Anthropic's Claude models, see the Google Vertex Anthropic Provider section below.

contents.heading: google-vertex-provider-usage
contents.content:
Vertex Gemini models share the Google provider's forward-compatible model
classification. Unrecognized gemini-* IDs and -latest aliases use the
newest supported Gemini request behavior, while known legacy IDs keep their
generation-specific tool, reasoning, function-response, and thought-signature
handling. The selected Vertex model must still support each requested feature.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance vertex from @ai-sdk/google-vertex:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createVertex from @ai-sdk/google-vertex and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Google Vertex supports multiple authentication methods depending on your runtime environment and requirements.

contents.heading: nodejs-runtime
contents.content: The Node.js runtime is the default runtime supported by the AI SDK. It supports all standard Google Cloud authentication options through the google-auth-library. Typical use involves setting a path to a json credentials file in the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable. The credentials file can be obtained from the Google Cloud Console.

contents.heading: nodejs-runtime
contents.content: If you want to customize the Google authentication options you can pass them as options to the createVertex function, for example:

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the provider instance:

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: project string

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
The Google Cloud project ID that you want to use for the API calls.
It uses the GOOGLE_VERTEX_PROJECT environment variable by default.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: location string

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
The Google Cloud location that you want to use for the API calls, e.g. us-central1.
It uses the GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION environment variable by default.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: googleAuthOptions object

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: Optional. The Authentication options used by the Google Auth Library. See also the GoogleAuthOptions interface.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
authClient object
An AuthClient to use.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
keyFilename string
Path to a .json, .pem, or .p12 key file.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
keyFile string
Path to a .json, .pem, or .p12 key file.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
credentials object
Object containing client_email and private_key properties, or the external account client options.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
clientOptions object
Options object passed to the constructor of the client.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
scopes string | string[]
Required scopes for the desired API request.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
projectId string
Your project ID.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
universeDomain string
The default service domain for a given Cloud universe.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: headers Resolvable<Record<string, string | undefined>>

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: Headers to include in the requests. Can be provided in multiple formats:

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: A record of header key-value pairs: Record<string, string | undefined>

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: A function that returns headers: () => Record<string, string | undefined>

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: An async function that returns headers: async () => Record<string, string | undefined>

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: A promise that resolves to headers: Promise<Record<string, string | undefined>>

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings
contents.content:
Optional. Base URL for the Google Vertex API calls e.g. to use proxy servers. By default, it is constructed using the location and project:
https://${location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${project}/locations/${location}/publishers/google

contents.heading: edge-runtime
contents.content:
Edge runtimes (like Vercel Edge Functions and Cloudflare Workers) are lightweight JavaScript environments that run closer to users at the network edge.
They only provide a subset of the standard Node.js APIs.
For example, direct file system access is not available, and many Node.js-specific libraries
(including the standard Google Auth library) are not compatible.

contents.heading: edge-runtime
contents.content: The Edge runtime version of the Google Vertex provider supports Google's Application Default Credentials through environment variables. The values can be obtained from a json credentials file from the Google Cloud Console.

contents.heading: edge-runtime
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance vertex from @ai-sdk/google-vertex/edge:

contents.heading: edge-runtime
edge-runtime
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createVertex from @ai-sdk/google-vertex/edge and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: edge-runtime
contents.content: For Edge runtime authentication, you'll need to set these environment variables from your Google Default Application Credentials JSON file:

contents.heading: edge-runtime
contents.content: GOOGLE_CLIENT_EMAIL

contents.heading: edge-runtime
contents.content: GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY

contents.heading: edge-runtime
contents.content: GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY_ID (optional)

contents.heading: edge-runtime
contents.content: These values can be obtained from a service account JSON file from the Google Cloud Console.

contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the provider instance:

contents.content: project string

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings-1
contents.content:
The Google Cloud project ID that you want to use for the API calls.
It uses the GOOGLE_VERTEX_PROJECT environment variable by default.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings-1
contents.content:
The Google Cloud location that you want to use for the API calls, e.g. us-central1.

clientEmail string

privateKeyId string
The private key ID from the service account JSON file (optional). Defaults to the contents of the GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY_ID environment variable.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings-1
contents.content: headers Resolvable<Record<string, string | undefined>>

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings-1
contents.content: Headers to include in the requests. Can be provided in multiple formats:

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings-1
contents.content: A record of header key-value pairs: Record<string, string | undefined>

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings-1
contents.content: A function that returns headers: () => Record<string, string | undefined>

contents.content: An async function that returns headers: async () => Record<string, string | undefined>
