contents.heading: optional-provider-settings-1
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: express-mode
contents.content: Express mode provides a simplified authentication method using an API key instead of OAuth or service account credentials. When using express mode, the project and location settings are not required.

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings-2
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: optional-provider-settings-2
contents.content:
The API key for Google Vertex AI. When provided, the provider uses express mode with API key authentication instead of OAuth.
It uses the GOOGLE_VERTEX_API_KEY environment variable by default.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Vertex API using the provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. gemini-2.5-pro.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
If you are using your own
models, the name
of your model needs to start with projects/.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Google Vertex models support also some model specific settings that are not part
of the standard call settings. You can pass them as
an options argument:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Google Vertex models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: cachedContent string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. The name of the cached content used as context to serve the prediction.
Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/cachedContents/{cachedContent}

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Enable structured output. Default is true.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
This is useful when the JSON Schema contains elements that are
not supported by the OpenAPI schema version that
Google Vertex uses. You can use this to disable
structured outputs if you need to.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: See Troubleshooting: Schema Limitations for more details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: safetySettings Array<{ category: string; threshold: string }>

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Safety settings for the model.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: category string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The category of the safety setting. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_UNSPECIFIED

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_CIVIC_INTEGRITY

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: threshold string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The threshold of the safety setting. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_BLOCK_THRESHOLD_UNSPECIFIED

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_NONE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: audioTimestamp boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Enables timestamp understanding for audio files. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
This is useful for generating transcripts with accurate timestamps.
Consult Google's Documentation for usage details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: labels object

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Defines labels used in billing reports.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Consult Google's Documentation for usage details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: imageConfig object

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Configuration for image generation. Only supported by Gemini image models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: See Google's GenerationConfig documentation for usage details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: aspectRatio string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. The aspect ratio of generated images. Defaults to 1:1 squares, or to matching the output image size to that of an input image. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: imageSize string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Controls the output image resolution. Defaults to 1K. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: 1K

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: 2K

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: 4K

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: personGeneration string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Controls the generation of people in images. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: PERSON_GENERATION_UNSPECIFIED

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: ALLOW_ALL

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: ALLOW_ADULT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: ALLOW_NONE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: prominentPeople string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Controls whether generation of prominent people (celebrities) is allowed. When set together with personGeneration, personGeneration takes precedence. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: PROMINENT_PEOPLE_UNSPECIFIED

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: ALLOW_PROMINENT_PEOPLE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_PROMINENT_PEOPLE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: imageOutputOptions { mimeType?: 'image/jpeg' | 'image/png', compressionQuality?: number }

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. The image output format for generated images.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: streamFunctionCallArguments boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. When set to true, function call arguments will be streamed
incrementally in streaming responses. This enables tool-input-delta events
to arrive as the model generates function call arguments, reducing perceived
latency for tool calls. Defaults to false. Only supported on the Vertex AI API (not the Gemini API) with Gemini 3+ models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Consult Google's Documentation for details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: sharedRequestType 'priority' | 'flex' | 'standard'

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Selects a pay-as-you-go (PayGo) tier by setting the
X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Shared-Request-Type request header. Use 'priority' for
consistent low-latency performance at a premium, or 'flex' for a 50%
discount with longer expected latency. Both are supported only on the
global endpoint and on a subset of Gemini models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
By default — with Provisioned Throughput allocated and requestType unset
— the request consumes Provisioned Throughput quota first and only falls
back to the chosen shared tier if PT capacity is exhausted. To bypass
Provisioned Throughput entirely, also set requestType: 'shared'.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
The served tier is reported back on
result.providerMetadata.googleVertex.usageMetadata.trafficType as
ON_DEMAND_PRIORITY, ON_DEMAND_FLEX, or (if downgraded under load) plain
ON_DEMAND.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
See Priority PayGo
and Flex PayGo
for supported models, ramp limits, and downgrade behavior.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: requestType 'shared'

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Sets the X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Request-Type request header. Combine
with sharedRequestType to skip Provisioned Throughput entirely and route
the request through shared PayGo capacity. See
Priority PayGo.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can use Google Vertex language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Google Vertex language models can also be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: With Code Execution, certain Gemini models on Vertex AI can generate and execute Python code. This allows the model to perform calculations, data manipulation, and other programmatic tasks to enhance its responses.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: You can enable code execution by adding the code_execution tool to your request.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: The response will contain tool-call and tool-result parts for the executed code.

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: URL Context allows Gemini models to retrieve and analyze content from URLs. Supported models: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, 2.5 Pro, 2.5 Flash, 2.0 Flash.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Google Search enables Gemini models to access real-time web information. Supported models: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, 2.5 Flash, 2.0 Flash, 2.5 Pro.

contents.heading: enterprise-web-search
contents.content: Enterprise Web Search provides grounding using a compliance-focused web index designed for highly-regulated industries such as finance, healthcare, and the public sector. Unlike standard Google Search grounding, Enterprise Web Search does not log customer data and supports VPC service controls. Supported models: Gemini 2.0 and newer.

contents.heading: google-maps
contents.content: Google Maps grounding enables Gemini models to access Google Maps data for location-aware responses. Supported models: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, 2.5 Flash, 2.0 Flash, 2.5 Pro, 3.0 Pro.

contents.heading: google-maps
contents.content: The optional retrievalConfig.latLng provider option provides location context for queries about nearby places. This configuration applies to any grounding tools that support location context.

contents.heading: streaming-function-call-arguments
contents.content:
For Gemini 3 Pro and later models on Vertex AI, you can stream function call
arguments as they are generated by setting streamFunctionCallArguments to
true. This reduces perceived latency when functions need to be called, as
tool-input-delta events arrive incrementally instead of waiting for the
complete arguments. This option defaults to false.

contents.heading: streaming-function-call-arguments
contents.content:
This feature is only available on the Vertex AI API. It is not supported on
the Gemini API. When used with the Google Generative AI provider, a warning
will be emitted and the option will be ignored.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: Google Vertex AI, through its support for Gemini models, can also emit "thinking" tokens, representing the model's reasoning process. The AI SDK exposes these as reasoning information.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: To enable thinking tokens for compatible Gemini models via Vertex, set includeThoughts: true in the thinkingConfig provider option. These options are passed through providerOptions.vertex:

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: When includeThoughts is true, parts of the API response marked with thought: true will be processed as reasoning.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: In generateText, these contribute to the reasoningText (string) and reasoning (array) fields.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: In streamText, these are emitted as reasoning stream parts.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content:
Refer to the Google Vertex AI documentation on
"thinking"
for model compatibility and further details.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: The Google Vertex provider supports file inputs, e.g. PDF files.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content:
The AI SDK will automatically download URLs if you pass them as data, except
for gs:// URLs. You can use the Google Cloud Storage API to upload larger

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
You can transcribe audio with Google Cloud Speech-to-Text models using the
.transcription() factory method together with
transcribe().

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The provider supports Chirp
models chirp_2 and chirp_3, plus telephony for phone-call audio.
Speech-to-Text uses standard Google Cloud credentials (OAuth, Application Default
Credentials, or a service account) and calls the Cloud Speech-to-Text API.
Express Mode API keys are not supported for transcription models. Set
GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION (or providerOptions.googleVertex.region) to a
Speech-to-Text region. For Chirp, chirp_2 is available in us-central1,
europe-west4, and asia-southeast1; chirp_3 in the us and eu
multi-regions. Chirp is not available in the global Speech-to-Text location,
and these regions differ from Vertex AI regions. telephony availability
depends on the selected Speech-to-Text region and language.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The synchronous API transcribes audio up to one minute or 10 MB, whichever is
reached first. The spoken language is auto-detected by default; pass
languageCodes to restrict it. For telephony, pass a supported language code
such as ['en-US'].

contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: languageCodes string[]

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:

language. Defaults to ['auto']. Multiple explicit language codes require a
multi-region Speech-to-Text endpoint such as us or eu.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: enableAutomaticPunctuation boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: Whether to add punctuation to the transcript. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: enableWordTimeOffsets boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to include word-level timestamps in result.segments. Defaults to
true. Google notes that enabling word-level timestamps can reduce
transcription quality and speed.

contents.content: region string

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:

location.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content:
Anthropic cache control is in a Pre-Generally Available (GA) state on Google
Vertex. For more see Google Vertex Anthropic cache control
documentation.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content:
In the messages and message parts, you can use the providerOptions property to set cache control breakpoints.
You need to set the anthropic property in the providerOptions object to { cacheControl: { type: 'ephemeral' } } to set a cache control breakpoint.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content:
The cache creation input tokens are then returned in the providerMetadata object
for generateText, again under the anthropic property.
When you use streamText, the response contains a promise
that resolves to the metadata. Alternatively you can receive it in the
onFinish callback.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content: You can also use cache control on system messages by providing multiple system messages at the head of your messages array:

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content: For more on prompt caching with Anthropic, see Google Vertex AI's Claude prompt caching documentation and Anthropic's Cache Control documentation.

contents.heading: tools
contents.content: Google Vertex Anthropic supports a subset of Anthropic's built-in tools. The following tools are available via the tools property of the provider instance:

contents.heading: tools
contents.content: Bash Tool: Allows running bash commands.

contents.heading: tools
contents.content: Text Editor Tool: Provides functionality for viewing and editing text files.

contents.heading: tools
contents.content: Computer Tool: Enables control of keyboard and mouse actions on a computer.

contents.heading: tools
contents.content: Web Search Tool: Provides access to real-time web content.

contents.heading: tools
tools
contents.content:
Google Vertex Anthropic does not support strict mode on tool definitions.
Setting strict: true on a tool will be ignored and a warning will be
emitted.

contents.heading: tools
contents.content: For more background on Anthropic tools, see Anthropic's documentation.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: The Bash Tool allows running bash commands. Here's how to create and use it:

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: command (string): The bash command to run. Required unless the tool is being restarted.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: restart (boolean, optional): Specifying true will restart this tool.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: The Text Editor Tool provides functionality for viewing and editing text files:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: command ('view' | 'create' | 'str_replace' | 'insert' | 'undo_edit'): The command to run. Note: undo_edit is not supported in textEditor_20250429 and textEditor_20250728.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: path (string): Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. /repo/file.py or /repo.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: file_text (string, optional): Required for create command, with the content of the file to be created.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: insert_line (number, optional): Required for insert command. The line number after which to insert the new string.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: new_str (string, optional): New string for str_replace command.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: insert_text (string, optional): Required for insert command, containing the text to insert.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: old_str (string, optional): Required for str_replace command, containing the string to replace.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: view_range (number[], optional): Optional for view command to specify line range to show.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: max_characters (number, optional): Optional maximum number of characters to view in the file (only available in textEditor_20250728).

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: The Computer Tool enables control of keyboard and mouse actions on a computer:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: action ('key' | 'type' | 'mouse_move' | 'left_click' | 'left_click_drag' | 'right_click' | 'middle_click' | 'double_click' | 'screenshot' | 'cursor_position'): The action to perform.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: coordinate (number[], optional): Required for mouse_move and left_click_drag actions. Specifies the (x, y) coordinates.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: text (string, optional): Required for type and key actions.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: The Web Search Tool provides Claude with direct access to real-time web content:

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: maxUses (number, optional): Maximum number of web searches Claude can perform during the conversation.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: allowedDomains (string[], optional): Optional list of domains that Claude is allowed to search.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: blockedDomains (string[], optional): Optional list of domains that Claude should avoid when searching.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: userLocation (object, optional): Optional user location information to provide geographically relevant search results.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: type ('approximate'): The type of location (must be approximate).

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: city (string, optional): The city name.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: region (string, optional): The region or state.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: country (string, optional): The country.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: timezone (string, optional): The IANA timezone ID.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: These tools can be used in conjunction with supported Claude models to enable more complex interactions and tasks.

contents.content: The Groq provider contains language model support for the Groq API.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content:
The Groq provider is available via the @ai-sdk/groq module.
You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance

and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Groq provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://api.groq.com/openai/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance

contents.heading: provider-instance

API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the GROQ_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance

Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create Groq models using a provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. gemma2-9b-it.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Groq offers several reasoning models such as qwen-qwq-32b and deepseek-r1-distill-llama-70b.
You can configure how the reasoning is exposed in the generated text by using the reasoningFormat option.
It supports the options parsed, hidden, and raw.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Groq language models:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: reasoningFormat 'parsed' | 'raw' | 'hidden'

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Controls how reasoning is exposed in the generated text. Only supported by reasoning models like qwen-qwq-32b and deepseek-r1-distill-* models.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: For a complete list of reasoning models and their capabilities, see Groq's reasoning models documentation.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'none' | 'default'

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Controls the level of effort the model will put into reasoning.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: qwen/qwen3-32b

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Supported values:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: none: Disable reasoning. The model will not use any reasoning tokens.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: default: Enable reasoning.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: gpt-oss20b/gpt-oss120b

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Supported values:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: low: Use a low level of reasoning effort.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: medium: Use a medium level of reasoning effort.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: high: Use a high level of reasoning effort.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Defaults to default for qwen/qwen3-32b.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Whether to use structured outputs.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Defaults to true.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: When enabled, object generation will use the json_schema format instead of json_object format, providing more reliable structured outputs.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: strictJsonSchema boolean

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Whether to use strict JSON schema validation. When true, the model uses constrained decoding to guarantee schema compliance.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Defaults to true.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Only used when structuredOutputs is enabled and a schema is provided. See Groq's Structured Outputs documentation for details on strict mode limitations.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help with monitoring and abuse detection.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: serviceTier 'on_demand' | 'performance' | 'flex' | 'auto'

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Service tier for the request. Defaults to 'on_demand'.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: 'on_demand': Default tier with consistent performance and fairness

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: 'performance': Prioritized tier for latency-sensitive workloads

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: 'flex': Higher throughput tier (10x rate limits) optimized for workloads that can handle occasional request failures

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: 'auto': Uses on_demand rate limits first, then falls back to flex tier if exceeded

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: For more details about service tiers and their benefits, see Groq's service tiers documentation.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Structured outputs are enabled by default for Groq models.
You can disable them by setting the structuredOutputs option to false.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: You can disable structured outputs for models that don't support them:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Structured outputs are only supported by newer Groq models like
moonshotai/kimi-k2-instruct-0905. For unsupported models, you can disable
structured outputs by setting structuredOutputs: false. When disabled, Groq
uses the json_object format which requires the word "JSON" to be included in
your messages.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Groq transcription API
using the .transcription() factory method.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. whisper-large-v3.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 (e.g. en) format will improve accuracy and latency.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
timestampGranularities string[]
The granularity of the timestamps in the transcription.
Defaults to ['segment'].
Possible values are ['word'], ['segment'], and ['word', 'segment'].
Note: There is no additional latency for segment timestamps, but generating word timestamps incurs additional latency.
Important: Requires responseFormat to be set to 'verbose_json'.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
responseFormat string
The format of the response. Set to 'verbose_json' to receive timestamps for audio segments and enable timestampGranularities.
Set to 'text' to return only the transcribed text.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
language string
The language of the input audio. Supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 format (e.g. 'en') will improve accuracy and latency.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
prompt string
An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment. The prompt should match the audio language.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
temperature number
The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use log probability to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.
Defaults to 0.
Optional.

metadata.title: Kling AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Kling AI provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content: The Kling AI provider contains support for Kling AI's video generation models, including text-to-video, image-to-video, motion control, and multi-shot video generation.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Kling AI provider is available in the @ai-sdk/klingai module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance klingai from @ai-sdk/klingai:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createKlingAI from @ai-sdk/klingai and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Kling AI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Kling AI API key. Defaults to the KLINGAI_API_KEY environment variable.
Create one in the Kling AI developer console.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: accessKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Kling AI access key. Defaults to the KLINGAI_ACCESS_KEY environment variable.
Legacy authentication — prefer apiKey.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: secretKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Kling AI secret key. Defaults to the KLINGAI_SECRET_KEY environment variable.
Legacy authentication — prefer apiKey.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://api-singapore.klingai.com.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content: Kling AI supports two authentication schemes:

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
API key (recommended). A single key that is sent as a bearer token. Create
one in the Kling AI developer console and set
it as KLINGAI_API_KEY, or pass it via the apiKey setting.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:
Access key / secret key (legacy). A key pair that the provider uses to
sign a short-lived JWT for each request. Set KLINGAI_ACCESS_KEY and
KLINGAI_SECRET_KEY, or pass the accessKey and secretKey settings.

contents.heading: authentication
contents.content:

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
You can create Kling AI video models using the .video() factory method.
For more on video generation with the AI SDK see generateVideo().

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content: This provider currently supports four video generation modes: text-to-video, image-to-video, reference-to-video (multi-image), and motion control.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
Not all options are supported by every model version and mode combination. See
the KlingAI Capability
Map
for detailed compatibility across models.

contents.heading: text-to-video
contents.content: Generate videos from text prompts:

contents.heading: image-to-video
contents.content: Generate videos from a start frame image with an optional text prompt. The popular start+end frame feature is available via the imageTail option:

contents.heading: multi-shot-video-generation
contents.content: Generate videos with multiple storyboard shots, each with its own prompt and duration (Kling v3.0+):

contents.heading: multi-shot-video-generation
contents.content: Multi-shot also works with image-to-video by combining a start frame image with per-shot prompts.

contents.heading: reference-to-video-multi-image
contents.content: Generate a video that combines reference images using the top-level inputReferences option.

contents.heading: motion-control
contents.content: Generate video by transferring motion from a reference video to a character image:

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
The following provider options are available via providerOptions.klingai. Options vary by mode — see the
KlingAI Capability Map for per-model support.

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: mode 'std' | 'pro'

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content:
Video generation mode. 'std' is cost-effective. 'pro' produces higher quality
but takes longer.

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: pollIntervalMs number

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: Polling interval in milliseconds for checking task status. Defaults to 5000.

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: pollTimeoutMs number

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: Maximum wait time in milliseconds for video generation. Defaults to 600000 (10 minutes).

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: watermarkEnabled boolean

contents.heading: common-options
contents.content: Whether to generate watermarked results simultaneously.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: negativePrompt string

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: A description of what to avoid in the generated video (max 2500 characters).

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: sound 'on' | 'off'

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Whether to generate audio simultaneously. Only V2.6 and subsequent models support this, and requires mode: 'pro'.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: cfgScale number

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Flexibility in video generation. Higher values mean stronger prompt adherence. Range: [0, 1]. Not supported by V2.x models.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: cameraControl object

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Camera movement control with a type preset ('simple', 'down_back', 'forward_up', 'right_turn_forward', 'left_turn_forward') and optional config with horizontal, vertical, pan, tilt, roll, zoom values (range: [-10, 10]).

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: multiShot boolean

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Enable multi-shot video generation (Kling v3.0+). When true, the video is split into up to 6 storyboard shots with individual prompts and durations.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: shotType 'customize' | 'intelligence'

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Storyboard method for multi-shot generation. 'customize' uses multiPrompt for user-defined shots. 'intelligence' lets the model auto-segment based on the main prompt. Required when multiShot is true.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: multiPrompt Array<{index, prompt, duration}>

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Per-shot details for multi-shot generation. Each shot has an index (number), prompt (string, max 512 characters), and duration (string, in seconds). Shot durations must sum to the total duration. Required when multiShot is true and shotType is 'customize'.

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: voiceList Array<{voice_id: string}>

contents.heading: text-to-video-and-image-to-video-options
contents.content: Voice references for voice control (Kling v3.0+). Up to 2 voices. Reference via <<<voice_1>>> template syntax in the prompt. Requires sound: 'on'. Cannot coexist with elementList on the I2V endpoint.

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: imageTail string

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: End frame image for start+end frame control. Accepts an image URL or raw base64-encoded data. Requires mode: 'pro' for most models.

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: staticMask string

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: Static brush mask image for motion brush. Accepts an image URL or raw base64-encoded data.

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: dynamicMasks Array

contents.heading: image-to-video-only-options
contents.content: Dynamic brush configurations for motion brush. Up to 6 groups, each with a mask (image URL or base64) and trajectories (array of {x, y} coordinates).

contents.heading: image-to-video-and-motion-control-options
contents.content: elementList Array<{element_id: number}>

contents.heading: image-to-video-and-motion-control-options
contents.content: Reference elements for element control (Kling v3.0+). Supports video character elements and multi-image elements. Up to 3 elements for I2V (cannot coexist with voiceList). Up to 1 element for motion control.

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content: videoUrl string (required)

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content: URL of the reference motion video. Supports .mp4/.mov, max 100MB, duration 3–30 seconds.

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content: characterOrientation 'image' | 'video' (required)

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content:
Orientation of the characters in the generated video.
'image' matches the reference image orientation (max 10s video).
'video' matches the reference video orientation (max 30s video).

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content: keepOriginalSound 'yes' | 'no'

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content: Whether to keep the original sound from the reference video. Defaults to 'yes'.

contents.heading: motion-control-only-options
contents.content:
Video generation is an asynchronous process that can take several minutes.
Consider setting pollTimeoutMs to at least 10 minutes (600000ms) for
reliable operation.

metadata.title: Luma
metadata.description: Learn how to use Luma AI models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: Luma AI provides state-of-the-art image generation models through their Dream Machine platform. Their models offer ultra-high quality image generation with superior prompt understanding and unique capabilities like character consistency and multi-image reference support.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Luma provider is available via the @ai-sdk/luma module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance luma from @ai-sdk/luma:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createLuma and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Luma provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://api.lumalabs.ai.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the LUMA_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content:
You can create Luma image models using the .image() factory method.
For more on image generation with the AI SDK see generateImage().

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: You can customize the generation behavior with optional settings:

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: Since Luma processes images through an asynchronous queue system, these settings allow you to tune the polling behavior:

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: maxImagesPerCall number

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: Override the maximum number of images generated per API call. Defaults to 1.

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: pollIntervalMillis number

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content:
Control how frequently the API is checked for completed images while they are
being processed. Defaults to 500ms.

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: maxPollAttempts number

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content:
Limit how long to wait for results before timing out, since image generation
is queued asynchronously. Defaults to 120 attempts.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Luma offers two main models:

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Model

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Description

contents.heading: model-capabilities

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: High-quality image generation with superior prompt understanding

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: photon-flash-1

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Faster generation optimized for speed while maintaining quality

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Both models support the following aspect ratios:

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: 16:9 (default)

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: For more details about supported aspect ratios, see the Luma Image Generation documentation.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Key features of Luma models include:

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Ultra-high quality image generation

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: 10x higher cost efficiency compared to similar models

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Superior prompt understanding and adherence

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Unique character consistency capabilities from single reference images

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Multi-image reference support for precise style matching

contents.heading: image-editing
contents.content: Luma supports different modes of generating images that reference other images.

contents.heading: modify-an-image
contents.content: Images have to be passed as URLs. weight can be configured for each image in the providerOptions.luma.images array.

contents.heading: modify-an-image
contents.content: Learn more at https://docs.lumalabs.ai/docs/image-generation#modify-image.

contents.heading: reference-an-image
contents.content: Use up to 4 reference images to guide your generation. Useful for creating variations or visualizing complex concepts. Adjust the weight for each image (0-1) to control the influence of reference images.

contents.heading: reference-an-image
contents.content: Learn more at https://docs.lumalabs.ai/docs/image-generation#image-reference

contents.heading: style-reference
contents.content: Apply specific visual styles to your generations using reference images. Control the style influence using the weight parameter.

contents.heading: style-reference
contents.content: Learn more at https://docs.lumalabs.ai/docs/image-generation#style-reference

contents.heading: character-reference
contents.content: Create consistent and personalized characters using up to 4 reference images of the same subject. More reference images improve character representation.

contents.heading: character-reference
contents.content: Learn more at https://docs.lumalabs.ai/docs/image-generation#character-reference

metadata.title: MiniMax
metadata.description: Learn how to use MiniMax models with the AI SDK.

contents.content:
The MiniMax provider offers access to the MiniMax-M
series of language models through the MiniMax API, including models with
reasoning capabilities, as well as video generation with the MiniMax-H series.
API keys can be obtained from the MiniMax Platform.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The MiniMax provider is available via the @ai-sdk/minimax module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance minimax from @ai-sdk/minimax:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: For custom configuration, you can import createMiniMax and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the MiniMax provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls. This provider speaks MiniMax's
Anthropic-compatible protocol, so the default prefix is
https://api.minimax.io/anthropic/v1 — not the OpenAI-compatible
https://api.minimax.io/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: videoBaseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for video generation API calls. The video API uses
the MiniMax V2 native endpoint (not the Anthropic-compatible endpoint).
The default prefix is https://api.minimax.io.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key for the MiniMax API. It defaults to the MINIMAX_API_KEY environment
variable. Language models send it in the x-api-key header (the
Anthropic-compatible protocol); video models send it as
Authorization: Bearer.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom fetch implementation

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can create language models using a provider instance:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can also use the .chat() or .languageModel() factory methods:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
MiniMax language models can be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
MiniMax-M models can produce intermediate reasoning ("thinking") before their
final response. You control this behavior through provider options. The reasoning
output is streamed through the standard AI SDK reasoning parts.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for MiniMax language models:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinking object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Controls the model's reasoning ("thinking") behavior.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: type 'adaptive' | 'disabled'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: 'adaptive': the model decides when to reason (deep reasoning enabled)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
'disabled': the model responds directly without reasoning, for higher
throughput and lower latency

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: When omitted, the model uses its provider-side default.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Thinking control is only supported on minimax-m3. The M2.x models always
think, so 'disabled' has no effect on them.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
You can generate videos with the MiniMax-H3 and MiniMax-H3-Max models using
the experimental_generateVideo
function. MiniMax-H3-Max is the faster variant: it renders at lower resolutions
and serves every mode except reference-to-video.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
Both models generate one video per call. Generation is asynchronous — the model
creates a task and polls until it completes, then returns the resulting MP4 URL.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
duration accepts a whole number of seconds and defaults to 5. MiniMax-H3
supports 4 to 15 seconds; MiniMax-H3-Max supports 5 to 15 seconds. A fractional
value is rounded and an out-of-range value is clamped, each with a warning.
MiniMax-H3 supports 768P and 2K output, while MiniMax-H3-Max supports 480P
and 768P.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
The API takes a named tier rather than a frame size, so a top-level resolution
is matched against a fixed table of one frame size per tier per aspect ratio:

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content: Tier

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content: Accepted resolution values

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content: 2K

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
Anything outside the table, or a tier the selected model does not support, warns
and falls back to the model default. providerOptions.minimax.resolution names
the tier exactly and wins over the top-level value, which is reported as ignored.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
For text-to-video, aspectRatio defaults to 16:9 when omitted. The MiniMax
API requires a concrete ratio for text-only requests and does not accept
adaptive. For reference-to-video, the API default is adaptive when
aspectRatio is omitted. For image-to-video with frame images, the aspect
ratio follows the input image.

contents.heading: video-models
contents.content:
Result URLs are time-limited. Download and persist the video to your own
storage promptly after generation.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content: The generation mode is inferred from the inputs you pass:

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content: Text-to-video — prompt only.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
First-frame image-to-video — pass image (or a frameImages entry with
frameType: 'first_frame') to animate a starting image.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
First-to-last keyframes — pass frameImages with both a first_frame and
a last_frame to control the transition.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
Reference-to-video (MiniMax-H3 only) — pass inputReferences (images
and/or videos, routed by media type) to keep a subject/style or follow motion.
Frame images and references are mutually exclusive. MiniMax-H3-Max does not
support reference-to-video inputs.

contents.heading: generation-modes
contents.content:
When a frame image is supplied, the aspect ratio follows the image and any
explicit aspectRatio is ignored.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for MiniMax video models:

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: resolution '480P' | '768P' | '2K'

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Output resolution. MiniMax-H3 supports '768P' and '2K' (the default).
MiniMax-H3-Max supports '480P' and '768P' (the default).

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Aspect ratio of the generated video. Overrides the top-level aspectRatio.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: referenceAudioUrls string[]

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
Reference audio URLs (or mm_file:// handles) for MiniMax-H3
reference-to-video generation. Must be paired with at least one reference
image or video. Up to 3. MiniMax-H3-Max does not support reference audio.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: aigcWatermark boolean

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Whether to embed an AIGC watermark in the output. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: pollIntervalMs number

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Interval in milliseconds between task status polls. Default: 10000.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: pollTimeoutMs number

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content: Maximum time in milliseconds to poll before timing out. Default: 600000.

contents.heading: video-provider-options
contents.content:
MiniMax mm_file:// handles are only forwarded as-is for
referenceAudioUrls. They cannot be used for image, frameImages, or
inputReferences: those inputs go through the AI SDK's file handling, which
base64-decodes any string that is not an http(s):// or data: URL. Pass
those inputs as public URLs, data URIs, or binary data instead.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: MiniMax video results include providerMetadata.minimax:

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: taskId string

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: ID of the MiniMax generation task.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: videoUrl string

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: The MiniMax-hosted MP4 URL (the same URL as video). Time-limited.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: resolvedInputs object

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content:
The inputs that were actually sent, after the caps and rejections H3 imposes
(warnings report that an input was dropped, but not how many survived).

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content:
imageCount number — number of images sent (frame images or reference
images).

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content:
referenceVideoUrls string[] — the URLs of the reference videos sent.
Inline video data is omitted, since it is sent as a data URI.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: duration number

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: Duration of the generated video in seconds, when reported by the API.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: ratio string

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: Aspect ratio of the generated video, when reported by the API.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: resolution string

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: Resolution tier of the generated video, when reported by the API.

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content: usage object

contents.heading: video-provider-metadata
contents.content:
Billed seconds, when reported by the API: totalSeconds, inputSeconds,
and outputSeconds.

metadata.title: Mistral AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use Mistral.

contents.content:
The Mistral AI provider contains language model,
embedding model, and speech model support for Mistral APIs.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Mistral provider is available in the @ai-sdk/mistral module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance mistral from @ai-sdk/mistral:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
If you need a customized setup, you can import createMistral from @ai-sdk/mistral
and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Mistral provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://api.mistral.ai/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the MISTRAL_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Mistral chat API using a provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. mistral-large-latest.
Some Mistral chat models support tool calls.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Mistral chat models also support additional model settings that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them as an options argument and utilize MistralLanguageModelOptions for typing:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Mistral models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: safePrompt boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to inject a safety prompt before all conversations.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to false.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: documentImageLimit number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Maximum number of images to process in a document.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: documentPageLimit number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Maximum number of pages to process in a document.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: strictJsonSchema boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to use strict JSON schema validation for structured outputs. Only applies when a schema is provided and only sets the strict flag in addition to using Custom Structured Outputs, which is used by default if a schema is provided.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to false.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to use structured outputs. When enabled, tool calls and object generation will be strict and follow the provided schema.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to true.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use. When set to false, the model will use at most one tool per response.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to true.

contents.heading: document-ocr
contents.content:
Mistral chat models support document OCR for PDF files.
You can optionally set image and page limits using the provider options.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Mistral offers reasoning models that provide step-by-step thinking capabilities:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: magistral-small-2507: Smaller reasoning model for efficient step-by-step thinking

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: magistral-medium-2507: More powerful reasoning model balancing performance and cost

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: These models return structured reasoning content that the AI SDK extracts automatically. The reasoning is available via the reasoningText property in the result:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: The SDK automatically parses Mistral's native reasoning format and provides separate reasoningText and text properties in the result. No middleware is needed.

contents.heading: configurable-reasoning
contents.content: Some Mistral models support configurable reasoning, which you can control via the reasoningEffort option.

contents.heading: configurable-reasoning
contents.content: So far, Mistral only supports 'high' and 'none' as effort levels.

contents.heading: example
contents.content: You can use Mistral language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: example
contents.content:
Mistral language models can also be used in the streamText function
and support structured data generation with Output
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Mistral chat models support structured outputs using JSON Schema. You can use generateText or streamText with Output
and Zod, Valibot, or raw JSON Schema. The SDK sends your schema via Mistral's response_format: { type: 'json_schema' }.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: You can enable strict JSON Schema validation using a provider option:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
When using structured outputs, the SDK no longer injects an extra "answer with
JSON" instruction. It relies on Mistral's native json_schema/json_object
response formats instead. You can customize the schema name/description via
the standard structured-output APIs.

contents.heading: speech-models

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
The Mistral speech model maps voice to Mistral's voice_id. It supports
mp3, wav, pcm, flac, and opus output formats and defaults to mp3.
The instructions, speed, and language settings are not supported and
produce warnings when provided.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Mistral also supports one-off voice cloning with base64-encoded reference
audio. Pass it through providerOptions.mistral.refAudio and use
MistralSpeechModelOptions for type checking:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
When refAudio is provided, it takes precedence over voice. Reference audio
is redacted from request metadata and API call errors returned by the provider.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
Only use reference audio with the speaker's explicit consent. Follow Mistral's
voice cloning usage policy and disclose AI-generated audio when required. This
provider integration supports non-streaming speech generation; Mistral's
streaming speech API is not exposed through SpeechModelV3.

metadata.title: Moonshot AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use Moonshot AI models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: The Moonshot AI provider offers access to powerful language models through the Moonshot API, including the Kimi series of models with reasoning capabilities.
API keys can be obtained from the Kimi API Platform.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Moonshot AI provider is available via the @ai-sdk/moonshotai module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance moonshotai from @ai-sdk/moonshotai:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: For custom configuration, you can import createMoonshotAI and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Moonshot AI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls.
The default prefix is https://api.moonshot.ai/v1

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header. It defaults to
the MOONSHOT_API_KEY environment variable

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom fetch implementation

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can create language models using a provider instance:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can also use the .chatModel() or .languageModel() factory methods:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Moonshot AI language models can be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Moonshot V1 models support the standard temperature, topP,
presencePenalty, and frequencyPenalty settings. Kimi models use fixed
sampling parameters; the provider omits those settings for Kimi requests and
returns an unsupported-setting warning when they are supplied.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Kimi K3 supports toolChoice: 'required'. Kimi K2.6 and the Kimi K2.7 Code
models reject that setting, so the provider omits it and returns an unsupported
warning for those model IDs. Other tool choice modes are passed through
unchanged.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Native structured outputs are enabled for Kimi K models and the official
Moonshot V1 text, auto, and vision models.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
The provider normalizes schemas to Moonshot's supported JSON Schema subset and
enables strict schema validation by default.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For unknown custom model IDs, object generation falls back to JSON mode instead
of schema-constrained decoding.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: For best reliability, it is strongly recommended to include your schema requirements in your prompt in addition to passing the schema through Output.

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
Moonshot AI supports optional participant names on system, user, and assistant
messages. Set providerOptions.moonshotai.name on each message that should
include a name:

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
The same option works with streamText. Names are omitted when unset. The
provider ignores a name on a tool message and returns an unsupported warning.
Avoid including unnecessary personal or identifying information in message
names.

contents.heading: partial-mode
contents.content:
Moonshot AI's Partial Mode
continues the content of a final assistant message. Set partial: true in that
assistant message's provider options:

contents.heading: partial-mode
contents.content:
The partial message must be the final assistant message in the prompt. Moonshot
returns only the continuation, so concatenate the prefix and generated text
when you need the complete response.

contents.heading: partial-mode
contents.content:
Partial Mode cannot be combined with Moonshot's json_object response format.
The provider rejects that combination before sending the request. A supported
json_schema response remains available, but structured-output parsing
validates only the returned continuation.

contents.heading: kimi-k3-dynamic-tool-loading
contents.content:
Kimi K3 can load complete function tool definitions at arbitrary positions in
a conversation. Add tools to the Moonshot provider options of an empty system
message. The provider sends { role: 'system', tools: [...] } without a
content field and applies the same Moonshot Flavored JSON Schema normalization
used for top-level tools.

contents.heading: kimi-k3-dynamic-tool-loading
contents.content:
Each entry must include its complete function definition. Top-level tools and
dynamically loaded tools can be used in the same request. Known unsupported
official models omit the dynamic message and return an unsupported warning;
custom model IDs retain it for forward compatibility.

contents.heading: kimi-k3-dynamic-tool-loading
contents.content:
Keep dynamic system messages in trusted server-side state. Tool names,
descriptions, and schemas are sent to Moonshot and consume context. Dynamic
declarations are request-local, so retain earlier declarations in later
requests while those tools should remain available. Appending messages also
preserves prompt-cache prefixes better than rewriting earlier declarations.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Kimi K3 always reasons and supports low, high, and max reasoning effort.
The default is max. You can configure the effort through provider options:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Kimi K2.5 and K2.6 can enable or disable thinking. Kimi K2.7 always has
thinking and preserved reasoning enabled. Keep reasoning history in multi-turn
Kimi K2.7 conversations. The reasoning output is exposed through the standard
AI SDK reasoning parts.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: log-probabilities
contents.content:
Moonshot AI can return token log probabilities for Chat Completions. Set
logprobs to request token probabilities, or set topLogprobs to request the
most likely alternatives at each token position. Setting topLogprobs
automatically enables logprobs.

contents.heading: log-probabilities
contents.content:
For generateText, log probabilities are available at
providerMetadata.moonshotai.logprobs. For streamText, the accumulated log
probabilities are included in the final finish part under the same metadata
path.

contents.heading: log-probabilities
contents.content:
Moonshot documents the request options and OpenAI Chat Completions
compatibility, but does not separately specify the log probability response
schema. The provider therefore preserves the OpenAI-compatible content
entries, including each token's logprob, nullable bytes, and
top_logprobs.

contents.heading: log-probabilities
contents.content:
Token probabilities and alternatives can significantly increase response size.
Request them only when needed, and avoid forwarding or persistently logging
provider metadata unless your application requires it.

contents.heading: video-input
contents.content: Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7 Code, Kimi K2.6, and Kimi K2.5 support video input. Pass the video as a file content part with a video media type:

contents.heading: video-input
contents.content: You can also pass a URL. Since Moonshot AI does not fetch external URLs, the AI SDK downloads the video and inlines it as base64 before sending:

contents.heading: video-input
contents.content:
Supported image media types are image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif,
image/webp, image/bmp, image/heic, and image/heif. Supported video
media types are video/mp4, video/mpeg, video/mov, video/avi,
video/x-flv, video/mpg, video/webm, video/wmv, and video/3gpp. Other
image and video media types are rejected before a request is sent.

contents.heading: video-input
contents.content:
Moonshot AI recommends videos up to 1080p. For larger videos, or videos you
reuse across many requests, upload them with the Moonshot Files
API instead. Audio and PDF inputs
are not supported by Moonshot AI chat completions.

contents.heading: predicted-outputs
predicted-outputs
contents.content: The content can also be an array of text parts:

contents.heading: predicted-outputs
contents.content:
Predicted content is sent to Moonshot AI as part of the request. Avoid
including sensitive or proprietary text unless you intend to share it with the
provider.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Moonshot AI language models:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: strictJsonSchema boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether to use strict JSON schema validation for structured outputs. Defaults
to true.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: logprobs boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether to return log probabilities for generated tokens. Results are
available in providerMetadata.moonshotai.logprobs.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: topLogprobs number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Number of most likely tokens to return at each token position. Accepts
integer values from 0 through 20 and automatically enables logprobs.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'low' | 'high' | 'max'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Reasoning effort for Kimi K3. Defaults to 'max'. You can also use the
generic reasoning setting.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: prediction { type: 'content'; content: string | Array<{ type: 'text'; text: string }> }

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Supplies static predicted output that can accelerate requests where most of
the response is already known.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinking object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Configuration for Kimi K2.5 and K2.6. Kimi K2.7 accepts only enabled
because its thinking cannot be disabled. Kimi K3 does not accept this field.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: type 'enabled' | 'disabled'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether to enable thinking mode. For Kimi K2.7 Code, only 'enabled' is
accepted.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: budgetTokens number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Deprecated. Moonshot Chat Completions does not support thinking budgets.
The provider omits this value and returns a warning. It remains accepted
for backwards compatibility.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: reasoningHistory 'disabled' | 'interleaved' | 'preserved'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Controls preserved reasoning behavior in multi-turn conversations:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
'disabled' and 'interleaved' are retained for compatibility. They do
not change the request, so the model's server-default behavior applies.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
'preserved' maps to thinking.keep: 'all' for Kimi K2.6. Kimi K2.7 and
K3 preserve reasoning by default.

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
Moonshot AI preserves provider-specific response fields in
providerMetadata.moonshotai for generated and streamed responses:

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: responseObject: chat.completion or chat.completion.chunk

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: choiceIndex: the selected response choice index

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: messageRole: the response message role, when supplied

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: toolCallTypes: the tool-call type for each returned call

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
These fields remain in provider metadata because they are specific to
Moonshot's Chat Completions response rather than shared AI SDK result fields.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content:
The Moonshot V1 series and Kimi K2.5 are unavailable to newly registered users
and are scheduled for full platform sunset on August 31, 2026. They remain
listed because they are still part of the Chat Completions API model surface,
but new applications should use Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7 Code, or Kimi K2.6.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Open Responses provider is available in the @ai-sdk/open-responses module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Create an Open Responses provider instance using createOpenResponses:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: The name and url options are required:

contents.heading: provider-instance

contents.heading: provider-instance

contents.heading: provider-instance

contents.heading: provider-instance
