contents.heading: enhance-your-chatbot-with-tools
contents.content: While large language models (LLMs) have incredible generation capabilities, they struggle with discrete tasks (e.g. mathematics) and interacting with the outside world (e.g. getting the weather). This is where tools come in.

contents.heading: enhance-your-chatbot-with-tools
contents.content: Tools are actions that an LLM can invoke. The results of these actions can be reported back to the LLM to be considered in the next response.

contents.heading: enhance-your-chatbot-with-tools
contents.content: For example, if a user asks about the current weather, without tools, the model would only be able to provide general information based on its training data. But with a weather tool, it can fetch and provide up-to-date, location-specific weather information.

contents.heading: enhance-your-chatbot-with-tools
contents.content: Let's enhance your chatbot by adding a simple weather tool.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content: Modify your app/api/chat+api.ts file to include the new weather tool:

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content: In this updated code:

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content: You import the tool function from the ai package and z from zod for schema validation.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content: You define a tools object with a weather tool. This tool:

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content: Has a description that helps the model understand when to use it.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content: Defines inputSchema using a Zod schema, specifying that it requires a location string to execute this tool. The model will attempt to extract this input from the context of the conversation. If it can't, it will ask the user for the missing information.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content: Defines an execute function that simulates getting weather data (in this case, it returns a random temperature). This is an asynchronous function running on the server so you can fetch real data from an external API.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content: Now your chatbot can "fetch" weather information for any location the user asks about. When the model determines it needs to use the weather tool, it will generate a tool call with the necessary input. The execute function will then be automatically run, and the tool output will be added to the messages as a tool message.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content:
You may need to restart your development server for the changes to take
effect.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content: Try asking something like "What's the weather in New York?" and see how the model uses the new tool.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content: Notice the blank response in the UI? This is because instead of generating a text response, the model generated a tool call. You can access the tool call and subsequent tool result on the client via the tool-weather part of the message.parts array.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route
contents.content:
Tool parts are always named tool-{toolName}, where {toolName} is the key
you used when defining the tool. In this case, since we defined the tool as
weather, the part type is tool-weather.

contents.heading: update-the-ui
contents.content: To display the weather tool invocation in your UI, update your app/(tabs)/index.tsx file:

contents.heading: update-the-ui
contents.content:
You may need to restart your development server for the changes to take
effect.

contents.heading: update-the-ui
contents.content: With this change, you're updating the UI to handle different message parts. For text parts, you display the text content as before. For weather tool invocations, you display a JSON representation of the tool call and its result.

contents.heading: update-the-ui
contents.content: Now, when you ask about the weather, you'll see the tool call and its result displayed in your chat interface.

contents.heading: enabling-multi-step-tool-calls
contents.content: You may have noticed that while the tool results are visible in the chat interface, the model isn't using this information to answer your original query. This is because once the model generates a tool call, it has technically completed its generation.

contents.heading: enabling-multi-step-tool-calls
contents.content: To solve this, you can enable multi-step tool calls using stopWhen. By default, stopWhen is set to stepCountIs(1), which means generation stops after the first step when there are tool results. By changing this condition, you can allow the model to automatically send tool results back to itself to trigger additional generations until your specified stopping condition is met. In this case, you want the model to continue generating so it can use the weather tool results to answer your original question.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route-1
contents.content: Modify your app/api/chat+api.ts file to include the stopWhen condition:

contents.heading: update-your-api-route-1
contents.content:
You may need to restart your development server for the changes to take
effect.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route-1
contents.content: Head back to the Expo app and ask about the weather in a location. You should now see the model using the weather tool results to answer your question.

contents.heading: update-your-api-route-1
contents.content: By setting stopWhen: stepCountIs(5), you're allowing the model to use up to 5 "steps" for any given generation. This enables more complex interactions and allows the model to gather and process information over several steps if needed. You can see this in action by adding another tool to convert the temperature from Fahrenheit to Celsius.

contents.heading: add-more-tools
contents.content: Update your app/api/chat+api.ts file to add a new tool to convert the temperature from Fahrenheit to Celsius:

contents.heading: add-more-tools
contents.content:
You may need to restart your development server for the changes to take
effect.

contents.heading: update-the-ui-for-the-new-tool
contents.content: To display the temperature conversion tool invocation in your UI, update your app/(tabs)/index.tsx file to handle the new tool part:

contents.heading: update-the-ui-for-the-new-tool
contents.content:
You may need to restart your development server for the changes to take
effect.

contents.heading: update-the-ui-for-the-new-tool
contents.content: Now, when you ask "What's the weather in New York in celsius?", you should see a more complete interaction:

contents.heading: update-the-ui-for-the-new-tool
contents.content: The model will call the weather tool for New York.

contents.heading: update-the-ui-for-the-new-tool
contents.content: You'll see the tool result displayed.

contents.heading: update-the-ui-for-the-new-tool
contents.content: It will then call the temperature conversion tool to convert the temperature from Fahrenheit to Celsius.

contents.heading: update-the-ui-for-the-new-tool
contents.content: The model will then use that information to provide a natural language response about the weather in New York.

contents.heading: update-the-ui-for-the-new-tool
contents.content: This multi-step approach allows the model to gather information and use it to provide more accurate and contextual responses, making your chatbot considerably more useful.

contents.heading: update-the-ui-for-the-new-tool
contents.content: This simple example demonstrates how tools can expand your model's capabilities. You can create more complex tools to integrate with real APIs, databases, or any other external systems, allowing the model to access and process real-world data in real-time. Tools bridge the gap between the model's knowledge cutoff and current information.

When to use AI SDK RSC

contents.content: The AI SDK is a powerful toolkit for building AI applications. This page will help you pick the right tools for your requirements.
Let’s start with a quick overview of the AI SDK, which is comprised of three parts:
AI SDK Core: A unified, provider agnostic API for generating text, structured objects, and tool calls with LLMs.
AI SDK UI: A set of framework-agnostic hooks for building chat and generative user interfaces.
AI SDK RSC: Stream generative user interfaces with React Server Components (RSC). Development is currently experimental and we recommend using AI SDK UI.

contents.heading: choosing-the-right-tool-for-your-environment
contents.content: When deciding which part of the AI SDK to use, your first consideration should be the environment and existing stack you are working with. Different components of the SDK are tailored to specific frameworks and environments.

contents.content: AI SDK UI supports the following frameworks: React, Svelte, and Vue.js. Here is a comparison of the supported functions across these frameworks:

contents.heading: when-to-use-ai-sdk-rsc
contents.content:
AI SDK RSC is currently experimental. We recommend using AI SDK
UI for production. For guidance on migrating from
RSC to UI, see our migration guide.

contents.heading: when-to-use-ai-sdk-rsc
contents.content:
React Server Components
(RSCs) provide a new approach to building React applications that allow components
to render on the server, fetch data directly, and stream the results to the client,
reducing bundle size and improving performance. They also introduce a new way to
call server-side functions from anywhere in your application called Server Actions.

contents.heading: when-to-use-ai-sdk-rsc
contents.content: AI SDK RSC provides a number of utilities that allow you to stream values and UI directly from the server to the client. However, it's important to be aware of current limitations:

contents.heading: when-to-use-ai-sdk-rsc
contents.content: Cancellation: currently, it is not possible to abort a stream using Server Actions. This will be improved in future releases of React and Next.js.

contents.heading: when-to-use-ai-sdk-rsc
contents.content: Increased Data Transfer: using createStreamableUI can lead to quadratic data transfer (quadratic to the length of generated text). You can avoid this using  createStreamableValue  instead, and rendering the component client-side.

contents.heading: when-to-use-ai-sdk-rsc
contents.content: Re-mounting Issue During Streaming: when using createStreamableUI, components re-mount on .done(), causing flickering.

contents.heading: when-to-use-ai-sdk-rsc
contents.content: Given these limitations, we recommend using AI SDK UI for production applications.

Tool parts are always named tool-{toolName}, where {toolName} is the key
you used when defining the tool. In this case, since we defined the tool as

By default, stopWhen is set to stepCountIs(1), which means generation stops after the first step when there are tool results. By changing this condition, you can allow the model to automatically send tool results back to itself to trigger additional generations until your specified stopping condition is met. In this case, you want the model to continue generating so it can use the weather tool results to answer your original question.

contents.heading: how-does-ai-sdksvelte-differ-from-ai-sdkreact
contents.content: The surface-level difference is that Svelte uses classes to manage state, whereas React uses hooks, so useChat in React is Chat in Svelte. Other than that, there are a few things to keep in mind:

contents.heading: arguments-to-classes-arent-reactive-by-default
contents.content:
Unlike in React, where hooks are rerun any time their containing component is invalidated, code in the script block of a Svelte component is only run once when the component is created.
This means that, if you want arguments to your class to be reactive, you need to make sure you pass a reference into the class, rather than a value:

contents.heading: arguments-to-classes-arent-reactive-by-default
contents.content: Keep in mind that this normally doesn't matter; most parameters you'll pass into the Chat class are static (for example, you typically wouldn't expect your onError handler to change).

contents.heading: you-cant-destructure-class-properties
contents.content: In vanilla JavaScript, destructuring class properties copies them by value and "disconnects" them from their class instance:

contents.heading: you-cant-destructure-class-properties
contents.content: The same is true of classes in Svelte:

contents.heading: instance-synchronization-requires-context
contents.content:
In React, hook instances with the same id are synchronized -- so two instances of useChat will have the same messages, status, etc. if they have the same id.
For most use cases, you probably don't need this behavior -- but if you do, you can create a context in your root layout file using createAIContext:

contents.content: The AI SDK is a powerful Typescript library designed to help developers build AI-powered applications.

In this quickstart tutorial, you'll build a simple agent with a streaming chat user interface. Along the way, you'll learn key concepts and techniques that are fundamental to using the AI SDK in your own projects.
If you are unfamiliar with the concepts of Prompt Engineering and HTTP Streaming, you can optionally read these documents first.

contents.heading: create-a-route-handler
contents.content: Define an asynchronous POST request handler using TanStack Start's server routes and extract messages from the body of the request. The messages variable contains a history of the conversation between you and the chatbot and provides the chatbot with the necessary context to make the next generation. The messages are of UIMessage type, which are designed for use in application UI - they contain the entire message history and associated metadata like timestamps.

contents.heading: create-a-route-handler
contents.content: Call streamText, which is imported from the ai package. This function accepts a configuration object that contains a model provider and messages (defined in step 1). You can pass additional settings to further customise the model's behaviour. The messages key expects a ModelMessage[] array. This type is different from UIMessage in that it does not include metadata, such as timestamps or sender information. To convert between these types, we use the convertToModelMessages function, which strips the UI-specific metadata and transforms the UIMessage[] array into the ModelMessage[] format that the model expects.

contents.heading: create-a-route-handler
contents.content: The streamText function returns a StreamTextResult. This result object contains the  toUIMessageStreamResponse  function which converts the result to a streamed response object.

contents.heading: create-a-route-handler
contents.content: Finally, return the result to the client to stream the response.

contents.content: The AI SDK is the TypeScript toolkit designed to help developers build AI-powered applications and agents with React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Node.js, and more.

contents.heading: why-use-the-ai-sdk
contents.content: Integrating large language models (LLMs) into applications is complicated and heavily dependent on the specific model provider you use.

contents.heading: why-use-the-ai-sdk
contents.content: The AI SDK standardizes integrating artificial intelligence (AI) models across supported providers. This enables developers to focus on building great AI applications, not waste time on technical details.

contents.heading: why-use-the-ai-sdk
contents.content: For example, here’s how you can generate text with various models using the AI SDK:

contents.heading: why-use-the-ai-sdk
contents.content: The AI SDK has two main libraries:

contents.heading: why-use-the-ai-sdk
contents.content: AI SDK Core: A unified API for generating text, structured objects, tool calls, and building agents with LLMs.

contents.heading: why-use-the-ai-sdk
contents.content: AI SDK UI: A set of framework-agnostic hooks for quickly building chat and generative user interface.

contents.heading: model-providers
contents.content: The AI SDK supports multiple model providers.

contents.heading: templates
contents.content: We've built some templates that include AI SDK integrations for different use cases, providers, and frameworks. You can use these templates to get started with your AI-powered application.

Upgrade to AI SDK 3.1

contents.heading: ai-sdk
contents.content: To update to AI SDK version 3.1, run the following command using your preferred package manager:

contents.heading: next-steps
contents.content: The release of AI SDK 3.1 introduces several new features that improve the way you build AI applications with the SDK:

contents.heading: next-steps
contents.content: AI SDK Core, a brand new unified API for interacting with large language models (LLMs).

contents.heading: next-steps
contents.content: streamUI, a new abstraction, built upon AI SDK Core functions that simplifies building streaming UIs.

contents.heading: migrating-from-legacy-providers-to-ai-sdk-core
contents.content: Prior to AI SDK Core, you had to use a model provider's SDK to query their models.

contents.heading: migrating-from-legacy-providers-to-ai-sdk-core
contents.content: In the following Route Handler, you use the OpenAI SDK to query their model. You then pipe that response into the OpenAIStream function which returns a ReadableStream that you can pass to the client using a new StreamingTextResponse.

contents.heading: migrating-from-legacy-providers-to-ai-sdk-core
contents.content: With AI SDK Core you have a unified API for any provider that implements the AI SDK Language Model Specification.

contents.heading: migrating-from-legacy-providers-to-ai-sdk-core
contents.content: Let’s take a look at the example above, but refactored to utilize the AI SDK Core API alongside the AI SDK OpenAI provider. In this example, you import the LLM function you want to use from the ai package, import the OpenAI provider from @ai-sdk/openai, and then you call the model and return the response using the toDataStreamResponse() helper function.

contents.heading: migrating-from-render-to-streamui
contents.content: The AI SDK RSC API was launched as part of version 3.0. This API introduced the render function, a helper function to create streamable UIs with OpenAI models. With the new AI SDK Core API, it became possible to make streamable UIs possible with any compatible provider.

contents.heading: migrating-from-render-to-streamui
contents.content: The following example Server Action uses the render function using the model provider directly from OpenAI. You first create an OpenAI provider instance with the OpenAI SDK. Then, you pass it to the provider key of the render function alongside a tool that returns a React Server Component, defined in the render key of the tool.

contents.heading: migrating-from-render-to-streamui
contents.content: With the new streamUI function, you can now use any compatible AI SDK provider. In this example, you import the AI SDK OpenAI provider. Then, you pass it to the model key of the new streamUI function. Finally, you declare a tool and return a React Server Component, defined in the generate key of the tool.

contents.content:
Check out the AI SDK 3.3 release blog
post for more information about
the release.
No breaking changes in this release.

The following changelog encompasses all changes made in the 3.2.x series,
introducing significant improvements and new features across the AI SDK and its associated libraries:

contents.heading: open-telemetry-support
contents.content: Added experimental OpenTelemetry support for all AI SDK Core functions, enabling better observability and tracing capabilities.

contents.heading: ai-sdk-ui-improvements
contents.content: Introduced the experimental useObject hook (for React) that can be used in conjunction with streamObject on the backend to enable seamless streaming of structured data.

contents.heading: ai-sdk-ui-improvements
contents.content: Enhanced useChat with experimental support for attachments and streaming tool calls, providing more versatile chat functionalities.

contents.heading: ai-sdk-ui-improvements
contents.content: Patched useChat to prevent empty submissions, improving the quality of user interactions by ensuring that only intended inputs are processed.

contents.heading: ai-sdk-ui-improvements
contents.content: Fix useChat's reload function, now correctly sending data, body, and headers.

contents.heading: ai-sdk-ui-improvements
contents.content: Implemented setThreadId helper for useAssistant, simplifying thread management.

contents.heading: ai-sdk-ui-improvements
contents.content: Documented the stream data protocol for useChat and useCompletion, allowing developers to use these functions with any backend. The stream data protocol also enables the use of custom frontends with streamText.

contents.heading: ai-sdk-ui-improvements
contents.content: Added support for custom fetch functions and request body customization, offering greater control over API interactions.

contents.heading: ai-sdk-ui-improvements
contents.content: Added onFinish to useChat hook for access to token usage and finish reason.

contents.heading: core-enhancements
contents.content: Implemented support for sending custom request headers, enabling more tailored API requests.

contents.heading: core-enhancements
contents.content: Added raw JSON schema support alongside existing Zod support, providing more options for schema and data validation.

contents.heading: core-enhancements
contents.content: Introduced usage information for embed and embedMany functions, offering insights into token usage.

contents.heading: core-enhancements
contents.content: Added support for additional settings including stopSequences and topK, allowing for finer control over text generation.

contents.heading: core-enhancements
contents.content: Provided access to information for all steps on generateText, providing access to intermediate tool calls and results.

contents.heading: new-providers
contents.content: AWS Bedrock provider.

contents.heading: provider-improvements
contents.content: Enhanced existing providers including Anthropic, Google, Azure, and OpenAI with various improvements and bug fixes.

contents.heading: provider-improvements
contents.content: Upgraded the LangChain adapter with StreamEvent v2 support and introduced the toDataStreamResponse function, enabling conversion of LangChain output streams to data stream responses.

contents.heading: provider-improvements
contents.content: Added legacy function calling support to the OpenAI provider.

contents.heading: provider-improvements
contents.content: Updated Mistral AI provider with fixes and improvements for tool calling support.

contents.heading: ui-framework-support-expansion
contents.content: SolidJS: Updated useChat and useCompletion to achieve feature parity with React implementations.

contents.heading: ui-framework-support-expansion
contents.content: Vue.js: Introduced useAssistant hook.

contents.heading: ui-framework-support-expansion
contents.content: Vue.js / Nuxt: Updated examples to showcase latest features and best practices.

contents.heading: ui-framework-support-expansion
contents.content: Svelte: Added tool calling support to useChat.

contents.heading: fixes-and-improvements
contents.content: Resolved various issues across different components of the SDK, including race conditions, error handling, and state management.

contents.heading: ui-message-parts
contents.content:
In AI SDK 4.2, we've redesigned how useChat handles model outputs with message parts and multiple steps.
This is a significant improvement that simplifies rendering complex, multi-modal AI responses in your UI.

contents.heading: whats-changed
contents.content:
Assistant messages with tool calling now get combined into a single message with multiple parts, rather than creating separate messages for each step.
This change addresses two key developments in AI applications:

contents.heading: whats-changed
contents.content: Diverse Output Types: Models now generate more than just text; they produce reasoning steps, sources, and tool calls.

contents.heading: whats-changed
contents.content: Interleaved Outputs: In multi-step agent use-cases, these different output types are frequently interleaved.

contents.heading: benefits-of-the-new-approach
contents.content:
Previously, useChat stored different output types separately, which made it challenging to maintain the correct sequence in your UI when these elements were interleaved in a response,
and led to multiple consecutive assistant messages when there were tool calls. For example:

contents.heading: benefits-of-the-new-approach
contents.content: This structure was limiting. The new message parts approach replaces separate properties with an ordered array that preserves the exact sequence:

contents.heading: migration
contents.content:
Existing applications using the previous message format will need to update their UI components to handle the new parts array.
The fields from the previous format are still available for backward compatibility, but we recommend migrating to the new format for better support of multi-modal and multi-step interactions.

contents.content: AI SDK 5.0 introduces changes to the message structure and persistence patterns. Unlike code migrations that can often be automated with codemods, data migration depends on your specific persistence approach, database schema, and application requirements.

This guide helps you get your application working with AI SDK 5.0 first using a runtime conversion layer. This allows you to update your app immediately without database migrations blocking you. You can then migrate your data schema at your own pace.

For more information about model messages, see the Model Message
reference.

contents.heading: content--parts-array
contents.content: For UIMessages (previously called Message), the .content property has been replaced with a parts array structure.

contents.heading: data-role-removed
contents.content: The data role has been removed from UI messages.

contents.heading: uimessage-reasoning-structure
contents.content: The reasoning property on UI messages has been moved to parts.

contents.heading: reasoning-part-property-rename
contents.content: The reasoning property on reasoning UI parts has been renamed to text.

contents.heading: file-part-changes
contents.content: File parts now use .url instead of .data and .mimeType.

contents.heading: stream-data-removal
contents.content: The StreamData class has been completely removed and replaced with UI message streams for custom data.

contents.heading: custom-data-streaming-writemessageannotationwritedata-removed
contents.content: The writeMessageAnnotation and writeData methods from DataStreamWriter have been removed. Instead, use custom data parts with the new UIMessage stream architecture.

contents.heading: custom-data-streaming-writemessageannotationwritedata-removed
contents.content:
For more detailed information about streaming custom data in v5, see the
Streaming Data guide.

contents.heading: provider-metadata--provider-options
contents.content: The providerMetadata input parameter has been renamed to providerOptions. Note that the returned metadata in results is still called providerMetadata.

contents.heading: tool-definition-changes-parameters--inputschema
contents.content: Tool definitions have been updated to use inputSchema instead of parameters and error classes have been renamed.

contents.heading: tool-result-content-experimental_totoolresultcontent--tomodeloutput
contents.content: The experimental_toToolResultContent option has been renamed to toModelOutput and is no longer experimental.

contents.heading: tool-property-changes-argsresult--inputoutput
contents.content: Tool call and result properties have been renamed for better consistency with schemas.

contents.heading: tool-execution-error-handling
contents.content: The ToolExecutionError class has been removed. Tool execution errors now appear as tool-error content parts in the result steps, enabling automated LLM roundtrips in multi-step scenarios.

contents.heading: tool-execution-error-handling
contents.content: For streaming scenarios, tool execution errors appear as tool-error parts in the stream, while other errors appear as error parts.

contents.heading: tool-call-streaming-now-default-toolcallstreaming-removed
contents.content: The toolCallStreaming option has been removed in AI SDK 5.0. Tool call streaming is now always enabled by default.

contents.heading: tool-part-type-changes-uimessage
contents.content: In v5, UI tool parts use typed naming: tool-${toolName} instead of generic types.

contents.heading: dynamic-tools-support
contents.content: AI SDK 5.0 introduces dynamic tools for handling tools with unknown types at development time, such as MCP tools without schemas or user-defined functions at runtime.

contents.heading: new-dynamictool-helper
contents.content: The new dynamicTool helper function allows you to define tools where the input and output types are not known at compile time.

contents.heading: mcp-tools-without-schemas
contents.content: MCP tools that don't provide schemas are now automatically treated as dynamic tools:

contents.heading: type-safe-handling-with-mixed-tools
contents.content: When using both static and dynamic tools together, use the dynamic flag for type narrowing:

contents.heading: new-dynamic-tool-ui-part
contents.content: UI messages now include a dynamic-tool part type for rendering dynamic tool invocations:

contents.heading: breaking-change-type-narrowing-required-for-tool-calls-and-results
contents.content: When iterating over toolCalls and toolResults, you now need to check the dynamic flag first for proper type narrowing:

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: Tool UI parts now use more granular states that better represent the streaming lifecycle and error handling.

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: State Changes:

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: partial-call → input-streaming (tool input being streamed)

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: call → input-available (tool input complete, ready to execute)

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: result → output-available (tool execution successful)

contents.heading: tool-ui-part-state-changes
contents.content: New: output-error (tool execution failed)

contents.heading: rendering-tool-invocations-catch-all-pattern
contents.content: In v4, you typically rendered tool invocations using a catch-all tool-invocation type. In v5, the recommended approach is to handle each tool specifically using its typed part name (e.g., tool-getWeather). However, if you need a catch-all pattern for rendering all tool invocations the same way, you can use the isToolUIPart and getToolName helper functions as a fallback.

contents.heading: media-type-standardization
contents.content: mimeType has been renamed to mediaType for consistency. Both image and file types are supported in model messages.

contents.heading: reasoning-text-property-rename
contents.content: The .reasoning property has been renamed to .reasoningText for multi-step generations.

contents.heading: generate-text-reasoning-property-changes
contents.content: In generateText() and streamText() results, reasoning properties have been renamed.

contents.heading: continuation-steps-removal
contents.content: The experimental_continueSteps option has been removed from generateText().

contents.heading: image-generation-changes
contents.content: Image model settings have been moved to providerOptions.

contents.heading: step-type-removal
contents.content: The stepType property has been removed from step results.

contents.heading: step-control-maxsteps--stopwhen
contents.content: For core functions like generateText and streamText, the maxSteps parameter has been replaced with stopWhen, which provides more flexible control over multi-step execution. The stopWhen parameter defines conditions for stopping the generation when the last step contains tool results. When multiple conditions are provided as an array, the generation stops if any condition is met.

contents.heading: step-control-maxsteps--stopwhen
contents.content: Common stopping patterns:

contents.heading: step-control-maxsteps--stopwhen
contents.content: Important: The stopWhen conditions are only evaluated when the last step contains tool results.

contents.heading: usage-vs-total-usage
contents.content: Usage properties now distinguish between single step and total usage.

contents.heading: ai-sdkrsc-package-extraction
contents.content: The ai/rsc export has been extracted to a separate package @ai-sdk/rsc.

contents.heading: react-ui-hooks-moved-to-ai-sdkreact
contents.content: The deprecated ai/react export has been removed in favor of @ai-sdk/react.

contents.heading: react-ui-hooks-moved-to-ai-sdkreact
contents.content: Don't forget to install the new package: npm install @ai-sdk/react

contents.heading: usechat-changes
contents.content: The useChat hook has undergone significant changes in v5, with new transport architecture, removal of managed input state, and more.

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content: The maxSteps parameter has been removed from useChat. You should now use server-side stopWhen conditions for multi-step tool execution control, and manually submit tool results and trigger new messages for client-side tool calls.

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content:
Important: When using sendAutomaticallyWhen, don't use await with
addToolOutput inside onToolCall as it can cause deadlocks. The await is
useful when you're not using automatic submission and need to ensure the
messages are updated before manually calling sendMessage().

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content: This change provides more flexibility for handling tool calls and aligns client behavior with server-side multi-step execution patterns.

contents.heading: maxsteps-removal
contents.content: For more details on the new tool submission approach, see the Tool Result Submission Changes section below.

contents.heading: initial-messages-renamed
contents.content: The initialMessages option has been renamed to messages.

contents.heading: sharing-chat-instances
contents.content: In v4, you could share chat state between components by using the same id parameter in multiple useChat hooks.

contents.heading: sharing-chat-instances
contents.content: In v5, you need to explicitly share chat instances by passing a shared Chat instance.

contents.heading: sharing-chat-instances
contents.content: For a complete example of sharing chat state across components, see the Share Chat State Across Components recipe.

contents.heading: chat-transport-architecture
contents.content: Configuration is now handled through transport objects instead of direct API options.

contents.heading: removed-managed-input-state
contents.content: The useChat hook no longer manages input state internally. You must now manage input state manually.

contents.heading: message-sending-append--sendmessage
contents.content: The append function has been replaced with sendMessage and requires structured message format.

contents.heading: message-regeneration-reload--regenerate
contents.content: The reload function has been renamed to regenerate with enhanced functionality.

contents.heading: onresponse-removal
contents.content: The onResponse callback has been removed from useChat and useCompletion.

contents.heading: send-extra-message-fields-default
contents.content: The sendExtraMessageFields option has been removed and is now the default behavior.

contents.heading: keep-last-message-on-error-removal
contents.content: The keepLastMessageOnError option has been removed as it's no longer needed.

contents.heading: chat-request-options-changes
contents.content: The data and allowEmptySubmit options have been removed from ChatRequestOptions.

contents.heading: request-options-type-rename
contents.content: RequestOptions has been renamed to CompletionRequestOptions.

contents.heading: addtoolresult-renamed-to-addtooloutput
contents.content: The addToolResult method has been renamed to addToolOutput. Additionally, the result parameter has been renamed to output for consistency with other tool-related APIs.

contents.heading: addtoolresult-renamed-to-addtooloutput
contents.content:
addToolResult is still available but deprecated. It will be removed in
version 6.

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: The automatic tool result submission behavior has been updated in useChat and the Chat component. You now have more control and flexibility over when tool results are submitted.

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: onToolCall no longer supports returning values to automatically submit tool results

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: You must explicitly call addToolOutput to provide tool results

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: Use sendAutomaticallyWhen with lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls helper for automatic submission

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: Important: Don't use await with addToolOutput inside onToolCall to avoid deadlocks

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: The maxSteps parameter has been removed from the Chat component and useChat hook

contents.heading: tool-result-submission-changes
contents.content: For multi-step tool execution, use server-side stopWhen conditions instead (see maxSteps Removal)

contents.heading: loading-state-changes
contents.content: The deprecated isLoading helper has been removed in favor of status.

contents.heading: resume-stream-support
contents.content: The resume functionality has been moved from experimental_resume to resumeStream.

contents.heading: dynamic-body-values
contents.content: In v4, the body option in useChat configuration would dynamically update with component state changes. In v5, the body value is only captured at the first render and remains static throughout the component lifecycle.

contents.heading: dynamic-body-values
contents.content: For more details on request configuration, see the Chatbot guide.

contents.heading: usage-information
contents.content: In v4, usage information was directly accessible through the onFinish callback's options parameter. In v5, usage data is attached as metadata to individual messages using the messageMetadata function in toUIMessageStreamResponse.

contents.heading: usage-information
contents.content: Then, on the client, you can access the message-level metadata.

contents.heading: usage-information
contents.content: You can also access your metadata from the onFinish callback of useChat:

contents.heading: request-body-preparation-experimental_preparerequestbody--preparesendmessagesrequest
contents.content: The experimental_prepareRequestBody option has been replaced with prepareSendMessagesRequest in the transport configuration.

contents.heading: ai-sdkvue-changes
contents.content: The Vue.js integration has been completely restructured, replacing the useChat composable with a Chat class.

contents.heading: message-structure-changes
contents.content: Messages now use a parts array instead of a content string.

contents.heading: ai-sdksvelte-changes
contents.content: The Svelte integration has also been updated with new constructor patterns and readonly properties.

contents.heading: properties-made-readonly
contents.content: Properties are now readonly and must be updated using setter methods.

contents.heading: removed-managed-input
contents.content: Like React and Vue, input management has been removed from the Svelte integration.

contents.heading: ai-sdkui-utils-package-removal
contents.content: The @ai-sdk/ui-utils package has been removed and its exports moved to the main ai package.

contents.heading: ai-sdkui-utils-package-removal
contents.content: Note: processDataStream was removed entirely in v5.0. Use readUIMessageStream instead for processing UI message streams, or use the more configurable Chat/useChat APIs for most use cases.

contents.heading: usecompletion-changes
contents.content: The data property has been removed from the useCompletion hook.

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content: The useAssistant hook has been removed.

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content:
The useAssistant hook was specific to the OpenAI Assistants API. OpenAI has
deprecated that API in favor of the Responses API. Configure useChat for your
route as shown above, then return a UI message stream from the route:

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content:
For persistent conversation state and built-in tools, see the
OpenAI Responses API guide.

contents.heading: useassistant-removal
contents.content:
If you need to connect useChat to another backend, see the
transport documentation and
stream protocol. For migrating existing
OpenAI Assistants data and API calls, see OpenAI's
Assistants migration guide.

contents.heading: attachments--file-parts
contents.content: The experimental_attachments property has been replaced with the parts array.

contents.heading: provider-options-for-embeddings
contents.content: Embedding model settings now use provider options instead of model parameters.

contents.heading: raw-response--response
contents.content: The rawResponse property has been renamed to response.

contents.heading: parallel-requests-in-embedmany
contents.content: embedMany now makes parallel requests with a configurable maxParallelCalls option.

contents.heading: langchain-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdklangchain
contents.content: The LangChainAdapter has been moved to @ai-sdk/langchain and the API has been updated to use UI message streams.

contents.heading: langchain-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdklangchain
contents.content: Don't forget to install the new package: npm install @ai-sdk/langchain

contents.heading: llamaindex-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdkllamaindex
contents.content: The LlamaIndexAdapter has been extracted to a separate package @ai-sdk/llamaindex and follows the same UI message stream pattern.

contents.heading: llamaindex-adapter-moved-to-ai-sdkllamaindex
contents.content: Don't forget to install the new package: npm install @ai-sdk/llamaindex

contents.heading: streaming-architecture
contents.content: The streaming architecture has been completely redesigned in v5 to support better content differentiation, concurrent streaming of multiple parts, and improved real-time UX.

contents.heading: stream-protocol-single-chunks--startdeltaend-pattern
contents.content: The fundamental streaming pattern has changed from single chunks to a three-phase pattern with unique IDs for each content block.

contents.heading: reasoning-streaming-pattern
contents.content: Reasoning content now follows the same start/delta/end pattern:

contents.heading: tool-input-streaming
contents.content: Tool inputs can now be streamed as they're being generated:

contents.heading: onchunk-callback-changes
contents.content: The onChunk callback now receives the new streaming chunk types with IDs and the start/delta/end pattern.

contents.heading: file-stream-parts-restructure
contents.content: File parts in streams have been flattened.

contents.heading: source-stream-parts-restructure
contents.content: Source stream parts have been flattened.

contents.heading: finish-event-changes
contents.content: Stream finish events have been renamed for consistency.

contents.heading: proprietary-protocol---server-sent-events
contents.content: The data stream protocol has been updated to use Server-Sent Events.

contents.heading: data-stream-response-helper-functions-renamed
contents.content: The streaming API has been completely restructured from data streams to UI message streams.

contents.heading: stream-transform-function-renaming
contents.content: Various stream-related functions have been renamed for consistency.

contents.heading: error-handling-geterrormessage--onerror
contents.content: The getErrorMessage option in toDataStreamResponse has been replaced with onError in toUIMessageStreamResponse, providing more control over error forwarding to the client.

contents.heading: error-handling-geterrormessage--onerror
contents.content: By default, error messages are NOT sent to the client to prevent leaking sensitive information. The onError callback allows you to explicitly control what error information is forwarded to the client.

contents.heading: id-generation-changes
contents.content: The createIdGenerator() function now requires a size argument.

contents.heading: idgenerator--idgenerator
contents.content: The type name has been updated.

contents.heading: language-model-v2-import
contents.content: LanguageModelV2 must now be imported from @ai-sdk/provider.

contents.heading: middleware-rename
contents.content: LanguageModelV1Middleware has been renamed and moved.

contents.heading: usage-token-properties
contents.content: Token usage properties have been renamed for consistency.

contents.heading: stream-part-type-changes
contents.content: The LanguageModelV2StreamPart type has been expanded to support the new streaming architecture with start/delta/end patterns and IDs.

contents.heading: raw-response--response-1
contents.content: Provider response objects have been updated.

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: The experimental_prepareStep option has been promoted and no longer requires the experimental prefix.

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: The prepareStep function receives { steps, stepNumber, model } and can return:

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: model: Different model for this step

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: activeTools: Which tools to make available

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: toolChoice: Tool selection strategy

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: system: System message for this step

contents.heading: preparestep-no-longer-experimental
contents.content: undefined: Use default settings

contents.heading: temperature-default-removal
contents.content: Temperature is no longer set to 0 by default.

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content:
If you have persisted messages in a database, see the Data Migration
Guide for comprehensive
guidance on migrating your stored message data to the v5 format.

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content: In v4, you would typically use helper functions like appendResponseMessages or appendClientMessage to format messages in the onFinish callback of streamText:

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content: In v5, message persistence is now handled through the toUIMessageStreamResponse method, which automatically formats response messages in the UIMessage format:

contents.heading: message-persistence-changes
contents.content:
Important: When using toUIMessageStreamResponse, you should always
provide both originalMessages and generateMessageId parameters. Without
these, you may experience duplicate or repeated assistant messages in your UI.
For more details, see Troubleshooting: Repeated Assistant
Messages.

contents.heading: message-id-generation
contents.content: The experimental_generateMessageId option has been moved from streamText configuration to toUIMessageStreamResponse, as it's designed for use with UIMessages rather than ModelMessages.

contents.heading: message-id-generation
contents.content: For more details on message IDs and persistence, see the Chatbot Message Persistence guide.

contents.heading: using-createuimessagestream
contents.content: For more complex scenarios, especially when working with data parts, you can use createUIMessageStream:

contents.heading: default-provider-instance-uses-responses-api
contents.content: In AI SDK 5, the default OpenAI provider instance uses the Responses API, while AI SDK 4 used the Chat Completions API. The Chat Completions API remains fully supported and you can use it with openai.chat(...).

contents.heading: default-provider-instance-uses-responses-api
contents.content:
The Responses and Chat Completions APIs have different behavior and defaults.
If you depend on the Chat Completions API, switch your model instance to
openai.chat(...) and audit your configuration.

contents.heading: strict-schemas-strictschemas-with-responses-api
contents.content: In AI SDK 4.0, you could set the strictSchemas option on Responses models (which defaulted to true). This option has been renamed to strictJsonSchema in AI SDK 5.0 and now defaults to false.

contents.heading: strict-schemas-strictschemas-with-responses-api
contents.content: If you call openai.chat(...) to use the Chat Completions API directly, you can type it with OpenAIChatLanguageModelOptions. AI SDK 5 adds the same strictJsonSchema option there as well.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: The structuredOutputs option is now configured using provider options rather than as a setting on the model instance.

contents.heading: compatibility-option-removal
contents.content: The compatibility option has been removed; strict compatibility mode is now the default.

contents.heading: legacy-function-calls-removal
contents.content: The useLegacyFunctionCalls option has been removed.

contents.heading: simulate-streaming
contents.content: The simulateStreaming model option has been replaced with middleware.

contents.heading: search-grounding-is-now-a-provider-defined-tool
contents.content: Search Grounding is now called "Google Search" and is now a provider defined tool.

contents.heading: snake-case--camel-case
contents.content: Provider options have been updated to use camelCase.

contents.heading: provider-utils-changes
contents.content: Deprecated CoreTool* types have been removed.

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: If you experience TypeScript server crashes, slow type checking, or errors like "Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite" when using Zod with AI SDK 5.0:

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: First, ensure you're using Zod 4.1.8 or later - this version includes a fix for module resolution issues that cause TypeScript performance problems.

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: If the issue persists, update your tsconfig.json to use moduleResolution: "nodenext":

contents.heading: typescript-performance-issues-with-zod
contents.content: This resolves the TypeScript performance issues while allowing you to continue using the standard Zod import. If this doesn't resolve the issue, you can try using a version-specific import path as an alternative solution. For detailed troubleshooting steps, see TypeScript performance issues with Zod.

contents.content:
AI SDK 6 is currently in beta and introduces new capabilities like agents and
tool approval. This guide will help you migrate from AI SDK 5.0 to 6.0 Beta.
Note that you may want to wait until the stable release for production
projects. See the AI SDK 6 Beta announcement
for more details on what's new.

contents.heading: recommended-migration-process
contents.content: Backup your project. If you use a versioning control system, make sure all previous versions are committed.

contents.heading: recommended-migration-process
contents.content: Upgrade to AI SDK 6.0 Beta.

contents.heading: recommended-migration-process
contents.content: Follow the breaking changes guide below.

contents.content: Verify your project is working as expected.

contents.heading: recommended-migration-process
contents.content: Commit your changes.

contents.heading: ai-sdk-60-beta-package-versions
contents.content: You need to update the following packages to the beta versions in your package.json file(s):

contents.content: ai package: 6.0.0-beta (or use the @beta dist-tag)

contents.heading: ai-sdk-60-beta-package-versions
contents.content: @ai-sdk/provider package: 3.0.0-beta (or use the @beta dist-tag)

contents.heading: ai-sdk-60-beta-package-versions
contents.content: @ai-sdk/provider-utils package: 4.0.0-beta (or use the @beta dist-tag)

contents.heading: ai-sdk-60-beta-package-versions
contents.content: @ai-sdk/* packages: 3.0.0-beta (or use the @beta dist-tag for other @ai-sdk packages)

contents.heading: ai-sdk-60-beta-package-versions
contents.content: An example upgrade command would be:

contents.heading: coremessage-removed
contents.content: The deprecated CoreMessage type and related functions have been removed (PR #10710). Replace convertToCoreMessages with convertToModelMessages.

contents.heading: generateobject-and-streamobject-deprecated
contents.content:
generateObject and streamObject have been deprecated (PR #10754).
They will be removed in a future version.
You can use generateText and streamText with an output setting instead.

contents.heading: strictjsonschema-defaults-to-true
contents.content: The strictJsonSchema setting for JSON outputs and tool calls is enabled by default (PR #10752). This improves stability and ensures valid JSON output that matches your schema.

contents.heading: strictjsonschema-defaults-to-true
contents.content: However, strict mode is stricter about schema requirements. If you receive schema rejection errors, adjust your schema (for example, use null instead of undefined) or disable strict mode.

contents.heading: strictjsonschema-no-longer-used-for-tool-strict-mode
contents.content: Strict mode for tools is now controlled by setting strict on each tool (PR #10817). This enables fine-grained control over strict tool calls, which is important since strict mode depends on the specific tool input schema.

contents.heading: structuredoutputs-option-removed-from-chat-model
contents.content: The structuredOutputs provider option has been removed from chat models (PR #10752). Use strictJsonSchema instead.

contents.heading: warning-logger-enabled
contents.content: AI SDK 6 introduces a warning logger that outputs deprecation warnings and best practice recommendations (PR #8343).

contents.heading: warning-logger-enabled
contents.content: To disable warning logging, set the AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS environment variable to false:

contents.heading: v2-model-compatibility-warning
contents.content: A warning is displayed when using v2 provider models with AISDK v6 (PR #10770). Update your provider implementations to use v3 models.

contents.heading: flexible-tool-content-support
contents.content: AI SDK 6 introduces more flexible tool output and result content support (PR #9605), enabling richer tool interactions and better support for complex tool execution patterns.

contents.heading: codemods
contents.content:
The AI SDK will provide Codemod transformations to help upgrade your codebase when a
feature is deprecated, removed, or otherwise changed.

contents.heading: codemods
contents.content:
Codemods are transformations that run on your codebase automatically. They
allow you to easily apply many changes without having to manually go through
every file.

contents.heading: codemods
contents.content:
Codemods are intended as a tool to help you with the upgrade process. They may
not cover all of the changes you need to make. You may need to make additional
changes manually.

contents.heading: embedding-model-method-renamed
contents.content: The textEmbeddingModel and textEmbedding methods on providers have been renamed to embeddingModel and embedding respectively. Additionally, generics have been removed from EmbeddingModel, embed, and embedMany (PR #10592).

contents.heading: unrecognized-models-treated-as-reasoning-models
contents.content: The @ai-sdk/openai provider now treats unrecognized model IDs as reasoning models by default (PR #9976). Previously, unrecognized models were treated as non-reasoning models.

contents.heading: unrecognized-models-treated-as-reasoning-models
contents.content: This change impacts users who configure @ai-sdk/openai with a custom baseUrl to use non-OpenAI models. Reasoning models exclude certain parameters like temperature, which may cause unexpected behavior if the model does not support reasoning. Consider using @ai-sdk/openai-compatible instead.

contents.heading: default-provider-uses-responses-api
contents.content: The @ai-sdk/azure provider now uses the Responses API by default when calling azure() (PR #9868). To use the previous Chat Completions API behavior, use azure.chat() instead.

contents.heading: default-provider-uses-responses-api
contents.content:
The Responses and Chat Completions APIs have different behavior and defaults.
If you depend on the Chat Completions API, switch your model instance to
azure.chat() and audit your configuration.

contents.heading: structured-outputs-mode
contents.content: Anthropic has  introduced native structured outputs for Claude Sonnet 4.5 and later models . The @ai-sdk/anthropic provider now includes a structuredOutputMode option to control how structured outputs are generated (PR #10502).

contents.heading: structured-outputs-mode
contents.content: The available modes are:

contents.heading: structured-outputs-mode
contents.content: 'outputFormat': Use Anthropic's native output_format parameter

contents.heading: structured-outputs-mode
contents.content: 'jsonTool': Use a special JSON tool to specify the structured output format

contents.heading: structured-outputs-mode
contents.content: 'auto' (default): Use 'outputFormat' when supported by the model, otherwise fall back to 'jsonTool'

contents.heading: mock-classes-updated
contents.content: V2 mock classes have been removed from the ai/test module. Use the new V3 mock classes instead for testing.

contents.heading: warning-types-unified
contents.content: Separate warning types for each generation function have been consolidated into a single Warning type exported from the ai package (PR #10631).

contents.heading: tool-call-repair-function-signature
contents.content: The system parameter in the ToolCallRepairFunction type now accepts SystemModelMessage in addition to string (PR #10635). This allows for more flexible system message configuration, including provider-specific options like caching.

structuredOutputs option removed from chat model

metadata.title: Versioning
metadata.description: Understand how the AI SDK approaches versioning.

contents.content: Each version number follows the format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
Major: Breaking API updates that require code changes.
Minor: Blog post that aggregates new features and improvements into a public release that highlights benefits.
Patch: New features and bug fixes.

contents.heading: api-stability
contents.content: We communicate the stability of our APIs as follows:

contents.heading: stable-apis
contents.content: All APIs without special prefixes are considered stable and ready for production use. We maintain backward compatibility for stable features and only introduce breaking changes in major releases.

contents.heading: experimental-apis
contents.content: APIs prefixed with experimental_ or Experimental_ (e.g. experimental_generateImage()) are in development and can change in any releases. To use experimental APIs safely:

contents.heading: experimental-apis
contents.content: Test them first in development, not production

contents.heading: experimental-apis
contents.content: Review release notes before upgrading

contents.heading: experimental-apis
contents.content: Prepare for potential code updates

contents.heading: experimental-apis
contents.content:
If you use experimental APIs, make sure to pin your AI SDK version number
exactly (avoid using ^ or ~ version ranges) to prevent unexpected breaking
changes.

contents.heading: deprecated-apis
contents.content: APIs marked as deprecated will be removed in future major releases. You can wait until the major release to update your code. To handle deprecations:

contents.heading: deprecated-apis
contents.content: Switch to the recommended alternative API

contents.heading: deprecated-apis
contents.content: Follow the migration guide (released alongside major releases)

contents.heading: deprecated-apis
contents.content:
For major releases, we provide automated codemods where possible to help
migrate your code to the new version.

metadata.title: cosineSimilarity
metadata.description: Calculate the cosine similarity between two vectors (API Reference)

contents.content:
When you want to compare the similarity of embeddings, standard vector similarity metrics
like cosine similarity are often used.

cosineSimilarity calculates the cosine similarity between two vectors.
A high value (close to 1) indicates that the vectors are very similar, while a low value (close to -1) indicates that they are different.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: A number between -1 and 1 representing the cosine similarity between the two vectors.

contents.content: The dynamicTool function creates tools where the input and output types are not known at compile time. This is useful for scenarios such as:

metadata.title: embedMany
metadata.description: API Reference for embedMany.

contents.content:
Embed several values using an embedding model. The type of the value is defined
by the embedding model.

embedMany automatically splits large requests into smaller chunks when the
model has a limit on either the number of embeddings or the UTF-8 input bytes
that can be processed in a single call. Providers can use a conservative byte
budget to keep requests below aggregate token limits without adding a tokenizer
to the AI SDK core package. An individual value larger than the byte budget is
sent in its own call because splitting it would change the resulting embedding.

metadata.title: AI SDK Core
metadata.description: Reference documentation for the AI SDK Core

contents.content:
AI SDK Core is a set of functions that allow you to interact with language models and other AI models.
These functions are designed to be easy-to-use and flexible, allowing you to generate text, structured data,
and embeddings from language models and other AI models.
AI SDK Core contains the following main functions:
It also contains the following helper functions:

metadata.title: jsonSchema
metadata.description: Helper function for creating JSON schemas

contents.content:
jsonSchema is a helper function that creates a JSON schema object that is compatible with the AI SDK.
It takes the JSON schema and an optional validation function as inputs, and can be typed.
You can use it to generate structured data and in tools.

jsonSchema is an alternative to using Zod schemas that provides you with flexibility in dynamic situations
(e.g. when using OpenAPI definitions) or for using other validation libraries.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: A JSON schema object that is compatible with the AI SDK.

metadata.title: LanguageModelV2Middleware
metadata.description: Middleware for enhancing language model behavior (API Reference)

contents.content: Language model middleware is an experimental feature.

Language model middleware provides a way to enhance the behavior of language models
by intercepting and modifying the calls to the language model. It can be used to add
features like guardrails, RAG, caching, and logging in a language model agnostic way.
See Language Model Middleware for more information.

metadata.description: Create a transport for Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients to communicate with MCP servers using standard input and output streams

contents.content: Creates a transport for Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients to communicate with MCP servers using standard input and output streams. This transport is only supported in Node.js environments.
This feature is experimental and may change or be removed in the future.

metadata.title: ModelMessage
metadata.description: Message types for AI SDK Core (API Reference)

contents.content:
ModelMessage represents the fundamental message structure used with AI SDK Core functions.
It encompasses various message types that can be used in the messages field of any AI SDK Core functions.
You can access the Zod schema for ModelMessage with the modelMessageSchema export.

contents.heading: systemmodelmessage
contents.content: A system message that can contain system information.

contents.heading: systemmodelmessage
contents.content: You can access the Zod schema for SystemModelMessage with the systemModelMessageSchema export.

contents.heading: systemmodelmessage
contents.content:
Use the top-level system property instead of a system message for system
instructions. AI SDK functions allow system messages in prompt or
messages by default with a warning. Set allowSystemInMessages to true
to suppress the warning, or false to reject them. System messages in
prompt or messages can create a prompt injection attack risk.

contents.heading: usermodelmessage
contents.content: A user message that can contain text or a combination of text, images, and files.

contents.heading: usermodelmessage
contents.content: You can access the Zod schema for UserModelMessage with the userModelMessageSchema export.

contents.heading: assistantmodelmessage
contents.content: An assistant message that can contain text, tool calls, or a combination of both.

contents.heading: assistantmodelmessage
contents.content: You can access the Zod schema for AssistantModelMessage with the assistantModelMessageSchema export.

contents.heading: toolmodelmessage
contents.content: A tool message that contains the result of one or more tool calls.

contents.heading: toolmodelmessage
contents.content: You can access the Zod schema for ToolModelMessage with the toolModelMessageSchema export.

contents.heading: textpart
contents.content: Represents a text content part of a prompt. It contains a string of text.

contents.heading: imagepart
contents.content: Represents an image part in a user message.

contents.heading: filepart
contents.content: Represents an file part in a user message.

contents.heading: toolcallpart

contents.heading: toolresultpart

metadata.title: createProviderRegistry

in a central place and access the models through simple string ids.

createProviderRegistry lets you create a registry with multiple providers that you
can access by their ids in the format providerId:modelId.

The provider id will become the prefix of the model id: providerId:modelId.

metadata.title: tool
metadata.description: Helper function for tool type inference

contents.content: Tool is a helper function that infers the tool input for its execute method.
It does not have any runtime behavior, but it helps TypeScript infer the types of the input for the execute method.

Without this helper function, TypeScript is unable to connect the inputSchema property to the execute method,
and the argument types of execute cannot be inferred.

metadata.title: zodSchema
metadata.description: Helper function for creating Zod schemas

contents.content:
zodSchema is a helper function that converts a Zod schema into a JSON schema object that is compatible with the AI SDK.
It takes a Zod schema and optional configuration as inputs, and returns a typed schema.
You can use it to generate structured data and in tools.

You can also pass Zod objects directly to the AI SDK functions. Internally,
the AI SDK will convert the Zod schema to a JSON schema using zodSchema().
However, if you want to specify options such as useReferences, you can pass
the zodSchema() helper function instead.

When using .meta() or .describe() to add metadata to your Zod schemas,
make sure these methods are called at the end of the schema chain.

metadata is attached to a specific schema
instance, and most schema methods (.min(), .optional(), .extend(), etc.)
return a new schema instance that does not inherit metadata from the previous one.
Due to Zod's immutability, metadata is only included in the JSON schema output
if .meta() or .describe() is the last method in the chain.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: A Schema object that is compatible with the AI SDK, containing both the JSON schema representation and validation functionality.

metadata.title: AI SDK Errors
metadata.description: Reference for AI SDK error classes and typed error handling.

contents.content:
AI SDK errors let you handle expected failure modes without matching error
message strings.

contents.heading: importing-errors
contents.content:
The AI SDK Core package is named ai, not @ai-sdk/ai. It re-exports many
provider-level errors from @ai-sdk/provider together with the higher-level
errors raised by AI SDK Core:

contents.heading: importing-errors
contents.content:
Provider implementations that depend directly on @ai-sdk/provider can import
provider-level errors from that package instead:

contents.heading: migrating-to-typed-error-handling
contents.content:
Replace message matching or an unconditionally generic catch block with the
most specific static isInstance guard available. Check AISDKError last when
you need a fallback for any AI SDK error:

contents.heading: migrating-to-typed-error-handling
contents.content:
Prefer ErrorClass.isInstance(error) over error instanceof ErrorClass when
the class provides a class-specific guard. The static guards use shared markers
and therefore work when multiple AI SDK package versions are loaded.

contents.heading: migrating-to-typed-error-handling
contents.content:
In AI SDK 5, NoSpeechGeneratedError and UnsupportedModelVersionError do not
provide class-specific guards. Use instanceof to distinguish those exact
classes. Their inherited isInstance method only checks whether a value is any
AISDKError.

contents.heading: migrating-to-typed-error-handling
contents.content:
The experimental transcription API can throw an
AI_NoTranscriptGeneratedError, but AI SDK 5 does not export its class. Handle
it with AISDKError.isInstance(error) and check error.name.

metadata.title: pruneMessages
metadata.description: API Reference for pruneMessages.

contents.content: The pruneMessages function is used to prune or filter an array of ModelMessage objects. This is useful for reducing message context (to save tokens), removing intermediate reasoning, or trimming tool calls and empty messages before sending to an LLM.

contents.heading: returns
contents.content: An array of ModelMessage objects, pruned according to the provided options.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: reasoning: Removes reasoning parts from assistant messages. Use 'all' to remove all, 'before-last-message' to keep reasoning in the last message, or 'none' to retain all reasoning.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: toolCalls: Prune tool-call, tool-result, and tool-approval chunks from assistant/tool messages. Options include:

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: 'all': Prune all such content.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: 'before-last-message': Prune except in the last message.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: before-last-N-messages: Prune except in the last N messages.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: 'none': Do not prune.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: Or provide an array for per-tool fine control.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: emptyMessages: Set to 'remove' (default) to exclude messages that have no content after pruning.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: Tip: pruneMessages is typically used prior to sending a context window to an LLM to reduce message/token count, especially after a series of tool-calls and approvals.

contents.heading: pruning-options
contents.content: For advanced usage and the full list of possible message parts, see ModelMessage and pruneMessages implementation.

Converts the output from language models hosted on Hugging Face into a ReadableStream.

While HuggingFaceStream is compatible with most Hugging Face language models, the rapidly evolving landscape of models may result in certain new or niche models not being supported. If you encounter a model that isn't supported, we encourage you to open an issue.

To ensure that AI responses are comprised purely of text without any delimiters that could pose issues when rendering in chat or completion modes, we standardize and remove special end-of-response tokens. If your use case requires a different handling of responses, you can fork and modify this stream to meet your specific needs.
Currently, </s> and <|endoftext|> are recognized as end-of-stream tokens.

metadata.title: Abort breaks resumable streams
metadata.description: Troubleshooting stream resumption failures when using abort functionality

title.children: Option 1: Use stream resumption without abort
Option 2: Use abort without stream resumption

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using useChat with resume: true for stream resumption, the abort functionality breaks. Closing a tab, refreshing the page, or calling the stop() function will trigger an abort signal that interferes with the resumption mechanism, preventing streams from being properly resumed.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: When a page is closed or refreshed, the browser automatically sends an abort signal, which breaks the resumption flow.

contents.heading: current-limitations
contents.content: We're aware of this incompatibility and are exploring solutions. In the meantime, please choose either stream resumption or abort functionality based on your application's requirements, but not both.

contents.heading: option-1-use-stream-resumption-without-abort
contents.content: If you need to support long-running generations that persist across page reloads:

contents.heading: option-2-use-abort-without-stream-resumption
contents.content: If you need to allow users to stop streams manually:

metadata.title: Server Action Plain Objects Error
metadata.description: Troubleshooting errors related to using AI SDK Core functions with Server Actions.

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: I am using streamText or streamObject with Server Actions, and I am getting a "only plain objects and a few built ins can be passed from client components" error.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: This error occurs when you're trying to return a non-serializable object from a Server Action to a Client Component. The streamText function likely returns an object with methods or complex structures that can't be directly serialized and passed to the client.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: To fix this issue, you need to ensure that you're only returning serializable data from your Server Action. Here's how you can modify your approach:

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Instead of returning the entire result object from streamText, extract only the necessary serializable data.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Use the createStreamableValue function to create a streamable value that can be safely passed to the client.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Here's an example that demonstrates how to implement this solution: Streaming Text Generation.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: This approach ensures that only serializable data (the text) is passed to the client, avoiding the "only plain objects" error.

metadata.description: Troubleshooting NoObjectGeneratedError with finish-reason content-filter caused by incompatible Zod schema types when using OpenAI structured outputs

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using generateObject or streamObject with OpenAI's structured output generation, you may encounter a NoObjectGeneratedError with the finish reason content-filter. This error occurs when your Zod schema contains incompatible types that OpenAI's structured output feature cannot process.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: OpenAI's structured output generation uses JSON Schema under the hood and has specific requirements for schema compatibility. The Zod methods .nullish() and .optional() generate JSON Schema patterns that are incompatible with OpenAI's implementation, causing the model to reject the schema and return a content-filter finish reason.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Replace .nullish() and .optional() with .nullable() in your Zod schemas when using structured output generation with OpenAI models.

metadata.title: Repeated assistant messages in useChat

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using useChat with streamText on the server, the assistant's messages appear duplicated in the UI - showing both the previous message and the new message, or showing the same message multiple times. This can occur when using tool calls or complex message flows.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: The duplication occurs because toUIMessageStreamResponse generates new message IDs for each new message.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Pass the original messages array to toUIMessageStreamResponse using the originalMessages option. By passing originalMessages, the method can reuse existing message IDs instead of generating new ones, ensuring the client properly updates existing messages rather than creating duplicates.

metadata.title: onFinish not called when stream is aborted
metadata.description: Troubleshooting onFinish callback not executing when streams are aborted with toUIMessageStreamResponse

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using toUIMessageStreamResponse with an onFinish callback, the callback may not execute when the stream is aborted. This happens because the abort handler immediately terminates the response, preventing the onFinish callback from being triggered.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: When a stream is aborted, the response is immediately terminated. Without proper handling, the onFinish callback has no chance to execute, preventing important cleanup operations like saving partial results or logging abort events.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Add consumeStream to the toUIMessageStreamResponse configuration. This ensures that abort events are properly captured and forwarded to the onFinish callback, allowing it to execute even when the stream is aborted.

contents.heading: issue

contents.heading: background

contents.heading: upgrade-zod-to-418-or-later
contents.content: The primary solution is to upgrade to Zod version 4.1.8 or later, which includes a fix for this module resolution issue:

contents.heading: upgrade-zod-to-418-or-later
contents.content: This version resolves the underlying problem where different module resolution settings were causing TypeScript to load the same Zod declarations twice, leading to expensive structural comparisons.

contents.heading: alternative-update-typescript-configuration
contents.content: If upgrading Zod isn't possible, you can update your tsconfig.json to use moduleResolution: "nodenext":

contents.heading: alternative-update-typescript-configuration
