metadata.title: Stale body values with useChat
metadata.description: Troubleshooting stale values when passing information via the body parameter of useChat

contents.heading: issue
contents.content: When using useChat and passing dynamic information via the body parameter at the hook level, the data remains stale and only reflects the value from the initial component render. This occurs because the body configuration is captured once when the hook is initialized and doesn't update with subsequent component re-renders.

contents.heading: background
contents.content: The hook-level body configuration is evaluated once during the initial render and doesn't re-evaluate when component state changes.

contents.heading: solution
contents.content: Pass dynamic variables via the second argument of the sendMessage function instead of at the hook level. Request-level options are evaluated on each call and take precedence over hook-level options.

contents.heading: alternative-dynamic-hook-level-configuration
contents.content: If you need hook-level configuration that responds to changes, you can use functions that return configuration values. However, for component state, you'll need to use useRef to access current values:

contents.heading: alternative-dynamic-hook-level-configuration
contents.content: Recommendation: Request-level configuration is simpler and more reliable for component state. Use it whenever you need to pass dynamic values that change during the component lifecycle.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The AI Gateway provider accepts provider options that control routing behavior and provider-specific configurations.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: You can use the gateway key in providerOptions to control how AI Gateway routes requests:

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: The following gateway provider options are available:

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: order string[]

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Specifies the sequence of providers to attempt when routing requests. The gateway will try providers in the order specified. If a provider fails or is unavailable, it will move to the next provider in the list.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: order: ['bedrock', 'anthropic'] will attempt Amazon Bedrock first, then fall back to Anthropic.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: only string[]

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Restricts routing to only the specified providers. When set, the gateway will never route to providers not in this list, even if they would otherwise be available.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: only: ['anthropic', 'vertex'] will only allow routing to Anthropic or Vertex AI.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: sort 'cost' | 'ttft' | 'tps'

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Sorts available providers by a performance or cost metric before routing. The gateway will try the best-scoring provider first and fall back through the rest in sorted order. If unspecified, providers are ordered using the gateway's default system ranking.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'cost' — lowest cost first

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'ttft' — lowest time-to-first-token first

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'tps' — highest tokens-per-second first

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: When combined with order, the user-specified providers are promoted to the front while remaining providers follow the sorted order.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: sort: 'ttft' will route to the provider with the fastest time-to-first-token.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: When sort is active, the response's providerMetadata.gateway.routing.sort object contains the sort option used, the resulting execution order, per-provider metric values, and any providers that were deprioritized.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: models string[]

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Specifies fallback models to use when the primary model fails or is unavailable. The gateway will try the primary model first (specified in the model parameter), then try each model in this array in order until one succeeds.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: models: ['openai/gpt-5.4-nano', 'gemini-3-flash-preview'] will try the fallback models in order if the primary model fails.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Optional identifier for the end user on whose behalf the request is being made. This is used for spend tracking and attribution purposes, allowing you to track usage per end-user in your application.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: user: 'user-123' will associate this request with end-user ID "user-123" in usage reports.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: tags string[]

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Optional array of tags for categorizing and filtering usage in reports. Useful for tracking spend by feature, prompt version, or any other dimension relevant to your application.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: tags: ['chat', 'v2'] will tag this request with "chat" and "v2" for filtering in usage analytics.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: byok Record<string, Array<Record<string, unknown>>>

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Request-scoped BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) credentials to use for this request. When provided, any cached BYOK credentials configured in the gateway system are not considered. Requests may still fall back to use system credentials if the provided credentials fail.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Each provider can have multiple credentials (tried in order). The structure is a record where keys are provider slugs and values are arrays of credential objects.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Examples:

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Single provider: byok: { 'anthropic': [{ apiKey: 'sk-ant-...' }] }

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Multiple credentials: byok: { 'vertex': [{ projectId: 'proj-1', privateKey: '...' }, { projectId: 'proj-2', privateKey: '...' }] }

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Multiple providers: byok: { 'anthropic': [{ apiKey: '...' }], 'bedrock': [{ accessKeyId: '...', secretAccessKey: '...' }] }

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: zeroDataRetention boolean

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Restricts routing requests to providers that have zero data retention agreements with Vercel for AI Gateway. If there are no providers available for the model with zero data retention, the request will fail. BYOK credentials are skipped when zeroDataRetention is set to true to ensure that requests are only routed to providers that support ZDR compliance. Request-level ZDR is only available for Vercel Pro and Enterprise plans.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: disallowPromptTraining boolean

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Restricts routing requests to providers that have agreements with Vercel for AI Gateway to not use prompts for model training. If there are no providers available for the model that disallow prompt training, the request will fail. BYOK credentials are skipped when disallowPromptTraining is set to true to ensure that requests are only routed to providers that do not train on prompt data.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: quotaEntityId string

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: The unique identifier for the entity against which quota is tracked. Used for quota management and enforcement purposes.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: has Array<'implicit-caching' | 'reasoning' | 'tool-use' | 'vision' | quantization:${string} | !quantization:${string}>

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Restricts routing to provider models that have all of the specified capabilities. Applies to both BYOK and system credentials, since the capability is a property of the model rather than the credential. If no provider model for the requested model satisfies the capabilities, the request fails. Unsupported values are rejected.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Supported capabilities:

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'implicit-caching' — models that perform automatic (implicit) prompt caching.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'reasoning' — models that support reasoning.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'tool-use' — models that support tool calling.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: 'vision' — models that accept image input.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Weight-format conditions route on the serving provider's recorded weight format: 'quantization:fp8' requires a provider serving fp8 weights, while '!quantization:fp8' excludes fp8 providers. A negated condition also matches providers whose weight format is not recorded, so exclusions remain usable while the catalog is populated.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: has: ['implicit-caching'] will only route to models that support implicit caching. Example: has: ['vision'] will only route to models that accept image input. Example: has: ['tool-use'] will only route to models that support tool calling. Example: has: ['!quantization:fp8'] will only route to providers that do not serve fp8 weights.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: providerTimeouts object

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Per-provider timeouts for BYOK credentials in milliseconds. Controls how long to wait for a provider to start responding before falling back to the next available provider.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: Example: providerTimeouts: { byok: { openai: 5000, anthropic: 2000 } }

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: For full details, see Provider Timeouts.

contents.heading: gateway-provider-options
contents.content: You can combine these options to have fine-grained control over routing and tracking:

contents.heading: model-fallbacks-example
contents.content: The models option enables automatic fallback to alternative models when the primary model fails:

contents.heading: zero-data-retention-example
contents.content: Set zeroDataRetention to true to route requests to providers that have zero data retention agreements with Vercel for AI Gateway. If there are no providers available for the model with zero data retention, the request will fail. When zeroDataRetention is false or not specified, there is no enforcement of restricting routing. BYOK credentials are skipped when zeroDataRetention is set to true to ensure that requests are only routed to providers that support ZDR compliance. Request-level ZDR is only available for Vercel Pro and Enterprise plans.

contents.heading: disallow-prompt-training-example
contents.content: Set disallowPromptTraining to true to route requests to providers that have agreements with Vercel for AI Gateway to not use prompts for model training. If there are no providers available for the model that disallow prompt training, the request will fail. When disallowPromptTraining is false or not specified, there is no enforcement of restricting routing. BYOK credentials are skipped when disallowPromptTraining is set to true to ensure that requests are only routed to providers that do not train on prompt data.

contents.heading: quota-entity-id-example
contents.content: Set quotaEntityId to track and enforce quota against a specific entity. This is useful for multi-tenant applications where you need to manage quota at the entity level (e.g., per organization or team).

contents.heading: filtering-by-model-capability
contents.content: Set has to restrict routing to provider models that have the specified capabilities. This applies to both BYOK and system credentials, since the capability is a property of the model rather than the credential. 'implicit-caching' limits routing to models that perform automatic prompt caching, 'vision' limits routing to models that accept image input, 'reasoning' limits routing to models that support reasoning, and 'tool-use' limits routing to models that support tool calling. Weight-format conditions ('quantization:fp8' to require, '!quantization:fp8' to exclude) limit routing by the serving provider's recorded weight format. If no provider model for the requested model satisfies the capabilities, the request fails.

contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Alibaba models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: enableThinking boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Enable thinking/reasoning mode for supported models. When enabled, the model generates reasoning content before the response.
Defaults to false.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinkingBudget number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Maximum number of reasoning tokens to generate. Limits the length of thinking content.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: preserveThinking boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Preserve reasoning from previous assistant messages for supported models.
When enabled, reasoning is sent separately as Alibaba reasoning_content and
preserve_thinking is enabled. Defaults to true for models that support
preserved thinking; set to false to opt out. Append AI SDK responseMessages
unchanged when continuing the conversation. See Alibaba's
preserved-thinking documentation
for the list of supported models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use.
Defaults to true.

contents.heading: thinking-mode
contents.content: Alibaba's Qwen models support thinking/reasoning mode for complex problem-solving:

contents.heading: thinking-mode
contents.content: For models that are thinking-only (like qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507), thinking mode is enabled by default.

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
For models that support preserved thinking, the AI SDK replays reasoning from
previous assistant messages as Alibaba reasoning_content by default, so the
model can build on its earlier thought process:

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
When continuing the conversation, append responseMessages unchanged. If you
rebuild assistant history from visible text only, the reasoning parts are
discarded before the provider can serialize them as reasoning_content. Set
preserveThinking: false to opt out of replay, and note the following caveats:

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
preserveThinking does not enable thinking by itself. Pair it with
enableThinking/thinkingBudget or the top-level reasoning option.

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
It is enabled by default only for models that Alibaba documents as supporting
preserved thinking; for other models, preserve_thinking is not sent unless
you set the option explicitly. See Alibaba's
preserved-thinking documentation
for the current list of supported models.

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
Reasoning from the current tool-call round (after the last user message) is
always sent back with tool results, as Alibaba recommends; the option only
controls reasoning from earlier rounds.

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content: Preserved reasoning increases input token usage and billing.

contents.heading: preserved-thinking-in-multi-turn-conversations
contents.content:
Historical reasoning remains separate from visible assistant text; it is never
merged into content.

contents.heading: tool-calling
contents.content: Alibaba models support tool calling with parallel execution:

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: Alibaba supports both implicit and explicit prompt caching to reduce costs for repeated prompts.

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: Implicit caching works automatically - the provider caches appropriate content without any configuration. For more control, you can use explicit caching by marking specific messages with cache_control:

contents.heading: multi-part-message-cache-control
contents.content: Note: The minimum content length for a cache block is 1,024 tokens.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
You can create text embedding models using the .textEmbeddingModel() factory method.
For more on embeddings with the AI SDK see embed()
and embedMany().

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: You can use Alibaba embedding models to generate embeddings with the embed function:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
Use embedMany to embed multiple text values. Alibaba text embedding models support
up to 10 values per API call; larger batches are split automatically by embedMany.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
Alibaba embedding models support additional provider options that can be passed via
providerOptions.alibaba:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: textType 'query' | 'document'

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
Differentiates query text from document text for asymmetric retrieval tasks.
Defaults to document.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: dimension number

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
The dimension of the output embedding vectors. Defaults to 1024.
text-embedding-v4 also supports 1536 and 2048 dimensions.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: outputType 'dense' | 'sparse' | 'dense&sparse'

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
Specifies the output vector type. Defaults to dense.
The AI SDK embedding interface returns dense number[] vectors, so sparse-only
output is not supported and will throw. Use dense&sparse to receive dense
embeddings in embedding/embeddings and sparse vectors in
providerMetadata.alibaba.sparseEmbeddings.

The tables above list currently documented Alibaba text embedding models. You

metadata.title: Amazon Bedrock
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Amazon Bedrock provider.

title.children: Using IAM Access Key and Secret Key
Using AWS SDK Credentials Chain (instance profiles, instance roles, ECS roles, EKS Service Accounts, etc.)

contents.content: The Amazon Bedrock provider for the AI SDK contains language model support for the Amazon Bedrock APIs.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Bedrock provider is available in the @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock module. You can install it with

contents.heading: prerequisites
contents.content: Access to Amazon Bedrock foundation models isn't granted by default. In order to gain access to a foundation model, an IAM user with sufficient permissions needs to request access to it through the console. Once access is provided to a model, it is available for all users in the account.

contents.heading: prerequisites
contents.content: See the Model Access Docs for more information.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Step 1: Creating AWS Access Key and Secret Key

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: To get started, you'll need to create an AWS access key and secret key. Here's how:

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Login to AWS Management Console

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Go to the AWS Management Console and log in with your AWS account credentials.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Create an IAM User

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Navigate to the IAM dashboard and click on "Users" in the left-hand navigation menu.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Click on "Create user" and fill in the required details to create a new IAM user.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Make sure to select "Programmatic access" as the access type.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: The user account needs the AmazonBedrockFullAccess policy attached to it.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Create Access Key

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Click on the "Security credentials" tab and then click on "Create access key".

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Click "Create access key" to generate a new access key pair.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Download the .csv file containing the access key ID and secret access key.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Step 2: Configuring the Access Key and Secret Key

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Within your project add a .env file if you don't already have one. This file will be used to set the access key and secret key as environment variables. Add the following lines to the .env file:

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content:
Many frameworks such as Next.js load the .env file
automatically. If you're using a different framework, you may need to load the
.env file manually using a package like
dotenv.

contents.heading: using-iam-access-key-and-secret-key
contents.content: Remember to replace YOUR_ACCESS_KEY_ID, YOUR_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and YOUR_REGION with the actual values from your AWS account.

contents.heading: using-aws-sdk-credentials-chain-instance-profiles-instance-roles-ecs-roles-eks-service-accounts-etc
contents.content: When using AWS SDK, the SDK will automatically use the credentials chain to determine the credentials to use. This includes instance profiles, instance roles, ECS roles, EKS Service Accounts, etc. A similar behavior is possible using the AI SDK by not specifying the accessKeyId and secretAccessKey, sessionToken properties in the provider settings and instead passing a credentialProvider property.

contents.heading: using-aws-sdk-credentials-chain-instance-profiles-instance-roles-ecs-roles-eks-service-accounts-etc
contents.content: Usage:

contents.heading: using-aws-sdk-credentials-chain-instance-profiles-instance-roles-ecs-roles-eks-service-accounts-etc
contents.content: @aws-sdk/credential-providers package provides a set of credential providers that can be used to create a credential provider chain.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance bedrock from @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createAmazonBedrock from @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The credentials settings fall back to environment variable defaults described
below. These may be set by your serverless environment without your awareness,
which can lead to merged/conflicting credential values and provider errors
around failed authentication. If you're experiencing issues be sure you are
explicitly specifying all settings (even if undefined) to avoid any
defaults.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Amazon Bedrock provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: region string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The AWS region that you want to use for the API calls.
It uses the AWS_REGION environment variable by default.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: accessKeyId string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The AWS access key ID that you want to use for the API calls.
It uses the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID environment variable by default.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: secretAccessKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The AWS secret access key that you want to use for the API calls.
It uses the AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variable by default.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: sessionToken string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional. The AWS session token that you want to use for the API calls.
It uses the AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable by default.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional. Base URL for the Bedrock Runtime API calls.
When omitted, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME takes precedence over
AWS_ENDPOINT_URL; otherwise, the provider generates the endpoint for the
configured AWS region and partition.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: credentialProvider () => Promise<{ accessKeyId: string; secretAccessKey: string; sessionToken?: string; }>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Optional. The AWS credential provider chain that you want to use for the API calls.
It uses the specified credentials by default.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Bedrock API using the provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. meta.llama3-70b-instruct-v1:0.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Amazon Bedrock models also support some model specific provider options that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them in the providerOptions argument:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Documentation for additional settings based on the selected model can be found within the Amazon Bedrock Inference Parameter Documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can use Amazon Bedrock language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Amazon Bedrock language models can also be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For Anthropic models, you can use the structuredOutputMode provider option to
choose how Amazon Bedrock generates structured outputs:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: "outputFormat": Use Bedrock's native output_config.format parameter.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: "jsonTool": Use a special json tool with required tool choice.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
"auto": Use native structured output when supported by the model and
request, and otherwise fall back to the JSON tool. This is the default.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
In "auto" mode, Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Claude Haiku 4.5 use the JSON tool
fallback because native structured output can be unreliable across workloads
and Bedrock accounts. You can set "outputFormat" to opt into native structured
output when it works for your account and workload, or use "jsonTool" to force
the fallback for any model:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For parity with the Anthropic provider,
providerOptions.anthropic.structuredOutputMode is also honored for Anthropic
models on Bedrock. When both are provided, the bedrock value takes precedence.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For an Anthropic application inference profile, prefer the Bedrock Anthropic
provider. It uses Bedrock's native InvokeModel API, which accepts application
inference profile ARNs, and identifies the model as Anthropic automatically:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Use modelFamily: 'anthropic' only when you need to use the generic
@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock provider, which uses Bedrock's Converse API (for
example, when IAM permits Converse but not InvokeModel). Application inference
profile ARNs do not identify their underlying model, so declaring the family
allows Anthropic-specific features, including native structured output:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For an underlying model that does not reliably support native structured
output, set structuredOutputMode to "jsonTool".

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content:
Amazon Bedrock supports file inputs on in combination with specific models,
e.g. anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: The Amazon Bedrock provider supports file inputs, e.g. PDF files.

contents.heading: guardrails
contents.content: You can use the bedrock provider options to utilize Amazon Bedrock Guardrails:

contents.heading: guardrails
contents.content: Tracing information will be returned in the provider metadata if you have tracing enabled.

contents.heading: guardrails
contents.content: See the Amazon Bedrock Guardrails documentation for more information.

contents.heading: citations
contents.content: Amazon Bedrock supports citations for document-based inputs across compatible models. When enabled:

contents.heading: citations
contents.content: Some models can read documents with visual understanding, not just extracting text

contents.heading: citations
contents.content: Models can cite specific parts of documents you provide, making it easier to trace information back to its source (Not Supported Yet)

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content:
Amazon Bedrock prompt caching is currently in preview release. To request
access, visit the Amazon Bedrock prompt caching
page.

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content: In messages, you can use the providerOptions property to set cache points. Set the bedrock property in the providerOptions object to { cachePoint: { type: 'default' } } to create a cache point.

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content: Cache usage information is returned in the providerMetadata object`. See examples below.

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content:
Cache points have model-specific token minimums and limits. For example,
Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 requires at least 1,024 tokens for a cache point and
allows up to 4 cache points. See the Amazon Bedrock prompt caching
documentation
for details on supported models, regions, and limits.

contents.heading: cache-points
contents.content: Cache points also work with streaming responses:

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Amazon Bedrock supports model creator-specific reasoning features:

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Anthropic (e.g. claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219): enable via the reasoningConfig provider option and specifying a thinking budget in tokens (minimum: 1024, maximum: 64000).

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Amazon (e.g. us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0): enable via the reasoningConfig provider option and specifying a maximum reasoning effort level ('low' | 'medium' | 'high').

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
For Anthropic models, Bedrock's maxTokens limit includes both thinking and
final text. The provider therefore adds budgetTokens to maxOutputTokens
when setting maxTokens. When maxOutputTokens is omitted, the provider adds
budgetTokens to the default of 4096.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details
on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: extended-context-window
contents.content: Claude Sonnet 4 models on Amazon Bedrock support an extended context window of up to 1 million tokens when using the context-1m-2025-08-07 beta feature.

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Via Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock provides three provider-defined tools that can be used to interact with external systems:

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Bash Tool: Allows running bash commands.

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Text Editor Tool: Provides functionality for viewing and editing text files.

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Computer Tool: Enables control of keyboard and mouse actions on a computer.

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: They are available via the tools property of the provider instance.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: The Bash Tool allows running bash commands. Here's how to create and use it:

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: command (string): The bash command to run. Required unless the tool is being restarted.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: restart (boolean, optional): Specifying true will restart this tool.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: The Text Editor Tool provides functionality for viewing and editing text files.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: For Claude 4 models (Opus & Sonnet):

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: For Claude 3.5 Sonnet and earlier models:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: command ('view' | 'create' | 'str_replace' | 'insert' | 'undo_edit'): The command to run. Note: undo_edit is only available in Claude 3.5 Sonnet and earlier models.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: path (string): Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. /repo/file.py or /repo.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: file_text (string, optional): Required for create command, with the content of the file to be created.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: insert_line (number, optional): Required for insert command. The line number after which to insert the new string.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: new_str (string, optional): New string for str_replace or insert commands.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: old_str (string, optional): Required for str_replace command, containing the string to replace.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: view_range (number[], optional): Optional for view command to specify line range to show.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: When using the Text Editor Tool, make sure to name the key in the tools object correctly:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: Claude 4 models: Use str_replace_based_edit_tool

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and earlier: Use str_replace_editor

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: The Computer Tool enables control of keyboard and mouse actions on a computer:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: action ('key' | 'type' | 'mouse_move' | 'left_click' | 'left_click_drag' | 'right_click' | 'middle_click' | 'double_click' | 'screenshot' | 'cursor_position'): The action to perform.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: coordinate (number[], optional): Required for mouse_move and left_click_drag actions. Specifies the (x, y) coordinates.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: text (string, optional): Required for type and key actions.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: These tools can be used in conjunction with the anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0 model to enable more complex interactions and tasks.

metadata.description: Learn how to use the Anthropic provider for the AI SDK.

title.children: Structured Outputs and Tool Input Streaming

contents.content: The Anthropic provider contains language model support for the Anthropic Messages API.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Anthropic provider is available in the @ai-sdk/anthropic module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance anthropic from @ai-sdk/anthropic:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createAnthropic from @ai-sdk/anthropic and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Anthropic provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://api.anthropic.com/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the x-api-key header.
It defaults to the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Anthropic Messages API using the provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. claude-3-haiku-20240307.
Some models have multi-modal capabilities.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can use Anthropic language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Anthropic language models can also be used in the streamText, generateObject, and streamObject functions
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Anthropic models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: disableParallelToolUse boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Disables the use of parallel tool calls. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: When set to true, the model will only call one tool at a time instead of potentially calling multiple tools in parallel.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: sendReasoning boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Include reasoning content in requests sent to the model. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
If you are experiencing issues with the model handling requests involving
reasoning content, you can set this to false to omit them from the request.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: effort "low" | "medium" | "high" | "xhigh" | "max"

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. See Effort section for more details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: taskBudget object

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. See Task Budgets section for more details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: speed "fast" | "standard"

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. See Fast Mode section for more details.

contents.heading: language-models

contents.heading: language-models

contents.heading: language-models

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. See Reasoning section for more details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: effort "high" | "medium" | "low"

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. See Effort section for more details.

contents.heading: language-models

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to enable tool streaming (and structured output streaming). Default to true.

contents.heading: language-models

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Determines how structured outputs are generated. Optional.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: "outputFormat": Use the output_format parameter to specify the structured output format.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: "jsonTool": Use a special "json" tool to specify the structured output format (default).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: "auto": Use "outputFormat" when supported, otherwise fall back to "jsonTool".

contents.heading: language-models

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Metadata to include with the request. See the Anthropic API documentation for details.

contents.heading: language-models

contents.heading: structured-outputs-and-tool-input-streaming
contents.content: By default, the Anthropic API returns streaming tool calls and structured outputs all at once after a delay. To enable incremental streaming of tool inputs (when using streamText with tools) and structured outputs (when using streamObject), you need to set the anthropic-beta header to fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14.

contents.heading: for-tool-input-streaming-with-streamtext
contents.content: Without this header, tool inputs and structured outputs may arrive all at once after a delay instead of streaming incrementally.

contents.heading: for-tool-input-streaming-with-streamtext
contents.content:
For claude-opus-5-5 and claude-fable-5-1, the default mode is "auto",
which uses native structured outputs through output_config.format. These
models reject forced tool use, so the "jsonTool" mode cannot be used with
them. If you request "jsonTool" anyway, the provider falls back to
"outputFormat" and emits a warning. Likewise, a required or named
toolChoice is downgraded to auto with a warning; instruct the model to use
the tool in your prompt and verify that a tool call was made.

contents.heading: effort
contents.content: Anthropic introduced an effort option with claude-opus-4-5 that affects thinking, text responses, and function calls. Effort defaults to high and you can set it to medium or low to save tokens and to lower time-to-last-token latency (TTLT). claude-opus-4-7, claude-opus-4-8, claude-opus-5, claude-opus-5-5, claude-fable-5, claude-fable-5-1, and claude-sonnet-5 additionally support xhigh for maximum reasoning effort.

contents.heading: effort
contents.content: On claude-opus-5, thinking can only be disabled at effort levels up to and including high. When you combine thinking: { type: 'disabled' } with effort: 'xhigh' or effort: 'max', the AI SDK lowers the effort to high and emits a warning instead of sending a request that the API would reject.

contents.heading: effort
contents.content:
On claude-opus-5-5, thinking is always adaptive and cannot be disabled, so
effort is the main control for latency and cost. The API default effort for
claude-opus-5-5 is medium. Start there and test other levels rather than
carrying over the setting you used on claude-opus-5. Set maxOutputTokens
with room for thinking as well as the reply; thinking counts toward the limit
even when its content is not returned.

contents.heading: fast-mode
contents.content: Anthropic supports a speed option for claude-opus-4-6 that enables faster inference with approximately 2.5x faster output token speeds.

contents.heading: fast-mode
contents.content: The speed option accepts 'fast' or 'standard' (default behavior).

contents.heading: data-residency
contents.content: Anthropic supports an inferenceGeo option that controls where model inference runs for a request.

contents.heading: data-residency
contents.content: The inferenceGeo option accepts 'us' (US-only infrastructure) or 'global' (default, any available geography).

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: Claude Fable 5 has safeguards that limit its performance in certain areas like cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry, and automated safety checks are run on every request.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: When one of these checks blocks a request, the API does not answer it. Instead it returns a classifier block: a 200 response with a refusal stop reason and an optional stop_details object describing the category that triggered the block. The AI SDK surfaces this as a content-filter finish reason, with the details available on providerMetadata.anthropic.stopDetails.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: A classifier block looks like this:

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: Branch on the finish reason rather than on the presence of stop_details — the API may return a refusal with no details at all.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: To avoid receiving a classifier block, pass the fallbacks option. When the primary model's classifiers block a turn, the API automatically retries it server-side on a fallback model and returns that model's answer. The required beta header is added for you.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: The recommended configuration is fallbacks: 'default', which lets the API route the retry to Anthropic's recommended fallback model based on the refusal category and removes the need to migrate when a fallback model is deprecated:

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: You can also pin an explicit fallback chain:

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: Each fallback entry requires a model and may additionally override max_tokens, thinking, output_config, and speed for that attempt only.

contents.heading: safety-classifiers-and-fallbacks
contents.content: When a fallback serves the turn, it is recorded in the per-model usage breakdown (usage.iterations) as a fallback_message entry. The AI SDK exposes this breakdown on providerMetadata.anthropic.iterations, so you can detect whether a fallback ran:

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: claude-opus-4-7 supports a taskBudget option that informs the model of the total token budget available for an agentic turn. The model uses this information to prioritize work, plan ahead, and wind down gracefully as the budget is consumed.

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: Task budgets are advisory — they do not enforce a hard token limit. The model will attempt to stay within budget, but actual usage may vary.

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: For long-running agents that compact and restart context, you can carry the remaining budget forward using the remaining field:

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: The taskBudget object accepts:

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: type "tokens" - Budget type. Currently only "tokens" is supported.

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: total number - Total task budget for the agentic turn. Minimum 20,000.

contents.heading: task-budgets
contents.content: remaining number - Budget left after prior compacted-away contexts. Must be between 0 and total. Defaults to total if omitted.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Anthropic has reasoning support for claude-opus-4-20250514, claude-sonnet-4-20250514, and claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219 models.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
You can enable it using the thinking provider option
and specifying a thinking budget in tokens.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: You can combine adaptive thinking with the effort option to control how much reasoning Claude uses:

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content:
claude-opus-5-5, claude-fable-5, and claude-fable-5-1 always run adaptive
thinking. The API rejects thinking: { type: 'disabled' } and budget-based
thinking: { type: 'enabled' } for these models. To keep existing code working,
the provider:

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content: removes thinking: { type: 'disabled' } and emits a warning,

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content: converts thinking: { type: 'enabled', budgetTokens } to { type: 'adaptive' } and emits a warning.

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content:
Use effort to control how much these models think. On claude-opus-5-5, set
effort: 'low' when time to first token matters, and move to medium if
quality drops:

contents.heading: adaptive-only-models
contents.content:
Responses from adaptive-only models can begin with a thinking block. Read the
response by content type (text, reasoning, tool-call) rather than
assuming the first part is text. Under the default display: 'omitted'
setting, thinking blocks are returned with empty text.

contents.heading: thinking-display-opus-47
contents.content: Starting with claude-opus-4-7, thinking content is omitted from the response by default — thinking blocks are present in the stream but their text is empty. To receive reasoning output, set display: 'summarized':

contents.heading: thinking-display-opus-47
contents.content:
If you stream reasoning to users with claude-opus-4-7, the default "omitted" display will
cause a long pause before output begins. Set display: "summarized" to restore visible
progress during thinking.

contents.heading: thinking-updates
contents.content:
Use display: 'updates' with claude-opus-5-5 or claude-fable-5-1 to stream
thinking summaries between tool calls. These models return progress notes
between tool calls as thinking blocks rather than text, so without this setting
a long tool-calling turn can look silent. The provider adds the required
thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18 beta header automatically:

contents.heading: thinking-block-binding
contents.content:
Fable 5.1 can recover from a thinking-block prefix mismatch by dropping the
mismatched block. Set blockBinding.prefixMismatchBehavior to drop_block.
You can provide block binding by itself to preserve the model's default
thinking mode, or combine it with adaptive thinking.

contents.heading: budget-based-thinking
contents.content:
For earlier models (claude-opus-4-20250514, claude-sonnet-4-20250514, claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929),
use type: 'enabled' with an explicit token budget:

contents.heading: budget-based-thinking
contents.content:
Anthropic's max_tokens limit includes both thinking and final text. To reserve
room for both, the provider adds budgetTokens to maxOutputTokens when
setting max_tokens. For known models, the combined value is capped at the
model's maximum output token limit.

contents.heading: budget-based-thinking
contents.content:
See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details
on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content:
In the messages and message parts, you can use the providerOptions property to set cache control breakpoints.
You need to set the anthropic property in the providerOptions object to { cacheControl: { type: 'ephemeral' } } to set a cache control breakpoint.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content:
The cache creation input tokens are then returned in the providerMetadata object
for generateText and generateObject, again under the anthropic property.
When you use streamText or streamObject, the response contains a promise
that resolves to the metadata. Alternatively you can receive it in the
onFinish callback.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content: You can also use cache control on system messages by providing multiple system messages at the head of your messages array:

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content: Cache control for tools:

contents.heading: longer-cache-ttl
contents.content: Anthropic also supports a longer 1-hour cache duration.

contents.heading: longer-cache-ttl
contents.content: Here's an example:

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: The minimum cacheable prompt length is:

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: 1024 tokens for Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Claude 3 Opus

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: 2048 tokens for Claude 3.5 Haiku and Claude 3 Haiku

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: Shorter prompts cannot be cached, even if marked with cacheControl. Any requests to cache fewer than this number of tokens will be processed without caching.

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content: For more on prompt caching with Anthropic, see Anthropic's Cache Control documentation.

contents.heading: limitations
contents.content:
Because the UIMessage type (used by AI SDK UI hooks like useChat) does not
support the providerOptions property, you can use convertToModelMessages
first before passing the messages to functions like generateText or
streamText. For more details on providerOptions usage, see
here.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: The Bash Tool allows running bash commands. Here's how to create and use it:

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: command (string): The bash command to run. Required unless the tool is being restarted.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: restart (boolean, optional): Specifying true will restart this tool.

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content:
The bash tool must have the name bash. Only certain Claude versions are
supported.

contents.heading: memory-tool
contents.content:
The Memory Tool allows Claude to use a local memory, e.g. in the filesystem.
Here's how to create it:

contents.heading: memory-tool
contents.content:
The memory tool must have the name memory. Only certain Claude versions are
supported.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: The Text Editor Tool provides functionality for viewing and editing text files.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content:
Different models support different versions of the tool. For Claude Sonnet 3.5
and 3.7 you need to use older tool versions and tool names.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: command ('view' | 'create' | 'str_replace' | 'insert' | 'undo_edit'): The command to run. Note: undo_edit is only available in Claude 3.5 Sonnet and earlier models.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: path (string): Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. /repo/file.py or /repo.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: file_text (string, optional): Required for create command, with the content of the file to be created.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: insert_line (number, optional): Required for insert command. The line number after which to insert the new string.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: new_str (string, optional): New string for str_replace or insert commands.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: old_str (string, optional): Required for str_replace command, containing the string to replace.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: view_range (number[], optional): Optional for view command to specify line range to show.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: The Computer Tool enables control of keyboard and mouse actions on a computer:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: action ('key' | 'type' | 'mouse_move' | 'left_click' | 'left_click_drag' | 'right_click' | 'middle_click' | 'double_click' | 'screenshot' | 'cursor_position'): The action to perform.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: coordinate (number[], optional): Required for mouse_move and left_click_drag actions. Specifies the (x, y) coordinates.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: text (string, optional): Required for type and key actions.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: These tools can be used in conjunction with the sonnet-3-5-sonnet-20240620 model to enable more complex interactions and tasks.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content:
Newer models use the computer toolset instead of a versioned computer tool.
claude-opus-5-5 accepts computer use only through the toolset and rejects the
older computer_* tool types with a 400. The toolset does not require a beta
header and has no display size parameters: coordinates are always in the pixel
space of the screenshots you return. Zoom is enabled by default, and Claude can
return several actions in one turn, each as its own tool call.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content:
The API returns each action as a separate tool_use block with
toolset_name: 'computer'. The AI SDK maps every action to the toolset tool and
passes the action name as action, so execute receives the same input shape
as the older computer tools. The tool name must be computer:

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: action ('screenshot' | 'zoom' | 'left_click' | 'right_click' | 'middle_click' | 'double_click' | 'triple_click' | 'left_click_drag' | 'mouse_move' | 'left_mouse_down' | 'left_mouse_up' | 'cursor_position' | 'scroll' | 'type' | 'key' | 'hold_key' | 'wait'): The member tool that Claude invoked.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: coordinate (number[], optional): The (x, y) pixel coordinates for click, move, and scroll actions.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: start_coordinate (number[], optional): Where a left_click_drag starts.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: region (number[], optional): [x1, y1, x2, y2] for the zoom action.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: text (string, optional): Text to type, the key combination for key and hold_key, or modifier keys to hold during click and scroll actions.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: repeat (number, optional): How many times to press the key for key.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: duration (number, optional): Seconds for hold_key and wait.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: scroll_direction ('up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right', optional) and scroll_amount (number, optional): For the scroll action.

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content: configs (object, optional): Per-action settings keyed by action name. Each entry accepts enabled (default true) and deferLoading (default false, for tool search).

contents.heading: computer-toolset
contents.content:
Tool calls and results of the toolset are serialized with toolset_name when
you pass the message history back. Keep the toolset tool in tools on
follow-up requests, or the provider falls back to the toolsetName provider
metadata on the tool calls of previous responses. Do not declare the toolset
together with an older computer_* tool.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: Anthropic provides a provider-defined web search tool that gives Claude direct access to real-time web content, allowing it to answer questions with up-to-date information beyond its knowledge cutoff.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: You can enable web search using the provider-defined web search tool:

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content:
Web search must be enabled in your organization's Console
settings.

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: The web search tool supports several configuration options:

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: maxUses number

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: Maximum number of web searches Claude can perform during the conversation.

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: allowedDomains string[]

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: Optional list of domains that Claude is allowed to search. If provided, searches will be restricted to these domains.

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: blockedDomains string[]

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: Optional list of domains that Claude should avoid when searching.

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: userLocation object

contents.heading: configuration-options
contents.content: Optional user location information to provide geographically relevant search results.

contents.heading: web-fetch-tool
contents.content: Anthropic provides a provider-defined web fetch tool that allows Claude to retrieve content from specific URLs. This is useful when you want Claude to analyze or reference content from a particular webpage or document.

contents.heading: web-fetch-tool
contents.content: You can enable web fetch using the provider-defined web fetch tool:

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: The web fetch tool supports several configuration options:

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: maxUses number

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: The maxUses parameter limits the number of web fetches performed.

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: allowedDomains string[]

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: Only fetch from these domains.

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: blockedDomains string[]

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: Never fetch from these domains.

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: citations object

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: Unlike web search where citations are always enabled, citations are optional for web fetch. Set "citations": {"enabled": true} to enable Claude to cite specific passages from fetched documents.

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: maxContentTokens number

contents.heading: configuration-options-1
contents.content: The maxContentTokens parameter limits the amount of content that will be included in the context.

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content: Web search errors are handled differently depending on whether you're using streaming or non-streaming:

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content:
Non-streaming (generateText, generateObject):
Web search errors throw exceptions that you can catch:

contents.heading: error-handling
contents.content:
Streaming (streamText, streamObject):
Web search errors are delivered as error parts in the stream:

contents.heading: mid-conversation-system-controls
contents.content:
With claude-opus-5-5 and claude-fable-5-1, a mid-conversation system message
can be cleared before the next user message with clearAt: 'next_user_message',
or set the effort for the next turn without invalidating the prompt cache. The provider adds the required
mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21 and
mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01 beta headers automatically.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-system-controls
mid-conversation-system-controls
contents.content:
clearAt and per-message effort apply only to mid-conversation system
messages. When used on the initial system message, the provider ignores them
and emits a warning. Use the top-level effort provider option to configure
effort for the full request.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-tool-changes
contents.content: With claude-opus-4-8, you can add or remove tools between turns of a conversation without invalidating the prompt cache. Attach toolChanges to a system message that appears mid-conversation (right before an assistant message or at the end of the messages). The required mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01 beta header is added automatically.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-tool-changes
contents.content: Tools referenced by a tool_addition must be declared in the tools option — typically with deferLoading: true, so they are not loaded into context until the addition surfaces them. A tool_removal removes a previously available tool from the conversation going forward.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-tool-changes
contents.content: To change a tool's definition, remove the old definition at the end of one request, then carry the conversation forward with the updated definition in tools on the next request.

contents.heading: mid-conversation-tool-changes
contents.content:
Tool changes are not supported on the initial system message. The AI SDK
ignores them there and emits a warning — configure the initial tool set via
the tools option instead.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: Anthropic provides a provider-defined code execution tool that gives Claude direct access to a real Python environment allowing it to execute code to inform its responses.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: You can enable code execution using the provider-defined code execution tool:

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content:
Three versions are available: codeExecution_20260120 (recommended, does not
require a beta header, supports Claude Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 4.5, and
Opus 4.5), codeExecution_20250825 (supports Python and Bash with enhanced
file operations), and codeExecution_20250522 (supports Bash only).

contents.heading: error-handling-1
contents.content: Code execution errors are handled differently depending on whether you're using streaming or non-streaming:

contents.heading: error-handling-1
contents.content:
Non-streaming (generateText, generateObject):
Code execution errors are delivered as tool result parts in the response:

contents.heading: error-handling-1
contents.content:
Streaming (streamText, streamObject):
Code execution errors are delivered as error parts in the stream:

contents.heading: agent-skills
contents.content: Anthropic Agent Skills enable Claude to perform specialized tasks like document processing (PPTX, DOCX, PDF, XLSX) and data analysis. Skills run in a sandboxed container and require the code execution tool to be enabled.

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: Anthropic provides several built-in skills:

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: pptx - Create and edit PowerPoint presentations

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: docx - Create and edit Word documents

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: pdf - Process and analyze PDF files

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: xlsx - Work with Excel spreadsheets

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: To use skills, you need to:

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: Enable the code execution tool

contents.heading: using-built-in-skills
contents.content: Specify the container with skills in providerOptions

contents.heading: custom-skills
contents.content: You can also use custom skills by specifying type: 'custom':

contents.heading: custom-skills
contents.content:
Skills use progressive context loading and execute within a sandboxed
container with code execution capabilities.

contents.heading: compaction
contents.content: The compact_20260112 edit type automatically summarizes earlier conversation context when token limits are reached. This is useful for long-running conversations where you want to preserve the essence of earlier exchanges while staying within token limits.

contents.heading: compaction
contents.content: Configuration:

contents.heading: compaction
contents.content: trigger - Condition that triggers compaction (e.g., { type: 'input_tokens', value: 50000 })

contents.heading: compaction
contents.content: instructions - Custom instructions for how the model should summarize the conversation. Use this to guide the compaction summary towards specific aspects of the conversation you want to preserve.

contents.heading: compaction
contents.content: pauseAfterCompaction - When true, the model will pause after generating the compaction summary, allowing you to inspect or process it before continuing. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: compaction
contents.content: When compaction occurs, the model generates a summary of the earlier context. This summary appears as a text block with special provider metadata.

contents.heading: detecting-compaction-in-streams
contents.content: When using streamText, you can detect compaction summaries by checking the providerMetadata on text-start events:

contents.heading: compaction-in-ui-applications
contents.content: When using useChat or other UI hooks, compaction summaries appear as regular text parts with providerMetadata. You can style them differently in your UI:

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content:
Anthropic Sonnet claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 supports reading PDF files.
You can pass PDF files as part of the message content using the file type:

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content: Option 1: URL-based PDF document

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content: Option 2: Base64-encoded PDF document

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content:
The model will have access to the contents of the PDF file and
respond to questions about it.
The PDF file should be passed using the data field,
and the mediaType should be set to 'application/pdf'.

metadata.title: AssemblyAI
metadata.description: Learn how to use the AssemblyAI provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content: The AssemblyAI provider contains transcription model support for the AssemblyAI transcription API.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The AssemblyAI provider is available in the @ai-sdk/assemblyai module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance assemblyai from @ai-sdk/assemblyai:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createAssemblyAI from @ai-sdk/assemblyai and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the AssemblyAI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the AssemblyAI transcription API
using the .transcription() factory method.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id, e.g. universal-3-5-pro.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The best model is a deprecated legacy model, sent using AssemblyAI's
deprecated speech_model request parameter. It still works, but using it emits a
deprecation warning — prefer universal-3-5-pro. The older nano model has been
removed by AssemblyAI and is no longer available. All newer models are sent using
the speech_models
request parameter, which the provider selects automatically based on the model id.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
universal-3-pro and universal-2 are fully supported and continue to work, but
using them emits an informational warning (not a deprecation) suggesting
universal-3-5-pro, AssemblyAI's latest flagship model.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying the contentSafety option will enable content safety filtering.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: audioEndAt number

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
End time of the audio in milliseconds.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: audioStartFrom number

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Start time of the audio in milliseconds.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: autoChapters boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to automatically generate chapters for the transcription.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: autoHighlights boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to automatically generate highlights for the transcription.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: boostParam enum

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Boost parameter for wordBoost.
Allowed values: 'low', 'default', 'high'.
Deprecated — only applies to the deprecated wordBoost; use keytermsPrompt instead.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: contentSafety boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to enable content safety filtering.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: contentSafetyConfidence number

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Confidence threshold for content safety filtering (25-100).
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: customSpelling array of objects

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Custom spelling rules for the transcription.
Each object has from (array of strings) and to (string) properties.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: disfluencies boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to include disfluencies (um, uh, etc.) in the transcription.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: domain string

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Enable a domain-specific model for specialized terminology.
Currently supports 'medical-v1' (Medical Mode).
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: entityDetection boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to detect entities in the transcription.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: filterProfanity boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to filter profanity in the transcription.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: formatText boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to format the text in the transcription.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: iabCategories boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to include IAB categories in the transcription.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: keytermsPrompt array of strings

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Domain-specific keyterms to boost recognition for (max 6 words per phrase).
Replaces wordBoost for newer models — supported by universal-3-pro,
universal-3-5-pro, and slam-1 (and universal-2 when enabled).
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: languageCode string

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Language code for the audio.
Supports numerous ISO-639-1 and ISO-639-3 language codes.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: languageConfidenceThreshold number

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Confidence threshold for language detection.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: languageDetection boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to enable language detection.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: languageDetectionOptions object

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Options for automatic language detection: expectedLanguages (array of
strings), fallbackLanguage (string), codeSwitching (boolean),
codeSwitchingConfidenceThreshold (number, 0-1).
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: multichannel boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to process multiple audio channels separately.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: prompt string

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Natural-language context (up to 1,500 words) to steer the model.
Only supported by universal-3-pro, universal-3-5-pro, and slam-1.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: punctuate boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to add punctuation to the transcription.
Optional.
