contents.heading: speaker-diarization-and-audio-intelligence-results
contents.content:
The AI SDK's transcribe result exposes text, segments, language, and
durationInSeconds. AssemblyAI's richer results — speaker diarization and
audio-intelligence features — don't fit that shape, so they are surfaced in two
places:

contents.heading: speaker-diarization-and-audio-intelligence-results
contents.content:
providerMetadata.assemblyai — structured results for the features you
enabled: utterances (speaker-diarized segments, when speakerLabels is set),
entities, sentimentAnalysisResults, contentSafetyLabels,
iabCategoriesResult, and autoHighlightsResult.

contents.heading: speaker-diarization-and-audio-intelligence-results
contents.content:
response.body — the complete, raw AssemblyAI transcript response, so any
field not surfaced above (e.g. chapters, word-level speaker labels) is
still available.

contents.heading: speaker-diarization-and-audio-intelligence-results
contents.content:
Note: timings inside providerMetadata and response.body (e.g.
utterances[].start) are in milliseconds, matching the AssemblyAI API —
whereas the top-level segments use seconds.

contents.heading: speaker-diarization-and-audio-intelligence-results
contents.content:
The following AssemblyAI features are deprecated by the API and not surfaced
in providerMetadata (their output remains on the raw response.body if
enabled): Summarization, Auto Chapters, and Custom Topics. Note also that some
features are language-gated (e.g. sentiment analysis is English-centric); see
AssemblyAI's documentation for per-language availability.

metadata.title: Azure OpenAI
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Azure OpenAI provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content: The Azure OpenAI provider contains language model support for the Azure OpenAI chat API.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI provider is available in the @ai-sdk/azure module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance azure from @ai-sdk/azure:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createAzure from @ai-sdk/azure and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can also use a complete Microsoft Foundry OpenAI v1 base URL:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
For Microsoft Entra ID authentication, you can provide a token provider.
Install @azure/identity separately if you want to use its credential helpers:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the OpenAI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: resourceName string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Azure resource name.
It defaults to the AZURE_RESOURCE_NAME environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The resource name is used in the assembled URL: https://{resourceName}.openai.azure.com/openai/v1{path}.
You can use baseURL instead to specify the URL prefix.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the api-key header.
It defaults to the AZURE_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: tokenProvider () => Promise<string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Microsoft Entra ID token provider that returns an access token to be sent using the Authorization header.
When provided, this is used instead of apiKey.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiVersion string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Sets a custom api version.
Defaults to v1.
This setting is applied when the provider constructs the v1 path or uses
deployment-based URLs. Complete v1 base URLs are used as-is.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Either this or resourceName can be used.
When a baseURL is provided, the resourceName is ignored.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
For Azure-hosted URLs ending in .openai.azure.com,
.services.ai.azure.com, or .cognitiveservices.azure.com, you can pass
either an unversioned OpenAI prefix such as https://your-resource.services.ai.azure.com/openai
or a complete v1 base URL such as https://your-resource.services.ai.azure.com/openai/v1.
The provider appends /v1 and the configured api-version to unversioned
resource URLs. Complete v1 URLs are used as-is.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Complete Microsoft Foundry project v1 URLs, such as
https://your-resource.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/your-project/openai/v1,
are also used as-is. If /v1 is omitted from a Foundry project URL, the
provider appends it without adding an api-version query parameter.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
With a non-Azure custom gateway baseURL, the resolved URL is {baseURL}{path};
the SDK does not append /v1 or an api-version query parameter in this mode.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: useDeploymentBasedUrls boolean

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use deployment-based URLs for API calls. Set to true to use the legacy deployment format:
{baseURL}/deployments/{deploymentId}{path}?api-version={apiVersion} instead of
{baseURL}/v1{path}?api-version={apiVersion}.
Defaults to false.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
This option is useful for compatibility with certain Azure OpenAI models or deployments
that require the legacy endpoint format.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI provider instance is a function that you can invoke to create a language model:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You need to pass your deployment name as the first argument.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Azure exposes the thinking of DeepSeek-R1 in the generated text using the <think> tag.
You can use the extractReasoningMiddleware to extract this reasoning and expose it as a reasoning property on the result:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: You can then use that enhanced model in functions like generateText and streamText.

contents.heading: example
contents.content: You can use OpenAI language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: example
contents.content:
OpenAI language models can also be used in the streamText, generateObject, and streamObject functions
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: example
contents.content:
Azure OpenAI sends larger chunks than OpenAI. This can lead to the perception
that the response is slower. See Troubleshooting: Azure OpenAI Slow To
Stream

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: When using OpenAI language models on Azure, you can configure provider-specific options using providerOptions.openai. More information on available configuration options are on the OpenAI provider page.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
The URL for calling Azure chat models will be constructed as follows:
https://RESOURCE_NAME.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/chat/completions?api-version=v1

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Azure OpenAI chat models support also some model specific settings that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for OpenAI chat models:

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: logitBias Record<number, number>

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Modifies the likelihood of specified tokens appearing in the completion.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Accepts a JSON object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in
the GPT tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. You
can use this tokenizer tool to convert text to token IDs. Mathematically,
the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling.
The exact effect will vary per model, but values between -1 and 1 should
decrease or increase likelihood of selection; values like -100 or 100
should result in a ban or exclusive selection of the relevant token.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: As an example, you can pass {"50256": -100} to prevent the token from being generated.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: logprobs boolean | number

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Return the log probabilities of the tokens. Including logprobs will increase
the response size and can slow down response times. However, it can
be useful to better understand how the model is behaving.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Setting to true will return the log probabilities of the tokens that
were generated.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Setting to a number will return the log probabilities of the top n
tokens that were generated.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use. Default to true.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to
monitor and detect abuse. Learn more.

contents.heading: deepseek-chat-models
contents.content: You can create Azure-hosted DeepSeek chat models using the .deepseek() factory method:

contents.heading: deepseek-chat-models
contents.content:
Use this factory for Azure DeepSeek models that support DeepSeek's chat
reasoning fields, such as deepseek-v4-pro and deepseek-v4-flash. The
factory parses streamed reasoning_content as AI SDK reasoning parts.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: You can use the Azure OpenAI responses API with the azure.responses(deploymentName) factory method.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
Further configuration can be done using OpenAI provider options.
You can validate the provider options using the OpenAIResponsesProviderOptions type.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
parallelToolCalls boolean
Whether to use parallel tool calls. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
store boolean
Whether to store the generation. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
metadata Record<string, string>
Additional metadata to store with the generation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
previousResponseId string
The ID of the previous response. You can use it to continue a conversation. Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
instructions string
Instructions for the model.
They can be used to change the system or developer message when continuing a conversation using the previousResponseId option.
Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
user string
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse. Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningEffort 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'
Reasoning effort for reasoning models. Defaults to medium. If you use providerOptions to set the reasoningEffort option, this model setting will be ignored.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
strictJsonSchema boolean
Whether to use strict JSON schema validation. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI responses provider also returns provider-specific metadata:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The following OpenAI-specific metadata is returned:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
responseId string
The ID of the response. Can be used to continue a conversation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
cachedPromptTokens number
The number of prompt tokens that were a cache hit.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningTokens number
The number of reasoning tokens that the model generated.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
The providerMetadata is only returned with the default responses API, and is
not supported when using 'azure.chat' or 'azure.completion'

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI responses API supports web search through the azure.tools.webSearch tool.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: The web search tool supports the following configuration options:

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: externalWebAccess boolean - Whether to use external web access for fetching live content. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: searchContextSize 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' - Controls the amount of context used for the search. Higher values provide more comprehensive results but may have higher latency and cost.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: userLocation - Optional location information to provide geographically relevant results. Includes type (always 'approximate'), country, city, region, and timezone.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: filters - Optional filter configuration to restrict search results.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: allowedDomains string[] - Up to 100 allowed domains for the search.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: blockedDomains string[] - Up to 100 blocked domains for the search.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: Omit the HTTP or HTTPS prefix from domain filters. Subdomains of configured domains are automatically included or excluded.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: For detailed information on configuration options see the Azure OpenAI Web Search Tool documentation.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content:
The 'web_search' tool is only supported with the default responses
API, and is not supported when using 'azure.chat' or 'azure.completion'

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI responses API supports file search through the azure.tools.fileSearch tool.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: You can force the use of the file search tool by setting the toolChoice parameter to { type: 'tool', toolName: 'file_search' }.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content:
The tool must be named file_search when using Azure OpenAI's file search
functionality. This name is required by Azure OpenAI's API specification and
cannot be customized.

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
Azure OpenAI Responses API
image_generation
is now Preview release(Not GA release).Image tool does not currently support
streaming mode. You can not use the image tool with streamText currently.

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
Azure OpenAI's Responses API supports multi-modal image generation as a provider-defined tool.
Availability is restricted to specific models (for example, gpt-5 variants).

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content: You can use the image tool with generateText.

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
To use image_generation, you must first create an image generation model. You
must add a deployment specification to the header
x-ms-oai-image-generation-deployment. Please note that the Responses API
model and the image generation model must be in the same resource.

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
When you set store: false, then previously generated images will not be
accessible by the model. We recommend using the image generation tool without
setting store: false.

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content: The Azure OpenAI responses API supports the code interpreter tool through the azure.tools.codeInterpreter tool. This allows models to write and execute Python code.

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content: The code interpreter tool can be configured with:

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content: container: Either a container ID string or an object with fileIds to specify uploaded files that should be available to the code interpreter

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content:
The tool must be named code_interpreter when using Azure OpenAI's code
interpreter functionality. This name is required by Azure OpenAI's API
specification and cannot be customized.

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content:
The Azure OpenAI Responses API supports reading PDF files.
You can pass PDF files as part of the message content using the file type:

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content:
The model will have access to the contents of the PDF file and
respond to questions about it.
The PDF file should be passed using the data field,
and the mediaType should be set to 'application/pdf'.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the completions API using the .completion() factory method.
The first argument is the model id.
Currently only gpt-35-turbo-instruct is supported.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
OpenAI completion models support also some model specific settings that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Azure OpenAI completion models:

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: echo: boolean

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: Echo back the prompt in addition to the completion.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: logitBias Record<number, number>

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: Modifies the likelihood of specified tokens appearing in the completion.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
Accepts a JSON object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in
the GPT tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. You
can use this tokenizer tool to convert text to token IDs. Mathematically,
the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling.
The exact effect will vary per model, but values between -1 and 1 should
decrease or increase likelihood of selection; values like -100 or 100
should result in a ban or exclusive selection of the relevant token.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
As an example, you can pass {"50256": -100} to prevent the <|endoftext|>
token from being generated.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: logprobs boolean | number

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
Return the log probabilities of the tokens. Including logprobs will increase
the response size and can slow down response times. However, it can
be useful to better understand how the model is behaving.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
Setting to true will return the log probabilities of the tokens that
were generated.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
Setting to a number will return the log probabilities of the top n
tokens that were generated.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: suffix string

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: The suffix that comes after a completion of inserted text.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to
monitor and detect abuse. Learn more.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Azure OpenAI embeddings API
using the .textEmbedding() factory method.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
Azure OpenAI embedding models support several additional settings.
You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Azure OpenAI embedding models:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: dimensions: number

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
The number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have.
Only supported in text-embedding-3 and later models.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to
monitor and detect abuse. Learn more.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content: You can create models that call the Azure OpenAI image generation API (DALL-E) using the .image() factory method. The first argument is your deployment name for the DALL-E model.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content: Azure OpenAI image models support several additional settings. You can pass them as providerOptions.openai when generating the image:

contents.heading: example-1
contents.content: You can use Azure OpenAI image models to generate images with the generateImage function:

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Azure OpenAI supports DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 models through deployments. The capabilities depend on which model version your deployment is using:

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Model Version

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Sizes

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: DALL-E 3

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: DALL-E 2

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content:
DALL-E models do not support the aspectRatio parameter. Use the size
parameter instead.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content:
When creating your Azure OpenAI deployment, make sure to set the DALL-E model
version you want to use.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can create models that call the Azure OpenAI transcription API using the .transcription() factory method.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. whisper-1.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
If you encounter a "DeploymentNotFound" error with transcription models,
try enabling deployment-based URLs:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
This uses the legacy endpoint format which may be required for certain Azure OpenAI deployments.
When using useDeploymentBasedUrls, the default api-version is not valid. You must set it to 2025-04-01-preview or an earlier value.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 (e.g. en) format will improve accuracy and latency.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
timestampGranularities string[]
The granularity of the timestamps in the transcription.
Defaults to ['segment'].
Possible values are ['word'], ['segment'], and ['word', 'segment'].
Note: There is no additional latency for segment timestamps, but generating word timestamps incurs additional latency.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
language string
The language of the input audio. Supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 format (e.g. 'en') will improve accuracy and latency.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
prompt string
An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment. The prompt should match the audio language.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
temperature number
The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use log probability to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.
Defaults to 0.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
include string[]
Additional information to include in the transcription response.

contents.content: Model

contents.content: Black Forest Labs image models support flexible provider options through the providerOptions.blackForestLabs object. You can pass any parameters supported by the specific endpoint's API. The supported parameters depend on the used model ID:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: imagePrompt - Base64-encoded image to use as additional visual context for generation

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: imagePromptStrength - Strength of the image prompt influence on generation (0.0 to 1.0)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: inputImage - Base64 encoded image or URL of image to use as reference. Supports up to 20MB or 20 megapixels.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: outputFormat - Desired format of the output image. Can be “jpeg” or “png”.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: promptUpsampling - If true, performs upsampling on the prompt

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: raw - Enable raw mode for more natural, authentic aesthetics

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: safetyTolerance - Moderation level for inputs and outputs. Value ranges from 0 (most strict) to 6 (more permissive).

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: webhookSecret - Secret for webhook signature verification, sent in the X-Webhook-Secret header.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: webhookUrl - URL for asynchronous completion notification. Must be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: pollIntervalMillis - Interval in milliseconds between polling attempts (default 500ms)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: pollTimeoutMillis - Overall timeout in milliseconds for polling before timing out (default 60s)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: width - Output width in pixels for models that support explicit dimensions. Range 256–1920, default 1024. When set, this overrides any width derived from size.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: height - Output height in pixels for models that support explicit dimensions. Range 256–1920, default 768. When set, this overrides any height derived from size.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: steps - Number of inference steps. Higher values may improve quality but increase generation time

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: guidance - Guidance scale for generation. Higher values follow the prompt more closely

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: inputImage2 … inputImage10 - Additional reference images (base64 string or URL) for models that support multiple inputs, used alongside inputImage.

metadata.title: DeepSeek
metadata.description: Learn how to use DeepSeek's models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: The DeepSeek provider offers access to powerful language models through the DeepSeek API.
API keys can be obtained from the DeepSeek Platform.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The DeepSeek provider is available via the @ai-sdk/deepseek module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance deepseek from @ai-sdk/deepseek:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: For custom configuration, you can import createDeepSeek and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the DeepSeek provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls.
The default prefix is https://api.deepseek.com/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header. It defaults to
the DEEPSEEK_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom fetch implementation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can create language models using a provider instance:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can also use the .chat() or .languageModel() factory methods:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
DeepSeek language models can be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
DeepSeek retired the deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner aliases on July 24,
2026. Use deepseek-flash (the alias for the current V4.x Flash release),
deepseek-v4-flash, or deepseek-v4-pro for the current API. Custom and legacy
model IDs remain accepted as strings for compatibility with custom endpoints.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for DeepSeek models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: logprobs boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Returns log probabilities for generated content and reasoning
tokens in providerMetadata.deepseek.logprobs.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: topLogprobs number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Returns the specified number of most likely tokens at each token
position. Accepts values from 0 through 20 and automatically enables
logprobs.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: userId string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. An opaque end-user identifier that DeepSeek uses for content-safety
tracing, KV-cache isolation, and scheduling isolation. The value must match
^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ and contain at most 512 characters. Do not include names,
email addresses, or other private user information.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinking object

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Controls thinking mode (chain-of-thought reasoning). You can enable thinking mode either by using the deepseek-v4-pro model or by setting this option.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: type: 'enabled' | 'disabled' - Enable or disable thinking mode. See DeepSeek's thinking mode docs.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'low' | 'high' | 'max'

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Controls thinking strength for DeepSeek V4 reasoning models.
medium is sent as high, and xhigh is sent as max. A compatibility
warning is returned whenever the requested value is mapped.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
For backwards compatibility, legacy provider options supplied at runtime are
also mapped to documented values: thinking.type: 'adaptive' becomes
'enabled', reasoningEffort: 'medium' becomes 'high', and
reasoningEffort: 'xhigh' becomes 'max'. Each mapping returns a compatibility
warning so callers can migrate to a canonical value.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
DeepSeek has deprecated the top-level frequencyPenalty and presencePenalty
settings. The provider omits these settings and returns a deprecation warning
when they are used. temperature and topP have no effect while thinking is
enabled, including the default thinking mode for DeepSeek V4 models, so the
provider omits them with an unsupported warning. Explicitly set
thinking.type to 'disabled' to use temperature and topP.

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
DeepSeek supports optional participant names on system, user, and assistant
messages. Set providerOptions.deepseek.name on each message that should
include a name:

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content: The same message option works with streamText:

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
Names are omitted when the option is not set. The name value must be a
string. DeepSeek does not support names on tool messages, so the provider
ignores that placement and returns an unsupported-feature warning. Avoid
including unnecessary personal or identifying information in message names.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: DeepSeek has reasoning support for the deepseek-v4-pro model. The reasoning is exposed through streaming:

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details
on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: chat-prefix-completion
contents.content:
DeepSeek's beta chat prefix completion
continues the content of a final assistant message. Create a provider with a
beta base URL and set prefix: true in that assistant message's provider
options:

contents.heading: chat-prefix-completion
contents.content:
The prefixed message must be an assistant message and the final message in the
prompt. The configured baseURL must end in /beta, including when using a
proxy. Invalid placement or a non-beta base URL causes the request to fail
before it is sent.

contents.heading: chat-prefix-completion
contents.content: Chat prefix completion is a DeepSeek beta feature and its behavior may change.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
DeepSeek exposes the response system fingerprint and context cache usage through
the providerMetadata property:

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: The metadata includes:

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: systemFingerprint: The backend configuration fingerprint for the response

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: promptCacheHitTokens: Number of input tokens that were cached

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content: promptCacheMissTokens: Number of input tokens that were not cached

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
For streamed responses, the latest non-null fingerprint from the response
chunks is returned.

contents.heading: provider-metadata
contents.content:
For more details about DeepSeek's caching system, see the DeepSeek caching
documentation.

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
DeepSeek preserves provider-specific response fields in
providerMetadata.deepseek for generated and streamed responses:

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: responseObject: chat.completion or chat.completion.chunk

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: choiceIndex: the selected response choice index

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: messageRole: the response message role, when supplied

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: toolCallTypes: the tool-call type for each returned call

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
These fields remain in provider metadata because they are specific to
DeepSeek's Chat Completions response rather than shared AI SDK result fields.

contents.heading: vision-file-parts
contents.content:
For inline images or image URLs, use file-part provider options to select the
image processing detail. DeepSeek supports low, high, original, and
auto:

contents.heading: vision-file-parts
contents.content:
Set fileData: true on an inline image file part to use DeepSeek's
file_data content-part representation. This preserves the file part's
filename. fileData cannot be used with image URLs or imageDetail.

contents.heading: vision-file-parts
contents.content:
DeepSeek accepts JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP image inputs. HTTP image URLs can be
at most 8,192 characters.

metadata.title: ElevenLabs
metadata.description: Learn how to use the ElevenLabs provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content: The ElevenLabs provider contains language model support for the ElevenLabs transcription and speech generation APIs.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The ElevenLabs provider is available in the @ai-sdk/elevenlabs module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance elevenlabs from @ai-sdk/elevenlabs:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createElevenLabs from @ai-sdk/elevenlabs and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the ElevenLabs provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the ELEVENLABS_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the ElevenLabs speech API
using the .speech() factory method.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. eleven_multilingual_v2.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying a voice to use for the generated audio.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: language_code string or nullOptional. Language code (ISO 639-1) used to enforce a language for the model. Currently, only Turbo v2.5 and Flash v2.5 support language enforcement. For other models, providing a language code will result in an error.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: voice_settings object or nullOptional. Voice settings that override stored settings for the given voice. These are applied only to the current request.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: stability double or nullOptional. Determines how stable the voice is and the randomness between each generation. Lower values introduce broader emotional range; higher values result in a more monotonous voice.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: use_speaker_boost boolean or nullOptional. Boosts similarity to the original speaker. Increases computational load and latency.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: similarity_boost double or nullOptional. Controls how closely the AI should adhere to the original voice.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: style double or nullOptional. Amplifies the style of the original speaker. May increase latency if set above 0.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: pronunciation_dictionary_locators array of objects or nullOptional. A list of pronunciation dictionary locators to apply to the text, in order. Up to 3 locators per request.Each locator object:

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: pronunciation_dictionary_id string (required)The ID of the pronunciation dictionary.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: version_id string or null (optional)The version ID of the dictionary. If not provided, the latest version is used.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: seed integer or nullOptional. If specified, the system will attempt to sample deterministically. Must be between 0 and 4294967295. Determinism is not guaranteed.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: previous_text string or nullOptional. The text that came before the current request's text. Can improve continuity when concatenating generations or influence current generation continuity.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: next_text string or nullOptional. The text that comes after the current request's text. Can improve continuity when concatenating generations or influence current generation continuity.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: previous_request_ids array of strings or nullOptional. List of request IDs for samples generated before this one. Improves continuity when splitting large tasks. Max 3 IDs. If both previous_text and previous_request_ids are sent, previous_text is ignored.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: next_request_ids array of strings or nullOptional. List of request IDs for samples generated after this one. Useful for maintaining continuity when regenerating a sample. Max 3 IDs. If both next_text and next_request_ids are sent, next_text is ignored.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: apply_text_normalization enumOptional. Controls text normalization.Allowed values: 'auto' (default), 'on', 'off'.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: 'auto': System decides whether to apply normalization (e.g., spelling out numbers).

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: 'on': Always apply normalization.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: 'off': Never apply normalization.For eleven_turbo_v2_5 and eleven_flash_v2_5, can only be enabled with Enterprise plans.

contents.heading: speech-models
contents.content: apply_language_text_normalization booleanOptional. Defaults to false. Controls language text normalization, which helps with proper pronunciation in some supported languages (currently only Japanese). May significantly increase latency.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the ElevenLabs transcription API
using the .transcription() factory method.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. scribe_v1.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 (e.g. en) format can sometimes improve transcription performance if known beforehand.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: languageCode string

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
An ISO-639-1 or ISO-639-3 language code corresponding to the language of the audio file.
Can sometimes improve transcription performance if known beforehand.
Defaults to null, in which case the language is predicted automatically.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: tagAudioEvents boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to tag audio events like (laughter), (footsteps), etc. in the transcription.
Defaults to true.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: numSpeakers integer

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The maximum amount of speakers talking in the uploaded file.
Can help with predicting who speaks when.
The maximum amount of speakers that can be predicted is 32.
Defaults to null, in which case the amount of speakers is set to the maximum value the model supports.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: timestampsGranularity enum

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The granularity of the timestamps in the transcription.
Defaults to 'word'.
Allowed values: 'none', 'word', 'character'.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: diarize boolean

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
Whether to annotate which speaker is currently talking in the uploaded file.
Defaults to true.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: fileFormat enum

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
The format of input audio.
Defaults to 'other'.
Allowed values: 'pcm_s16le_16', 'other'.
For 'pcm_s16le_16', the input audio must be 16-bit PCM at a 16kHz sample rate, single channel (mono), and little-endian byte order.
Latency will be lower than with passing an encoded waveform.

metadata.title: Fal
metadata.description: Learn how to use Fal AI models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: Fal AI provides a generative media platform for developers with lightning-fast inference capabilities. Their platform offers optimized performance for running diffusion models, with speeds up to 4x faster than alternatives.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Fal provider is available via the @ai-sdk/fal module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance

contents.heading: provider-instance

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Fal provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://fal.run.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the FAL_API_KEY environment variable, falling back to FAL_KEY.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Fal image models support flexible provider options through the providerOptions.fal object. You can pass any parameters supported by the specific Fal model's API. Common options include:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: imageUrl - Reference image URL for image-to-image generation

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: strength - Controls how much the output differs from the input image

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: guidanceScale - Controls adherence to the prompt (range: 1-20)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: numInferenceSteps - Number of denoising steps (range: 1-50)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: enableSafetyChecker - Enable/disable safety filtering

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: outputFormat - Output format: 'jpeg' or 'png'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: syncMode - Wait for completion before returning response

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: acceleration - Speed of generation: 'none', 'regular', or 'high'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: safetyTolerance - Content safety filtering level (1-6, where 1 is strictest)

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Deprecation Notice: snake_case parameter names (e.g., image_url,
guidance_scale) are deprecated and will be removed in @ai-sdk/fal v2.0.

Optional.

chunkLevel string
Level of the chunks to return. Either 'segment' or 'word'.

Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models

Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:

Batch size for processing.

Optional.

contents.heading: error-diagnostics
contents.content: GMI Cloud's edge reports a generic banner in error.message on rejections and nests the backend engine's diagnostic in error.details. This provider unwraps the nested diagnostic, so AI_APICallError.message carries the engine's reason (e.g. The request is invalid: Invalid max_tokens value, the valid range of max_tokens is [1, 393216].) instead of Backend request failed with status 400.

metadata.title: Google Generative AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use Google Generative AI Provider.

title.children: Combine URL Context with Search Grounding

contents.content:
The Google Generative AI provider contains language and embedding model support for
the Google Generative AI APIs.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Google provider is available in the @ai-sdk/google module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance google from @ai-sdk/google:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createGoogleGenerativeAI from @ai-sdk/google and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Google Generative AI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the x-goog-api-key header.
It defaults to the GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Google Generative AI API using the provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. gemini-2.5-flash.
The models support tool calls and some have multi-modal capabilities.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can use Google Generative AI language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Google Generative AI language models can also be used in the streamText, generateObject, and streamObject functions
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
To remain forward-compatible, the provider treats unrecognized gemini-*
model IDs and -latest aliases like the newest supported Gemini generation.
Currently, this means Gemini 3 request behavior for provider-defined and mixed
tools, thinkingLevel reasoning, multimodal function responses, and thought
signatures. Known legacy Gemini model IDs keep their generation-specific
request behavior. This SDK default controls request serialization; the
selected model must still support each feature in the Google API.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Google Generative AI also supports some model specific settings that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Google Generative AI models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: cachedContent string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. The name of the cached content used as context to serve the prediction.
Format: cachedContents/{cachedContent}

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Enable structured output. Default is true.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
This is useful when the JSON Schema contains elements that are
not supported by the OpenAPI schema version that
Google Generative AI uses. You can use this to disable
structured outputs if you need to.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: See Troubleshooting: Schema Limitations for more details.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: safetySettings Array<{ category: string; threshold: string }>

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Safety settings for the model.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: category string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The category of the safety setting. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: threshold string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The threshold of the safety setting. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: HARM_BLOCK_THRESHOLD_UNSPECIFIED

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: BLOCK_NONE

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
responseModalities string[]
The modalities to use for the response. The following modalities are supported: TEXT, IMAGE. When not defined or empty, the model defaults to returning only text.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinkingConfig { thinkingLevel?: 'low' | 'high'; thinkingBudget?: number; includeThoughts?: boolean }

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Configuration for the model's thinking process. Only supported by specific Google Generative AI models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinkingLevel 'low' | 'high'

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Controls the thinking depth for Gemini 3 and later models. Use 'low' for faster responses or 'high' for deeper reasoning. Gemini 3.1 Pro supports 'low', 'medium', and 'high', Gemini 3 Pro supports 'low' and 'high', while Gemini 3 Flash supports all four levels: 'minimal', 'low', 'medium', and 'high'.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: thinkingBudget number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Gives the model guidance on the number of thinking tokens it can use when generating a response. Setting it to 0 disables thinking, if the model supports it.
For more information about the possible value ranges for each model see Google Generative AI thinking documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
This option is for Gemini 2.5 models. Gemini 3 and later models should use
thinkingLevel instead.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: includeThoughts boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. If set to true, thought summaries are returned, which are synthisized versions of the model's raw thoughts and offer insights into the model's internal reasoning process.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: imageConfig { aspectRatio: string }

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. Configuration for the models image generation. Only supported by specific Google Generative AI models.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: aspectRatio string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Model defaults to generate 1:1 squares, or to matching the output image size to that of your input image. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: imageSize string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Controls the output image resolution. Defaults to 1K. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: 1K

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: 2K

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: 4K

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: audioTimestamp boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Enables timestamp understanding for audio-only files.
See Google Cloud audio understanding documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: mediaResolution string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Optional. If specified, the media resolution specified will be used. Can be one of the following:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: MEDIA_RESOLUTION_UNSPECIFIED

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: MEDIA_RESOLUTION_LOW

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: MEDIA_RESOLUTION_MEDIUM

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: MEDIA_RESOLUTION_HIGH

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: See Google API MediaResolution documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: labels Record<string, string>

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Defines labels used in billing reports. Available on Vertex AI only.
See Google Cloud labels documentation.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: serviceTier 'standard' | 'flex' | 'priority'

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. The service tier to use for the request.
Set to 'flex' for 50% cheaper processing at the cost of increased latency.
Set to 'priority' for ultra-low latency at a 75-100% price premium over 'standard'.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: threshold string

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Optional. Standalone threshold setting that can be used independently of safetySettings.
Uses the same values as the safetySettings threshold.

contents.heading: thinking
contents.content: The Gemini 2.5 and Gemini 3-and-later series models use an internal "thinking process" that significantly improves their reasoning and multi-step planning abilities, making them highly effective for complex tasks such as coding, advanced mathematics, and data analysis. For more information see Google Generative AI thinking documentation.

contents.heading: gemini-3-and-later-models
contents.content: For Gemini 3 and later models, use the thinkingLevel parameter to control the depth of reasoning:

contents.heading: gemini-25-models
contents.content: For Gemini 2.5 models, use the thinkingBudget parameter to control the number of thinking tokens:

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: The Google Generative AI provider supports file inputs, e.g. PDF files.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: You can also use YouTube URLs directly:

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content:
The AI SDK will automatically download URLs if you pass them as data, except
for https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/files/ and YouTube
URLs. You can use the Google Generative AI Files API to upload larger files to
that location. YouTube URLs (public or unlisted videos) are supported directly

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: you can specify one YouTube video URL per request.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: See File Parts for details on how to use files in prompts.

contents.heading: cached-content
contents.content: Google Generative AI supports both explicit and implicit caching to help reduce costs on repetitive content.

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Gemini 2.5 models automatically provide cache cost savings without needing to create an explicit cache. When you send requests that share common prefixes with previous requests, you'll receive a 75% token discount on cached content.

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: To maximize cache hits with implicit caching:

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Keep content at the beginning of requests consistent

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Add variable content (like user questions) at the end of prompts

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Ensure requests meet minimum token requirements:

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Gemini 2.5 Flash: 1024 tokens minimum

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content: Gemini 2.5 Pro: 2048 tokens minimum

contents.heading: implicit-caching
contents.content:
Usage metadata was added to providerMetadata in @ai-sdk/google@1.2.23. If
you are using an older version, usage metadata is available in the raw HTTP
response body returned as part of the return value from generateText.

contents.heading: explicit-caching
contents.content: For guaranteed cost savings, you can still use explicit caching with Gemini 2.5 and 2.0 models. See the models page to check if caching is supported for the used model:

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: With Code Execution, certain models can generate and execute Python code to perform calculations, solve problems, or provide more accurate information.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: You can enable code execution by adding the code_execution tool to your request.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: The response will contain the tool calls and results from the code execution.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content:
With Google Search grounding,
the model has access to the latest information using Google Search.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: The googleSearch tool accepts the following optional configuration options:

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: searchTypes object

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Enables specific search types. Both can be combined.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: webSearch: Enable web search grounding (pass {} to enable). This is the default.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: imageSearch: Enable image search grounding (pass {} to enable).

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: timeRangeFilter object

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Restricts search results to a specific time range. Both startTime and endTime are required.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: startTime: Start time in ISO 8601 format (e.g. '2025-01-01T00:00:00Z').

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: endTime: End time in ISO 8601 format (e.g. '2025-12-31T23:59:59Z').

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: When Google Search grounding is enabled, the model will include sources in the response.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Additionally, the grounding metadata includes detailed information about how search results were used to ground the model's response. Here are the available fields:

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: webSearchQueries (string[] | null)

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Array of search queries used to retrieve information

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Example: ["What's the weather in Chicago this weekend?"]

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: searchEntryPoint ({ renderedContent: string } | null)

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Contains the main search result content used as an entry point

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: The renderedContent field contains the formatted content

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: groundingSupports (Array of support objects | null)

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Contains details about how specific response parts are supported by search results

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Each support object includes:

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: segment: Information about the grounded text segment

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: text: The actual text segment

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: startIndex: Starting position in the response

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: endIndex: Ending position in the response

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: groundingChunkIndices: References to supporting search result chunks

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: confidenceScores: Confidence scores (0-1) for each supporting chunk

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Example response:

contents.heading: file-search
contents.content: The File Search tool lets Gemini retrieve context from your own documents that you have indexed in File Search stores. The provider enables this tool for Gemini 2.5 and Gemini 3-and-later model IDs, including unrecognized future Gemini IDs.

contents.heading: file-search
contents.content: File Search responses include citations via the normal sources field and expose raw grounding metadata in providerMetadata.google.groundingMetadata.

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: Google provides a provider-defined URL context tool.

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: The URL context tool allows you to provide specific URLs that you want the model to analyze directly in from the prompt.

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: The URL context metadata includes detailed information about how the model used the URL context to generate the response. Here are the available fields:

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: urlMetadata ({ retrievedUrl: string; urlRetrievalStatus: string; }[] | null)

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: Array of URL context metadata

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: Each object includes:

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: retrievedUrl: The URL of the context

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: urlRetrievalStatus: The status of the URL retrieval

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: Example response:

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: With the URL context tool, you will also get the groundingMetadata.

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content:
The URL context tool is only supported for Gemini 2.0 Flash models and above.
Check the supported models for URL context
tool.

contents.heading: combine-url-context-with-search-grounding
contents.content: You can combine the URL context tool with search grounding to provide the model with the latest information from the web.

contents.heading: google-maps-grounding
contents.content:
With Google Maps grounding,
the model has access to Google Maps data for location-aware responses. This enables providing local data and geospatial context, such as finding nearby restaurants.

contents.heading: google-maps-grounding
contents.content: The optional retrievalConfig.latLng provider option provides location context for queries about nearby places. This configuration applies to any grounding tools that support location context, including Google Maps and Google Search.

contents.heading: google-maps-grounding
contents.content: When Google Maps grounding is enabled, the model's response will include sources pointing to Google Maps URLs. The grounding metadata includes maps chunks with place information:

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content:
With RAG Engine Grounding,
the model has access to your custom knowledge base using the Vertex RAG Engine.
This enables the model to provide answers based on your specific data sources and documents.

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content:
RAG Engine Grounding is only supported with Vertex Gemini models. You must use
the Google Vertex provider (@ai-sdk/google-vertex) instead of the standard
Google provider (@ai-sdk/google) to use this feature.

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: When RAG Engine Grounding is enabled, the model will include sources from your RAG corpus in the response.

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: Additionally, the grounding metadata includes detailed information about how RAG results were used to ground the model's response. Here are the available fields:

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: groundingChunks (Array of chunk objects | null)

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: Contains the retrieved context chunks from your RAG corpus

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: Each chunk includes:

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: retrievedContext: Information about the retrieved context

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: uri: The URI or identifier of the source document

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: title: The title of the source document (optional)

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: text: The actual text content of the chunk

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: groundingSupports (Array of support objects | null)

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: Contains details about how specific response parts are supported by RAG results

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: Each support object includes:

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: segment: Information about the grounded text segment

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: text: The actual text segment

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: startIndex: Starting position in the response

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: endIndex: Ending position in the response

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: groundingChunkIndices: References to supporting RAG result chunks

contents.heading: rag-engine-grounding
contents.content: confidenceScores: Confidence scores (0-1) for each supporting chunk

contents.heading: schema-limitations
contents.content:
The Google Generative AI API uses a subset of the OpenAPI 3.0 schema,
which does not support features such as unions.
The errors that you get in this case look like this:

By default, structured outputs are enabled (and for tool calling they are required).
You can disable structured outputs for object generation as a workaround:

contents.heading: gemma-models
contents.content: You can use Gemma models with the Google Generative AI API.

contents.heading: gemma-models
contents.content: Gemma models don't natively support the systemInstruction parameter, but the provider automatically handles system instructions by prepending them to the first user message. This allows you to use system instructions with Gemma models seamlessly:

contents.heading: gemma-models
contents.content: The system instruction is automatically formatted and included in the conversation, so Gemma models can follow the guidance without any additional configuration.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Google Generative AI embeddings API
using the .textEmbedding() factory method.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: The Google Generative AI provider sends API calls to the right endpoint based on the type of embedding:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Single embeddings: When embedding a single value with embed(), the provider uses the single :embedContent endpoint, which typically has higher rate limits compared to the batch endpoint.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Batch embeddings: When embedding multiple values with embedMany() or multiple values in embed(), the provider uses the :batchEmbedContents endpoint.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Google Generative AI embedding models support additional settings, including multimodal embeddings. You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: When using embedMany, provide per-value multimodal content via the content option. Each entry corresponds to a value at the same index; use null for text-only entries:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Google Generative AI embedding models:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: outputDimensionality: number

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Optional reduced dimension for the output embedding. If set, excessive values in the output embedding are truncated from the end.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: taskType: string

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Optional. Specifies the task type for generating embeddings. Supported task types include:

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY: Optimized for text similarity.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: CLASSIFICATION: Optimized for text classification.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: CLUSTERING: Optimized for clustering texts based on similarity.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT: Optimized for document retrieval.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: RETRIEVAL_QUERY: Optimized for query-based retrieval.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: QUESTION_ANSWERING: Optimized for answering questions.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: FACT_VERIFICATION: Optimized for verifying factual information.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY: Optimized for retrieving code blocks based on natural language queries.

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: content: array

contents.heading: embedding-models
contents.content: Optional. Per-value multimodal content parts for embedding non-text content (images, video, PDF, audio). Each entry corresponds to the embedding value at the same index — its parts are merged with the text value in the request. Use null for entries that are text-only. The array length must match the number of values being embedded. Each non-null entry is an array of parts, where each part can be either { text: string } or { inlineData: { mimeType: string, data: string } }. Supported by gemini-embedding-2-preview.

metadata.title: Google Vertex AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use the Google Vertex AI provider.

contents.content: The Google Vertex provider for the AI SDK contains language model support for the Google Vertex AI APIs. This includes support for Google's Gemini models, Anthropic's Claude partner models, xAI's Grok partner models, and MaaS (Model as a Service) open models.

The Google Vertex provider is compatible with both Node.js and Edge runtimes.
The Edge runtime is supported through the @ai-sdk/google-vertex/edge
sub-module. More details can be found in the Google Vertex Edge
Runtime, Google Vertex Anthropic Edge
Runtime, and Google Vertex MaaS Edge
Runtime sections below.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Google Vertex, Google Vertex Anthropic, Google Vertex xAI, and Google Vertex MaaS providers are available in the @ai-sdk/google-vertex module. You can install it with

contents.heading: google-vertex-provider-usage
contents.content: The Google Vertex provider instance is used to create model instances that call the Vertex AI API. The models available with this provider include Google's Gemini models. If you're looking to use Anthropic's Claude models, see the Google Vertex Anthropic Provider section below.

contents.heading: google-vertex-provider-usage
contents.content:
Vertex Gemini models share the Google provider's forward-compatible model
classification. Unrecognized gemini-* IDs and -latest aliases use the
newest supported Gemini request behavior, while known legacy IDs keep their
generation-specific tool, reasoning, function-response, and thought-signature
handling. The selected Vertex model must still support each requested feature.

contents.heading: nodejs-runtime
contents.content: The Node.js runtime is the default runtime supported by the AI SDK. It supports all standard Google Cloud authentication options through the google-auth-library. Typical use involves setting a path to a json credentials file in the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable. The credentials file can be obtained from the Google Cloud Console.

contents.heading: edge-runtime
contents.content:
Edge runtimes (like Vercel Edge Functions and Cloudflare Workers) are lightweight JavaScript environments that run closer to users at the network edge.
They only provide a subset of the standard Node.js APIs.
For example, direct file system access is not available, and many Node.js-specific libraries
(including the standard Google Auth library) are not compatible.
