contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: With Code Execution, certain Gemini models on Vertex AI can generate and execute Python code. This allows the model to perform calculations, data manipulation, and other programmatic tasks to enhance its responses.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: You can enable code execution by adding the code_execution tool to your request.

contents.heading: code-execution
contents.content: The response will contain tool-call and tool-result parts for the executed code.

contents.heading: url-context
contents.content: URL Context allows Gemini models to retrieve and analyze content from URLs. Supported models: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, 2.5 Pro, 2.5 Flash, 2.0 Flash.

contents.heading: google-search
contents.content: Google Search enables Gemini models to access real-time web information. Supported models: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, 2.5 Flash, 2.0 Flash, 2.5 Pro.

contents.heading: enterprise-web-search
contents.content: Enterprise Web Search provides grounding using a compliance-focused web index designed for highly-regulated industries such as finance, healthcare, and the public sector. Unlike standard Google Search grounding, Enterprise Web Search does not log customer data and supports VPC service controls. Supported models: Gemini 2.0 and newer.

contents.heading: google-maps
contents.content: Google Maps grounding enables Gemini models to access Google Maps data for location-aware responses. Supported models: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, 2.5 Flash, 2.0 Flash, 2.5 Pro, 3.0 Pro.

contents.heading: google-maps
contents.content: The optional retrievalConfig.latLng provider option provides location context for queries about nearby places. This configuration applies to any grounding tools that support location context.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: Google Vertex AI, through its support for Gemini models, can also emit "thinking" tokens, representing the model's reasoning process. The AI SDK exposes these as reasoning information.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: To enable thinking tokens for compatible Gemini models via Vertex, set includeThoughts: true in the thinkingConfig provider option. Since the Vertex provider uses the Google provider's underlying language model, these options are passed through providerOptions.google:

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: When includeThoughts is true, parts of the API response marked with thought: true will be processed as reasoning.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: In generateText, these contribute to the reasoningText (string) and reasoning (array) fields.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content: In streamText, these are emitted as reasoning stream parts.

contents.heading: reasoning-thinking-tokens
contents.content:
Refer to the Google Vertex AI documentation on
"thinking"
for model compatibility and further details.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: The Google Vertex provider supports file inputs, e.g. PDF files.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content:
The AI SDK will automatically download URLs if you pass them as data, except
for gs:// URLs. You can use the Google Cloud Storage API to upload larger
files to that location.

contents.heading: file-inputs
contents.content: See File Parts for details on how to use files in prompts.

See Google Vertex AI documentation on configuring safety filters.

The Google Vertex API uses a subset of the OpenAPI 3.0 schema,
which does not support features such as unions.
The errors that you get in this case look like this:

You can disable structured outputs for object generation as a workaround:

contents.heading: edge-runtime-1
contents.content:
Edge runtimes (like Vercel Edge Functions and Cloudflare Workers) are lightweight JavaScript environments that run closer to users at the network edge.
They only provide a subset of the standard Node.js APIs.
For example, direct file system access is not available, and many Node.js-specific libraries
(including the standard Google Auth library) are not compatible.

Some models have multi-modal capabilities.

contents.heading: language-models-1
contents.content: You can use Anthropic language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: language-models-1
contents.content:
Anthropic language models can also be used in the streamText, generateObject, and streamObject functions
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models-1
contents.content:
The Anthropic API returns streaming tool calls all at once after a delay. This
causes the streamObject function to generate the object fully after a delay
instead of streaming it incrementally.

contents.content: Optional. Include reasoning content in requests sent to the model. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: language-models-1

If you are experiencing issues with the model handling requests involving
reasoning content, you can set this to false to omit them from the request.

contents.heading: reasoning

See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content:
Anthropic cache control is in a Pre-Generally Available (GA) state on Google
Vertex. For more see Google Vertex Anthropic cache control
documentation.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content:
In the messages and message parts, you can use the providerOptions property to set cache control breakpoints.
You need to set the anthropic property in the providerOptions object to { cacheControl: { type: 'ephemeral' } } to set a cache control breakpoint.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content:
The cache creation input tokens are then returned in the providerMetadata object
for generateText and generateObject, again under the anthropic property.
When you use streamText or streamObject, the response contains a promise
that resolves to the metadata. Alternatively you can receive it in the
onFinish callback.

contents.heading: cache-control
contents.content: You can also use cache control on system messages by providing multiple system messages at the head of your messages array:

contents.heading: cache-control

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Anthropic provides three built-in tools that can be used to interact with external systems:

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Bash Tool: Allows running bash commands.

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Text Editor Tool: Provides functionality for viewing and editing text files.

contents.heading: computer-use
contents.content: Computer Tool: Enables control of keyboard and mouse actions on a computer.

contents.heading: computer-use

contents.heading: computer-use

contents.heading: bash-tool
contents.content: The Bash Tool allows running bash commands. Here's how to create and use it:

contents.heading: bash-tool

contents.heading: bash-tool

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: The Text Editor Tool provides functionality for viewing and editing text files:

contents.heading: text-editor-tool

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: path (string): Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. /repo/file.py or /repo.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: file_text (string, optional): Required for create command, with the content of the file to be created.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: insert_line (number, optional): Required for insert command. The line number after which to insert the new string.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: old_str (string, optional): Required for str_replace command, containing the string to replace.

contents.heading: text-editor-tool
contents.content: view_range (number[], optional): Optional for view command to specify line range to show.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: The Computer Tool enables control of keyboard and mouse actions on a computer:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: Parameters:

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: action ('key' | 'type' | 'mouse_move' | 'left_click' | 'left_click_drag' | 'right_click' | 'middle_click' | 'double_click' | 'screenshot' | 'cursor_position'): The action to perform.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: coordinate (number[], optional): Required for mouse_move and left_click_drag actions. Specifies the (x, y) coordinates.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: text (string, optional): Required for type and key actions.

contents.heading: computer-tool
contents.content: These tools can be used in conjunction with the claude-3-5-sonnet-v2@20241022 model to enable more complex interactions and tasks.

contents.content: The Groq provider contains language model support for the Groq API.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content:
The Groq provider is available via the @ai-sdk/groq module.
You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance groq from @ai-sdk/groq:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
If you need a customized setup, you can import createGroq from @ai-sdk/groq
and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Groq provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://api.groq.com/openai/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the GROQ_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create Groq models using a provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. gemma2-9b-it.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Groq offers several reasoning models such as qwen-qwq-32b and deepseek-r1-distill-llama-70b.
You can configure how the reasoning is exposed in the generated text by using the reasoningFormat option.
It supports the options parsed, hidden, and raw.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Groq language models:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: reasoningFormat 'parsed' | 'raw' | 'hidden'

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Controls how reasoning is exposed in the generated text. Only supported by reasoning models like qwen-qwq-32b and deepseek-r1-distill-* models.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: For a complete list of reasoning models and their capabilities, see Groq's reasoning models documentation.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'low' | 'meduim' | 'high' | 'none' | 'default'

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Controls the level of effort the model will put into reasoning.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: qwen/qwen3-32b

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Supported values:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: none: Disable reasoning. The model will not use any reasoning tokens.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: default: Enable reasoning.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: gpt-oss20b/gpt-oss120b

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Supported values:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: low: Use a low level of reasoning effort.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: medium: Use a medium level of reasoning effort.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: high: Use a high level of reasoning effort.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Defaults to default for qwen/qwen3-32b.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Whether to use structured outputs.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Defaults to true.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: When enabled, object generation will use the json_schema format instead of json_object format, providing more reliable structured outputs.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help with monitoring and abuse detection.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: serviceTier 'on_demand' | 'flex' | 'auto'

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Service tier for the request. Defaults to 'on_demand'.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: 'on_demand': Default tier with consistent performance and fairness

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: 'flex': Higher throughput tier (10x rate limits) optimized for workloads that can handle occasional request failures

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: 'auto': Uses on_demand rate limits first, then falls back to flex tier if exceeded

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: For more details about service tiers and their benefits, see Groq's Flex Processing documentation.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Structured outputs are enabled by default for Groq models.
You can disable them by setting the structuredOutputs option to false.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: You can disable structured outputs for models that don't support them:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Structured outputs are only supported by newer Groq models like
moonshotai/kimi-k2-instruct-0905. For unsupported models, you can disable
structured outputs by setting structuredOutputs: false. When disabled, Groq
uses the json_object format which requires the word "JSON" to be included in
your messages.

contents.heading: browser-search-tool
contents.content: Groq provides a browser search tool that offers interactive web browsing capabilities. Unlike traditional web search, browser search navigates websites interactively, providing more detailed and comprehensive results.

contents.heading: supported-models
contents.content: Browser search is only available for these specific models:

contents.heading: supported-models
contents.content: openai/gpt-oss-20b

contents.heading: supported-models
contents.content: openai/gpt-oss-120b

contents.heading: supported-models
contents.content:
Browser search will only work with the supported models listed above. Using it
with other models will generate a warning and the tool will be ignored.

contents.heading: key-features
contents.content: Interactive Browsing: Navigates websites like a human user

contents.heading: key-features
contents.content: Comprehensive Results: More detailed than traditional search snippets

contents.heading: key-features
contents.content: Server-side Execution: Runs on Groq's infrastructure, no setup required

contents.heading: key-features
contents.content: Powered by Exa: Uses Exa search engine for optimal results

contents.heading: key-features
contents.content: Currently Free: Available at no additional charge during beta

contents.heading: best-practices
contents.content: Use toolChoice: 'required' to ensure the browser search is activated

contents.heading: best-practices
contents.content: Only supported on openai/gpt-oss-20b and openai/gpt-oss-120b models

contents.heading: best-practices
contents.content: The tool works automatically - no configuration parameters needed

contents.heading: best-practices
contents.content: Server-side execution means no additional API keys or setup required

contents.heading: model-validation
contents.content: The provider automatically validates model compatibility:

contents.heading: model-validation
contents.content:
For more details about browser search capabilities and limitations, see the
Groq Browser Search
Documentation.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Groq transcription API
using the .transcription() factory method.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The first argument is the model id e.g. whisper-large-v3.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: You can also pass additional provider-specific options using the providerOptions argument. For example, supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 (e.g. en) format will improve accuracy and latency.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
timestampGranularities string[]
The granularity of the timestamps in the transcription.
Defaults to ['segment'].
Possible values are ['word'], ['segment'], and ['word', 'segment'].
Note: There is no additional latency for segment timestamps, but generating word timestamps incurs additional latency.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
language string
The language of the input audio. Supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 format (e.g. 'en') will improve accuracy and latency.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
prompt string
An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment. The prompt should match the audio language.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
temperature number
The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use log probability to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.
Defaults to 0.
Optional.

metadata.title: Luma
metadata.description: Learn how to use Luma AI models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: Luma AI provides state-of-the-art image generation models through their Dream Machine platform. Their models offer ultra-high quality image generation with superior prompt understanding and unique capabilities like character consistency and multi-image reference support.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Luma provider is available via the @ai-sdk/luma module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance luma from @ai-sdk/luma:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createLuma and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Luma provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
The default prefix is https://api.lumalabs.ai.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the LUMA_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: image-models
contents.content:
You can create Luma image models using the .image() factory method.
For more on image generation with the AI SDK see generateImage().

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: You can customize the generation behavior with optional settings:

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: Since Luma processes images through an asynchronous queue system, these settings allow you to tune the polling behavior:

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: maxImagesPerCall number

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: Override the maximum number of images generated per API call. Defaults to 1.

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: pollIntervalMillis number

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content:
Control how frequently the API is checked for completed images while they are
being processed. Defaults to 500ms.

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content: maxPollAttempts number

contents.heading: image-model-settings
contents.content:
Limit how long to wait for results before timing out, since image generation
is queued asynchronously. Defaults to 120 attempts.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Luma offers two main models:

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Model

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Description

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: photon-1

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: High-quality image generation with superior prompt understanding

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: photon-flash-1

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Faster generation optimized for speed while maintaining quality

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Both models support the following aspect ratios:

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: 16:9 (default)

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: For more details about supported aspect ratios, see the Luma Image Generation documentation.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Key features of Luma models include:

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Ultra-high quality image generation

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: 10x higher cost efficiency compared to similar models

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Superior prompt understanding and adherence

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Unique character consistency capabilities from single reference images

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content: Multi-image reference support for precise style matching

contents.heading: advanced-options
contents.content: Luma models support several advanced features through the providerOptions.luma parameter.

contents.heading: image-reference
contents.content: Use up to 4 reference images to guide your generation. Useful for creating variations or visualizing complex concepts. Adjust the weight (0-1) to control the influence of reference images.

contents.heading: style-reference
contents.content: Apply specific visual styles to your generations using reference images. Control the style influence using the weight parameter.

contents.heading: character-reference
contents.content: Create consistent and personalized characters using up to 4 reference images of the same subject. More reference images improve character representation.

contents.heading: modify-image
contents.content: Transform existing images using text prompts. Use the weight parameter to control how closely the result matches the input image (higher weight = closer to input but less creative).

contents.heading: modify-image
contents.content: For color changes, it's recommended to use a lower weight value (0.0-0.1).

contents.heading: modify-image
contents.content: For more details about Luma's capabilities and features, visit the Luma Image Generation documentation.

metadata.title: Mistral AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use Mistral.

contents.content:
The Mistral AI provider contains language model,
embedding model, and speech model support for Mistral APIs.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Mistral provider is available in the @ai-sdk/mistral module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
If you need a customized setup, you can import createMistral from @ai-sdk/mistral
and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the Mistral chat API using a provider instance.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. mistral-large-latest.
Some Mistral chat models support tool calls.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Mistral chat models also support additional model settings that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them as an options argument and utilize MistralLanguageModelOptions for typing:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Mistral models:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: safePrompt boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to inject a safety prompt before all conversations.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to false.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: documentImageLimit number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Maximum number of images to process in a document.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: documentPageLimit number

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Maximum number of pages to process in a document.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: strictJsonSchema boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to use strict JSON schema validation for structured outputs. Only applies when a schema is provided and only sets the strict flag in addition to using Custom Structured Outputs, which is used by default if a schema is provided.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to false.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to use structured outputs. When enabled, tool calls and object generation will be strict and follow the provided schema.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to true.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use. When set to false, the model will use at most one tool per response.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: Defaults to true.

contents.heading: document-ocr
contents.content:
Mistral chat models support document OCR for PDF files.
You can optionally set image and page limits using the provider options.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: Mistral offers reasoning models that provide step-by-step thinking capabilities:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: magistral-small-2506: Smaller reasoning model for efficient step-by-step thinking

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: magistral-medium-2506: More powerful reasoning model balancing performance and cost

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: These models return content that includes <think>...</think> tags containing the reasoning process. To properly extract and separate the reasoning from the final answer, use the extract reasoning middleware:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: The middleware automatically parses the <think> tags and provides separate reasoningText and text properties in the result.

contents.heading: example
contents.content: You can use Mistral language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: example
contents.content:
Mistral language models can also be used in the streamText, generateObject, and streamObject functions
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Mistral chat models support structured outputs using JSON Schema. You can use generateObject or streamObject
with Zod, Valibot, or raw JSON Schema. The SDK sends your schema via Mistral's response_format: { type: 'json_schema' }.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: You can enable strict JSON Schema validation using a provider option:

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
When using structured outputs, the SDK no longer injects an extra "answer with
JSON" instruction. It relies on Mistral's native json_schema/json_object
response formats instead. You can customize the schema name/description via
the standard structured-output APIs.

metadata.title: Moonshot AI
metadata.description: Learn how to use Moonshot AI models with the AI SDK.

contents.content: The Moonshot AI provider offers access to powerful language models through the Moonshot API, including the Kimi series of models with reasoning capabilities.
API keys can be obtained from the Kimi API Platform.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The Moonshot AI provider is available via the @ai-sdk/moonshotai module. You can install it with:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance moonshotai from @ai-sdk/moonshotai:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: For custom configuration, you can import createMoonshotAI and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the Moonshot AI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls.
The default prefix is https://api.moonshot.ai/v1

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header. It defaults to
the MOONSHOT_API_KEY environment variable

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom fetch implementation

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can create language models using a provider instance:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: You can also use the .chatModel() or .languageModel() factory methods:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Moonshot AI language models can be used in the streamText function
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Moonshot V1 models support the standard temperature, topP,
presencePenalty, and frequencyPenalty settings. Kimi models use fixed
sampling parameters; the provider omits those settings for Kimi requests and
returns an unsupported-setting warning when they are supplied.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Kimi K3 supports toolChoice: 'required'. Kimi K2.6 and the Kimi K2.7 Code
models reject that setting, so the provider omits it and returns an
unsupported-setting warning for those model IDs. Other tool choice modes are
passed through unchanged.

contents.heading: log-probabilities
contents.content:
Moonshot V1 models can return token log probabilities through provider
options. Set logprobs to true, or set topLogprobs to automatically enable
log probabilities and request up to 20 alternatives per token:

contents.heading: log-probabilities
contents.content:
The complete content logprob objects are available in Moonshot provider
metadata for both generated and streamed responses.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
Native structured outputs are enabled for Kimi K models and the official
Moonshot V1 text, auto, and vision models.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
The provider normalizes schemas to Moonshot's supported JSON Schema subset and
enables strict schema validation by default.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For unknown custom model IDs, object generation falls back to JSON mode instead
of schema-constrained decoding.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content:
For best reliability, include your schema requirements in the prompt in
addition to passing the schema to generateObject.

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
Moonshot AI supports optional participant names on system, user, and assistant
messages. Set providerOptions.moonshotai.name on each message that should
include a name:

contents.heading: message-names
contents.content:
The same option works with streamText. Names are omitted when unset. The
provider ignores a name on a tool message and returns a warning. Avoid including
unnecessary personal or identifying information in message names.

contents.heading: partial-mode
contents.content:
Moonshot AI Partial Mode
continues a prefix supplied as the final assistant message. Set
providerOptions.moonshotai.partial to true on that message:

contents.heading: partial-mode
contents.content:
The partial assistant message must be the final prompt message. Partial Mode
cannot be combined with JSON object response format; JSON schema response format
is supported.

contents.heading: kimi-k3-dynamic-tool-loading
contents.content:
Kimi K3 can load complete function tool definitions at arbitrary positions in
a conversation. Add tools to the Moonshot provider options of an empty system
message. The provider sends { role: 'system', tools: [...] } without a
content field and normalizes each input schema to Moonshot Flavored JSON
Schema.

contents.heading: kimi-k3-dynamic-tool-loading
contents.content:
Each entry must include its complete function definition. Top-level tools and
dynamically loaded tools can be used in the same request. Known unsupported
official models omit the dynamic message and return a warning; custom model IDs
retain it for forward compatibility.

contents.heading: kimi-k3-dynamic-tool-loading
contents.content:
Keep dynamic system messages in trusted server-side state. Tool names,
descriptions, and schemas are sent to Moonshot and consume context. Dynamic
declarations are request-local, so retain earlier declarations in later
requests while those tools should remain available.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Kimi K3 always reasons and supports low, high, and max reasoning effort.
The default is max. You can configure the effort through provider options:

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content:
Kimi K2.5 and K2.6 can enable or disable thinking. Kimi K2.7 always has
thinking and preserved reasoning enabled. Keep reasoning history in multi-turn
Kimi K2.7 conversations. The reasoning output is exposed through the standard
AI SDK reasoning parts.

contents.heading: reasoning-models
contents.content: See AI SDK UI: Chatbot for more details on how to integrate reasoning into your chatbot.

contents.heading: predicted-outputs
predicted-outputs
contents.content: The content can also be an array of text parts:

contents.heading: predicted-outputs
contents.content:
Predicted content is sent to Moonshot AI as part of the request. Avoid
including sensitive or proprietary text unless you intend to share it with the
provider.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for Moonshot AI language models:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: strictJsonSchema boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether to use strict JSON schema validation for structured outputs. Defaults
to true.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: logprobs boolean

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Whether to return log probabilities for generated tokens.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: topLogprobs number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Number of most likely tokens to return at each token position, from 0 to 20.
Setting this option automatically enables logprobs.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'low' | 'high' | 'max'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Reasoning effort for Kimi K3. Defaults to 'max'.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: prediction { type: 'content'; content: string | Array<{ type: 'text'; text: string }> }

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Supplies static predicted output that can accelerate requests where most of
the response is already known.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: thinking object

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Configuration for Kimi K2.5 and K2.6. Kimi K2.7 accepts only enabled
because its thinking cannot be disabled. Kimi K3 does not accept this field.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: type 'enabled' | 'disabled'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Whether to enable thinking mode. For Kimi K2.7 Code, only 'enabled' is
accepted.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: budgetTokens number

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
Deprecated. Moonshot Chat Completions does not support thinking budgets.
The provider omits this value and returns a warning. It remains accepted
for backwards compatibility.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: reasoningHistory 'disabled' | 'interleaved' | 'preserved'

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content: Controls preserved reasoning behavior in multi-turn conversations:

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
'disabled' and 'interleaved' are retained for compatibility. They do
not change the request, so the model's server-default behavior applies.

contents.heading: provider-options
contents.content:
'preserved' maps to thinking.keep: 'all' for Kimi K2.6. Kimi K2.7 and
K3 preserve reasoning by default.

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
Moonshot AI preserves provider-specific response fields in
providerMetadata.moonshotai for generated and streamed responses:

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: responseObject: chat.completion or chat.completion.chunk

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: choiceIndex: the selected response choice index

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: messageRole: the response message role, when supplied

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content: toolCallTypes: the tool-call type for each returned call

contents.heading: chat-response-metadata
contents.content:
These fields remain in provider metadata because they are specific to
Moonshot AI's Chat Completions response rather than shared AI SDK result
fields.

contents.heading: model-capabilities
contents.content:
The Moonshot V1 series and Kimi K2.5 are unavailable to newly registered users
and are scheduled for full platform sunset on August 31, 2026. They remain
listed because they are still part of the Chat Completions API model surface,
but new applications should use Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7 Code, or Kimi K2.6.

metadata.title: OpenAI
metadata.description: Learn how to use the OpenAI provider for the AI SDK.

contents.content: The OpenAI provider contains language model support for the OpenAI responses, chat, and completion APIs, as well as embedding model support for the OpenAI embeddings API.

contents.heading: setup
contents.content: The OpenAI provider is available in the @ai-sdk/openai module. You can install it with

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can import the default provider instance openai from @ai-sdk/openai:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: If you need a customized setup, you can import createOpenAI from @ai-sdk/openai and create a provider instance with your settings:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: You can use the following optional settings to customize the OpenAI provider instance:

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: baseURL string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Use a different URL prefix for API calls, e.g. to use proxy servers.
It defaults to the OPENAI_BASE_URL environment variable, and then to
https://api.openai.com/v1.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: apiKey string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
API key that is being sent using the Authorization header.
It defaults to the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: name string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
The provider name. You can set this when using OpenAI compatible providers
to change the model provider property. Defaults to openai.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: organization string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: OpenAI Organization.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: project string

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: OpenAI project.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: headers Record<string,string>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: Custom headers to include in the requests.

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content: fetch (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

contents.heading: provider-instance
contents.content:
Custom fetch implementation.
Defaults to the global fetch function.
You can use it as a middleware to intercept requests,
or to provide a custom fetch implementation for e.g. testing.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content: The OpenAI provider instance is a function that you can invoke to create a language model:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
It automatically selects the correct API based on the model id.
You can also pass additional settings in the second argument:

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
The available options depend on the API that's automatically chosen for the model (see below).
If you want to explicitly select a specific model API, you can use .responses, .chat, or .completion.

contents.heading: language-models
contents.content:
Since AI SDK 5, the OpenAI responses API is called by default (unless you
specify e.g. 'openai.chat')

contents.heading: example
contents.content: You can use OpenAI language models to generate text with the generateText function:

contents.heading: example
contents.content:
OpenAI language models can also be used in the streamText, generateObject, and streamObject functions
(see AI SDK Core).

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: You can use the OpenAI responses API with the openai(modelId) or openai.responses(modelId) factory methods. It is the default API that is used by the OpenAI provider (since AI SDK 5).

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
Further configuration can be done using OpenAI provider options.
You can validate the provider options using the OpenAIResponsesProviderOptions type.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The following provider options are available:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
parallelToolCalls boolean
Whether to use parallel tool calls. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: store boolean

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: Whether to store the generation. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
maxToolCalls integer
The maximum number of total calls to built-in tools that can be processed in a response.
This maximum number applies across all built-in tool calls, not per individual tool.
Any further attempts to call a tool by the model will be ignored.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
metadata Record<string, string>
Additional metadata to store with the generation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
conversation string
The ID of the OpenAI Conversation to continue.
You must create a conversation first via the OpenAI API.
Cannot be used in conjunction with previousResponseId.
Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
previousResponseId string
The ID of the previous response. You can use it to continue a conversation. Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
instructions string
Instructions for the model.
They can be used to change the system or developer message when continuing a conversation using the previousResponseId option.
Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
user string
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse. Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningEffort 'none' | 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max'
Reasoning effort for reasoning models. Defaults to medium. If you use providerOptions to set the reasoningEffort option, this model setting will be ignored.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
Supported reasoning efforts vary by model. GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 support 'none',
'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', and 'max'. GPT-6 Astra does not
support 'none'.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
GPT-6 and later models do not support temperature, topP, logprobs, or
the legacy promptCacheRetention option. The provider removes these settings
and returns a warning. Use the Responses API for GPT-6 tool calling.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningEffortUpdate 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max'
Updates the reasoning effort for GPT-6 and later models starting with the
current response without changing the request-level effort. Use this with
previousResponseId to preserve the original prompt prefix for caching.
Configuration updates require standard, single-agent mode and cannot be
combined with automatic truncation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningMode 'standard' | 'pro'
Controls how much model work GPT-5.6 performs before returning a final answer. 'standard' is the default. Use 'pro' for difficult tasks where quality matters more than latency and token usage.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningContext 'auto' | 'current_turn' | 'all_turns'
Controls which available reasoning items GPT-5.6 can reuse. 'auto' uses the model default, 'current_turn' excludes reasoning from earlier turns, and 'all_turns' makes compatible earlier reasoning available. The effective context is returned as providerMetadata.openai.reasoningContext.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningSummary 'auto' | 'detailed'
Controls whether the model returns its reasoning process. Set to 'auto' for a condensed summary, 'detailed' for more comprehensive reasoning. Defaults to undefined (no reasoning summaries). When enabled, reasoning summaries appear in the stream as events with type 'reasoning' and in non-streaming responses within the reasoning field.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
strictJsonSchema boolean
Whether to use strict JSON schema validation. Defaults to false.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
serviceTier 'auto' | 'flex' | 'priority' | 'default'
Service tier for the request. Set to 'flex' for 50% cheaper processing
at the cost of increased latency (available for o3, o4-mini, and gpt-5 models).
Set to 'priority' for faster processing with Enterprise access (available for gpt-4, gpt-5, gpt-5-mini, o3, o4-mini; gpt-5-nano is not supported).

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: Defaults to 'auto'.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
textVerbosity 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'
Controls the verbosity of the model's response. Lower values result in more concise responses,
while higher values result in more verbose responses. Defaults to 'medium'.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
include Array<string>
Specifies additional content to include in the response. Supported values:
['file_search_call.results'] for including file search results in responses.
['message.output_text.logprobs'] for logprobs.
Defaults to undefined.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
truncation string
The truncation strategy to use for the model response.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: Auto: If the input to this Response exceeds the model's context window size, the model will truncate the response to fit the context window by dropping items from the beginning of the conversation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: disabled (default): If the input size will exceed the context window size for a model, the request will fail with a 400 error.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
promptCacheKey string
A cache key for manual prompt caching control. Used by OpenAI to cache responses for similar requests to optimize your cache hit rates.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
promptCacheOptions object
Configures prompt caching for GPT-5.6 and later models. mode can be 'implicit' or 'explicit', and ttl currently only supports '30m'. In explicit mode, only content blocks marked with a prompt cache breakpoint are cached.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
promptCacheRetention 'in_memory' | '24h'
The legacy retention policy for models before GPT-5.6. Set to '24h' to enable extended prompt caching on supported models. For GPT-5.6 and later models, use promptCacheOptions.ttl instead.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
safetyIdentifier string
A stable identifier used to help detect users of your application that may be violating OpenAI's usage policies. The IDs should be a string that uniquely identifies each user.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The OpenAI responses provider also returns provider-specific metadata:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content: The following OpenAI-specific metadata is returned:

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
responseId string
The ID of the response. Can be used to continue a conversation.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
reasoningContext string
The effective persisted-reasoning context returned by GPT-5.6.

contents.heading: responses-models
contents.content:
usage.cacheWriteTokens number
The number of input tokens written to the prompt cache.

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
GPT-6 and later models can change reasoning effort between responses without
changing the request-level reasoningEffort setting. The provider sends
reasoningEffortUpdate as an OpenAI configuration_update input item before
the next user message. Keeping the request-level effort unchanged preserves the
original prompt prefix for prompt caching.

contents.heading: changing-reasoning-effort-mid-conversation
contents.content:
The response metadata continues to report the request-level reasoning effort,
not the effective effort selected by reasoningEffortUpdate. Configuration
updates are not supported with reasoningMode: 'pro' or truncation: 'auto'.

contents.heading: reasoning-output
contents.content: For reasoning models like gpt-5, you can enable reasoning summaries to see the model's thought process. Different models support different summarizers—for example, o4-mini supports detailed summaries. Set reasoningSummary: "auto" to automatically receive the richest level available.

contents.heading: reasoning-output
contents.content: For non-streaming calls with generateText, the reasoning summaries are available in the reasoning field of the response:

contents.heading: reasoning-output
contents.content: Learn more about reasoning summaries in the OpenAI documentation.

contents.heading: verbosity-control
contents.content: You can control the length and detail of model responses using the textVerbosity parameter:

contents.heading: verbosity-control
contents.content: The textVerbosity parameter scales output length without changing the underlying prompt:

contents.heading: verbosity-control
contents.content: 'low': Produces terse, minimal responses

contents.heading: verbosity-control
contents.content: 'medium': Balanced detail (default)

contents.heading: verbosity-control
contents.content: 'high': Verbose responses with comprehensive detail

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: The OpenAI responses API supports web search through the openai.tools.webSearch tool.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: The web search tool supports the following configuration options:

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: externalWebAccess boolean - Whether to use external web access for fetching live content. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: searchContextSize 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' - Controls the amount of context used for the search. Higher values provide more comprehensive results but may have higher latency and cost.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: userLocation - Optional location information to provide geographically relevant results. Includes type (always 'approximate'), country, city, region, and timezone.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: filters - Optional filter configuration to restrict search results.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: allowedDomains string[] - Up to 100 allowed domains for the search.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: blockedDomains string[] - Up to 100 blocked domains for the search.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: Omit the HTTP or HTTPS prefix from domain filters. Subdomains of configured domains are automatically included or excluded.

contents.heading: web-search-tool
contents.content: For detailed information on configuration options see the OpenAI Web Search Tool documentation.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: The OpenAI responses API supports file search through the openai.tools.fileSearch tool.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content: You can force the use of the file search tool by setting the toolChoice parameter to { type: 'tool', toolName: 'file_search' }.

contents.heading: file-search-tool
contents.content:
The tool must be named file_search when using OpenAI's file search
functionality. This name is required by OpenAI's API specification and cannot
be customized.

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
OpenAI's Responses API supports multi-modal image generation as a provider-defined tool.
Availability is restricted to specific models (for example, gpt-5 variants).

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content: You can use the image tool with either generateText or streamText:

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
When you set store: false, then previously generated images will not be
accessible by the model. We recommend using the image generation tool without
setting store: false.

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content:
For complete details on model availability, image quality controls, supported sizes, and tool-specific parameters,
refer to the OpenAI documentation:

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content: Image generation overview and models: OpenAI Image Generation

contents.heading: image-generation-tool
contents.content: Image generation tool parameters (background, size, quality, format, etc.): Image Generation Tool Options

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content:
The OpenAI responses API supports the code interpreter tool through the openai.tools.codeInterpreter tool.
This allows models to write and execute Python code.

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content: The code interpreter tool can be configured with:

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content: container: Either a container ID string or an object with fileIds to specify uploaded files that should be available to the code interpreter

contents.heading: code-interpreter-tool
contents.content:
The tool must be named code_interpreter when using OpenAI's code interpreter
functionality. This name is required by OpenAI's API specification and cannot
be customized.

contents.heading: local-shell-tool
contents.content:
The OpenAI responses API support the local shell tool for Codex models through the openai.tools.localShell tool.
Local shell is a tool that allows agents to run shell commands locally on a machine you or the user provides.

contents.heading: local-shell-tool
contents.content:
The tool must be named local_shell. This name is required by OpenAI's API
specification and cannot be customized. The model can only be

contents.heading: async-tool-calling
contents.content:
GPT-6 Astra and later Responses models support
async tool calling.
An async tool lets the model continue generating independent output after issuing
the call instead of waiting for its result. Your application still executes the
tool and sends its result in a later request using the original tool call ID.

contents.heading: async-tool-calling
contents.content: Enable async calling on a function tool with providerOptions.openai.async:

contents.heading: async-tool-calling
contents.content:
The generated tool call exposes the provider marker as
providerMetadata.openai.async. Use providerMetadata.openai.responseId as the
next request's previousResponseId, and submit the result in a tool message with
the original toolCallId.

contents.heading: async-tool-calling
contents.content:
With streamText, OpenAI can continue streaming text after the completed
tool-call part. Use the tool's onInputAvailable callback to start work as soon
as that part arrives. If execute returns the same already-running promise, tool
execution overlaps the rest of the model stream. Omit execute when the job
should outlive the current generation and submit its result in a later request.

contents.heading: async-tool-calling
contents.content:
Async calling applies to directly called function tools. It does not apply to
hosted tools such as web search or code interpreter.

contents.heading: image-inputs
contents.content:
The OpenAI Responses API supports Image inputs for appropriate models.
You can pass Image files as part of the message content using the 'image' type:

contents.heading: image-inputs
contents.content:
The model will have access to the image and will respond to questions about it.
The image should be passed using the image field.

contents.heading: image-inputs
contents.content: You can also pass a file-id from the OpenAI Files API.

contents.heading: image-inputs
contents.content: You can also pass the URL of an image.

contents.heading: pdf-inputs
contents.content:
The OpenAI Responses API supports reading PDF files.
You can pass PDF files as part of the message content using the file type:

contents.heading: pdf-inputs
contents.content: You can also pass a file-id from the OpenAI Files API.

contents.heading: pdf-inputs
contents.content: You can also pass the URL of a pdf.

contents.heading: pdf-inputs
contents.content:
The model will have access to the contents of the PDF file and
respond to questions about it.
The PDF file should be passed using the data field,
and the mediaType should be set to 'application/pdf'.

contents.heading: structured-outputs
contents.content: The OpenAI Responses API supports structured outputs. You can enforce structured outputs using generateObject or streamObject, which expose a schema option. Additionally, you can pass a Zod or JSON Schema object to the experimental_output option when using generateText or streamText.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the OpenAI chat API using the .chat() factory method.
The first argument is the model id, e.g. gpt-4.
The OpenAI chat models support tool calls and some have multi-modal capabilities.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
OpenAI chat models support also some model specific provider options that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them in the providerOptions argument:

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for OpenAI chat models:

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: logitBias Record<number, number>

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Modifies the likelihood of specified tokens appearing in the completion.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Accepts a JSON object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in
the GPT tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. You
can use this tokenizer tool to convert text to token IDs. Mathematically,
the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling.
The exact effect will vary per model, but values between -1 and 1 should
decrease or increase likelihood of selection; values like -100 or 100
should result in a ban or exclusive selection of the relevant token.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: As an example, you can pass {"50256": -100} to prevent the token from being generated.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: logprobs boolean | number

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Return the log probabilities of the tokens. Including logprobs will increase
the response size and can slow down response times. However, it can
be useful to better understand how the model is behaving.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Setting to true will return the log probabilities of the tokens that
were generated.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Setting to a number will return the log probabilities of the top n
tokens that were generated.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: parallelToolCalls boolean

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Whether to enable parallel function calling during tool use. Defaults to true.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: user string

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to
monitor and detect abuse. Learn more.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: reasoningEffort 'none' | 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max'

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Reasoning effort for reasoning models. Defaults to medium. If you use
providerOptions to set the reasoningEffort option, this
model setting will be ignored.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Supported reasoning efforts vary by model. GPT-5.6 supports 'none', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', and 'max'.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: structuredOutputs boolean

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Whether to use structured outputs.
Defaults to true.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: When enabled, tool calls and object generation will be strict and follow the provided schema.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: maxCompletionTokens number

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Maximum number of completion tokens to generate. Useful for reasoning models.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: store boolean

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Whether to enable persistence in Responses API.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: metadata Record<string, string>

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Metadata to associate with the request.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: prediction Record<string, any>

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Parameters for prediction mode.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: serviceTier 'auto' | 'flex' | 'priority' | 'default'

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Service tier for the request. Set to 'flex' for 50% cheaper processing
at the cost of increased latency (available for o3, o4-mini, and gpt-5 models).
Set to 'priority' for faster processing with Enterprise access (available for gpt-4, gpt-5, gpt-5-mini, o3, o4-mini; gpt-5-nano is not supported).

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Defaults to 'auto'.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: strictJsonSchema boolean

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content:
Whether to use strict JSON schema validation.
Defaults to false.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: textVerbosity 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Controls the verbosity of the model's responses. Lower values will result in more concise responses, while higher values will result in more verbose responses.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: promptCacheKey string

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: A cache key for manual prompt caching control. Used by OpenAI to cache responses for similar requests to optimize your cache hit rates.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: promptCacheOptions object

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: Configures prompt caching for GPT-5.6 and later models. mode can be 'implicit' or 'explicit', and ttl currently only supports '30m'. In explicit mode, only content blocks marked with a prompt cache breakpoint are cached.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: promptCacheRetention 'in_memory' | '24h'

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: The legacy retention policy for models before GPT-5.6. Set to '24h' to enable extended prompt caching on supported models. For GPT-5.6 and later models, use promptCacheOptions.ttl instead.

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: safetyIdentifier string

contents.heading: chat-models
contents.content: A stable identifier used to help detect users of your application that may be violating OpenAI's usage policies. The IDs should be a string that uniquely identifies each user.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
OpenAI has introduced the o1,o3, and o4 series of reasoning models.
Currently, o4-mini, o3, o3-mini, and o1 are available via both the chat and responses APIs. The
models codex-mini-latest and computer-use-preview are available only via the responses API.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: Reasoning models currently only generate text, have several limitations, and are only supported using generateText and streamText.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: They support additional settings and response metadata:

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: You can use providerOptions to set

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: the reasoningEffort option (or alternatively the reasoningEffort model setting), which determines the amount of reasoning the model performs.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content: You can use response usage.reasoningTokens to access the number of reasoning tokens that the model generated.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
System messages are automatically converted to OpenAI developer messages for
reasoning models when supported.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
Reasoning models require additional runtime inference to complete their
reasoning phase before generating a response. This introduces longer latency
compared to other models.

contents.heading: reasoning
contents.content:
maxOutputTokens is automatically mapped to max_completion_tokens for
reasoning models.

contents.heading: structured-outputs-1
contents.content:
Structured outputs are enabled by default.
You can disable them by setting the structuredOutputs option to false.

contents.heading: structured-outputs-1
contents.content:
OpenAI structured outputs have several
limitations,
in particular around the supported schemas,
and are therefore opt-in.

contents.heading: structured-outputs-1
contents.content:
For example, optional schema properties are not supported.
You need to change Zod .nullish() and .optional() to .nullable().

contents.heading: logprobs
contents.content:
OpenAI provides logprobs information for completion/chat models.
You can access it in the providerMetadata object.

contents.heading: image-support
contents.content:
The OpenAI Chat API supports Image inputs for appropriate models.
You can pass Image files as part of the message content using the 'image' type:

contents.heading: image-support
contents.content:
The model will have access to the image and will respond to questions about it.
The image should be passed using the image field.

contents.heading: image-support
contents.content: You can also pass the URL of an image.

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content:
The OpenAI Chat API supports reading PDF files.
You can pass PDF files as part of the message content using the file type:

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content:
The model will have access to the contents of the PDF file and
respond to questions about it.
The PDF file should be passed using the data field,
and the mediaType should be set to 'application/pdf'.

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content: You can also pass a file-id from the OpenAI Files API.

contents.heading: pdf-support
contents.content: You can also pass the URL of a PDF.

contents.heading: predicted-outputs
contents.content:
OpenAI supports predicted outputs for gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini.
Predicted outputs help you reduce latency by allowing you to specify a base text that the model should modify.
You can enable predicted outputs by adding the prediction option to the providerOptions.openai object:

contents.heading: predicted-outputs
contents.content:
OpenAI provides usage information for predicted outputs (acceptedPredictionTokens and rejectedPredictionTokens).
You can access it in the providerMetadata object.

contents.heading: predicted-outputs
contents.content:
OpenAI Predicted Outputs have several
limitations,
e.g. unsupported API parameters and no tool calling support.

contents.heading: image-detail
contents.content: You can use the openai provider option to set the image input detail to high, low, original, or auto:

contents.heading: image-detail
contents.content: For GPT-5.6, original preserves the input dimensions without resizing to a patch budget or pixel-dimension limit. auto and an omitted detail setting use the same sizing behavior as original, which can increase input token usage for large images.

contents.heading: image-detail
contents.content:
Because the UIMessage type (used by AI SDK UI hooks like useChat) does not
support the providerOptions property, you can use convertToModelMessages
first before passing the messages to functions like generateText or
streamText. For more details on providerOptions usage, see
here.

contents.heading: distillation
contents.content:
OpenAI supports model distillation for some models.
If you want to store a generation for use in the distillation process, you can add the store option to the providerOptions.openai object.
This will save the generation to the OpenAI platform for later use in distillation.

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content:
OpenAI has introduced Prompt Caching for supported models
including gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini.

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content:
Prompt caching is automatically enabled for these models, when the prompt is 1024 tokens or longer. It does
not need to be explicitly enabled.

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: Cache reads are reported in usage.cachedInputTokens.

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: For GPT-5.6 and later models, cache writes are reported in providerMetadata.openai.usage.cacheWriteTokens.

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: For GPT-5.6 and later models, promptCacheOptions.ttl sets a minimum cache lifetime of 30 minutes. Earlier models generally retain in-memory prefixes for 5-10 minutes of inactivity, up to one hour.

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: To improve cache hit rates, you can manually control caching using the promptCacheKey option:

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: GPT-5.6 and later models support explicit cache breakpoints on system messages and supported text, image, and file content blocks. Set a request-level cache key and mark the end of each reusable prefix with promptCacheBreakpoint:

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: In 'implicit' mode, OpenAI places an automatic breakpoint on the latest message and also honors explicit breakpoints. In 'explicit' mode, only marked content blocks are eligible for caching; a request without any explicit breakpoint does not use prompt caching.

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: In AI SDK v5, a breakpoint on a tool-result part applies to the whole tool result. When the result contains multiple nested output parts, the OpenAI provider places the API breakpoint on the final nested part because the v5 provider interface does not carry provider options on each nested output item.

contents.heading: prompt-caching
contents.content: For models before GPT-5.6 that support extended caching, you can keep cached prefixes active for up to 24 hours:

contents.heading: audio-input
contents.content: With the gpt-4o-audio-preview model, you can pass audio files to the model.

contents.heading: audio-input
contents.content:
The gpt-4o-audio-preview model is currently in preview and requires at least
some audio inputs. It will not work with non-audio data.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
You can create models that call the OpenAI completions API using the .completion() factory method.
The first argument is the model id.
Currently only gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct is supported.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
OpenAI completion models support also some model specific settings that are not part of the standard call settings.
You can pass them as an options argument:

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: The following optional provider options are available for OpenAI completion models:

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: echo: boolean

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: Echo back the prompt in addition to the completion.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: logitBias Record<number, number>

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content: Modifies the likelihood of specified tokens appearing in the completion.

contents.heading: completion-models
contents.content:
Accepts a JSON object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in
the GPT tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. You
can use this tokenizer tool to convert text to token IDs. Mathematically,
the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling.
The exact effect will vary per model, but values between -1 and 1 should
decrease or increase likelihood of selection; values like -100 or 100

contents.heading: transcription-models

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:

Defaults to ['segment'].
Possible values are ['word'], ['segment'], and ['word', 'segment'].
Note: There is no additional latency for segment timestamps, but generating word timestamps incurs additional latency.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
language string
The language of the input audio. Supplying the input language in ISO-639-1 format (e.g. 'en') will improve accuracy and latency.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
prompt string
An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment. The prompt should match the audio language.
Optional.

contents.heading: transcription-models
contents.content:
temperature number
The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use log probability to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.
Defaults to 0.
Optional.

Additional information to include in the transcription response.

metadata.description: Learn how to use Perplexity's Sonar API with the AI SDK.

contents.content: The Perplexity provider offers access to Sonar API - a language model that uniquely combines real-time web search with natural language processing. Each response is grounded in current web data and includes detailed citations, making it ideal for research, fact-checking, and obtaining up-to-date information.
API keys can be obtained from the Perplexity Platform.

contents.content: The Vercel provider gives you access to the v0 API, designed for building modern web applications. The v0 models support text and image inputs and provide fast streaming responses.
You can create your Vercel API key at v0.dev.

The v0 API is currently in beta and requires a Premium or Team plan with
usage-based billing enabled. For details, visit the pricing
page. To request a higher limit, contact Vercel at
support@v0.dev.
